chapters.title: Chapter 451
paragraphs: “Benefactor, where are you going?”
“Huh?”
I flinched as I quietly edged toward the door. Cheongpung, who had gathered up his belongings, tilted his head at me.
“What? Why?”
“Are you going somewhere?”
“I, uh... something urgent came up.”
“You said we had to leave right away.”
“Listen, Young Hero Cheong. I wasn’t going to go into this, but...”
I deliberately hardened my expression.
“I’m going to relieve myself. Happy?”
“But the privy isn’t in that direction.”
*He was annoyingly sharp.*
Martial arts were his minor, while eating and shitting were his major. He had to know the location of every privy on the island.
After a moment’s hesitation, I answered.
“...I’m going to piss outside.”
Even I had to admit it was a desperate excuse.
Only then did Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin realize something was off. They stopped packing their bags and turned toward me.
“Young Hero Gung, doesn’t the Captain seem unusually talkative today?”
“Yeah. Why does he look so restless?”
“That’s because I’m trying to decide which of you two to hit first.”
Normally, they would have backed down the moment I said something like that. But after being thoroughly conditioned by my violence, the two of them had grown considerably.
“Hmm. If this were our usual Captain, his hands would have moved before his words. But he’s trying to talk his way out of it? There’s definitely something going on.”
“Right?”
“Absolutely. Do you think I’ve only been beaten once or twice? There’s a logic and flow to these things.”
As Hyuk Mujin stared at me through narrowed eyes, Gung Gibang’s eyes suddenly widened, and he glanced around.
“Wait. Where did Mungyeong go?”
“Oh, you’re right. He was here a moment ago. Where the hell did he go?”
*Where else? He was already outside waiting for me.*
*Let’s talk.*
I sighed as I recalled the Sound Transmission Mungyeong had sent me earlier.
Denying it any longer would only make them more suspicious.
“He’s outside. We have something to discuss in private.”
“In the privy? Just the two of you?”
“...What the hell are you talking about, you lunatic? You’re making it sound suggestive.”
Hyuk Mujin gave me a dubious look.
“Captain, I’ve already been conditioned to insults and violence, so I’ll be fine. But please don’t expose Mungyeong to any strange influences.”
*What the hell was this lunatic talking about? I was the one about to end up covered in blood.*
I was too dumbfounded to speak, and Gung Gibang added his two cents.
“Hyuk’s right. The more I see that kid, the more thoughtful and kind he seems. Don’t pick on him for no reason.”
“Wow. You bastards, seriously...”
I stopped myself.
“Forget it. What would you two know?”
Cheongpung had at least finally noticed what was going on and kept his mouth shut like a mute with honey in it...
No, now that I looked closer, he really was stuffing candy into his mouth.
*Where does he keep getting that candy?*
If I stayed here any longer, I was going to lose my mind.
Shaking my head, I ignored the voices behind me and left the house.
Outside, Mungyeong stood waiting in the courtyard, dressed in spotless white robes.
“You’re late.”
“It didn’t take that long...”
“You’re late.”
“Sorry...”
“You’re late.”
*Please save me.*
The pressure of that broken-record routine was no joke. His aura bore down on me so subtly that no one else could detect it, and I swallowed hard.
“S-sorry I’m late. But what’s going on?”
“Pardon?”
“Huh?”
“What do you mean? You called me out earlier because you had something to say.”
*Had Cannes named him Actor of the Year or something?*
He blinked as if he truly had no idea what I was talking about. For a moment, even I nearly fell for it.
The monster wearing the skin of a young medical apprentice smiled brightly and continued.
“Oh, you want us to move somewhere else for a moment? Understood.”
“No. If possible, I think it would be better to talk right here...”
“Oh, you want us to move somewhere else for a moment? Understood.”
“...Fine. Let’s go.”
*I miss my mother.*
Holding back tears, I followed Mungyeong.
We avoided the occasional disciples of the Zhuge Clan and Wudang, along with the river bandits of Water Dragon Stronghold, until we reached a deserted area. Only then did Mungyeong finally speak.
“Dark Heaven. Was this their doing?”
“Yeah. It looks that way.”
“There’s no one here.”
I corrected myself at the speed of light.
“It appears so, sir.”
“So it is not certain yet.”
“There is always some possibility of error. But although we haven’t found the formation, I’m convinced Dark Heaven was responsible.”
“Dark Heaven. Dark Heaven...”
Mungyeong muttered the words under his breath, then suddenly raised his head.
He silently gazed at the dark night sky, where even the full moon had hidden itself. After a moment, he abruptly asked, “Did you notice anything strange about the corpses?”
“Something strange?”
“The wounds left on them.”
Every death left traces. This was especially true of deaths caused by battles between martial artists.

I had heard that a widely experienced master with a deep understanding of various martial arts could identify the weapon used—and even determine which form had killed the victim—simply by examining the wounds on a corpse.
And the young medical apprentice before me possessed both the discernment and martial prowess to make him one of the finest examiners of the dead in Murim.
“I have never seen wounds like these before. They seem to follow the principles of the very basic Three Calamities Sword Technique, yet they undulate like waves. They are exceedingly strange.”
Mungyeong slowly raised one hand and swept it through the air. Thread-thin strands of internal energy flowed from it, glowing faintly in the darkness.
“If I had to guess, the culprit did not use an ordinary weapon. It was an unusual weapon with a winding blade, something akin to a Snake Sword.”
“I thought they’d been cut with Force.”
“Your guess is correct. It was Force—or something every bit as sharp.”
The only thing as sharp as Force was Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
And no matter how thoroughly Dark Heaven had prepared, there was no way so many of its forces could have been armed with weapons made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
*No matter how much gold you have, Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron is difficult to obtain.*
This was not a question of capital. It was a question of resource scarcity.
As I stood lost in thought, Mungyeong asked, “Did you examine all the corpses?”
“Not all of them. I looked at the ones that stood out. I’m not particularly knowledgeable, so even after examining them myself, I couldn’t tell which martial arts or forms had been used.”
“One of the corpses you examined belonged to Hwang Chung, the Yangtze One Saber. What did you make of it?”
“He’d been cut cleanly in two at the waist by Force. But the decay was so severe that I couldn’t determine anything beyond that...”
“And the Mad Water Saber Demon and the Wave Fox?”
“Those two...”
I suddenly frowned.
A detail shared by all three corpses had just occurred to me.
*...Only their upper bodies remained.*
The lower halves of all three corpses were nowhere to be found.
I had seen several other corpses like that, so it had not struck me as strange at the time. Now that I thought about it, though, it was certainly suspicious.
“Didn’t the fish eat them?”

“That would not be entirely wrong. From what I determined, the massacre at Donghu Stronghold took place ten days ago. The cold has been gone for some time, so severe decay is only natural. The corpses submerged in water would have fared even worse.”
Warm sunlight and damp air had erased many of the traces left behind by death.
But they had not erased everything.
“By comparison, the commoners’ corpses still had their limbs relatively intact. Did you notice that?”
“Yes. Those who hadn’t learned martial arts weren’t cut apart. They were crushed.”
Unlike the corpses of the river bandits, the bodies of the children, women, and elderly had not been severed. Their entire bodies had simply been crushed and pulverized.
And there was one more thing.

“The houses and the surrounding ground had caved in everywhere. That would have been impossible without a force of ten thousand geun, and it is not a method an internal-arts master with profound internal energy would choose.”
“So, an external-arts master?”
“There’s no one here, remember?”
“...I was just talking to myself.”
*He was awfully sensitive about this.*
After hurriedly making that excuse, I fell silent and considered the matter.
Martial arts in Murim could broadly be divided into two categories.
Internal arts emphasized the efficient use and application of internal energy. External arts also used internal energy, but focused on tempering the body to their absolute limits.
Most people faced those two paths upon entering the world of martial arts, and most chose the former.
Partly because training in external arts was excruciating, but also because achieving any meaningful results required long years of grueling perseverance.
*Which means there are only a handful of Supreme Peak external-arts masters capable of this level of destruction.*
There were hardly any Supreme Peak masters in the world to begin with, even if you turned the whole realm upside down and shook it out.
I glanced at Mungyeong, silently asking for an answer. A faint crease appeared on the young medical apprentice’s smooth forehead.
“Looking at me will do you no good. I do not know his identity either. No—I should say their identities, not his.”
“There are two?”
“At least two. Three at most.”
“Three Supreme Peak masters...”
“Based on my guess, they are even more formidable than the Qilian Three Fiends we faced in Sichuan. At least one of them uses an unusual weapon.”
*For fuck’s sake. This isn’t some five-star establishment. Why are there three Supreme Peak masters?*

It was only because Mungyeong and Jeok Cheongang were holding down the fort that I could afford to leave at all. Without them here, I would have been too worried about what might happen to go anywhere.
“With this much information, the Third Fiend might know something. He must have at least heard who his comrades were.”
The Third Fiend we had captured in Sichuan was one of the reasons I was going to the Zhuge Clan.
I had heard that he had become like a bipolar patient after his balls were crushed, but if I worked him over with enough care and dedication, he would not last long.
*Maybe we can even put him out front and have him lead us to the formation.*
That hopeful thought had barely crossed my mind when Mungyeong spoke.
“Perhaps it is someone everyone already knows.”
“What?”
“I mean the one who uses that unusual weapon.”
It took me quite a while to grasp what he meant.
The realization struck like a hammer to the back of my head.
I stared blankly at Mungyeong.
“Are you serious?”
“A seasoned Supreme Peak master. Forms and wounds so unusual that they are difficult to read. There cannot be many people at that realm who wield such a weapon.”
“Then it really is...”
A dry voice emerged from between Mungyeong’s lips.
“The Dongting Fisherman. For now, he is the most likely suspect.”
The eccentric master who had never left the area around Dongting Lake in his entire life.

Unusually, he used a fishing rod made of black wood as his signature weapon. He was a Supreme Peak master who had crossed Tianling Falls and disappeared after becoming enraged by the tragic news concerning his friend, the head of the Sea Serpent Society.
*Everything fits perfectly.*
I had forgotten for a moment.
I had forgotten about his existence.
This was no baseless suspicion.
Unlike the others, the Dongting Fisherman’s corpse had never been found. The only trace he had left behind was his broken black-wood fishing rod.
It was only a guess, but what if the Dongting Fisherman really was a member of Dark Heaven?
“But the Dongting Fisherman Zhuge Feng told me about had absolutely no reason to do something like this...”
“Everything has a reason. The Dongting Fisherman is only human. He must have had a shadow he showed no one. Zhuge Feng is likely suspicious of him by now as well.”
Mungyeong turned away, his voice cold.
“Always be suspicious, and stay alert. May martial fortune be with you.”

chapters.title: Chapter 452
paragraphs: Unlike the journey in, the way out wasn’t as difficult as I’d expected.

Part of that was because the whirlpools of Tianling Falls mostly spiraled outward. It also helped that the veteran river bandits from Water Dragon Stronghold, who had spent years working aboard ships, were making full use of their skills.
“Turn to port!”
“Starboard! Don’t row until the signal!”
“More, more, more... Now!”
“Yaaah!”
Whoooosh! Splash!
“The boat—the boat’s tilting!”
“Great Hero Jin!”
“Help us!”
“...Damn it, you bastards.”
Come to think of it, maybe it was a little difficult after all.
Still, it was nothing we couldn’t handle. Even without powerful allies like Jeok Cheongang and Mungyeong, Cheongpung and I could overcome most crises if we stepped in.
*The first time is hard. Why would the second be?*
The river bandits weren’t the only ones who had grown accustomed to the violent whirlpools of Tianling Falls. I had prepared in advance as well, and thrust both palms forward with all my strength.
Boom!
The tilting swift ship regained its balance. Now it was time to pick up speed and escape this damned whirlpool.
I called out to the man I had stationed at the stern for precisely this situation.
“Cheongpung, now!”
“Yee-haw!”
“You crazy bastard! Stop hanging there and playing around!”
“Oh, sorry, Benefactor. I didn’t mean to. Before I knew it...”
“Just hurry up and do it!”
“Yes!”
Boom, boom, boom!
Cheongpung was about as far from normal as a person could get, but his skills were undeniable.

Dozens of palm shadows infused with powerful internal energy struck through the air and lashed the surface of the water. The resulting thrust sent the swift ship vaulting over the whirlpool of Tianling Falls before landing on the other side.
Boom! Splash!
A towering spray engulfed the hull. Drenched from head to toe in river water, Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin muttered under their breath.
“Damn it. Last time we got dunked, and now we’re getting drenched. We really do get everything.”
“I swear, once this is over, I’m never coming back to the Yangtze. Not ever. Every day feels like living the life of a goddamn beggar.”
“...Are you picking a fight with me?”
“No. Honestly, doesn’t it feel like we’re living as beggars?”
“That’s true. It pisses me off, but you’re right. You’re right, and it still pisses me off.”
“Damn. I really do feel like a beggar.”
“...I get it, so shut up.”
Those two acted like this every chance they got.
Leaving behind the bickering of our two human pieces of sweet-and-sour pork—dunked on the way in and drenched on the way out—the swift ship cleared Tianling Falls safely and sped across the Yangtze.
About three shichen later, the ship that had departed at dawn reached the ferry landing at Zaoyang. By then, it was already close to noon.
“The waterways of the Yangtze do not reach Mount Longzhong, where the Zhuge Clan is located. From here, you will have to travel by land.”
The deputy Stronghold Lord of Water Dragon Stronghold had come in Mu Song’s place. I nodded at his explanation.
Hubei Province had highly developed land and water transportation, but that didn’t mean every tributary of the Yangtze was connected. A boat couldn’t travel where there was no water.
*It’s not like these people are Vikings.*
Fortunately, the broad, level highways were well maintained. We could reach our destination quickly by carriage or by using movement techniques.
Zaoyang and Mount Longzhong were relatively close, so the journey shouldn’t take long.
The Zhuge Clan retainer whom Zhuge Feng had ordered to accompany us wasn’t standing around idle, either.

“I will send word to the Zaoyang branch immediately and have carriages prepared. Relay stations have been established all along the main roads, so if we change carriages along the way, we will reach our family home in no time.”
“Oh, right.”
The Zhuge Clan was a prestigious major faction that divided control of Hubei Province with Wudang.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan had also established branches and sub-branches throughout Shanxi Province to solidify its control over the region. The Zhuge Clan’s network was probably even more extensive.
*It’s like a major brand opening chain stores.*
*Then we should arrive in half a day at the latest.*
I had just stepped off the ship after roughly calculating the travel time in my head when—
Clack, clack, clack.
A group appeared to the sound of perfectly synchronized footsteps and surrounded the ferry landing.
I frowned as I stared at the unwelcome guests.
*What is this now?*
There were nearly thirty martial artists.
Every one of them wore a lustrous blue silk martial uniform and carried a high-quality steel longsword at their waist. Hyuk Mujin’s eyes widened.
“That’s...”
“What? Do you know them?”
“No. I was just surprised by those silk uniforms.”
“What?”

“That’s Shu brocade from Sichuan. It’s considered one of the finest silks under heaven. My father dreamed of filling an entire warehouse with it. That’s how expensive and precious it is... And they made martial uniforms out of it. I don’t know who their employer is, but they must be loaded.”
I’d told the bastard to identify them, and he was evaluating the quality of their silk instead.
As I stared at him in disbelief, Gung Gibang clicked his tongue and cut in.
“I can’t tell whether that bastard is a martial artist or a cloth merchant. Don’t expect anything from that Hyuk brat. Ask this elder instead.”
“I don’t know about making you an elder, but I can make you a cripple. Tell us before my fist gets there.”
“...They’re martial artists from Qingxia Hall. I told you, so please loosen that fist a little.”
“Qingxia Hall? What do those bastards do?”
Gung Gibang glanced at my still-clenched fist and answered.
“They aren’t an official sect, but they wield considerable influence in Hubei Province in various ways.”
“They look pretty pathetic for people with that kind of influence.”
I glanced at the martial artists standing in formation in the distance.
They wore uniforms made of expensive Shu brocade and carried quality swords, but that was all.
Most were Second or Third Rate swordsmen who fell short of First Rate. Perhaps they cared more about their appearance than their martial arts, because every one of them was well built and handsome.
*They’re even wearing makeup.*
At this point, weren’t they idols rather than martial artists?
It almost made me wonder if the K-pop craze that had begun in Korea had crossed worlds and spread all the way to Murim.
Qingxia Bulletproof Martial Artist Corps. Maybe they had come to play a gig under a name like that.
“Those guys’ group name—or rather, their organization’s name—was Qingxia Hall, right? They’re actually a big deal in Hubei?”
“I’ve heard they throw considerable weight around.”
“They look like they’d piss themselves the moment a real fight started...”
Did Hubei decide its sect rankings through popularity votes?
While I was seriously pondering the question, the Zhuge Clan retainer spoke.
“Qingxia Hall is a sort of social club.”
“A social club?”

“Yes. It was formed by the sons and daughters of influential people with varying degrees of power throughout Hubei Province. They are always running around together and causing all kinds of trouble, but they have such powerful backing that matters usually fizzle out without consequence.”
“Oh. A gold-spoon club.”
“I’m sorry, what did you say?”
“Nothing important. In that case, we can just continue on our way.”
So that was all they were. A noisy empty cart decked out in gaudy finery.
Pathetic people like that could be found anywhere. Having lost interest in Qingxia Hall, I took the lead and started walking.
“Which way do we go to reach the Zaoyang branch?”
“It will take less than fifteen minutes from here. First, we should head to the main road over there...”
The Zhuge Clan retainer trailed off.
An extravagantly luxurious procession was approaching from the main road he had just indicated—more lavish than anything I had ever seen.
“The heroes of Qingxia Hall are passing through!”
At the shrill cry of a middle-aged man with weasel whiskers, musicians walking along both sides of the procession began to play. Beautiful women scattered flower petals through the air.
The main road was instantly swept up in a festive atmosphere.
The commoners traveling along it watched the procession with expressions mingling anticipation and discontent.
Their countless gazes converged on ten young men and women riding in four-bearer palanquins carved with dragons and phoenixes.
Wreathed in the easy smiles only the rich could afford, they looked down at the poorly dressed commoners and tossed something from their hands.
Clatter, clatter, clatter!
Not hidden weapons... money. Gleaming silver nyang, each worth a hundred iron coins.
Only then did I understand the anticipation on the commoners’ faces.
“Waaah!”
“Silver nyang! It’s silver!”
“Jang-pal, you vile bastard! How dare you try to snatch someone else’s silver nyang? Take your hand off it right now!”
“Bullshit. Didn’t you see my hand get there first?”
“You fucking son of a—!”
Cheers and curses rose over the ceaselessly falling petals and silver nyang.
A woman bit into her unexpected windfall to test it. Men loudly insisted that they were the rightful owners, then promptly began fighting over it.
Meanwhile, the young men and women in the palanquins laughed as they watched the spectacle.
“What a complete shitshow.”
The sight made me shake my head.

The rich kids scattering money and enjoying the people’s reactions as if they were watching a circus looked pathetic. The sight of the commoners fighting tooth and nail for a single silver nyang left a bitter taste in my mouth and made me feel sorry for them.
But it had nothing to do with me.
“Forget about that. Let’s just get going...”
I trailed off and blinked.
What the hell was this?
Gone.
The bastards who had been beside me moments ago were nowhere to be seen. Only the Zhuge Clan retainer remained, standing there awkwardly.
“Wait, where did every one of those bastards go?”
The retainer hesitated, then raised a hand and pointed in one direction.
“They’re over there.”
I turned my head and was rendered speechless.
Whoosh, whoosh-whoosh!
“No! You can’t!”
“My silver!”
One person was darting through the crowd with ghostlike movements, snatching silver nyang out of the air.
No. Not one person.
One fucking beggar.
*The Myriad-Li Chasing Wind Movement Technique?*
That lunatic was actually using a secret technique of the Beggars’ Sect for this?

He was faster and more agile than I had ever seen him. He had complained endlessly that he’d only mastered the technique to the fifth stage, yet the movements he was displaying now were at least seventh-stage.
*That bastard is single-handedly disgracing the Beggars’ Sect.*
Even for a beggar, how could he be this devoted to his calling?
But I had no time to worry about another sect’s reputation. The Jin Family of Taiyuan’s own dark horse was no less impressive.
“Haap!”
Whoosh! Rat-a-tat-tat!
Hyuk Mujin kicked off the ground and soared into the air, swinging his sword. The silver nyang caught in its powerful, fluid arc popped into the air, then showered down onto the flat of his blade.
Hyuk Mujin’s face lit up when he checked the silver.
“Wow! Ten silver nyang!”
That bastard had ten hits coming. Guaranteed.
I swallowed the curses rising to my throat and searched for the last remaining person.
*Where is that Cheongpung bastard?*
Unlike Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin, who were scooping up silver nyang with all their might, Cheongpung was nowhere to be seen.
But I knew the habits of the creature called Cheongpung inside and out, so it didn’t take me long to find him.
“First, ten sweets, please. Oh, and some jeonbyeong too. Not the ones you just picked up—the big ones over there, and give me plenty. Wow, thank you! By any chance, where’s the dumpling shop?”
Snap.
Something inside my head broke. My eyes rolled back until only the whites showed, and I roared.
“You fucking bastards!”

The deputy Stronghold Lord of Water Dragon Stronghold had come in Mu Song’s place.
I nodded at his explanation.
Hubei Province had highly developed land and water transportation, but that didn’t mean every tributary of the Yangtze was connected.
A boat couldn’t travel where there was no water.
*It’s not like these people are Vikings.*
Fortunately, the broad, level highways were well maintained.
We could reach our destination quickly by carriage or by using movement techniques.
Zaoyang and Mount Longzhong were relatively close, so the journey shouldn’t take long.
The Zhuge Clan retainer whom Zhuge Feng had ordered to accompany us wasn’t standing around idle, either.
“I will send word to the Zaoyang branch immediately and have carriages prepared.
Relay stations have been established all along the main roads, so if we change carriages along the way, we will reach our family home in no time.”
“Oh, right.”
The Zhuge Clan was a prestigious major faction that divided control of Hubei Province with Wudang.
The Jin Family of Taiyuan had also established branches and sub-branches throughout Shanxi Province to solidify its control over the region.
The Zhuge Clan’s network was probably even more extensive.
*It’s like a major brand opening chain stores.*
*Then we should arrive in half a day at the latest.*

Clack, clack, clack.

There were nearly thirty martial artists.

“What?

“No.

“What?”

I’d told the bastard to identify them, and he was evaluating the quality of their silk instead.

Ask this elder instead.”
“I don’t know about making you an elder, but I can make you a cripple.

“Qingxia Hall?

chapters.title: Chapter 453
paragraphs: “You fucking baaaastards!”
For a moment, it felt as though a cold wind had swept through.
Or maybe my shout had simply been loud enough to feel like one.
Probably the latter.
Whoooosh.
Dozens of people who had been scrambling for silver nyang froze, and silence fell over the noisy main road.
Then one short command broke the stillness.
“I’m counting to three.”
“Fall in.”
Give a dog three years at a village school and it can recite poetry. Beat it for long enough and it can memorize the Four Books and Three Classics.
That was why the village-school dog—or rather, Hyuk Mujin—who had been conditioned by a year of my violence and profanity moved faster than anyone else.
“Faaall iiiin!”
Screaming his acknowledgment, Hyuk Mujin came running and stopped dead in front of me.
A beat later, Gung Gibang grasped the situation and used his movement technique, arriving almost simultaneously with Hyuk Mujin. As for Cheongpung...
“Pancakes! Please give me the pancakes, quick! Benefactor is angry!”
That sibu-leol bastard. He was still making sure to get his snacks.
Once they had been wrapped, Cheongpung raced toward me like a streak of light. I spoke to him gently.
“Take your time. I’m not angry.”
“Wow! Really?”
“Yeah. I’m not angry. I’m fucking pissed.”
“Ah, ah...”
I looked at the fidgeting Cheongpung and the other two, who were subtly avoiding my gaze.
*When the hell are these bastards going to become human?*
They should have been squeezing out every last ounce of strength to reach the Zhuge Clan, yet here they were using martial arts to pick up a few silver nyang.
Gung Gibang had even sneakily snatched silver nyang out of someone else’s hand. At this point, he was not a beggar. He was a bandit.
*Life, for fuck’s sake...*
I’d gone to such lengths lately to improve employee benefits, and this was what I got.
I looked up at the clear sky and spat into my palm.
“Hyuk Mujin. Stick out your forehead.”
“Pardon?”
Hyuk Mujin jerked his head up, looking incredulous.
“Just me?”
“Yeah. You first.”
“What about Gung Gibang?”
“He’s a beggar down to the bone. Honestly, it’s hard to criticize a beggar for picking up silver nyang.”
“An accurate and wise judgment.”
Gung Gibang, who had been watching my mood, cut in with a solemn voice. Hyuk Mujin opened his round eyes.
“No, what do you mean, ‘hard to criticize’? You get angry every time I call you a beggar.”
“Me? What nonsense. I’m a beggar from head to toe. I was born a beggar, and I’ll live as one until the day I die.”
“...You really are a beggar.”
“Thank you for the compliment.”
“Gung Gibang, you beggar bastard.”
“Ah, how sweet.”
After glaring at Gung Gibang as if he wanted to kill him, Hyuk Mujin spoke again.
“What about Cheongpung?”
“Cheongpung is Cheongpung.”
Huashan or whatever, Cheongpung had always been like that.
That one sentence said it all. Hyuk Mujin muttered,
“That makes no sense, but somehow I understand...”
“People are watching. Let’s get this over with.”
“How many?”
“You tell me. How many blows will it take for you to reflect on your actions?”
“Then... one?”
“Three.”
“Damn it. Understood.”
“You cursed, so five.”
“...Just hit me ten times. Beat me to death.”
“Bonus points for such resolve, worthy of a martial artist. So, one blow. How many?”
“One!”
Hyuk Mujin shouted his reply with all his might and thrust his forehead forward.
That was when it happened.
“You there. Stop.”
I lowered my hand and turned around.
The main road had gone deathly silent. Ten men and women seated in four-bearer palanquins were staring at us with a mixture of displeasure and interest.
All of them wore lavish clothing that flaunted their immense wealth, but one young man stood out in particular.
He was the one who had just spoken.
“I stopped. Why?”
The young man’s eyes widened at my question. He blinked for a while, as if unable to believe what he had heard, then let out a quiet laugh.
“It seems you do not know who this Young Master is.”
“Do I need to?”
“What an arrogant bastard!”
The young man wasn’t the one who said that.
I watched as a man kicked off from one of the palanquins and shot into the air.
*What’s this now?*
Whoosh, clang!
The sparrow-eyed man performed three somersaults in midair before landing and drawing his sword, his eyes blazing with fury.
The onlookers gasped at the flashy display.
“You appear to be a wandering martial artist, but as if causing a disturbance in broad daylight were not enough, you dare address a person of noble standing with such insolence—”
“You’ve got a lot of jewels on that thing. Are they supposed to distract people?”
I stared at the jewels decorating his sword. Dozens of gems in a variety of colors were shining in the sunlight.
“What?”
“It’s dazzling. Put it away.”
Clang!
The sparrow-eyed man’s eyes widened.
Unable to withstand the force of my finger flick, the sword flew from his hand and buried itself deep in the ground.
“Who the fuck points a sword at someone like that? In broad daylight, no less.”
*Oh, look at him throwing a fit.*
He was probably somewhere around First Rate.
He seemed to have polished his skills to a decent level, but he was an extreme poseur obsessed with appearances.
“T-this bastard...!”
“And you were the ones making all the noise. I just quieted things down. Don’t make this any more complicated than it needs to be. Just leave, all right?”
I meant it.
It wasn’t as if I’d never had a fly or two buzzing around me before. This wasn’t my home, and I was only passing through. There was no reason to spray insecticide on every mosquito that came at me.
Better to wave them away and keep going.
But no matter how sincerely you tried to explain something, there were always people who failed to understand the first time.
Shing, shing-shing!

Dozens of sword blades flashed from every direction. Martial artists from Qingxia Hall, dressed in blue silk martial uniforms, surrounded us in layer after layer. The sparrow-eyed man’s earlier panic gave way to smug satisfaction.
“You seem to be a fairly well-known wandering martial artist. Kneel and beg forgiveness while you still can. Who knows? Perhaps the Young Master will mercifully spare you.”
I glanced over the sparrow-eyed man’s shoulder. Led by the young man who appeared to be their leader, the others were watching us with sparkling eyes.
They looked exactly like zoo visitors watching monkeys.
“I don’t think the people over there are feeling particularly merciful.”
“What?”
“Of course, neither am I. And from what I’ve learned, this is the most effective medicine. Isn’t that right?”
I slowly raised my fist, and the Bermuda Triangle, which had been watching only my expression, responded enthusiastically.
“Exactly. They won’t come to their senses until they’ve been beaten like dogs on the hottest day of summer.”
“I was the first one to take that medicine. Cured me on the spot.”
“Benefactor, can I go buy dumplings while you do that?”
“No. Stay there. This’ll be over soon anyway.”
Step.
“W-wait!”
The moment I stepped forward, panic filled the sparrow-eyed man’s eyes.
A Third Rate thug would charge in out of sheer stubbornness because he would not know his opponent’s level. But that man was a martial artist who had learned martial arts to a certain degree.
He had clearly realized that neither he nor the Qingxia Hall martial artists serving as an ornamental backdrop were any match for me.
“W-we’re Qingxia Hall!”
“Oh. So?”
“H-have you never heard of Qingxia Hall’s reputation?”
“Nope. My hearing hasn’t been too good lately.”
Step.
“Stop! I said stop!”
“Ahem.”
By then, the sparrow-eyed man wasn’t the only one getting desperate.
The Zhuge Clan retainer, who had been clicking his tongue as he watched, cleared his throat and spoke.
“I will explain the situation, so perhaps it would be best if you stopped...”
Whack! Thud!
“Pardon me? What did you just say?”
The Zhuge Clan retainer looked back and forth between me, standing there with my fist clenched, and the sparrow-eyed man, who lay unconscious with his nose crushed.
He muttered awkwardly,
“I said it might be best if you stopped...”
“Pardon?”
“There may be various complications...”
“Pardon?”
“It would be better to avoid any unnecessary conflict...”
“What was that?”
“...Never mind.”
“Ah. All right.”
I wiped the blood from my fist on my trouser leg and looked around.
Gung Gibang was muttering that he’d known the man would end up like that, while Hyuk Mujin beamed at his unexpected reprieve.
And Cheongpung...
“Hey! Where do you think you’re going?”
“Gasp! Benefactor!”
Was that bastard seriously trying to buy dumplings right now...?
Cheongpung was silently inching away. Watching his retreating back, I began to wonder if he was really human.
*I’m definitely catching that bastard.*
I stepped forward with grim resolve. The ornamental guards surrounding us sucked in their breaths and moved aside.
But they weren’t the only Qingxia Hall martial artists present.
“Ha-ha-ha! How amusing. Truly amusing. Don’t you agree?”
At the young man’s laughing question, the four huge men carrying his palanquin answered in unison.
“Yes, my lord.”
“We cannot send off the benefactor who gave this Young Master such a good laugh. I am fine, so go and bring him here.”
“Loyalty!”
Their shout rang with internal energy. The huge men set down the palanquin and charged toward me with the speed of the wind.
They had transformed from mere sedan bearers into outstanding Peak masters, attacking while covering all four directions.
Whoooooosh!
Each threw a punch carrying fierce qi, the four strikes interlocking with exquisite precision.
Thud-thud-thud-thud!
With exactly four sounds of impact, four bodies sprawled face-first onto the ground at the same speed with which they had charged.
None of them got back up.
“What the sibu-leol?”
Complete silence descended over the main road.
I nudged the unconscious giants with my foot, then shrugged at the young man. The corners of his mouth, which had been raised so high moments before, were now trembling.
“Interesting. Very interesting. Don’t you all think so too?”
The Zhuge Clan retainer put a hand to his forehead, while Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin nodded mechanically.
“This is the most fun I’ve had in all my thirty years as a beggar.”
“Captain, I laughed so hard my belly button fell off. I can’t see where it rolled, so I’m still looking for it.”
“Right. In times as bleak as these, how could we simply let the man who gave us such wonderful entertainment leave? So... grab that bastard by the collar and escort him over here.”
“Loyalty, loyalty!”
“I give up. Whatever happens, you’ll deal with it yourself.”
Hyuk Mujin, desperate to avoid even a single blow, threw himself into the task with greater enthusiasm than anyone else. Gung Gibang stepped forward as well, despite his grumbling.
The situation had completely reversed from how it had begun.
Once even their trusted guards were defeated, the men and women of Qingxia Hall began shrieking at the tops of their lungs.
“Y-you bastard! Do you know who I am?”
“You wretched scoundrel! How dare you defy the laws of the Great Nation!”
“If you lay a hand on me, do you think my family will stand by and do nothing?”
I had only meant to grab one person, but these people were apparently set items that came attached in a chain.
I turned to the first one who had shouted.
“Who are you?”
“I am the Young Bureau Head of the Daejuksan Escort Bureau...”
“Oh, Juksan Escort Bureau?”
“So you do know us!”
“I don’t, you sibu-leol bastard. Get down before I beat you into juk.”
They might have thrown their weight around in Hubei Province, but if I’d never heard of them, they were nobodies.
I continued quietly.
“Get down now, and I’ll only destroy the palanquin. Refuse, and I’ll destroy your legs along with it. What’ll it be?”
The Young Bureau Head of the Daejuksan Escort Bureau widened his eyes and answered,
“I’ll get down.”
“You should’ve done that from the start. Why are your eyes so wide?”
“I’m sorry. If I don’t do this, I think I might cry...”
Ah. That was understandable.
After dealing with one of them easily, I turned to the sharp-voiced woman.
“What family did you say you were from?”
“Hmph! No matter how much of a scoundrel you are, surely you’ve heard of the name of the Hyungmun Sword Family!”
“Never heard of it. Stop talking nonsense and get down.”
“Next. Where are you from?”
“I-I’m from the Eungseong Merchant Association...”
“Eungseong, Eung-shit, whatever. Get down unless you want me to beat you until you crap yourself.”
“Yes, sir.”
After two or three of them climbed down from their sedan chairs, the rest began touching their feet to the ground one by one without even speaking.
All except one.
“So, who are you?”
Every trace of laughter had vanished from the young man’s face. His eyes gleamed coldly.
“You have crossed a line you should never have crossed.”
“Looks like you’ve crossed your lifeline too. So who are you?”
“Heh. What a ridiculous situation.”
The young man gave a hollow laugh, then shouted in a dignified voice,
“I, Ju Wongong, am a noble scion of the dragon’s blood and a third cousin of His Majesty the Emperor! If you know your crime, kneel even now!”
“Okay, Celestial Dragon. Get down.”

sentences.text: “You fucking baaaastards!”
For a moment, it felt as though a cold wind had swept through.
Or maybe my shout had simply been loud enough to feel like one.
Probably the latter.
Whoooosh.
Dozens of people who had been scrambling for silver nyang froze, and silence fell over the noisy main road.
Then one short command broke the stillness.
“I’m counting to three.”
“Fall in.”
Give a dog three years at a village school and it can recite poetry.
Beat it for long enough and it can memorize the Four Books and Three Classics.
That was why the village-school dog—or rather, Hyuk Mujin—who had been conditioned by a year of my violence and profanity moved faster than anyone else.
“Faaall iiiin!”
Screaming his acknowledgment, Hyuk Mujin came running and stopped dead in front of me.
A beat later, Gung Gibang grasped the situation and used his movement technique, arriving almost simultaneously with Hyuk Mujin.
As for Cheongpung...
“Pancakes!
Please give me the pancakes, quick!
Benefactor is angry!”
That sibu-leol bastard.
He was still making sure to get his snacks.
Once they had been wrapped, Cheongpung raced toward me like a streak of light.
I spoke to him gently.
“Take your time.
I’m not angry.”
“Wow!
Really?”
“Yeah.
I’m not angry.
I’m fucking pissed.”
“Ah, ah...”
I looked at the fidgeting Cheongpung and the other two, who were subtly avoiding my gaze.
*When the hell are these bastards going to become human?*
They should have been squeezing out every last ounce of strength to reach the Zhuge Clan, yet here they were using martial arts to pick up a few silver nyang.
Gung Gibang had even sneakily snatched silver nyang out of someone else’s hand.
At this point, he was not a beggar.
He was a bandit.
*Life, for fuck’s sake...*
I’d gone to such lengths lately to improve employee benefits, and this was what I got.
I looked up at the clear sky and spat into my palm.
“Hyuk Mujin.
Stick out your forehead.”
“Pardon?”
Hyuk Mujin jerked his head up, looking incredulous.
“Just me?”
“Yeah.
You first.”
“What about Gung Gibang?”
“He’s a beggar down to the bone.
Honestly, it’s hard to criticize a beggar for picking up silver nyang.”
“An accurate and wise judgment.”
Gung Gibang, who had been watching my mood, cut in with a solemn voice.
Hyuk Mujin opened his round eyes.
“No, what do you mean, ‘hard to criticize’?
You get angry every time I call you a beggar.”
“Me?
What nonsense.
I’m a beggar from head to toe.
I was born a beggar, and I’ll live as one until the day I die.”
“...You really are a beggar.”
“Thank you for the compliment.”
“Gung Gibang, you beggar bastard.”
“Ah, how sweet.”
After glaring at Gung Gibang as if he wanted to kill him, Hyuk Mujin spoke again.
“What about Cheongpung?”
“Cheongpung is Cheongpung.”
Huashan or whatever, Cheongpung had always been like that.
That one sentence said it all.
Hyuk Mujin muttered,
“That makes no sense, but somehow I understand...”
“People are watching.
Let’s get this over with.”
“How many?”
“You tell me.
How many blows will it take for you to reflect on your actions?”
“Then... one?”
“Three.”
“Damn it.
Understood.”
“You cursed, so five.”
“...Just hit me ten times.
Beat me to death.”
“Bonus points for such resolve, worthy of a martial artist.
So, one blow.
How many?”
“One!”
Hyuk Mujin shouted his reply with all his might and thrust his forehead forward.
That was when it happened.
“You there.
Stop.”
I lowered my hand and turned around.
The main road had gone deathly silent.
Ten men and women seated in four-bearer palanquins were staring at us with a mixture of displeasure and interest.
All of them wore lavish clothing that flaunted their immense wealth, but one young man stood out in particular.
He was the one who had just spoken.
“I stopped.
Why?”
The young man’s eyes widened at my question.
He blinked for a while, as if unable to believe what he had heard, then let out a quiet laugh.
“It seems you do not know who this Young Master is.”
“Do I need to?”
“What an arrogant bastard!”
The young man wasn’t the one who said that.
I watched as a man kicked off from one of the palanquins and shot into the air.
*What’s this now?*
Whoosh, clang!
The sparrow-eyed man performed three somersaults in midair before landing and drawing his sword, his eyes blazing with fury.
The onlookers gasped at the flashy display.
“You appear to be a wandering martial artist, but as if causing a disturbance in broad daylight were not enough, you dare address a person of noble standing with such insolence—”
“You’ve got a lot of jewels on that thing.
Are they supposed to distract people?”
I stared at the jewels decorating his sword.
Dozens of gems in a variety of colors were shining in the sunlight.
“What?”
“It’s dazzling.
Put it away.”
Clang!
The sparrow-eyed man’s eyes widened.
Unable to withstand the force of my finger flick, the sword flew from his hand and buried itself deep in the ground.
“Who the fuck points a sword at someone like that?
In broad daylight, no less.”
*Oh, look at him throwing a fit.*
He was probably somewhere around First Rate.
He seemed to have polished his skills to a decent level, but he was an extreme poseur obsessed with appearances.
“T-this bastard...!”
“And you were the ones making all the noise.
I just quieted things down.
Don’t make this any more complicated than it needs to be.
Just leave, all right?”
I meant it.
It wasn’t as if I’d never had a fly or two buzzing around me before.
This wasn’t my home, and I was only passing through.
There was no reason to spray insecticide on every mosquito that came at me.
Better to wave them away and keep going.
But no matter how sincerely you tried to explain something, there were always people who failed to understand the first time.
Shing, shing-shing!
Dozens of sword blades flashed from every direction.
Martial artists from Qingxia Hall, dressed in blue silk martial uniforms, surrounded us in layer after layer.
The sparrow-eyed man’s earlier panic gave way to smug satisfaction.
“You seem to be a fairly well-known wandering martial artist.
Kneel and beg forgiveness while you still can.
Who knows?
Perhaps the Young Master will mercifully spare you.”
I glanced over the sparrow-eyed man’s shoulder.
Led by the young man who appeared to be their leader, the others were watching us with sparkling eyes.
They looked exactly like zoo visitors watching monkeys.
“I don’t think the people over there are feeling particularly merciful.”
“What?”
“Of course, neither am I.
And from what I’ve learned, this is the most effective medicine.
Isn’t that right?”
I slowly raised my fist, and the Bermuda Triangle, which had been watching only my expression, responded enthusiastically.
“Exactly.
They won’t come to their senses until they’ve been beaten like dogs on the hottest day of summer.”
“I was the first one to take that medicine.
Cured me on the spot.”
“Benefactor, can I go buy dumplings while you do that?”
“No.
Stay there.
This’ll be over soon anyway.”
Step.
“W-wait!”
The moment I stepped forward, panic filled the sparrow-eyed man’s eyes.
A Third Rate thug would charge in out of sheer stubbornness because he would not know his opponent’s level.
But that man was a martial artist who had learned martial arts to a certain degree.
He had clearly realized that neither he nor the Qingxia Hall martial artists serving as an ornamental backdrop were any match for me.
“W-we’re Qingxia Hall!”
“Oh.
So?”
“H-have you never heard of Qingxia Hall’s reputation?”
“Nope.
My hearing hasn’t been too good lately.”
Step.
“Stop!
I said stop!”
“Ahem.”
By then, the sparrow-eyed man wasn’t the only one getting desperate.
The Zhuge Clan retainer, who had been clicking his tongue as he watched, cleared his throat and spoke.
“I will explain the situation, so perhaps it would be best if you stopped...”
Whack!
Thud!
“Pardon me?
What did you just say?”
The Zhuge Clan retainer looked back and forth between me, standing there with my fist clenched, and the sparrow-eyed man, who lay unconscious with his nose crushed.
He muttered awkwardly,
“I said it might be best if you stopped...”
“Pardon?”
“There may be various complications...”
“Pardon?”
“It would be better to avoid any unnecessary conflict...”
“What was that?”
“...Never mind.”
“Ah.
All right.”
I wiped the blood from my fist on my trouser leg and looked around.
Gung Gibang was muttering that he’d known the man would end up like that, while Hyuk Mujin beamed at his unexpected reprieve.
And Cheongpung...
“Hey!
Where do you think you’re going?”
“Gasp!
Benefactor!”
Was that bastard seriously trying to buy dumplings right now...?
Cheongpung was silently inching away.
Watching his retreating back, I began to wonder if he was really human.
*I’m definitely catching that bastard.*
I stepped forward with grim resolve.
The ornamental guards surrounding us sucked in their breaths and moved aside.
But they weren’t the only Qingxia Hall martial artists present.
“Ha-ha-ha!
How amusing.
Truly amusing.
Don’t you agree?”
At the young man’s laughing question, the four huge men carrying his palanquin answered in unison.
“Yes, my lord.”
“We cannot send off the benefactor who gave this Young Master such a good laugh.
I am fine, so go and bring him here.”
“Loyalty!”
Their shout rang with internal energy.
The huge men set down the palanquin and charged toward me with the speed of the wind.
They had transformed from mere sedan bearers into outstanding Peak masters, attacking while covering all four directions.
Whoooooosh!
Each threw a punch carrying fierce qi, the four strikes interlocking with exquisite precision.
Thud-thud-thud-thud!
With exactly four sounds of impact, four bodies sprawled face-first onto the ground at the same speed with which they had charged.
None of them got back up.
“What the sibu-leol?”
Complete silence descended over the main road.
I nudged the unconscious giants with my foot, then shrugged at the young man.
The corners of his mouth, which had been raised so high moments before, were now trembling.
“Interesting.
Very interesting.
Don’t you all think so too?”
The Zhuge Clan retainer put a hand to his forehead, while Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin nodded mechanically.
“This is the most fun I’ve had in all my thirty years as a beggar.”
“Captain, I laughed so hard my belly button fell off.
I can’t see where it rolled, so I’m still looking for it.”

I had only meant to grab one person, but these people were apparently set items that came attached in a chain.

chapters.title: Chapter 454
paragraphs: The young man who had frozen with his eyes wide—or rather, Ju Wongong—asked in a trembling voice,
“W-what did you say?”
Had this bastard’s ears been plugged this whole time? He kept making me repeat myself.
Ignoring the people staring back and forth between Ju Wongong and me with their mouths hanging open, I spoke again.
“Get down.”
“I-I am Ju Wongong!”
“Main character, Ju Wongong, whatever. Get down.”
“You are a subject of the Great Nation! How dare you show such disrespect to a member of His Majesty the Emperor’s own bloodline?”
“I have a friend named Johnson. If he were here, he’d have violated something else.”
“I’ll say it one last time. Get down.”
He had no idea what I meant, but anyone with human instincts could sense danger.
Ju Wongong’s butt twitched instinctively, and he slowly rose to his feet.
Yet even as his eyes darted around in anxiety at this unprecedented situation, he didn’t forget to threaten me until the bitter end. Apparently, he still trusted his imperial pedigree to protect him.
“D-do you think you’ll get away with this?”
“Yeah. I think I will.”
“To insult an imperial relative? This is treason!”
“As long as it’s not hair loss.”
“What kind of bastard says things like that...!”
Although I answered casually, I was not entirely wrong.
The imperial family bore the same Zhu surname as the Son of Heaven and carried the blood of dragons. That alone made them noble.
Even though Murim and the government maintained a relationship of mutual noninterference, disrespecting or threatening an imperial relative was treated as a serious crime.
There was a reason the Zhuge Clan retainer had been whining like a dog desperate to relieve itself.
“P-perhaps it would be best if you stopped now.”
I frowned at his whisper.
“Why?”
“Pardon?”
“What did I do? I didn’t swear at him or threaten to kill him. His side even attacked first. All I did was tell him to get down from the four-person sedan chair.”
“...Well, if you put it that way, you’re right. But he is still an imperial relative.”

“Imperial relatives come in all grades. If he’s eight degrees removed, he’s not really a blood relative. They just have a few drops of blood in common. If I spat into the Yangtze right now, the river and I would probably be about eight degrees apart too.”
“Gasp. Great Hero Jin, please.”
“It’s fine. I said it quietly, so no one could’ve heard us anyway.”
At that moment, Ju Wongong misread our whispering and shouted triumphantly.

“It seems you have finally grasped the gravity of the situation. But it is already too late! The imperial court will soon dispatch a hundred thousand troops to exterminate the nine branches of your kin, along with those of every other traitor!”
“Oh. A Buster Call.”
“What have you been babbling about this whole time, you traitorous bastard?”
“Gasp!”
“Eek!”
When unmistakable fury filled Ju Wongong’s eyes, the commoners sucked in their breaths and threw themselves flat on the ground. Some had already begun fleeing in every direction.
They seemed eager to avoid being dragged into someone else’s trouble. That meant fewer eyes watching us, so I had no complaints.
*They keep threatening people with the nine branches of their kin whenever they get bored.*
Did they not bother with anything less?
As I let out a deep sigh, the Zhuge Clan retainer whispered,
“Don’t be too frightened. His talk of a hundred thousand troops is only a bluff.”
“...Do you think I’m an idiot? Why would I believe that?”
“Master Ju was exiled for using his imperial authority to embezzle a fortune, so he won’t want to make this matter any bigger. Please apologize and withdraw while you still can.”
“Wait. Exiled?”
“Yes.”
“Him?”

“He is an imperial relative. No matter how distant his branch may be, his blood cannot be ignored. Besides, he is a distant branch with no chance of inheriting the throne, so even when he commits a crime, they allow him to enjoy a certain amount of special treatment.”
“In short, he’s such a fucking nobody that no one around him even bothers with him?”
“...Great Hero Jin, please choose your words more carefully.”
I let the retainer’s complaint go in one ear and out the other, then laughed quietly.

I had wondered why someone who was supposedly an imperial relative was hanging around with a gang of thugs on a main road in Hubei instead of living in the imperial palace. It turned out he was even less important than I had imagined.
Though I had already suspected as much when he started talking about being eight degrees removed.
“First, I shall gouge out those arrogant eyes of yours for failing to recognize this noble self. Then I shall tear you limb from limb, and afterward—”
“Yeah, yeah. I get it. Look at this first, then we can talk about the rest.”
I pulled something from inside my robe and tossed it at Ju Wongong as he delivered his grand speech.
At the same time, the man who had been puffing out his chest flailed both arms and sat down hard.
“A hidden weapon! A hidden weapon! This bastard is trying to assassinate an imperial relative!”
“...You really are something else.”
And then—
The “hidden weapon” landed with a soft clack in front of Ju Wongong’s feet, scattering a brilliant light beneath everyone’s gaze.
“Huh?”
Ju Wongong stared at the object with puzzled eyes, his mouth hanging open.
“Huh? Huh? Huhhhhhh!”
It didn’t take long for his question marks to become exclamation marks, or for his anger to turn to shock.
He looked back and forth between me and Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao’s token, engraved with clouds and a dragon. Then he spoke in a grave voice.
“I shall show you mercy and forgive you.”
What a load of crap.
“So you were on your way to Dongting Lake?”
“That is correct! No, I mean, yes, that is so!”
Ju Wongong nodded vigorously at my gentle tone.

The decorative showpieces from Qingxia Hall whom he had hired were warning people to keep their mouths shut alongside the government troops, who had arrived late. Meanwhile, Cheongpung, who had somehow succeeded in buying dumplings in bulk, opened his eyes wide at the mention of Dongting Lake.
“Wow! Dongting Lake!”
Ju Wongong had finally learned the identity of this dumpling ghost. His uneasy gaze flicked toward the sword hanging at Cheongpung’s waist.
“W-well, I could invite you along if you wished...”
I muttered,
“You don’t mean that at all.”
“That is a misunderstanding! No, I mean, you misunderstand.”
“Do you misunderstand things this often? Considering you attacked people who were trying to pass by peacefully, it certainly seems that way.”
“That was... I shall apologize once again. I never dreamed that you possessed His Highness Prince Shangshan’s token.”
“Oh, I see. So if I hadn’t had the token, you would’ve brought a hundred thousand troops to exterminate nine branches of my family, gouged out my eyes, and torn me limb from limb?”
“W-why would you say such a thing? Ha, ha-ha-ha.”
His forced laughter was almost pitiful.
*I didn’t know the token would have this much power either.*
There was a reason Ju Wongong had become so submissive.
Even animals were judged as purebred or mixed-breed. How much more would the imperial family—the noblest bloodline in the world—care about such distinctions?
Even though the same imperial blood ran in their veins, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao was the Son of Heaven’s only younger full brother and the sole prince he had personally appointed.

After the late Emperor’s death, the ruthless man who now sat upon the throne had eliminated countless blood relatives in the struggle for succession. Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao was that ruthless Emperor’s one soft spot.
Ju Wongong, on the other hand, came from a collateral branch eight degrees removed.
The direct imperial line possessed legitimacy and authority. Even by counting degrees of kinship, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao was a distant and exalted elder of the household to Ju Wongong.
*This is what they call using barbarians to defeat barbarians.*
Defeat barbarians with barbarians, and a weak Celestial Dragon with a strong Celestial Dragon.
The chairman of my fan club was this formidable. Just thinking about it made my heart swell.
“Well, putting that aside, what are you planning to do at Dongting Lake?”
“W-well, the weather is pleasant, so I thought I might go boating...”
At my incredulous expression, Ju Wongong hurriedly corrected himself.
“I intended to go boating while also inspecting the people’s welfare, since I heard the mood in Hubei Province has been rather grim lately.”
“...Shouldn’t you inspect your own life first? I heard you were exiled for siphoning off a fortune through back channels.”
“Ahem! Ahem!”
“And you brought all these people along for a boat ride? At a time like this?”

Everyone in Hubei Province with eyes and ears was trembling with anxiety over the grim rumors that refused to die down, yet this exiled imperial relative was planning a lavish boating excursion on Dongting Lake.
If Mr. Current Situation heard about this and smashed Ju Wongong’s skull with a sledgehammer, Ju Wongong would have no right to complain.
*That’s rich people for you.*
I shook my head and rose from my seat.
The matter had been settled without too much fuss, so I intended to leave and forget about it. Ju Wongong seemed to take it differently.
“W-wait a moment. Where are you going?”
“I’m a busy man. I have more important things to do than go boating on Dongting Lake. Why?”
“If I have offended you, I shall apologize once again. And in that spirit...”
Ju Wongong trailed off and gave a meaningful glance.
The Qingxia Hall martial artists who had been waiting for his signal carried over one of the ornate sedan chairs positioned throughout the procession.
They hadn’t even drawn back its curtains, yet a faint fragrance drifted into my nose.
*Don’t tell me...*
There was an old saying that the thing you dismissed with “surely not” was the thing most likely to get you. This time was no different.
“Show yourself.”
The moment Ju Wongong spoke, the sedan chair’s door slid open.
A woman carefully stepped down, and an exclamation escaped my lips before I could stop it.
“...Whoa.”
People often describe celebrities as pretty or handsome.
But the woman before me possessed something beyond those ordinary standards.
*Beautiful.*
Yes. That was probably the right word.
She was beautiful enough to draw admiration even from me, despite the fact that I had already guessed Ju Wongong’s intentions.

Beautiful enough to make Gung Gibang hurriedly wash his face with spit and Hyuk Mujin stare in a daze. Beautiful enough to make Cheongpung—who had been holding a meat dumpling in one hand and a vegetable dumpling in the other, trying to choose between them—drop them both.
As the quiet shock rippled through the crowd, Ju Wongong’s voice reached me.

“She is the singing courtesan I keep at my side. As you can see, her beauty deserves to be called unrivaled beneath the heavens. She is also extraordinarily skilled in music. Anyone who hears her play loses himself completely.”
I wasn’t so sure she needed the music. She looked capable of stealing a person’s soul without playing a single note.
Ju Wongong laughed quietly at the admiration plain on my face, then turned to the woman.
“What are you waiting for? Hurry and greet him.”
Her red lips slowly parted.
“This humble girl is called Honglan. It is my greatest pleasure to meet such an honored guest.”
“...Amazing.”
Before the shock of her appearance had even faded, exclamations burst out from every direction.
Her voice was clear and pure, yet alluring.
Honglan. Red Orchid. The name suited her better than anyone.
*Of course, it wasn’t her real name, and she wasn’t an ordinary singing courtesan either.*
Like most courtesans, including Wolhwa, Honglan concealed her true name.
And unlike Ju Wongong, who knew absolutely nothing about martial arts, she had received at least some training.
*Lower District Sect?*
Her slender shoulder twitched at my Sound Transmission, and Honglan gave a slight nod.
*The Lower District Sect. I had a feeling that was it.*
The Lower District Sect had more disciples than any organization apart from the Beggars’ Sect.
Ju Wongong didn’t seem aware of it, but like the Lower District Sect’s other courtesans, Honglan had learned enough martial arts to protect herself.
“So? What do you think, Great Hero Jin? Give me the opportunity, and this Young Master will treat you properly. Of course, Honglan will sit beside you...”
*Let’s see you refuse to come along after this.*
The words were written plainly across Ju Wongong’s smug face.
I gazed at Honglan for a moment, then smiled.
“Forget it. Let’s each continue on our way.”
“Then we can all go somewhere else together—hm? W-wait. What did you just say?”
“Why are you so flustered? I’m pretty sure I said I had something urgent to do. Is my memory failing me?”
“N-no. But Honglan is here...”
I raised a hand and cut Ju Wongong off.

I had already wasted enough time getting dragged into this nonsense. If I were the kind of man who lost his head over a beautiful woman and followed her wherever she went, I wouldn’t have survived this long.
“Don’t overdo the partying. You’d be better off going home and keeping your head down. See you.”
I was about to turn away when Ju Wongong held something out to me.
“Wait! Then at least this.”
“I heard that His Highness Prince Shangshan received your autograph, Great Hero Jin. Please give me one as well...”
At this rate, my fan café would be reaching Leaf Level 2 soon.

“D-do you think you’ll get away with this?”
“Yeah.
I think I will.”
“To insult an imperial relative?
This is treason!”
“As long as it’s not hair loss.”
“What kind of bastard says things like that...!”
Although I answered casually, I was not entirely wrong.
The imperial family bore the same Zhu surname as the Son of Heaven and carried the blood of dragons.
That alone made them noble.
Even though Murim and the government maintained a relationship of mutual noninterference, disrespecting or threatening an imperial relative was treated as a serious crime.
There was a reason the Zhuge Clan retainer had been whining like a dog desperate to relieve itself.
“P-perhaps it would be best if you stopped now.”
I frowned at his whisper.
“Why?”
“Pardon?”
“What did I do?
I didn’t swear at him or threaten to kill him.
His side even attacked first.
All I did was tell him to get down from the four-person sedan chair.”
“...Well, if you put it that way, you’re right.
But he is still an imperial relative.”
“Imperial relatives come in all grades.
If he’s eight degrees removed, he’s not really a blood relative.
They just have a few drops of blood in common.
If I spat into the Yangtze right now, the river and I would probably be about eight degrees apart too.”
“Gasp.
Great Hero Jin, please.”
“It’s fine.
I said it quietly, so no one could’ve heard us anyway.”
At that moment, Ju Wongong misread our whispering and shouted triumphantly.
“It seems you have finally grasped the gravity of the situation.
But it is already too late!
The imperial court will soon dispatch a hundred thousand troops to exterminate the nine branches of your kin, along with those of every other traitor!”
“Oh.
A Buster Call.”
“What have you been babbling about this whole time, you traitorous bastard?”
“Gasp!”
“Eek!”
When unmistakable fury filled Ju Wongong’s eyes, the commoners sucked in their breaths and threw themselves flat on the ground.
Some had already begun fleeing in every direction.
They seemed eager to avoid being dragged into someone else’s trouble.
That meant fewer eyes watching us, so I had no complaints.
*They keep threatening people with the nine branches of their kin whenever they get bored.*
Did they not bother with anything less?
As I let out a deep sigh, the Zhuge Clan retainer whispered,
“Don’t be too frightened.
His talk of a hundred thousand troops is only a bluff.”
“...Do you think I’m an idiot?
Why would I believe that?”
“Master Ju was exiled for using his imperial authority to embezzle a fortune, so he won’t want to make this matter any bigger.
Please apologize and withdraw while you still can.”
“Wait.
Exiled?”
“Yes.”
“Him?”
“He is an imperial relative.
No matter how distant his branch may be, his blood cannot be ignored.
Besides, he is a distant branch with no chance of inheriting the throne, so even when he commits a crime, they allow him to enjoy a certain amount of special treatment.”
“In short, he’s such a fucking nobody that no one around him even bothers with him?”
“...Great Hero Jin, please choose your words more carefully.”
I let the retainer’s complaint go in one ear and out the other, then laughed quietly.
I had wondered why someone who was supposedly an imperial relative was hanging around with a gang of thugs on a main road in Hubei instead of living in the imperial palace.
It turned out he was even less important than I had imagined.
Though I had already suspected as much when he started talking about being eight degrees removed.
“First, I shall gouge out those arrogant eyes of yours for failing to recognize this noble self.
Then I shall tear you limb from limb, and afterward—”
“Yeah, yeah.
I get it.
Look at this first, then we can talk about the rest.”
I pulled something from inside my robe and tossed it at Ju Wongong as he delivered his grand speech.
At the same time, the man who had been puffing out his chest flailed both arms and sat down hard.
“A hidden weapon!
A hidden weapon!
This bastard is trying to assassinate an imperial relative!”
“...You really are something else.”
And then—
The “hidden weapon” landed with a soft clack in front of Ju Wongong’s feet, scattering a brilliant light beneath everyone’s gaze.
“Huh?”
Ju Wongong stared at the object with puzzled eyes, his mouth hanging open.
“Huh?
Huh?
Huhhhhhh!”
It didn’t take long for his question marks to become exclamation marks, or for his anger to turn to shock.
He looked back and forth between me and Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao’s token, engraved with clouds and a dragon.
Then he spoke in a grave voice.
“I shall show you mercy and forgive you.”
What a load of crap.
“So you were on your way to Dongting Lake?”
“That is correct!
No, I mean, yes, that is so!”
Ju Wongong nodded vigorously at my gentle tone.
The decorative showpieces from Qingxia Hall whom he had hired were warning people to keep their mouths shut alongside the government troops, who had arrived late.
Meanwhile, Cheongpung, who had somehow succeeded in buying dumplings in bulk, opened his eyes wide at the mention of Dongting Lake.
“Wow!
Dongting Lake!”
Ju Wongong had finally learned the identity of this dumpling ghost.
His uneasy gaze flicked toward the sword hanging at Cheongpung’s waist.
“W-well, I could invite you along if you wished...”
I muttered,
“You don’t mean that at all.”
“That is a misunderstanding!
No, I mean, you misunderstand.”
“Do you misunderstand things this often?
Considering you attacked people who were trying to pass by peacefully, it certainly seems that way.”
“That was...
I shall apologize once again.
I never dreamed that you possessed His Highness Prince Shangshan’s token.”
“Oh, I see.
So if I hadn’t had the token, you would’ve brought a hundred thousand troops to exterminate nine branches of my family, gouged out my eyes, and torn me limb from limb?”
“W-why would you say such a thing?
Ha, ha-ha-ha.”
His forced laughter was almost pitiful.
*I didn’t know the token would have this much power either.*
There was a reason Ju Wongong had become so submissive.
Even animals were judged as purebred or mixed-breed.
How much more would the imperial family—the noblest bloodline in the world—care about such distinctions?
Even though the same imperial blood ran in their veins, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao was the Son of Heaven’s only younger full brother and the sole prince he had personally appointed.
After the late Emperor’s death, the ruthless man who now sat upon the throne had eliminated countless blood relatives in the struggle for succession.
Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao was that ruthless Emperor’s one soft spot.
Ju Wongong, on the other hand, came from a collateral branch eight degrees removed.
The direct imperial line possessed legitimacy and authority.
Even by counting degrees of kinship, Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao was a distant and exalted elder of the household to Ju Wongong.
*This is what they call using barbarians to defeat barbarians.*
Defeat barbarians with barbarians, and a weak Celestial Dragon with a strong Celestial Dragon.
The chairman of my fan club was this formidable.
Just thinking about it made my heart swell.
“Well, putting that aside, what are you planning to do at Dongting Lake?”
“W-well, the weather is pleasant, so I thought I might go boating...”
At my incredulous expression, Ju Wongong hurriedly corrected himself.
“I intended to go boating while also inspecting the people’s welfare, since I heard the mood in Hubei Province has been rather grim lately.”
“...Shouldn’t you inspect your own life first?
I heard you were exiled for siphoning off a fortune through back channels.”
“Ahem!
Ahem!”
“And you brought all these people along for a boat ride?
At a time like this?”

Everyone in Hubei Province with eyes and ears was trembling with anxiety over the grim rumors that refused to die down, yet this exiled imperial relative was planning a lavish boating excursion on Dongting Lake.
If Mr.
Current Situation heard about this and smashed Ju Wongong’s skull with a sledgehammer, Ju Wongong would have no right to complain.
*That’s rich people for you.*
I shook my head and rose from my seat.
The matter had been settled without too much fuss, so I intended to leave and forget about it.
Ju Wongong seemed to take it differently.
“W-wait a moment.
Where are you going?”
“I’m a busy man.
I have more important things to do than go boating on Dongting Lake.
Why?”
“If I have offended you, I shall apologize once again.
And in that spirit...”
Ju Wongong trailed off and gave a meaningful glance.
The Qingxia Hall martial artists who had been waiting for his signal carried over one of the ornate sedan chairs positioned throughout the procession.
They hadn’t even drawn back its curtains, yet a faint fragrance drifted into my nose.
*Don’t tell me...*
There was an old saying that the thing you dismissed with “surely not” was the thing most likely to get you.
This time was no different.
“Show yourself.”
The moment Ju Wongong spoke, the sedan chair’s door slid open.
A woman carefully stepped down, and an exclamation escaped my lips before I could stop it.
“...Whoa.”
People often describe celebrities as pretty or handsome.
But the woman before me possessed something beyond those ordinary standards.
*Beautiful.*
Yes.
That was probably the right word.
She was beautiful enough to draw admiration even from me, despite the fact that I had already guessed Ju Wongong’s intentions.
Beautiful enough to make Gung Gibang hurriedly wash his face with spit and Hyuk Mujin stare in a daze.
Beautiful enough to make Cheongpung—who had been holding a meat dumpling in one hand and a vegetable dumpling in the other, trying to choose between them—drop them both.
As the quiet shock rippled through the crowd, Ju Wongong’s voice reached me.
“She is the singing courtesan I keep at my side.
As you can see, her beauty deserves to be called unrivaled beneath the heavens.
She is also extraordinarily skilled in music.
Anyone who hears her play loses himself completely.”
I wasn’t so sure she needed the music.
She looked capable of stealing a person’s soul without playing a single note.
Ju Wongong laughed quietly at the admiration plain on my face, then turned to the woman.
“What are you waiting for?
Hurry and greet him.”
Her red lips slowly parted.
“This humble girl is called Honglan.
It is my greatest pleasure to meet such an honored guest.”
“...Amazing.”
Before the shock of her appearance had even faded, exclamations burst out from every direction.
Her voice was clear and pure, yet alluring.
Honglan.
Red Orchid.
The name suited her better than anyone.
*Of course, it wasn’t her real name, and she wasn’t an ordinary singing courtesan either.*
Like most courtesans, including Wolhwa, Honglan concealed her true name.
And unlike Ju Wongong, who knew absolutely nothing about martial arts, she had received at least some training.
*Lower District Sect?*
Her slender shoulder twitched at my Sound Transmission, and Honglan gave a slight nod.
*The Lower District Sect.
I had a feeling that was it.*
The Lower District Sect had more disciples than any organization apart from the Beggars’ Sect.
Ju Wongong didn’t seem aware of it, but like the Lower District Sect’s other courtesans, Honglan had learned enough martial arts to protect herself.
“So?
What do you think, Great Hero Jin?
Give me the opportunity, and this Young Master will treat you properly.
Of course, Honglan will sit beside you...”
*Let’s see you refuse to come along after this.*
The words were written plainly across Ju Wongong’s smug face.
I gazed at Honglan for a moment, then smiled.
“Forget it.
Let’s each continue on our way.”
“Then we can all go somewhere else together—hm?
W-wait.
What did you just say?”
“Why are you so flustered?
I’m pretty sure I said I had something urgent to do.
Is my memory failing me?”
“N-no.
But Honglan is here...”
I raised a hand and cut Ju Wongong off.
I had already wasted enough time getting dragged into this nonsense.
If I were the kind of man who lost his head over a beautiful woman and followed her wherever she went, I wouldn’t have survived this long.
“Don’t overdo the partying.
You’d be better off going home and keeping your head down.
See you.”
I was about to turn away when Ju Wongong held something out to me.
“Wait!
Then at least this.”
“I heard that His Highness Prince Shangshan received your autograph, Great Hero Jin.
Please give me one as well...”
At this rate, my fan café would be reaching Leaf Level 2 soon.
