paragraphs: “Cough, cough.”
Hunched over like a shrimp, the old man coughed with difficulty.
Whenever he moved, the chill rising from the underground prison’s cold stone floor seeped into his bones.
Yet no illness could take root in his body.
The several jiazi of internal energy accumulated in his dantian over the long years no longer obeyed his control, but they were more than enough to protect his aged body.
And that only enraged him further.
*Damn it...!*
The already ugly old man’s features twisted into the face of a fiend.
Once, he had crossed the continent and left countless storms of blood in his wake. Now he was being treated like livestock that could be slaughtered at any moment.
“Then kill me! If you’re going to subject me to such humiliation, just kill me already!”
As the old man writhed and let out a tearing scream, the chains binding his body tightly grated against one another.
But like the internal energy sealed within his dantian, the dozen or so iron balls attached to those chains did not budge an inch.
“You bastaaaardsss!”
Though his martial arts had been sealed and he could no longer display his former might, his innate viciousness remained unchanged.
The old man glared through the thick iron bars with bloodshot eyes. Faces that must have been laughing at him somewhere flashed before his eyes like hallucinations.
“You bastards...!”
A grudge etched into his bones and soul.
They had killed his two brothers, born on the same day and hour as him, with whom he had spent his entire life. The old man himself had been captured and subjected to every humiliation imaginable.
They had even crushed his testicles as though castrating livestock. Calling them mortal enemies did not begin to describe it.
“Fine. Then I’ll survive, no matter what it takes.”
Flames poured from the old man’s eyes.
“I will escape this place and rip you bastards apart alive!”
His shout, thick with killing intent, echoed through the underground prison.
That was when a voice spoke.
“I heard your escape pledge. Quite moving.”
*When did he—?*
The old man blinked. One of the faces that had flashed before his eyes moments ago was now staring at him from beyond the bars.
The smile on the young man’s lips sent a chill through his chest.
“Y-you...”
“How’s the busted part? Must hurt every time you take a piss.”
The old man almost nodded without realizing it.
But this young man’s name stood alongside the others at the very top of his kill list. He was someone the old man had to kill, whatever the cost.
The old man glared at him through the bars, eyes gleaming.
“If you’re curious, lift the seal on my martial arts right now. I’ll show you myself.”
“I’m not particularly curious about that...”
The smile on the young man’s lips—Jin Taekyung’s lips—vanished as if wiped away.
“You’ll have to tell me everything else you know, Third Fiend.”
In the modern world, torturing prisoners was classified as an illegal act. If such a fact became known, even a Great Nation would be condemned by the international community.
But this was Murim. The authority of the law was hazy, and the line between man and beast even hazier.
And as far as I was concerned, the Third Fiend was closer to a beast wearing human skin.
*There’s no reason to hesitate.*
He had harmed countless people over the course of many years.
He was a fiend who had slaughtered hundreds—thousands—of people merely to satisfy his bloodlust.
There was no room for flimsy morality on the bloody road he had walked, or in this damp, dark underground prison.
I stared coldly at the Third Fiend.
“Guhk... Hnggg...”
His body hung limp, bound to an iron chair.
Bloodstained saliva dripped from his open mouth, and his limbs, torn and broken all over, spasmed with pain.
“How is he?”
At my question, the old man examining him scratched his head with a bloodstained iron skewer.
“He has already reached his limit. At this point, we must assume he has confessed everything he knows.”
If torture skill were divided into realm stages, I was barely First Rate. The old man before me was a Supreme Peak master.

He had handled prisoners with such efficient cruelty during the Great Faction War that Zhuge Gonghu, the Fan-Wisdom King, had taken note of his methods and invited him to join the Zhuge Clan after the war.
“If we keep going...”
“He will die. Without fail. And in this old man’s opinion, beating him any further will yield nothing more.”
The old man’s voice rang with certainty.
The appearance of the Third Fiend, who had become half a corpse, and his aura, which seemed ready to go out at any moment, lent even greater weight to those words.
But this wasn’t enough. I stared at the Third Fiend as he trembled, nearly senseless.
*Is this really everything?*
It wasn’t as though he had known nothing.
For the first few shichen, he had held out through sheer spite. But as the torture neared its final stages, he had grown talkative enough to fill five bamboo slips with densely packed writing.
Yet most of it was useless or concerned events from the past, and the information I needed most had never come out.
*The series of incidents happening in Hubei Province right now.*
The Sea Serpent Society had fallen, and Donghu Stronghold had been massacred.
The casualties had already far exceeded a thousand, including innocent commoners who did not know even a single martial move or half a stance.
As far as I knew, only one group possessed both the power and the sheer brutality to commit such madness.
*Dark Heaven.*
The problem was that I could not get hold of their trail.
Where and how had they attacked the Sea Serpent Society and Donghu Stronghold? Where had they hidden the Moving Formation?
And finally, where were the perpetrators now, and what were they doing?
“This won’t do.”
Muttering under my breath, I grabbed the unconscious Third Fiend by the wrist. The old man, who had been standing nearby with a bored expression, hurriedly tried to stop me.
“Great Hero, if you do that—!”
“It’s fine. I’m not trying to kill him.”
I sent internal energy through the Third Fiend’s wrist. As the warmth of Scorching Yang Qi flowed along his acupoints, color returned to his pale cheeks and his eyelids lifted.
My face appeared in his unfocused, trembling gray eyes.
“Y-you...”
“Wake up. It’s still too early.”
“J-just kill me.”
“Tell me everything you know, and you’ll get your wish. But if you insist on pretending to be a loyal servant...”
I poured more force into the faint stream of internal energy. The Third Fiend’s eyes flew open with a sharp gasp.
His body was already ruined inside and out. It could not endure the heat of Scorching Yang Qi.
“Ghk... Gack.”
His painful, gasping breaths carried the smell of meat being cooked. But I continued staring at the Third Fiend without wavering.
“That’s not the answer I want.”
“This old man—I have already told you everything.”
“Not that either.”
“Ghk. P-please...”
“If you can still hold out like this, you’re nowhere near death yet. Just like there’s still information I haven’t heard.”
“What else could you possibly want me to say...?”
“I’ve told you several times already. Everything about Dark Heaven. What’s happening in Hubei Province, and the Dongting Fisherman.”
“I told you, I don’t know—kuweeegh!”
With every exchange, the Scorching Yang Qi grew stronger.
The Third Fiend trembled violently, eyes rolling back until only the whites showed. A scream tore from his lips.
“Kill me! Hurry up and kill me! Even as a vengeful ghost, I’ll chew through your flesh and bones...!”
Damn it. That was as far as I could go.
I abruptly withdrew the internal energy I had been forcing into him. The Third Fiend immediately went limp, like a puppet with its strings cut.
Changing the flow, I gently stabilized his body from within. The old man, already standing by, quickly took his pulse and checked his condition.
“He’s a hard one to kill. Stopped right on the threshold of the afterlife.”
I knew. I had controlled my strength as carefully as possible to keep him alive.
*He can’t die here.*
The Third Fiend was one of the great fiends of the previous generation and a Supreme Peak master of Dark Heaven.
If we kept him alive and escorted him to Henan, there might be a way to learn even more information.
Of course, I couldn’t dismiss the possibility that those bamboo slips contained everything he knew.
No. That was probably the likeliest possibility.
*If he still didn’t talk after all this... maybe he really has told us everything.*
The mental strength and endurance of a Supreme Peak master defied imagination.
Yet the Third Fiend had begged me—someone no different from his mortal enemy—to stop. He had screamed for me to kill him instead.
And still, he had never changed his story.
*I—I and my brothers only followed orders under the Demon Lord! I don’t know anything about Dark Heaven’s headquarters or what happened elsewhere, I tell you!*
Remembering the cries he had repeated throughout the torture, I called out a name.
“Gung Gibang. Any news?”
Gung Gibang, leaning against the iron bars, shook his head.
“Nothing. Our Hubei branch still hasn’t found them.”
“Three Supreme Peak masters—or hundreds of people and ships—must have been mobilized. There’s no way they could’ve avoided attention. If we focus on outsiders, we might have a chance...”

“We already are, but it isn’t easy. Hundreds of large ships travel the Hubei stretch of the Yangtze every day, and the people moving by land are too numerous to count. And if this happened a good ten days ago... there’s a strong chance they’ve already left Hubei by one means or another.”
“Damn it.”
Unlike Shanxi Province, which was treated as a borderland, Hubei Province was part of the region known as the Central Plains, and its industries were well developed.
With merchants and travelers constantly pouring in and out of such a vast territory, even the Beggars’ Sect was bound to struggle.
Gung Gibang watched my expression, then spoke cautiously.

“Cheongpung and Hyuk Mujin went to the Lower District Sect, so all we can do is hope they found something. Their findings probably won’t be much different from those of our Hubei branch, but... we have to hold on to hope.”
Gung Gibang was right.
Half a shichen later, Cheongpung and Hyuk Mujin returned to the Zhuge Clan carrying a large bundle of bamboo slips.
A single man’s sobriquet was written on the cord binding them together.
Dongting Fisherman.
“This...”
Hyuk Mujin swallowed hard before continuing.

“It seems the Lower District Sect had some sort of dispute with the Dongting Fisherman. They said they’ve been keeping a close watch on him for several years under the Sect Leader’s orders... You should probably read it yourself.”
I quickly skimmed the contents of the bamboo slips.
Their records on the Dongting Fisherman went back no fewer than three years, and the bundle in my hands contained only a portion of them.
The records from one month ago through today revealed one fact.
*The Dongting Fisherman is still in Hubei Province.*
Which meant...
Clatter!
I shoved the bamboo slips into my robe and immediately went in search of one man.
Zhuge Gyun, the Divine Marvel Dragon and Lesser Family Head of the Zhuge Clan, had been issuing orders in place of the Family Head, Zhuge Feng. His eyes widened at my noisy arrival.
“What brings you here in such haste? My ancestor Zhuge Wuhou said that a junzi should always conduct himself properly and remain tranquil...”
“Shut up. Are the people ready?”
“The people my fath—no, the Family Head mentioned are already prepared to leave. Do you intend to depart immediately?”
“Yeah. But I think I need to stop somewhere else first.”
“Pardon? Where...?”
“Dongting Lake.”

It could not endure the heat of Scorching Yang Qi.
“Ghk...
Gack.”
His painful, gasping breaths carried the smell of meat being cooked.
But I continued staring at the Third Fiend without wavering.
“That’s not the answer I want.”
“This old man—I have already told you everything.”
“Not that either.”
“Ghk.
P-please...”
“If you can still hold out like this, you’re nowhere near death yet.
Just like there’s still information I haven’t heard.”
“What else could you possibly want me to say...?”
“I’ve told you several times already.
Everything about Dark Heaven.
What’s happening in Hubei Province, and the Dongting Fisherman.”
“I told you, I don’t know—kuweeegh!”
With every exchange, the Scorching Yang Qi grew stronger.
The Third Fiend trembled violently, eyes rolling back until only the whites showed.
A scream tore from his lips.
“Kill me!
Hurry up and kill me!
Even as a vengeful ghost, I’ll chew through your flesh and bones...!”
Damn it.
That was as far as I could go.
I abruptly withdrew the internal energy I had been forcing into him.
The Third Fiend immediately went limp, like a puppet with its strings cut.
Changing the flow, I gently stabilized his body from within.
The old man, already standing by, quickly took his pulse and checked his condition.
“He’s a hard one to kill.
Stopped right on the threshold of the afterlife.”
I knew.
I had controlled my strength as carefully as possible to keep him alive.
*He can’t die here.*
The Third Fiend was one of the great fiends of the previous generation and a Supreme Peak master of Dark Heaven.
If we kept him alive and escorted him to Henan, there might be a way to learn even more information.
Of course, I couldn’t dismiss the possibility that those bamboo slips contained everything he knew.
No.
That was probably the likeliest possibility.
*If he still didn’t talk after all this... maybe he really has told us everything.*
The mental strength and endurance of a Supreme Peak master defied imagination.
Yet the Third Fiend had begged me—someone no different from his mortal enemy—to stop.
He had screamed for me to kill him instead.
And still, he had never changed his story.
*I—I and my brothers only followed orders under the Demon Lord!
I don’t know anything about Dark Heaven’s headquarters or what happened elsewhere, I tell you!*
Remembering the cries he had repeated throughout the torture, I called out a name.
“Gung Gibang.
Any news?”
Gung Gibang, leaning against the iron bars, shook his head.
“Nothing.
Our Hubei branch still hasn’t found them.”
“Three Supreme Peak masters—or hundreds of people and ships—must have been mobilized.
There’s no way they could’ve avoided attention.
If we focus on outsiders, we might have a chance...”
“We already are, but it isn’t easy.
Hundreds of large ships travel the Hubei stretch of the Yangtze every day, and the people moving by land are too numerous to count.
And if this happened a good ten days ago... there’s a strong chance they’ve already left Hubei by one means or another.”
“Damn it.”
Unlike Shanxi Province, which was treated as a borderland, Hubei Province was part of the region known as the Central Plains, and its industries were well developed.
With merchants and travelers constantly pouring in and out of such a vast territory, even the Beggars’ Sect was bound to struggle.
Gung Gibang watched my expression, then spoke cautiously.
“Cheongpung and Hyuk Mujin went to the Lower District Sect, so all we can do is hope they found something.
Their findings probably won’t be much different from those of our Hubei branch, but... we have to hold on to hope.”
Gung Gibang was right.
Half a shichen later, Cheongpung and Hyuk Mujin returned to the Zhuge Clan carrying a large bundle of bamboo slips.
A single man’s sobriquet was written on the cord binding them together.
Dongting Fisherman.
“This...”
Hyuk Mujin swallowed hard before continuing.
“It seems the Lower District Sect had some sort of dispute with the Dongting Fisherman.
They said they’ve been keeping a close watch on him for several years under the Sect Leader’s orders...
You should probably read it yourself.”
I quickly skimmed the contents of the bamboo slips.
Their records on the Dongting Fisherman went back no fewer than three years, and the bundle in my hands contained only a portion of them.
The records from one month ago through today revealed one fact.
*The Dongting Fisherman is still in Hubei Province.*
Which meant...
Clatter!
I shoved the bamboo slips into my robe and immediately went in search of one man.
Zhuge Gyun, the Divine Marvel Dragon and Lesser Family Head of the Zhuge Clan, had been issuing orders in place of the Family Head, Zhuge Feng.
His eyes widened at my noisy arrival.
“What brings you here in such haste?
My ancestor Zhuge Wuhou said that a junzi should always conduct himself properly and remain tranquil...”
“Shut up.
Are the people ready?”
“The people my fath—no, the Family Head mentioned are already prepared to leave.
Do you intend to depart immediately?”
“Yeah.
But I think I need to stop somewhere else first.”
“Pardon?
Where...?”
“Dongting Lake.”

chapters.title: Chapter 456
paragraphs: “Dongting Lake, out of nowhere? What do you mean?”
Zhuge Gyun’s confusion lasted only a moment. Though he occasionally behaved like an eccentric, his mind was as sharp as one would expect from a scion of the Zhuge Clan.
His epithet, the Divine Marvel Dragon, had not been bestowed on him merely because of his deep understanding of mechanisms and formations.
“Are you trying to find the Dongting Fisherman?”

Several shichen earlier, when I first arrived at the Zhuge Clan, Zhuge Gyun had heard the full circumstances of the case from me. He also knew that the Dongting Fisherman had been identified as one of the culprits.
“Yeah.”
“Given how suddenly you’re acting... I assume your information came from the Beggars’ Sect and the Lower District Sect.”
“More precisely, the Lower District Sect. They’ve been watching the Dongting Fisherman for three years.”
“Not watching. Monitoring. Our family had also noticed that something had happened between the Dongting Fisherman and the Lower District Sect Leader.”
“Either way, it works in our favor. Read this.”
Zhuge Gyun took the bamboo slip from me, and his eyes moved rapidly across it.
He read every last word in mere moments, then rubbed his temple and muttered, “The Dongting Fisherman is still in Hubei Province?”
“That’s what the Lower District Sect’s intelligence says.”

“This is insufficient. According to what is written on this bamboo slip, the Lower District Sect has not determined the Dongting Fisherman’s exact whereabouts. They merely failed to detect him leaving Hubei Province.”
“I’ve considered that too. But what if the information is accurate?”
“If it is...”
The Dongting Fisherman, whom everyone believed to be dead, was alive and well somewhere in Hubei Province?
That could mean only one thing.

“If the Dongting Fisherman really is a Dark Heaven underling and one of the culprits who massacred Donghu Stronghold, then it would certainly be possible. No—in fact, it would make it even more certain that he is a culprit.”
Zhuge Gyun nodded gravely.
“Indeed. If he were not affiliated with Dark Heaven, he would already have informed the world of the tragedy at Donghu Stronghold and requested assistance from our family and Wudang.”
After the Sea Serpent Society, three strongholds of the Yangtze River Channel League—including Donghu Stronghold—had been annihilated.

If we had not arrived when we did—and if it had not been for Ship-Fire Boy Mu Song and the swift ship under his command—the tragedy at Donghu Stronghold beyond Tianling Falls would have remained unknown for much longer.

“But one question remains. This is not something that can be concealed forever. It might take time, but the truth was bound to come out. If Dark Heaven had truly intended to cover it up, they would have handled everything more quietly, without drawing public attention. They could have laid the blame for the Sea Serpent Society’s destruction on the Yangtze River Channel League.”
He was right. The Zhuge Clan and Wudang had been unable to cross Tianling Falls only because they lacked vessels sturdy enough for the journey and skilled boatmen to pilot them.
Even if they could not rely on Mu Song and the river bandits of Water Dragon Stronghold, they would eventually have found suitable men elsewhere.
Zhuge Gyun stared pensively at the bamboo slip before raising his head to look at me.
“Then why go this far?”
I took a drink from the cup on the table to wet my throat.
“Under ordinary circumstances, they would’ve done it to buy time.”
“Exactly. Dark Heaven would have needed time to escape. But the fact that the Dongting Fisherman is still in Hubei Province is strange.”
“Yeah. It’s strange. So strange that the pieces don’t fit.”
When I answered without hesitation, Zhuge Gyun’s eyebrows rose slightly.
“You have another theory.”
“I said under ordinary circumstances.”
“Then...”
“Dark Heaven isn’t made up of ordinary people. You experienced them in Henan, so you should know that.”
“They throw a pebble first to draw everyone’s attention, then get a boulder ready. This won’t end with the Sea Serpent Society and three strongholds. They’re definitely after something bigger.”
Dark Heaven’s power and audacity defied common sense.
Two Supreme Peak masters of the previous generation, both counted among the Ten Kings, had already died. Thousands more had fallen in sprays of blood.
And the two blood-soaked disasters Dark Heaven had caused shared one clear objective.
“Divine artifacts...”
At Zhuge Gyun’s low murmur, I quietly nodded.
In Henan, Dark Heaven had stolen Shaolin Temple’s divine artifact, the Green Jade Buddha Staff. When they attacked Sichuan, they had attempted to seize the Myriad-Poison Ring.
Fortunately, their operation in Sichuan had failed, but what they were after was obvious.
*Divine artifacts—or the destruction of the prestigious great sects known as the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families.*
It was hard to believe that people like that had gone to such lengths merely to wipe out a sect like the Sea Serpent Society, whose members were just trying to make a living, and three strongholds.
It might have made sense if they had targeted the headquarters of the Yangtze River Channel League, where the Seafaring King was based.
Zhuge Gyun’s expression stiffened.
“Then the culprits, including the Dongting Fisherman, have ample reason to remain in Hubei Province.”

“It’s still only speculation, but for now, we have to assume they drew everyone’s attention elsewhere in preparation for something bigger. The delay was just a smokescreen meant to convince us they’d already left Hubei Province.”
“The darkest place is directly beneath the lamp... But could they not have already vanished through that bizarre Moving Formation?”
“You might as well tell me Cheongpung walked past a dumpling shop.”
“Oh. Now that you put it that way, I understand completely.”
I stared hard into empty space.
“What happened to the Sea Serpent Society and Donghu Stronghold was the pebble. The boulder comes next.”
The pond called Hubei Province was vast. Even if a pebble fell into it, the ripples would not travel far before subsiding.
If a boulder fell, however, it would send water surging into the air—and the fish in the pond would not escape unharmed.
We had to stop the boulder from falling before the pond was dyed with blood.
“I will inform the local authorities and Wudang in preparation for the worst. I will also strengthen our defenses inside and out.”
“Watch the government troops carefully. You’ve heard what happened in Sichuan, haven’t you?”
The forces of Dark Heaven, led by the Western Heaven Demon Lord, had disguised themselves as government troops and swept through the Tang Clan, Emei, and Qingcheng.
It was already common knowledge. There was no way Zhuge Gyun, the Lesser Family Head of the Zhuge Clan, could be unaware of it.
“I am already taking precautions, though I doubt they will use the same method twice.”
“Inform Donghu Stronghold too. The swift ship from Water Dragon Stronghold should be waiting at the Zaoyang ferry, so entrust the letter to our family retainers.”

A messenger pigeon would have been faster and more convenient, but it could be intercepted along the way. Besides, the Zhuge Clan had no messenger pigeons trained to fly to and from Donghu Stronghold.
*The other two strongholds that had been able to communicate with Donghu Stronghold had already been wiped out, too.*
The gruesome sea of corpses and blood flashed before my eyes, and my fist tightened before I realized it.
Shanxi. Henan. Sichuan. Then the monster wave in Sichuan Province in the modern world. Traveling between two worlds, I had already witnessed far too many deaths.
Scrape.
As I rose from my seat, Zhuge Gyun asked, “Are you leaving right now?”
“The sooner, the better. I don’t know where the Dongting Fisherman is, but we need to start at Dongting Lake and look for traces.”
“That will not be easy. The Dongting Fisherman spent his entire life around Dongting Lake, so he likely knows several secret refuges unknown to the rest of the world.”
I clenched my fist.
“Hey. Are you Dark Heaven?”
“Pardon?”
“I asked if you’re Dark Heaven.”
“Ah, no.”
“Then stop saying ominous things and cheer me on, you bastard.”
Zhuge Gyun glanced at my fist and answered at once.
“Yes, sir. For now, I will mobilize all of our family’s intelligence resources and cooperate with the Beggars’ Sect and the Lower District Sect to search every region outside Dongting Lake.”
“Do a good job. I’m leaving.”
I was about to turn away when I realized I had forgotten one important question.
“Wait. Does the Zhuge Clan have any divine artifacts?”

“Of course. There is the Four-Wheeled Cart our ancestor Zhuge Wuhou rode during his lifetime, the Twenty-Four Chapters on the Art of War, in which he compiled his insights, and the White Feather Fan.”
“...That’s quite a collection.”
I had no idea how impressive a wheelchair, a book, and a fan could be as divine artifacts, but it was worth checking just in case.
I turned to Zhuge Gyun.
“Let me see them for a minute. There’s something I need to confirm.”
“We had them, but we don’t anymore.”

“The Twenty-Four Chapters on the Art of War were lost during a war, and the White Feather Fan crumbled with age. As for the Four-Wheeled Cart, I heard that one of our former Family Heads rode it and broke it around two hundred years ago. I cannot remember his name.”
What the fuck.
Was this some grand strategy to destroy their own treasures before Dark Heaven could steal them?
Judging by the artifacts themselves, they seemed to have been significant only because Zhuge Wuhou had left them behind. Still, the whole thing was absurd.
“The Four-Wheeled Cart is still here in its broken state. Would you like me to show it to you?”
“No. Forget it.”
I answered firmly and left the pavilion. Outside, beneath the night sky that had once again grown dark, three people stood waiting with all their preparations complete.
Or was it four?
“That bastard’s still breathing, right?”
“Yes, Benefactor.”
Just as I had in Sichuan, Cheongpung carried a wooden pack frame on his back. The Third Fiend lay atop it, every acupoint sealed and his body bound in chains.
“He is very weak, but he should be fine if I use my internal energy from time to time to bolster his vitality.”
“That’s enough.”
There was a simple reason for bringing the Third Fiend along. I wanted to find out whether there were any codes or markings that only members of Dark Heaven could recognize.
That was the sole value of keeping him alive.
“Let’s go to Dongting Lake.”
We left the Zhuge Clan and raced like comets along the straight highway.
The wind rushing over my body seemed tinged with the smell of blood.
Whoooosh!
We raced without conserving our strength.
Hyuk Mujin had less internal energy and an inferior movement technique compared to me, Cheongpung, and Gung Gibang, so he kept falling behind. But it was not much of a problem.
“Get on my back.”
Drenched in sweat from head to toe, Hyuk Mujin shook his head with effort.
“Huff, huff. No, sir. I can keep running!”
“I know you’re struggling. Get on.”
“Huff, I am truly fine. I am the Vice Squad Leader of the Jin Dragon Squad of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan! I cannot cause trouble for my family or Captain—”
“Did a guy like you run around trying to pick up silver nyang?”
“Get on if you don’t want to die. Otherwise, I’m leaving you behind.”
“Yes, sir.”
Hyuk Mujin was a fairly large man, but I possessed an extraordinary Strength stat. Carrying one person while running was no great burden.
*Why do I suddenly feel like Red Hare?*
I don’t know how long we ran with that strange feeling.
The sky had been only slightly dim when we left the Zhuge Clan, but now it was completely dark. Even the travelers on the highway had disappeared.
After more than two shichen had passed, Gung Gibang, who had been exerting his movement technique at full strength, opened his mouth.
His words, reeking of filth and sickly sweetness, pierced my ears.
“Wuhan.”
Wuhan was the capital of Hubei Province, a city a stone’s throw from Dongting Lake.
But perhaps because of the recent string of ominous incidents, the streets that should have bustled all night were silent. Not even a rat showed its face.
*Of course. No ordinary person wants to wander around at night and die like a dog for no reason.*
I was thinking that as we crossed Wuhan’s maze of streets when it happened.
“Dongting Lake! A ship has sunk in Dongting Lake!”
A scream rang out in the distance, shattering the deep, dark silence.

chapters.title: Chapter 457
paragraphs: “Dongting Lake! A ship has sunk in Dongting Lake!”
“P-please, help us! People have fallen into the water!”
*Clang, clang—!*
Screams rang out in the distance, and the sharp peal of warning bells echoed through the darkness.
But another sound had reached my ears a moment earlier.
*Ding.*
*This is...*
A familiar notification.
A chill of foreboding ran down my spine. I stared at the translucent System window floating before my eyes.

**System An unexpected Quest, **The Tragedy of Dongting Lake**, has been generated! - You cannot refuse the Quest! **Quest The Tragedy of Dongting Lake** Dongting Lake is one of the most celebrated scenic destinations under heaven. Poets and men of letters climb Yiyang Tower to enjoy its beautiful vistas and compose verses about nature, while those blessed with power and wealth launch large, splendid pleasure boats and revel for days and nights. But today, this clear, blue-green lake is filled with shattered wreckage and corpses. Unless someone steps forward, those still alive will meet the same fate! **Grade:** Peak **Restriction:** Jin Taekyung **Mission:** Rescue People (Incomplete) **Reward:** ??? **Failure:** The deaths of the people *A considerable amount of time has already passed. You must rescue the people before it is too late!*
As I finished reading the final line of the Quest window, a small holographic window appeared in the air.
**System Time Limit:** 45 minutes 36 seconds
Damn it. Less than an hour.
*If we waste even a moment... everyone will die.*
There wasn’t even time to wonder how such a catastrophe had happened. Someone’s life might depend on every minute—maybe even every second.
I drew as much internal energy as possible from my dantian and opened my mouth.
“From this moment on, run to Dongting Lake as if your lives depend on it. We save the people first.”
*Whoosh!*
No one answered. Their faces simply hardened as they accelerated again.
Using the distant cries and warning bells as our compass, we ran and ran.
By the time the first digit of the time limit changed from four to two, we could finally see it.
*Fwoom, roar!*
Dozens of vessels, large and small, burned across the broad waters, engulfed in flames as countless shouts rang out from every direction.
“Bring boats! Even a ferryboat will do, so hurry!”
“We don’t have enough boatmen!”
“More! Bring more people! Things have come to this, so where are the military vessels? What are they doing?”
“Ahhh! Ahhh!”
With every step, the scene came into sharper focus.
More than a hundred people raced frantically along the shore of Dongting Lake, while several small ferryboats moved slowly across the water.
*That won’t be enough.*
They were doing everything they could, but their efforts fell woefully short of what was needed to rescue so many people.
Even I, with martial arts that more than qualified me as a superhuman, felt my breath catch at the sight.
*How are we supposed to save them?*
I had heard plenty about the vastness of Dongting Lake, but seeing it for myself, I realized it was far larger than I had imagined.

There was no way the vessels would be packed close together on such a vast lake. Judging from the distances between them, every ship must have been out enjoying itself at least several hundred zhang from the others.
And this was only what I could see immediately. How many more boats and people were submerged beyond my sight?
*Damn it.*
I bit down hard on my lip and accelerated.
The murmurs grew louder as people spotted us racing toward them like the wind.
A military officer who appeared to belong to the local authorities cried out urgently.
“A-are you martial artists? Please, help—”
“No time for explanations. We’re borrowing some boats.”
“Pardon?”
Leaving the dumbfounded officer behind, I thundered an order.
“Gung Gibang, Hyuk Mujin! Smash the ferryboats!”
*Whoosh!*
There was no hesitation or doubt in either man’s movements.
Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin shot past me with forceful shouts, unleashing palm force and sword strikes.
*Slash, boom!*
The two ferries being hurriedly moved by the people were transformed into hundreds of pieces of wood in an instant.
The military officer, momentarily stunned by what had happened before he could even say anything, screamed,
“What in the world are you doing!”
Shocked cries erupted from every direction.
“T-the ferryboats...!”
“Those bastards are the villains who caused this disaster! They must be trying to keep us from rescuing the people!”
Shock and anger spread rapidly. All manner of curses poured in from every side, along with gazes brimming with killing intent.
But I didn’t care.
No—it would be more accurate to say I had no time to care.
**System Time Limit:** 28 minutes 52 seconds
Barely thirty minutes remained.
Explaining myself now would only cost more lives.
Fortunately, there were three martial artists here who could understand my intentions and act on them.
“Cheongpung, Gung Gibang!”
“Got it!”
“Yes, Benefactor!”
Realizing what I meant, Gung Gibang and Cheongpung scooped up the ferryboat fragments and hurled them with all their strength toward the dark waters of Dongting Lake.
*Whoosh, splash!*
Dozens of wooden fragments sliced through the darkness and scattered across the lake.
“W-what!”
“Could this be...?”
A few people finally realized what we were doing, their eyes widening. But there still weren’t enough fragments.
Some might even sink before our feet reached them.
In that case...
*We’ll have to make the path as we go.*
The instant I reached that decision, I stamped down hard.
*Boom!*
The sand and dust piled along the shore surged into the air all at once, making the unprepared people cough.
Taking advantage of the moment when everyone’s vision was obscured, I reached out.
As my hand met damp, solid wood, I spoke the command only I could use.
*Store in Inventory.*
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*
**System Ferryboat Fragment** has been stored in your Inventory! Ferryboat Fragment** has been stored in your Inventory...
Notifications rang in my ears as the wooden fragments dissolved into thin air.
I left behind only enough fragments to avoid arousing suspicion, then shouted forcefully,
“Cheongpung and Gung Gibang, come with me! Hyuk Mujin, stay here and gather boats and people!”
“Y-yes, sir!”

Hyuk Mujin had been gasping for breath for some time now, and he barely managed to squeeze out the words. By then, Cheongpung, Gung Gibang, and I were already shooting toward the dark waters of Dongting Lake.
*Whoosh!*
Heat surged from my lower abdomen and flowed down into my legs.
Formidable internal energy flooded a body whose muscles and elasticity were so perfect they could be mistaken for a Heavenly Martial Physique.
*Now!*
*Boom!*
A massive shock wave burst from my toes, pressed down against the ground, and shoved back the rippling water. Sand and gravel scattered as dust, while a cool wind swept across my entire body.
If I reached out, I felt as though I could pluck the stars scattered across the night sky from the heavens.
But only for a moment.
Every leap was followed by a fall.
*Whoooosh!*
The black water, surging violently, rushed toward us.
My eyes, as keen as a wild animal’s, easily picked out a half-submerged piece of wood.
*Tap. Thump!*
My landing was light, but the second leap that followed was heavy.
Cheongpung, Gung Gibang, and I launched ourselves forward again.
Using the scattered ferryboat fragments as stepping stones, we leaped once, twice, three times...
Only after repeating the process several times did the vessel that had seemed so far away draw close enough to make out clearly.
But as the distance shrank, the foreboding in my heart grew.
*I can’t feel any life force.*
There were no survivors’ screams, no movement—nothing that should have been there if anyone was still alive.
And it did not take long for the foreboding I felt to become reality.
*Tap.*
On the vessel, most of whose hull was already submerged, Gung Gibang and Cheongpung landed on the bow and muttered like men groaning in pain.
“This is...”
“...Benefactor.”
Their voices sounded faint, as if they were coming from hundreds of zhang away.
In that suffocating silence, I stared blankly around me.
Everywhere I looked, countless corpses floated among the wreckage of shattered ships.
They were dead.
All of them.
A potbellied man who appeared to be a merchant, dressed in splendid silk. A gaunt, shabby-looking boatman. Musicians and courtesans who seemed to have been hired to liven up the festivities.
There were hundreds within sight alone.
No lively music drifted across the black water. No laughter.
All that remained was destruction and death—and the fear plainly etched into the faces of the dead.
*How could this have happened?*
For a moment, my mind went completely blank.
As if possessed, I raced across the water from fragment to fragment, using Qi Sense without restraint in search of even a single survivor.
But...
*Beep.*
**System Qi Sense** has failed. - The qi of the desired target could not be detected within range.
The System was more merciless than ever.
The translucent holographic window and grating failure notification told me that there was not a single survivor nearby.
“What in the world...”
I muttered in despair—and then a thought flashed through my mind like lightning.
*Wait. The System?*
I hurriedly raised my head and stared into the air.
The translucent holographic window was still there.
**System Time Limit:** 9 minutes 43 seconds
It felt as if someone had struck me hard in the back of the head.
If there truly were no survivors, the Quest should have been canceled or a failure notification should have appeared. The System was faster and more direct than anything.
But the Quest was still in progress, and the System window displaying the time limit hadn’t disappeared.
That could only mean one thing.
As I stood there, frozen stiff, Gung Gibang spoke to me in a cautious voice.
“Unfortunately, it seems pointless to keep searching for survivors...”
“There are survivors.”
“What?”
“We just can’t see them. There are survivors somewhere much farther away. I’m sure of it.”
Gung Gibang had been about to say something, but his expression hardened when he saw the certainty on my face.
Cheongpung spoke in a voice more serious than usual.
“If what you say is true, Benefactor...”
“Then we find them and save them. No matter what it takes.”
Gung Gibang stared at me for a moment, then nodded.
“We’ll have to split up. If we tear apart the sunken boats around here and use the pieces, we might be able to keep going for another half a shichen.”
“You have fifteen minutes. Search as far as you can before then. If you don’t find any survivors, come back.”
The time limit showed how much time the survivors had left. Searching beyond that would be meaningless.
My unusually firm tone puzzled them, but they soon accepted the order without another word.
“We’ll do that.”
“Fifteen minutes. I’ll remember, Benefactor.”
“Then we split up and each take a different direction. See you soon.”
*Thump, whoosh!*
With that, I kicked off the bow and leaped.
Watching the time limit dwindle by the second, I pushed my internal energy and senses to their limits and raced on and on across Dongting Lake, vast as the open sea.
**System Time Limit:** 1 minute 12 seconds
*Am I too late?*
And just as I was about to give up on everything—
“P-please, save me...”
A tiny, faint voice reached my ears.

chapters.title: Chapter 458
paragraphs: *P-please, save me...*
Like a dying ember, the voice was tiny and faint.
But that alone was enough. My heart, weighed down by the helplessness of having failed to save anyone, began pounding fiercely, and strength surged through my limp body.
I launched myself toward the voice.
*Inventory: Open. Summon!*
*Thud!*
One of the few remaining fragments of the ferryboat skimmed across the moon’s reflection on the water.
I leaped through the air like a bird, drew up the last of my internal energy, and focused it in my eyes.
My drastically enhanced vision took in the scene below with perfect clarity.
*That’s...*
Wreckage and corpses.
Though the vessel had been smashed apart beyond recognition, there was no doubt it had once been the largest and most splendid ship I had seen on Dongting Lake.
*There’s a survivor somewhere among them.*
The problem was that there were far too many corpses and pieces of wreckage in sight.
But there was no time to hesitate.
**System Time Limit:** 59 seconds
Fifty-nine seconds. The survivor’s life depended on this brief span of less than a minute.
I closed my eyes and steadied my breathing. Then I drew up every last bit of my internal energy, which was already nearly depleted.
*Fwoooooosh!*
Qi Sense.
The Scorching Yang Qi extending from my entire body raced across the rippling water.
It swept through more than a hundred corpses whose souls had already departed and the countless pieces of wreckage, searching every inch.
And finally—
I saw it.
No—I felt it.
Dozens of zhang away, a faint presence was sinking farther beneath the surface with every passing moment.
I opened my eyes halfway.
**System Time Limit:** 32 seconds
The Scorching Yang Qi circulating through my body rushed toward my lower half.
When I stepped on empty air with the tips of my toes, the compressed air exploded outward, and a cold wind swept across my entire body.
*Boom! Fwoooooosh!*
I shot forward like a meteor. The wind split apart, and space vanished.
The scenery flashed past on either side, but my gaze remained fixed on a single point.
The rough, surging black water.
There was a survivor in there.
*Damn it. I can’t even swim.*
The thought had barely crossed my mind when the waters of Dongting Lake slammed into my entire body.
*Splash! Gurgle!*
The impact knocked the breath out of me.
If I had not learned martial arts, my bones would have broken and my internal organs would have been badly jarred.
I sank beneath the surface, trailing a cloud of bubbles.
A school of fish scattered in alarm at the sudden arrival of an unwelcome visitor, revealing two figures slowly sinking into the depths.
**System Time Limit:** 20 seconds
*More. More. More...*
I summoned every last ounce of strength and pushed forward. Grabbing the wrists of the two unconscious, limp figures, I surged upward with all my might.
Ten seconds. Nine, eight...
The faint moonlight reflected on the surface drew closer.
My arms and legs felt as heavy as if iron balls had been tied to them, while the two people in my hands weighed like thousand-catty boulders.
And then—
*Splash!*
“Puaaah!”
I expelled the breath I had been holding.
Air cold enough to sting flowed deep into my lungs.
But pulling the survivors out of the water did not mean everything was over.
**System Time Limit:** 3 seconds
In that moment, I instinctively realized what I had to do.
*Save them.*
That single thought moved my body, which had briefly gone still.
I thrust both palms, infused with what little internal energy I had left, toward the two people.
*Boom!*
Their bodies jerked, and water splashed.
But the survivors showed no response. Instead, the number on the System window floating in the air changed.
**System Time Limit:** 2 seconds
*One more time...*
*Boom!*
**System Time Limit:** 1 second
Everything slowed down.
That paltry digit, 1, seemed larger and heavier than ever, crushing me beneath its weight.
I stared blankly at the System window, eyes wide, when—
“Puh.”
“Cough, cough.”
The survivors finally began breathing again. At the same moment, the System window froze just as it was about to change to its final number.
Then a bell rang out like a celebratory salute.
*Ding.*

**System You succeeded in **Rescuing Lives**! - You completed the unexpected Quest **The Tragedy of Dongting Lake**! - You have successfully completed the Quest. An appropriate Reward will be granted! - You acquired a considerable amount of EXP and Fame! - You acquired the Title **Water Rescue Worker**!
As the notifications rang in my ears, I muttered,
“Fuuuck.”
Joy and relief at having finally succeeded were secondary. Worn down by the forced march that had begun at the Zhuge Clan, my body felt unbearably heavy.
Maybe it was because the tension I’d barely managed to hold suddenly let go.
*...Damn it. It’ll take forever to get back to land.*
At this rate, would I end up needing to be rescued too?
I was floating there with the two survivors, buoyed by the water, when—
*Whoooooosh!*
Something sliced through the water in the distance as fast as a jet ski and stopped right in front of me.
A pure-white body and scales, along with two horns.
“A water snake...? No, a Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake?”
*Hiss. Hiss. Hiss-hiss!*
*No, don’t go!*
I hurriedly shouted at the creature as it flicked its tongue and turned away.
“Hey! Hey! Water snake! Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake!”
*Hiss!*
“You little bastard, did you just spit at me—wait.”
Was this its way of showing that it was sulking?
One thought suddenly came to mind, and I opened my mouth in an earnest yet cautious voice.
“Mimi... Mimi-chan?”
*Hiss-rik! Hiss-ririk!*
Only then did the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake—or rather, Mimi-chan—nod in satisfaction and extend its tail toward me as if telling me to grab on.
Right on cue, someone shouted from far away.
“Mimi! Rescue Benefactor!”
*Hiss-rik!*
Yeah, fuck it. I didn’t care what the move was called. Just get me out of here.
I sat on a damp rock and stared at the rippling water.
Two people. Only two.
Of the countless people who had buried their bones in Dongting Lake today, the two I had saved were the only survivors.
*...Only two out of all those people.*
I had suspected it from the moment the Quest was completed, but reality was even more brutal and merciless than I had imagined.
And the countless deaths left behind by today’s tragedy had given rise to even greater sorrow.
“Sniff, sob!”
“Oh, poor Chil-Sam’s father!”
“What kind of monstrous bastard could have done this?”
By then, over a thousand people had gathered along the shore of Dongting Lake, giving voice to every kind of emotion.

A Confucian scholar lamented, unable to continue speaking. Behind a government soldier clutching a fallen comrade’s corpse and weeping came the wails of a woman with an infant strapped to her back. An old man, the veins standing out on his neck, even swung his long-stemmed tobacco pipe at some unseen culprit.
There was no longer any laughter or singing to be found at Dongting Lake, one of the most famous scenic sites under heaven.
Only the sorrow and lamentation of those left behind remained, along with the anger carried in all those emotions.
But nothing changed.
The waters of Dongting Lake had grown calm, as if nothing had happened, while the faint dawn mist spreading across the lake created a beautiful scene.
*Is this what the Wuling Peach Blossom Spring, where immortals are said to live, looks like?*
I stared silently at the scene before me, then spoke without warning.
“This feels like... something, doesn’t it?”
I was not talking to myself.
Cheongpung, who had not left my side for more than fifteen minutes, answered,
“Yes. It feels like shit.”
Under normal circumstances, I would have snorted with laughter despite myself. But now, there was only emptiness.
I fidgeted with a pebble and asked,
“I only said ‘something.’ I didn’t know Cheongpung knew how to swear.”
“I didn’t at first, but I know a little now. I learned by watching someone.”
“You’d better keep that a secret from Great Hero Mae Jonghak.”
“Why, Benefactor?”
“Why do you think? How would you feel if Mimi suddenly called you a fucking bastard one day?”
“Hmm. I don’t think I’d like it.”
“...Wouldn’t most people be surprised that a snake was talking before getting angry? Either way, you’d be surprised and angry. Great Hero Mae Jonghak would feel the same.”
“Oh. I see.”
“Yeah. That’s how it is.”
“What should I do if I accidentally swear in front of Grandpa?”
“Say Gung Gibang taught you. Or Hyuk Mujin.”
“Okay.”
Silence descended.
That conversation had been nothing more than whatever nonsense came to mind. I had felt that I needed to say something—anything. Maybe doing so would make things a little better.
Both Cheongpung and I knew the truth.
We also knew that none of this would make us feel any better.
“Fuck...”
I muttered the curse like a lament.
I did not know whether today was simply an unusual day, or whether those creatures also understood the circumstances and were grieving.
There was no birdsong.
Only the wails and sobs of the people filled the air around us.
I listened quietly to those stifling, unbearable sounds, then clenched the pebble in my palm as hard as I could.
*Crack. Crunch.*
A handful of powder spilled from my fist.
No—it was carried by a breeze that had blown in from somewhere and settled lightly on the surface of the water.
As if they were mortal remains imbued with someone’s spirit.
Cheongpung watched in silence before suddenly speaking.
“Benefactor.”
“What?”
“What should I do at times like this?”
“So many people have died. In Henan, in Sichuan, at Donghu Stronghold, and today, here.”
His voice trembled faintly as he continued.
“I keep thinking about the dead. And I get angry. I hate the people who keep killing others, and I feel pathetic because I can’t do anything.”
“...I was like that too. No, I still am.”
“What did you do whenever you felt this way, Benefactor?”
“Me?”
I turned my head and finally met Cheongpung’s gaze.
His usually crystal-clear eyes were swirling with a mixture of emotions.
Within that confusion, I saw my past self—and the present me staring at Cheongpung now.
*Was I like this?*
The person I saw reflected in Cheongpung’s eyes was simply impassive.
I was not exhausted like Gung Gibang or Hyuk Mujin, nor was I trembling with anger and sorrow like those who had lost their families and companions.
No, it was not that I could no longer feel emotions.
I had merely learned to contain them.
There I stood, like a rock battered again and again over the years, worn and ground down until it had finally grown accustomed to the blows.
“Who knows? What did I do back then?”
After thinking for a moment, I slowly continued.
“I wasn’t any different from you, Cheongpung. I swore nonstop at those bastards who deserved to die, blamed myself for my helplessness, and then made a vow.”
“A vow?”
“Yeah. A vow.”
I raised a finger and pointed at the grieving people and the corpses laid out along the shore.
“I vowed to kill every last bastard who did this. That was my vow.”
“I’m no saint. I won’t be satisfied until I pay them back at least in equal measure. This time is no different.”
The words slipped from my lips in a dry, cold voice that sounded foreign, almost as if it belonged to someone else.
Just then—
“Captain.”
Hyuk Mujin approached us, exhaustion plainly visible on his face.
“The survivors have regained consciousness.”
“That’s good. Both of them?”
“No, sir. Only one of them, for now.”
It was unfortunate, but I had suspected as much. The treatment I had given them after the rescue had only been an emergency measure.
“Then let’s go.”
“Yes, sir. This way.”
Cheongpung and I followed Hyuk Mujin.
At last, we came face-to-face with the survivor who had regained consciousness.
“We’ve met again rather quickly, haven’t we?”
At my greeting, Honglan, the dazzlingly beautiful singing courtesan, bowed with the utmost respect.
“It is an honor to see you, Benefactor.”

sentences.text: *P-please, save me...*
Like a dying ember, the voice was tiny and faint.
But that alone was enough.
My heart, weighed down by the helplessness of having failed to save anyone, began pounding fiercely, and strength surged through my limp body.
I launched myself toward the voice.
*Inventory: Open.
Summon!*
*Thud!*
One of the few remaining fragments of the ferryboat skimmed across the moon’s reflection on the water.
I leaped through the air like a bird, drew up the last of my internal energy, and focused it in my eyes.
My drastically enhanced vision took in the scene below with perfect clarity.
*That’s...*
Wreckage and corpses.
Though the vessel had been smashed apart beyond recognition, there was no doubt it had once been the largest and most splendid ship I had seen on Dongting Lake.
*There’s a survivor somewhere among them.*
The problem was that there were far too many corpses and pieces of wreckage in sight.
But there was no time to hesitate.
**System Time Limit:** 59 seconds
Fifty-nine seconds.
The survivor’s life depended on this brief span of less than a minute.
I closed my eyes and steadied my breathing.
Then I drew up every last bit of my internal energy, which was already nearly depleted.
*Fwoooooosh!*
Qi Sense.
The Scorching Yang Qi extending from my entire body raced across the rippling water.
It swept through more than a hundred corpses whose souls had already departed and the countless pieces of wreckage, searching every inch.
And finally—
I saw it.
No—I felt it.
Dozens of zhang away, a faint presence was sinking farther beneath the surface with every passing moment.
I opened my eyes halfway.
**System Time Limit:** 32 seconds
The Scorching Yang Qi circulating through my body rushed toward my lower half.
When I stepped on empty air with the tips of my toes, the compressed air exploded outward, and a cold wind swept across my entire body.
*Boom!
Fwoooooosh!*
I shot forward like a meteor.
The wind split apart, and space vanished.
The scenery flashed past on either side, but my gaze remained fixed on a single point.
The rough, surging black water.
There was a survivor in there.
*Damn it.
I can’t even swim.*
The thought had barely crossed my mind when the waters of Dongting Lake slammed into my entire body.
*Splash!
Gurgle!*
The impact knocked the breath out of me.
If I had not learned martial arts, my bones would have broken and my internal organs would have been badly jarred.
I sank beneath the surface, trailing a cloud of bubbles.
A school of fish scattered in alarm at the sudden arrival of an unwelcome visitor, revealing two figures slowly sinking into the depths.
**System Time Limit:** 20 seconds
*More.
More.
More...*
I summoned every last ounce of strength and pushed forward.
Grabbing the wrists of the two unconscious, limp figures, I surged upward with all my might.
Ten seconds.
Nine, eight...
The faint moonlight reflected on the surface drew closer.
My arms and legs felt as heavy as if iron balls had been tied to them, while the two people in my hands weighed like thousand-catty boulders.
And then—
*Splash!*
“Puaaah!”
I expelled the breath I had been holding.
Air cold enough to sting flowed deep into my lungs.
But pulling the survivors out of the water did not mean everything was over.
**System Time Limit:** 3 seconds
In that moment, I instinctively realized what I had to do.
*Save them.*
That single thought moved my body, which had briefly gone still.
I thrust both palms, infused with what little internal energy I had left, toward the two people.
*Boom!*
Their bodies jerked, and water splashed.
But the survivors showed no response.
Instead, the number on the System window floating in the air changed.
**System Time Limit:** 2 seconds
*One more time...*
*Boom!*
**System Time Limit:** 1 second
Everything slowed down.
That paltry digit, 1, seemed larger and heavier than ever, crushing me beneath its weight.
I stared blankly at the System window, eyes wide, when—
“Puh.”
“Cough, cough.”
The survivors finally began breathing again.
At the same moment, the System window froze just as it was about to change to its final number.
Then a bell rang out like a celebratory salute.
*Ding.*
**System You succeeded in **Rescuing Lives**! - You completed the unexpected Quest **The Tragedy of Dongting Lake**! - You have successfully completed the Quest.
An appropriate Reward will be granted! - You acquired a considerable amount of EXP and Fame! - You acquired the Title **Water Rescue Worker**!
As the notifications rang in my ears, I muttered,
“Fuuuck.”
Joy and relief at having finally succeeded were secondary.
Worn down by the forced march that had begun at the Zhuge Clan, my body felt unbearably heavy.
Maybe it was because the tension I’d barely managed to hold suddenly let go.
*...Damn it.
It’ll take forever to get back to land.*
At this rate, would I end up needing to be rescued too?
I was floating there with the two survivors, buoyed by the water, when—
*Whoooooosh!*
Something sliced through the water in the distance as fast as a jet ski and stopped right in front of me.
A pure-white body and scales, along with two horns.
“A water snake...?
No, a Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake?”
*Hiss.
Hiss.
Hiss-hiss!*
*No, don’t go!*
I hurriedly shouted at the creature as it flicked its tongue and turned away.
“Hey!
Hey!
Water snake!
Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake!”
*Hiss!*
“You little bastard, did you just spit at me—wait.”
Was this its way of showing that it was sulking?
One thought suddenly came to mind, and I opened my mouth in an earnest yet cautious voice.
“Mimi...
Mimi-chan?”
*Hiss-rik!
Hiss-ririk!*
Only then did the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake—or rather, Mimi-chan—nod in satisfaction and extend its tail toward me as if telling me to grab on.
Right on cue, someone shouted from far away.
“Mimi!
Rescue Benefactor!”
*Hiss-rik!*
Yeah, fuck it.
I didn’t care what the move was called.
Just get me out of here.
I sat on a damp rock and stared at the rippling water.
Two people.
Only two.
Of the countless people who had buried their bones in Dongting Lake today, the two I had saved were the only survivors.
*...Only two out of all those people.*
I had suspected it from the moment the Quest was completed, but reality was even more brutal and merciless than I had imagined.
And the countless deaths left behind by today’s tragedy had given rise to even greater sorrow.
“Sniff, sob!”
“Oh, poor Chil-Sam’s father!”
“What kind of monstrous bastard could have done this?”

A Confucian scholar lamented, unable to continue speaking.
Behind a government soldier clutching a fallen comrade’s corpse and weeping came the wails of a woman with an infant strapped to her back.
An old man, the veins standing out on his neck, even swung his long-stemmed tobacco pipe at some unseen culprit.
There was no longer any laughter or singing to be found at Dongting Lake, one of the most famous scenic sites under heaven.
Only the sorrow and lamentation of those left behind remained, along with the anger carried in all those emotions.

The waters of Dongting Lake had grown calm, as if nothing had happened, while the faint dawn mist spreading across the lake created a beautiful scene.

chapters.title: Chapter 459
paragraphs: A flower’s natural beauty does not fade merely because it has been drenched in water.
The same was true of Honglan. She looked haggard after everything she had endured, yet even so, she was as lovely as a hydrangea blossom.
“It is an honor to see you, Benefactor.”
At that moment, I finally understood what people meant when they described a voice as sounding like rolling jade beads.
Her face, bare of makeup, was dazzlingly fair, and beneath her long lashes shone two eyes like morning stars.
“Good heavens.”
“How can anyone be this beautiful...?”
Exclamations rose from every direction.
Those admiring Honglan’s beauty hurriedly closed their mouths and left when they noticed my gaze.
Perhaps they were ashamed of behaving that way while hundreds of people had been drowned.
Then again, it also showed just how extraordinary Honglan’s beauty was—that it could make them forget everything that had happened.
*If we weren’t in a situation like this, I wouldn’t have been any different.*
I composed myself and spoke.
“I’m glad you regained consciousness. How are you feeling?”
Honglan lowered her head slightly before answering.
“Although I cannot compare to my Benefactor, this lowly woman has also trained in martial arts. I do not seem to have much trouble moving.”
From what I had sensed, her martial arts barely qualified as First Rate.

She might not have been skilled enough to be called a seasoned First Rate master, but a martial artist who had strengthened her body and cultivated internal energy possessed far greater vitality than any ordinary civilian.
*Thank heavens.*
Honglan’s being a martial artist had been a stroke of incredible luck, both for her and for the other survivor we had rescued with her.
I asked the military officer who was still standing nearby,
“Where is Ju Wongong?”
Ju Wongong. A carefree distant relative of the imperial family who had taken a pleasure boat out onto Dongting Lake despite the troubled mood of the times.
He was the other survivor.

“If you mean Young Master Ju, we placed him under heavy guard and moved him somewhere safe. According to the physician, he is out of immediate danger, but no one can say when he will regain consciousness.”
He was the same military officer who had been directing everyone when we first arrived at Dongting Lake.
Responsible for the security and defense of Dongting Lake, one of the major areas of Hubei Province, he continued with a rigid expression.

“When we reported what happened, the City Lord was furious. Though the attempt failed, trying to assassinate a member of the imperial family is among the gravest of crimes. We will immediately mobilize the entire fleet and every soldier in the city to make an example of these insolent rebels—”
“Assassinating a member of the imperial family wasn’t their objective.”
“What?”
I stared at the confused officer and continued.
“They’re called Dark Heaven. You may have heard of them.”
“Dark Heaven...? Aren’t they a gang of thugs that has been causing trouble in the martial world recently?”
“A gang of thugs?”
A scoff escaped me at his choice of words.
Dark Heaven’s name had begun spreading among ordinary people after the Shaolin Bloodshed, but the officer before me had no idea how powerful or terrifying they truly were.
Gung Gibang, standing beside me, spoke with an incredulous expression.
“Officer, did you know that this ‘gang of thugs’ killed Master Hong Dao, the Abbot of Shaolin Temple and the Dharma King?”
“Th-that...”

“The Poison King, Great Hero Tang Sadok, the Grand Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan, was killed too. So was the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun of Emei Sect. Three Supreme Peak masters of the previous generation who once shook the martial world, along with more than two thousand martial artists, are dead. And you call them a gang of thugs?”
“I-I heard those rumors, but I did not know the full extent of their power. Then are you saying Dark Heaven was responsible for this?”
“There’s a limit to how ignorant a man can be. Good grief. Even a passing mutt would laugh.”
“That’s enough.”
I raised a hand to stop Gung Gibang, then addressed the officer, whose face had turned red with embarrassment.
“Regardless, my point is that Ju Wongong was not their target.”
“Th-then what makes you think that?”
“If Dark Heaven had wanted Ju Wongong dead, he would already be gone from this world.”

“If they wanted to kill him, they could have done it any way they pleased. He couldn’t have stopped them even if they ambushed him in broad daylight. Why wait until he took a pleasure boat out onto Dongting Lake, then destroy it along with all the other vessels? Why not even confirm whether their target was dead or alive?”
To Dark Heaven, Ju Wongong’s life was like an object in a cloth bundle—something they could take out or put away whenever they pleased.
Besides, there was no particular reason for them to target a distant imperial relative who had committed a crime and been exiled.
If their goal was to create chaos, the Emperor or Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao would have been far more attractive targets.
I spoke firmly.
“Their objective wasn’t to assassinate a member of the imperial family. Ju Wongong was merely one of the fish that happened to get caught in the net they cast.”
“Then what in the world were they after...?”
“We’ll find out once we catch the culprit.”
“What?”
“I mean the culprit who carried this out directly. Dark Heaven being behind everything is already a foregone conclusion.”
The officer had been staring blankly with his mouth open. Now he hurriedly asked,
“G-Great Hero, are you saying you know who the culprit is?”
“There is someone I suspect, but testimony from someone who saw it happen firsthand would be more reliable.”
I turned my head and looked at Honglan.
With Ju Wongong hovering between life and death, she was the only witness who held the key to unraveling everything.
“Did you see the culprit?”
The question was brief, but it was enough. With everyone’s eyes fixed on her, Honglan’s red lips slowly parted.
“Yes.”
Shock and agitation spread through the room in an instant. Amid the commotion, I clenched my fist tightly.
*Finally.*
The string of incidents that had begun with the Sea Serpent Society. The bastard—or bastards—behind them had never shown so much as a hair.
Now they were finally beginning to reveal themselves.
I couldn’t let go of this tail now that I had found it. I had to seize it with all my strength, drag the body out after it, and finish the job.
Remembering the countless corpses they had left behind, I asked again.
“Tell us exactly what you saw.”
“It was...”
A shallow furrow appeared on Honglan’s smooth, unlined brow.
She seemed to be recalling what had happened. After hesitating for a moment and steadying her breathing, she began to speak.
“Everything happened in an instant. The festivities were in full swing when the two military vessels nearby sank one after the other, only moments apart. That was how it began.”
I listened closely to Honglan’s story.

Ju Wongong might have been a distant relative, but he was still a member of the imperial family. The two military ships assigned to escort him had been overwhelmed by a sudden ambush, and the pleasure boat, where the festivities had been reaching their peak, had fallen into chaos as well.

“But no one could stop it. Nothing was visible, yet the ship suddenly tilted with a tremendous roar. Then a single streak of Force flew in from somewhere and swept through the vessel. That was all it took.”
“Force...!”
“I am certain. That single attack killed most of the Peak masters guarding Young Master Ju and the martial artists of Qingxia Hall.”
The scene seemed to unfold before my eyes.
Nothing was more destructive than Force. Even someone who had never seen it before would recognize that dazzling light for what it was the moment they faced it.
The same was true of Honglan, and it must have been an attack that Ju Wongong’s guards and the bumbling martial artists of Qingxia Hall had been powerless to stop.
Perhaps because she was recalling that horrifying moment, Honglan’s voice began to tremble faintly.
“But in the final moment, the guards risked their lives to push Young Master Ju away, and I embraced him before throwing myself into the river.”
Honglan’s quick thinking had saved both her and Ju Wongong.
Most of those who froze in terror were slaughtered soon afterward. Those who were still breathing could not long endure the bitter cold of the night or the injuries they had suffered in the fall.
And then...
Honglan said that, through the black waters of Dongting Lake, she had seen something rapidly receding into the distance.
“It was a person. Just one.”
The tail had finally revealed itself. I bit my lip hard and asked again.
“Are you certain?”
“How could I lie to you, Benefactor? It was only for the briefest moment, but I saw him clearly with my own two eyes.”
Honglan was the sole witness, and she was also a martial artist who had reached the First Rate realm. If she was that certain, it was highly likely to be true.
*That’s right. It was him.*
Just as one man came to mind, the military officer, who had been listening with a dazed expression, abruptly spoke.
“A-are you all out of your minds? No matter how powerful martial artists may be, this is not land. This is Dongting Lake! Dongting Lake is as deep and vast as the open sea!”
“Does anyone here not know that?”
Gung Gibang muttered the words like a sigh, while Hyuk Mujin clicked his tongue.
“And?”

“What do you mean, ‘and’? I have heard plenty about the miraculous abilities of martial artists like you, but this is absurd! Even the water bandits of the Yangtze River Channel League whom I encountered from time to time were never capable of such feats. How could anyone swim so quickly across such a vast expanse of water, much less sink dozens of vessels single-handedly, including the Great Nation’s military vessels—”
“He could. If he is the man I’m thinking of.”
A clear voice rang out. Under everyone’s gaze, Honglan slowly parted her lips.

“He is a master of water arts who can breathe like a fish, swim faster than one, and easily sink dozens of vessels by himself. I do not know how formidable the water bandits you encountered may have been, but here on Dongting Lake, even the Seafaring King himself could not stand against him.”
Honglan’s gaze turned toward the blue-green waters beyond the camp.
Dongting Lake. A scenic site known throughout the land for its long history and beautiful landscapes.
And one old fisherman who had guarded Dongting Lake all his life.
No.
A Supreme Peak master of the previous generation, and a master of water arts who stood shoulder to shoulder with the Seafaring King.
I quietly murmured his alias.
“The Dongting Fisherman.”
The Lower District Sect’s information had been correct. The Dongting Fisherman had not yet left Hubei Province.
He had faked his death and remained here at Dongting Lake, hiding in plain sight while evading everyone’s suspicion and attention.
And at last, I had found Dark Heaven’s tail—the Dongting Fisherman.
*I’ve finally made it this far. You damn old bastard.*
We had already paid far too high a price in lives. Before any more time passed, I had to capture the Dongting Fisherman and uncover every detail of Dark Heaven’s movements and plans.
It was the only way to prevent an even greater tragedy.
That was why Honglan’s next words were like a torch lighting the path ahead.
“Did you know, Benefactor, that the Dongting Fisherman has hidden secret refuges throughout Dongting Lake?”
“Are you saying you might know where they are?”
“I do not know their exact locations, but I know several places where they might be. Once you have finished preparing, please tell me. This humble woman can guide you there herself.”
I clenched my fist tightly. Then I immediately sprang to my feet.
“Let’s go. Right now.”
