Dark Heaven’s name had begun spreading among ordinary people after the Shaolin Bloodshed, but the officer before me had no idea how powerful or terrifying they truly were.
Gung Gibang, standing beside me, spoke with an incredulous expression.
“Officer, did you know that this ‘gang of thugs’ killed Master Hong Dao, the Abbot of Shaolin Temple and the Dharma King?”
“Th-that...”
“The Poison King, Great Hero Tang Sadok, the Grand Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan, was killed too.
So was the Heaven-Shaking Venerable Nun of Emei Sect.
Three Supreme Peak masters of the previous generation who once shook the martial world, along with more than two thousand martial artists, are dead.
And you call them a gang of thugs?”
“I-I heard those rumors, but I did not know the full extent of their power.
Then are you saying Dark Heaven was responsible for this?”
“There’s a limit to how ignorant a man can be.
Good grief.
Even a passing mutt would laugh.”
“That’s enough.”
I raised a hand to stop Gung Gibang, then addressed the officer, whose face had turned red with embarrassment.
“Regardless, my point is that Ju Wongong was not their target.”
“Th-then what makes you think that?”
“If Dark Heaven had wanted Ju Wongong dead, he would already be gone from this world.”
“If they wanted to kill him, they could have done it any way they pleased.
He couldn’t have stopped them even if they ambushed him in broad daylight.
Why wait until he took a pleasure boat out onto Dongting Lake, then destroy it along with all the other vessels?
Why not even confirm whether their target was dead or alive?”
To Dark Heaven, Ju Wongong’s life was like an object in a cloth bundle—something they could take out or put away whenever they pleased.
Besides, there was no particular reason for them to target a distant imperial relative who had committed a crime and been exiled.
If their goal was to create chaos, the Emperor or Prince Shangshan Zhu Bao would have been far more attractive targets.
I spoke firmly.
“Their objective wasn’t to assassinate a member of the imperial family.
Ju Wongong was merely one of the fish that happened to get caught in the net they cast.”
“Then what in the world were they after...?”
“We’ll find out once we catch the culprit.”
“What?”
“I mean the culprit who carried this out directly.
Dark Heaven being behind everything is already a foregone conclusion.”
The officer had been staring blankly with his mouth open.
Now he hurriedly asked,
“G-Great Hero, are you saying you know who the culprit is?”
“There is someone I suspect, but testimony from someone who saw it happen firsthand would be more reliable.”
I turned my head and looked at Honglan.
With Ju Wongong hovering between life and death, she was the only witness who held the key to unraveling everything.
“Did you see the culprit?”
The question was brief, but it was enough.
With everyone’s eyes fixed on her, Honglan’s red lips slowly parted.
“Yes.”
Shock and agitation spread through the room in an instant.
Amid the commotion, I clenched my fist tightly.
*Finally.*
The string of incidents that had begun with the Sea Serpent Society.
The bastard—or bastards—behind them had never shown so much as a hair.
Now they were finally beginning to reveal themselves.
I couldn’t let go of this tail now that I had found it.
I had to seize it with all my strength, drag the body out after it, and finish the job.
Remembering the countless corpses they had left behind, I asked again.
“Tell us exactly what you saw.”
“It was...”
A shallow furrow appeared on Honglan’s smooth, unlined brow.
She seemed to be recalling what had happened.
After hesitating for a moment and steadying her breathing, she began to speak.
“Everything happened in an instant.
The festivities were in full swing when the two military vessels nearby sank one after the other, only moments apart.
That was how it began.”
I listened closely to Honglan’s story.
Ju Wongong might have been a distant relative, but he was still a member of the imperial family.
The two military ships assigned to escort him had been overwhelmed by a sudden ambush, and the pleasure boat, where the festivities had been reaching their peak, had fallen into chaos as well.
“But no one could stop it.
Nothing was visible, yet the ship suddenly tilted with a tremendous roar.
Then a single streak of Force flew in from somewhere and swept through the vessel.
That was all it took.”
“Force...!”
“I am certain.
That single attack killed most of the Peak masters guarding Young Master Ju and the martial artists of Qingxia Hall.”
The scene seemed to unfold before my eyes.
Nothing was more destructive than Force.
Even someone who had never seen it before would recognize that dazzling light for what it was the moment they faced it.
The same was true of Honglan, and it must have been an attack that Ju Wongong’s guards and the bumbling martial artists of Qingxia Hall had been powerless to stop.
Perhaps because she was recalling that horrifying moment, Honglan’s voice began to tremble faintly.
“But in the final moment, the guards risked their lives to push Young Master Ju away, and I embraced him before throwing myself into the river.”
Honglan’s quick thinking had saved both her and Ju Wongong.
Most of those who froze in terror were slaughtered soon afterward.
Those who were still breathing could not long endure the bitter cold of the night or the injuries they had suffered in the fall.
And then...
Honglan said that, through the black waters of Dongting Lake, she had seen something rapidly receding into the distance.
“It was a person.
Just one.”
The tail had finally revealed itself.
I bit my lip hard and asked again.
“Are you certain?”
“How could I lie to you, Benefactor?
It was only for the briefest moment, but I saw him clearly with my own two eyes.”
Honglan was the sole witness, and she was also a martial artist who had reached the First Rate realm.
If she was that certain, it was highly likely to be true.
*That’s right.
It was him.*
Just as one man came to mind, the military officer, who had been listening with a dazed expression, abruptly spoke.
“A-are you all out of your minds?
No matter how powerful martial artists may be, this is not land.
This is Dongting Lake!
Dongting Lake is as deep and vast as the open sea!”
“Does anyone here not know that?”
Gung Gibang muttered the words like a sigh, while Hyuk Mujin clicked his tongue.
“And?”
“What do you mean, ‘and’?
I have heard plenty about the miraculous abilities of martial artists like you, but this is absurd!
Even the water bandits of the Yangtze River Channel League whom I encountered from time to time were never capable of such feats.
How could anyone swim so quickly across such a vast expanse of water, much less sink dozens of vessels single-handedly, including the Great Nation’s military vessels—”
“He could.
If he is the man I’m thinking of.”
A clear voice rang out.
Under everyone’s gaze, Honglan slowly parted her lips.
“He is a master of water arts who can breathe like a fish, swim faster than one, and easily sink dozens of vessels by himself.
I do not know how formidable the water bandits you encountered may have been, but here on Dongting Lake, even the Seafaring King himself could not stand against him.”
Honglan’s gaze turned toward the blue-green waters beyond the camp.
Dongting Lake.
A scenic site known throughout the land for its long history and beautiful landscapes.
And one old fisherman who had guarded Dongting Lake all his life.
No.
A Supreme Peak master of the previous generation, and a master of water arts who stood shoulder to shoulder with the Seafaring King.
I quietly murmured his alias.
“The Dongting Fisherman.”
The Lower District Sect’s information had been correct.
The Dongting Fisherman had not yet left Hubei Province.
He had faked his death and remained here at Dongting Lake, hiding in plain sight while evading everyone’s suspicion and attention.
And at last, I had found Dark Heaven’s tail—the Dongting Fisherman.
*I’ve finally made it this far.
You damn old bastard.*
We had already paid far too high a price in lives.
Before any more time passed, I had to capture the Dongting Fisherman and uncover every detail of Dark Heaven’s movements and plans.
It was the only way to prevent an even greater tragedy.
That was why Honglan’s next words were like a torch lighting the path ahead.
“Did you know, Benefactor, that the Dongting Fisherman has hidden secret refuges throughout Dongting Lake?”
“Are you saying you might know where they are?”
“I do not know their exact locations, but I know several places where they might be.
Once you have finished preparing, please tell me.
This humble woman can guide you there herself.”
I clenched my fist tightly.
Then I immediately sprang to my feet.
“Let’s go.
Right now.”

chapters.title: Chapter 460
paragraphs: The weather was bad in more ways than one.
The waters of Dongting Lake, which had swallowed dozens of vessels and claimed lives overnight, were rough, and the wind blowing in from the distance was violent.
Even the old boatman who knew Dongting Lake like the back of his hand seemed to think that setting out in such weather was a terrible idea.
“I—I can’t do it, sirs.”
Those were the first words from the boatman, who had clearly been dragged here against his will. He continued with an anxious look on his face.
“The places you wish to visit are unusually narrow, with treacherous currents even by Dongting Lake’s standards... In weather like this, it’s simply impossible.”

“That is precisely why we are asking for your help. Merchant ships and military vessels may not be able to enter, but a sturdy ferryboat piloted by the finest boatman on Dongting Lake should manage it.”
“No matter how you put it...”
“Boatman?”
“Y-yes?”
“Please.”
A man was still a man, no matter how old he got.
Dazed by Honglan’s gentle voice and dazzling beauty, the old boatman did not come to his senses until after he had climbed aboard the ferryboat.
“I must be mad. Completely mad. I know what happened last night, yet here I am, about to set out on the water. What will I do if we run into the Hidden Shadow Ghost...?”
*The Hidden Shadow Ghost?*
An unfamiliar name had slipped into his grumbling. I turned and found the terrified boatman staring back at me.
He swallowed hard before answering.

“Just as the name suggests, it’s a ghostly creature. Plenty of boatmen have fallen victim to it lately. One was an old friend of mine. He went out at night hoping to earn a few extra coins, and then...”
The old boatman stared at the rippling waters of Dongting Lake with eyes steeped in fear.

“They call it the Hidden Shadow Ghost because its victims die without ever seeing so much as its shadow. This is only the humble opinion of an old man, but it must be responsible for everything that’s been happening lately. All of it is the work of that evil spirit.”
Gung Gibang clicked his tongue and cut in.

“Evil spirit, my ass. Listen, boatman. Do you think I’ve only heard stories like this once or twice? If all those tales were true, half the fish under heaven would have human faces, and the mountains would be crawling with thousand-year-old white tigers and dragons.”
“I swear there isn’t a word of falsehood in it. With one heaven-defying atrocity after another, the Divine Spirit of Dongting Lake must have been angered.”
“An evil spirit wasn’t enough, so now there’s a divine spirit too? Forget it. Let’s stop talking.”
“But every boatman in Hubei Province has heard the story...”
“Do I look like a boatman to you?”
“N-no, sir. Anyone can see you’re the most beggarly of beggars.”
“Ah, he’s not wrong, but now I’m suddenly pissed off.”
“P-please calm yourself, honored sir. This old man is guilty of nothing more than repeating what he heard.”
The old boatman sounded deeply aggrieved.
He had spent his entire life as a boatman in the Murim, where all sorts of legends and superstitions were treated as fact.
Perhaps that was why he seemed firmly convinced that the recent string of gruesome incidents was the work of the evil spirit known as the Hidden Shadow Ghost.
*Come to think of it, it might not be complete nonsense.*
Judging by Honglan and Cheongpung’s expressions, they had reached the same conclusion.
The moment our eyes met, they both spoke at once.
“Benefactor, could it be...”
“Benefactor, could the Hidden Shadow Ghost that boatman mentioned be...”
“Wait. I know what both of you are trying to say, so you don’t need to say it. And if you absolutely insist on calling me Benefactor, take turns. It’s confusing.”
One Benefactor parrot had already been more than enough. Now there were two.
At times like this, I almost felt like I had become someone important.
Then again, Honglan had good reason after I saved her life. But was Cheongpung seriously planning to treat me as his Benefactor forever just because I had given him a few sweets when he was hungry?
I sighed and continued.
“Anyway, there’s a good chance the Hidden Shadow Ghost is the Dongting Fisherman. If not, it could be bandits taking advantage of the chaos.”
“That’s exactly what I was going to say, Benefactor.”
Not to be outdone by Cheongpung, Honglan nodded as well.
“This humble woman thinks so too, Benefactor.”
“I said one person at a time.”
Whatever the case, it was unlikely to have been a simple accident of nature.
From what we had heard, more than a few boatmen had died. The old boatman’s next words lent even more weight to our suspicions.
“Come to think of it, all the dead boatmen disappeared in roughly the same area. Hm? Wait a moment. The place you honored guests are heading toward is nearby too...”
The old boatman suddenly froze and slowly raised his head.
He looked us over one by one without a word, then quietly lowered the oar he had been holding to set off and stood up.
“Where are you going?”
At my question, the old boatman gave an awkward smile.
“Well, I seem to have forgotten to relieve myself.”
“Mujin.”
“Yes, Captain.”
“The boatman needs to pee.”
“Does he?”
By now, Hyuk Mujin and I understood each other without needing to say much.
When Mujin—practically a giant beside the old boatman—blocked his path, the boatman’s eyes grew moist like those of a calf being led to the slaughterhouse.
“Do you still need to go?”
At Hyuk Mujin’s low voice, the boatman shook his head.
“...Come to think of it, I don’t.”
“Good. We’ll let you go before whatever you fear comes to pass, so don’t worry too much.”
I felt bad for treating an old boatman this way, but an experienced guide was essential if we wanted to reach the Dongting Fisherman’s refuge.
Our destination lay along a narrow passage that could accommodate only a few ferryboats at a time.
Even if the government mobilized a fleet of a hundred ships and tens of thousands of soldiers, they would never be able to enter. They would only become a burden.
*If we end up fighting the Dongting Fisherman, bringing more people will only increase the casualties.*

Our best option was for the government to seal off every route between Dongting Lake and the Yangtze in case he tried to flee, while a small elite force—including Cheongpung and me—pursued and either captured or killed him.
And just as important as dealing with the Dongting Fisherman was preventing any more pointless sacrifices.
Having finished thinking it through, I abruptly spoke.
“Hyuk Mujin, Gung Gibang, Young Lady Hong. You three...”
“No.”
“Where’s that dog barking?”
“I will contribute what little strength I have.”
Their answers came before I could finish, leaving me momentarily speechless. Hyuk Mujin and Gung Gibang clicked their tongues at the sight.
“It’s obvious. Completely obvious.”
“I can see exactly what you’re about to say.”
“We came all this way. How could we turn back now? What kind of man would that make me?”
“I feel the same. The Successor Beggar of the mighty Beggars’ Sect cannot be frightened off by something like this.”
“Captain, whenever something looks even slightly dangerous, you always tell us to stay behind. At this point, it’s practically your defining trait. Captain’s special.”
“You’re surprisingly timid.”
“But why have you been copying everything I say, Young Hero Gung? It’s really starting to bother me.”
“You damned bastard. Why pick a fight when things were going so well? Have you lost your mind?”
“Beggars’ Sect special. Not content with picking up discarded food from inns, you pick up other people’s words too.”
“...I’ve never seen such a bastard who’s worse than a dog.”

“Regardless, I’m going with you no matter what you say, Captain. When I was young, a gifted fortune-teller read my fate and told me I would live in wealth and glory, eating well and living comfortably past the age of one hundred. There’s no way I’m dying today.”
Gung Gibang stared incredulously at Hyuk Mujin as he made this bold declaration, then shook his head.

“Forget it. I shouldn’t have said anything. And I agree with that Hyuk bastard, so don’t even think about leaving me behind. I have inherited the supreme arts of the Beggars’ Sect. Even if I’m not as strong as you or Cheongpung, protecting my own life will be no trouble.”
My lips moved, but I could not bring myself to speak.
When it came down to it, neither of them was someone others could afford to underestimate.

Hyuk Mujin had begun learning martial arts relatively late, yet he had grown explosively while passing through countless crises alongside me. Gung Gibang was talented enough to become the Successor Beggar, as well as a Peak master who had entered a mature realm.
*But I’m afraid.*
I was afraid of losing people close to me. Afraid that what happened that day would happen all over again.
As I hesitated, Cheongpung suddenly spoke.
“Benefactor. If you go, I can follow you to the very depths of hell.”
“Young Hero Cheongpung.”
“Please don’t tell me I can’t. I am a proper man and a martial artist too.”
“Young Hero Cheongpung.”
Cheongpung smiled faintly and shook his head.
“Benefactor, please don’t say anything. All you need to do is trust us as much as I trust you.”
“No, that isn’t what I meant. You’re obviously coming with us, so why did you step forward and...”
“Oh. Ah...”
“Stop saying pointless things and sit down. Don’t ruin the mood.”
“...Yes, Benefactor.”
A quiet laugh escaped me at his crestfallen expression. I nodded to Hyuk Mujin and Gung Gibang.
“Remember one thing. No matter what happens, follow my judgment. Even if I order you to abandon me and run.”
“Captain, that...”
Gung Gibang discreetly jabbed Hyuk Mujin in the side.
“Of course. We’ll remember. The Hyuk bastard will too. Right?”
“Hm? Ah, yes.”
Their intentions were obvious, but I pretended not to notice.
I would do everything in my power to prevent that situation from arising. I was confident I could separate them before they fell into danger.
But the last person posed a problem.
“You already know what I’m going to say, don’t you?”
Honglan’s red lips slowly parted.
“You will need someone who knows the exact route.”
“We’ll be fine. According to you, Young Lady Hong, the finest boatman on Dongting Lake is already with us.”
“What if something unexpected happens?”
“We’ll deal with it.”
“I may be insignificant compared to you and the others, but I too have reached the First Rate realm...”
“I know. And I also know that this First Rate master spent several shichen submerged in the river while holding on to a strong man, and has only been conscious for half a shichen.”
Honglan bit down softly on her lip, struck where it hurt.
She knew better than anyone.
Being able to move around as she did now and fighting a fierce battle were two entirely different things.
“Once again, it seems all I can do is watch.”
“Once again?”
“Yes. Back then, long ago. Last night. And now.”
Reading the question in my eyes, Honglan smiled. It was more bitter than any smile I had seen from her before.
“A great many things happened before a little girl who lost her clan and her parents overnight could become the woman she is today...”
“Ah.”
“Please excuse me for a moment.”
She looked up at me with shining eyes and quietly reached out a hand.
Her pale, slender fingers brushed through my tangled hair and grazed my neck. I flinched despite myself.
“Young Lady Hong, what are you...”
“All done. Ah, much better. Would you like to see?”
I followed Honglan’s fingers with my gaze and looked down at the clear waters of Dongting Lake.
Someone’s reflection floated on the surface.
My hair had been neatly arranged and secured with a beautiful silver hairpin.
When I raised my head, Honglan was smiling brightly.
“Benefactor—no, Great Hero Jin.”
Her hair, now unbound, swayed gently in the wind. It rippled and shimmered until it seemed almost radiant.
“I wish you good fortune in battle.”
Her quiet voice slowly faded from my ears.
Leaving Honglan behind, the boatman drove his oar powerfully through the water.

Gung Gibang discreetly jabbed Hyuk Mujin in the side.
“Of course.
We’ll remember.
The Hyuk bastard will too.
Right?”
“Hm?
Ah, yes.”
Their intentions were obvious, but I pretended not to notice.
I would do everything in my power to prevent that situation from arising.
I was confident I could separate them before they fell into danger.
But the last person posed a problem.
“You already know what I’m going to say, don’t you?”
Honglan’s red lips slowly parted.
“You will need someone who knows the exact route.”
“We’ll be fine.
According to you, Young Lady Hong, the finest boatman on Dongting Lake is already with us.”
“What if something unexpected happens?”
“We’ll deal with it.”
“I may be insignificant compared to you and the others, but I too have reached the First Rate realm...”
“I know.
And I also know that this First Rate master spent several shichen submerged in the river while holding on to a strong man, and has only been conscious for half a shichen.”
Honglan bit down softly on her lip, struck where it hurt.
She knew better than anyone.
Being able to move around as she did now and fighting a fierce battle were two entirely different things.
“Once again, it seems all I can do is watch.”
“Once again?”
“Yes.
Back then, long ago.
Last night.
And now.”
Reading the question in my eyes, Honglan smiled.
It was more bitter than any smile I had seen from her before.
“A great many things happened before a little girl who lost her clan and her parents overnight could become the woman she is today...”
“Ah.”
“Please excuse me for a moment.”
She looked up at me with shining eyes and quietly reached out a hand.
Her pale, slender fingers brushed through my tangled hair and grazed my neck.
I flinched despite myself.
“Young Lady Hong, what are you...”
“All done.
Ah, much better.
Would you like to see?”
I followed Honglan’s fingers with my gaze and looked down at the clear waters of Dongting Lake.
Someone’s reflection floated on the surface.
My hair had been neatly arranged and secured with a beautiful silver hairpin.
When I raised my head, Honglan was smiling brightly.
“Benefactor—no, Great Hero Jin.”
Her hair, now unbound, swayed gently in the wind.
It rippled and shimmered until it seemed almost radiant.
“I wish you good fortune in battle.”
Her quiet voice slowly faded from my ears.
Leaving Honglan behind, the boatman drove his oar powerfully through the water.

chapters.title: Chapter 461
paragraphs: When it came to speed, a ferryboat couldn’t match the Yangtze River Channel League’s swift ships—or even an ordinary vessel. Especially in weather as foul as today’s.
*Hoooooosh! Splash!*
The ferryboat rocked in the fierce wind and churning current.
Its small hull offered little resistance to the elements. Veins bulged along the arms of the old boatman gripping the oars.

As befitted an experienced boatman, he had guided the ferryboat skillfully despite the bad weather. But the closer we came to our destination, the more violent the current grew, and he was nearing his limit.
*This is probably as far as he can take us.*
It would have been insane to come this far relying on nothing but a single ferryboat and an old boatman.
I rolled my neck from side to side and stepped forward.
“Shall we begin?”
At those words, three people opened their eyes. They had been circulating their qi without moving an inch despite the rocking hull.
“I’m ready, Benefactor.”
“To use one of the Beggars’ Sect’s finest arts for something like this... Master would certainly have a thing or two to say if he saw me.”
“Captain, what should I do?”
Cheongpung, Gung Gibang, and Hyuk Mujin had replenished their qi. I quickly gave them their orders.
“Cheongpung, follow me to the stern. Gung Gibang, take the bow. Mujin, protect the boatman. I’ll call when I need you, so move the instant I do.”
As the three took their positions, the old boatman, who had been struggling at the oars, blinked.
“E-excuse me, what exactly are you talking about...?”
Before he could finish, a fierce blast of palm force shot from Cheongpung’s hands and slammed into the water.
*Boom! Fwoooooosh!*
“Waaaaaagh!”
The so-called palm-force booster.
The ferryboat was far smaller and lighter than even the sleek-hulled swift ships. It soared through the air.
The boatman’s scream mingled with the wind tearing past us.
Using that scream as my signal, I stepped forward.
*Now.*
*Whoooosh!*
Just as the airborne ferryboat was about to drop back onto the water, I drew up the internal energy filling my dantian and sent it surging into my palms.
*Boom! Booooom!*
My Flame Divine Palm had now reached eighty percent mastery. Its heat made the surrounding air blaze, and the descending ferryboat leaped upward again like a flying fish.
The boatman’s eyes bulged. He pointed ahead with a trembling finger.
“Reefs! There are reeeefs ahead!”
Did anyone really think the Dongting Fisherman would establish one of his secret refuges somewhere easy to reach?

The route we were taking was too narrow for ordinary vessels to enter. The current was also unusually strong, making it difficult for a light boat like a ferryboat to escape once it was caught in the flow.
Once the current swept a boat away, it would be easy for it to crash against one of the reefs scattered throughout the passage.
“You fucking bastards! I told you I wasn’t coming!”
The old boatman’s heartfelt scream rang out. At that exact moment, I shouted a name.
“Gung Gibang!”
“Got it!”
Gung Gibang answered energetically and flung his sleeves, which were little more than rags.
The Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms—said to be passed down to only two people among the Beggars’ Sect’s hundred thousand disciples, the Sect Leader and the Successor Beggar—erupted through the air.
*Kwoooooo-boooom!*
Palm force poured down like a rainstorm, shattering the reef that towered like an iron wall into countless fragments.
The second and third reefs that appeared beyond it could not withstand the might of the Eighteen Dragon-Subduing Palms either.
*Kraaaaaash!*
The ferryboat broke through the scattered fragments of reef and landed on the surface.
Spray surged up on both sides of the hull, and several fish that had leaped from somewhere slapped the old boatman across the cheeks.
“Gah... Uhhh...”
He was completely out of it.
I shook the drooling boatman by the shoulder. His eyes had gone half vacant.
“Wake up. Stay with us.”
“Ugh... Uhhh. You fucking...”
“This isn’t working. Mujin.”
“By your command.”
Hyuk Mujin rolled up both sleeves and planted a solid slap across the boatman’s face.
*Smack!*
The boatman’s eyes snapped back into focus.
“Gah! What was that—”
*Smack!*
“...I-I’m already awake.”
“Stop.”
“Yes, sir.”
Nothing brought someone to their senses like a good slap across the face.
I turned to the boatman as he rubbed his reddened cheeks.
“Where do you think we are?”
“No matter how honored you gentlemen may be, treating a man like this is—”
“Mujin.”
“By your command.”
“I’ll check immediately, sir.”
The boatman sprang to his feet and looked around.
The channel was barely wide enough for two or three ferryboats to pass side by side.
Sheer cliffs loomed on either bank, and violent currents churned across the water. Thick fog hung over everything.
The old boatman narrowed his eyes and carefully examined the area before nodding.
“Yes. This is the first of the places you mentioned.”
According to the Lower District Sect’s information Honglan had relayed to us, there were five likely locations for the Dongting Fisherman’s secret refuge.
We had reached the closest of them.
That was certainly good news, but it was too early to celebrate.
“Getting here quickly is all well and good, but... how are we supposed to find it now?”
At Gung Gibang’s question, I scanned our surroundings.
“I don’t know. The information Young Lady Hong gave us wasn’t exact, either. We’ll have to search the area thoroughly.”
“Ugh. This is going to take forever.”
“Don’t jinx us. Just be grateful Young Lady Hong’s information got us this far.”
A secret refuge wasn’t called a secret refuge for nothing.
Honglan’s information had not included its exact location, but merely narrowing down the Dongting Fisherman’s hidden retreat to this area was already a major gain.
Even if the first location turned out to be a dead end, something would eventually be caught once we drew the net tight enough.
*Unless it jumps out on its own before we catch it.*
As I carefully surveyed the area, my face suddenly began to prickle.
I glanced aside. Four pairs of eyes had been staring at me strangely, but they immediately darted away.
“What?”
“W-what do you mean? I was just... thinking it was nice that you were still thinking about Young Lady Hong in the middle of all this.”
“Ahem. Captain, you have my full support.”
“Ah, youth is a fine thing. I was popular with the ladies myself until about thirty years ago. They used to call me the Fisher of Women’s Hearts on Dongting Lake. Hahaha.”
It was obvious what they were all thinking.
I was inwardly clicking my tongue when my eyes happened to meet Cheongpung’s. He flinched like a bird that had been shot and frantically waved both hands.
“No! No, Benefactor! I wasn’t thinking about anything!”
“What on earth were you thinking about? I haven’t even said anything yet.”

“Really, I wasn’t! I swear I wasn’t imagining Young Lady Hong and Benefactor falling passionately in love, getting married, having two children, and living happily ever after! Or imagining myself living next door and visiting Benefactor all the time!”
“Gasp!”
Only then did Cheongpung realize his mistake. He clapped both hands over his mouth, but it was already too late.
*He imagined all that in the space of a few seconds?*
At that rate, he could quit being a martial artist and become a novelist.
His pen name could be Huashan Divine Dragon. If he published under Huashan’s name and got Sword Saint Mae Jonghak to write a blurb, his books would sell like crazy.
Of course, if he made me the protagonist, he would get the shit beaten out of him just as quickly.
“Good grief. What is wrong with you people...? Never mind. Forget it.”
There was no point wasting my breath. I sighed and quickly issued new orders.
It wasn’t because my face had somehow grown hot, or because the faint scent clinging to Honglan’s silver hairpin kept tickling my nose.
*...Really.*

“Cheongpung and Gung Gibang, use the Wall Lizard Technique to search the cliffs. Mujin, take the boat around and search below. We don’t know what might appear or when, so don’t let your guard down for a single moment.”
At my serious tone, the faint smiles vanished from everyone’s lips.
If the Dongting Fisherman really was here, a fight would be unavoidable.

I did not know exactly how powerful he was, but if a Supreme Peak master of the Dongting Fisherman’s caliber launched a surprise attack, Cheongpung and I were probably the only ones who could properly respond.
“Remember this. If you let your guard down, you die.”
Of course, we would do everything in our power to prevent that from happening. But in the world of martial artists, life and death could be decided in an instant.
Everyone nodded gravely. I was about to turn away when Hyuk Mujin suddenly spoke.
“What are you doing?”
“We’re searching together. Did you think I was going to sit around and have fun by myself?”
“No, that isn’t what I meant. Weren’t you planning to remain on the ferryboat?”
“Cheongpung and Gung Gibang have the cliffs covered, and you’ll be searching below, so I need to look somewhere else.”
“Somewhere else? Where else is there to...”
Hyuk Mujin stopped mid-sentence.
“Don’t tell me...”
“That’s right.”
I looked down at the churning river.
“We have to search underwater too. If it were anyone else, I might not consider it, but this is the Dongting Fisherman’s refuge. It’s a perfectly reasonable possibility.”
“But you’ve never learned water arts, have you?”
“Hmm. Probably not.”

At my confident answer, Cheongpung and Gung Gibang—who had been about to climb the cliffs with the Wall Lizard Technique—each added a warning. Even the old boatman, holding his oar aloft like a weapon, joined in.
“Benefactor, my grandfather once told me that you must never fight a master of water arts underwater.”
“I agree. You haven’t learned water arts, so you couldn’t possibly search this entire stretch by yourself. And if your opponent is the Dongting Fisherman, you should avoid it all the more.”
“I know you are an exceptional martial artist, honored sir, but the water here is deep and the current is fierce. One wrong move, and you could truly be in grave danger.”
I couldn’t find a single flaw in any of their arguments.
A battle between Supreme Peak masters could be decided by the smallest detail.
And the difference between fighting on land and fighting underwater was as vast as the difference between heaven and earth.
*The martial arts I’ve learned are particularly vulnerable underwater too.*
Most of the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts were based on Scorching Yang Qi—in other words, fire qi.
By their very nature, they could not display the same power underwater as they could on land.
That was also why Jeok Cheongang hated the Yangtze so much. He knew that if a life-and-death duel broke out there, he would be fighting at a disadvantage.
*Hmm. I take that back. Thinking about it again, he probably just hated water itself.*
Regardless, it would not have been particularly surprising if the Dongting Fisherman had established a secret refuge underwater, away from other people’s eyes and footsteps.
He was a master of water arts who could breathe like a fish and move even faster than one.
But I hadn’t volunteered without a plan.
My entire swimming career consisted of a children’s swimming class I had taken when I was seven. There was another reason I had decided to enter those deep, raging waters.
*I’ve never used it before, but... if the description is accurate, this should be more than possible.*
I exhaled briefly and removed my shirt and shoes.
Before Hyuk Mujin could recover from his surprise and stop me, I leaped straight into the river.
*Splash! Whoooooosh!*
The water was as cold as ice, yet crystal clear.
Schools of brightly colored fish swam together. Far below, unidentifiable aquatic plants swayed in the depths.
And then... at last, the sound I had been waiting for rang out.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*

**System The **Water Rescue Worker** Title’s effect has activated! - The special Skill embedded in the Title has been applied! Water Rescue Worker’s Webbing** has been generated! Water Rescue Worker’s Gills** have been generated! - The special Skill will remain active for 24 hours and cannot be used again for one week! - The martial arts you have learned are incompatible with the surrounding environment. The power of **Fire Gate Clan** martial arts is reduced by 20 percent underwater!
As the System notifications appeared, my body began to change.
*Shhhhhhh.*
A faint light visible only to me swept over my entire body. Transparent webbing formed between my fingers and toes.
*This is...*
Even underwater, I felt as light and mobile as I did on land.
My vision grew even clearer. When I exhaled the breath I had been holding, the cold water turned into air and rushed into my lungs.
*This works even better than I expected.*
I had never imagined the **Water Rescue Worker** Title I’d earned by completing the sudden Quest *The Tragedy of Dongting Lake* would prove useful so soon.
*This should be more than enough.*
Grinning, I began to swim smoothly.
My transparent webbing sliced through the fierce current, propelling me into the distance faster than a fish.

chapters.title: Chapter 462
paragraphs: The old boatman could not believe what was happening before his eyes.
*What in the world is going on?*
He had worked as a boatman for nearly forty years, ever since he was around twenty, but in all that time, he had never experienced anything as bizarre as this.
*Tap-tap-tap-tap!*
Two figures raced across the sheer cliff above him. It was not the first time he had seen them today, but the sight amazed him every time.
The boatman stared upward, his mouth hanging open.
*Are those apes or people?*
He had encountered countless martial artists during his years as a boatman, but this was the first time he had ever witnessed such astonishing martial arts firsthand.
Most of the martial artists who used his ferryboat were wandering martial artists with mediocre skills and shallow pockets, or disciples of small and middling sects.
*I had my suspicions when the government troops suddenly showed up and ordered me to follow them...*
He had seen it clearly: Officer Gwak, who was in charge of Dongting Lake, had been visibly flustered as he addressed these people with honorifics.
Considering how arrogant the man usually was, there was no doubt that today’s passengers were important figures who carried considerable weight even in the Murim.
*If this goes well, I might make a tidy sum.*

He had been considering retirement lately. Whenever he heard about the nonstop tragedies of the past month, unease had settled in one corner of his heart, and his old bones had begun aching more than usual.
He had nearly made up his mind after hearing that hundreds of people had been slaughtered en masse on Dongting Lake the previous night.
*The spirit of Dongting Lake must have grown enraged. The heavenly patterns are ominous, so evil spirits like the Hidden Shadow Ghost are running wild.*
Boatmen were famous for believing in all sorts of superstitions, and old men were prone to retelling legends as though they were facts.
It was only natural that a man who had spent his entire life as a boatman—and had grown old doing it—would decide to retire.
But if important people were calling for him, what choice did he have? When they had dragged him away like a criminal and ordered him to launch the ferryboat, he had been prepared to die.
*Tap-tap-tap-tap!*
But seeing those figures filled him with hope.
Hope that he could survive, of course, but also that he might make enough money to retire in comfort.
*They must possess incredible martial arts!*
They said martial masters of the highest realms could fold the earth beneath their feet and walk through the air.
What those people were doing was not much different from the rumors the old boatman had heard secondhand.
Even the young man who seemed to be their leader was cutting through the rough water as though he were a fish.
*No, that’s not right. This is already the fourth location. He isn’t like a fish—he is a fish.*
What kind of human being had webbed feet and gills? Whenever that young man entered the water, he stayed under for at least a full shichen.
He had already repeated that impossible feat three times. If anyone deserved to be called a martial master, it was him.
*Masters like these could deal with some miscellaneous Fiend like the Hidden Shadow Ghost in an instant.*
If he could only make it out alive, retiring with a fortune would be easy.
Just as the old boatman was brimming with hope, a shout rang out from the cliff above.
“Young Hero Cheongpung! Is there anything over there?”
“I’ll tell you when I see something!”
“If you find anything, tell us right away!”
“Yes, I certainly will... Ah!”
“Gasp! What is it? What happened?”
A heavy tension abruptly settled over the area.
Hyuk Mujin, who was scanning the surroundings from the slowly moving ferryboat, swallowed hard. So did Gung Gibang, whose eyes were gleaming sharply from the opposite cliff.
Then, under everyone’s gaze, Cheongpung shouted,
“Wow, it’s a swallow’s nest! I’ve never seen one this big before!”
The air froze solid.
The boatman suddenly thought,
*...Spirit of Dongting Lake, please protect this old man.*
At this rate, he was about to lose what little faith he had left in them.
While the old boatman prayed to the spirit without anyone knowing, it happened.
*Splash! Tap!*
A shadow shot out of the water amid a spray of droplets and landed lightly on the ferryboat.

The figure had a build large enough to be called massive, with flexible muscles that looked as hard as steel. A beautiful silver hairpin that suited him strangely well held his disheveled hair in place.
“Welcome back.”
At Hyuk Mujin’s greeting, Jin Taekyung silently nodded.
Seeing his furrowed brow, the old boatman cautiously asked,
“Nothing this time either?”
It was a pointless question. If he had found something, his expression would not have been so dark.
Jin Taekyung stood deep in thought, his brows drawn together, before finally speaking.
“This is the fourth location, right?”
“Yes, that it is.”
The old boatman answered while carefully watching Taekyung’s mood.
These incredible passengers had already come up empty-handed three times. Including this place, they had now failed to find anything at four locations.
Riding in the same boat as martial masters in a foul mood was hardly pleasant.
The one thing that was both fortunate and unfortunate was that one final location remained.
*Fwoosh. Hissss!*
Jin Taekyung lightly circulated his internal energy, evaporating the water clinging to him, and asked,
“How long will it take to reach the last location?”
“If we continue the way we have been, half an hour should be enough. But...”
The old boatman swallowed before continuing.
“The wind and current are growing stronger the farther we go. It’ll be getting dark by the time we arrive, so perhaps it would be better to try another day.”
“No. It has to be today.”
“We have to go. Right now.”
His tone was as sharp and decisive as a knife stroke. The old boatman closed his mouth.
For some reason, the weather was ominously foul today. The sky, which should have been clear, was choked with dark clouds, while the fierce wind and current showed no sign of settling down.
*I’ve got a bad feeling about this.*
The foreboding he had felt only in the past, when floods or storms were bearing down on them, pricked at every inch of the veteran boatman’s body.
But he forced himself to ignore the unease seeping into his chest.
*Have I grown timid with age? No, that can’t be it.*
A sudden flood or storm? It made no sense.
Boatmen like him were more sensitive to changes in the river than anyone.
The current had certainly grown unusually rough over the past month, but it was not the rainy season. A disaster of that scale was impossible.
The boatman was still mulling it over when he realized that a large hand had settled on his shoulder.
“Boatman. Aren’t you going?”
“...I’m going.”
At Hyuk Mujin’s weighty voice, the boatman slowly began turning the ferryboat.
Of course, he did not forget to curse inwardly at the rude fellow who looked like the weakest of the group.
“Boatman. Were you cursing me just now?”
The boatman’s oar slipped, and the ferryboat rocked.
The rapids had grown even rougher than when they first set out, dragging at the small hull. Jin Taekyung stepped forward and swept both palms outward.
*Boom!*
The ferryboat regained its balance and surged ahead.
As Taekyung gazed at the gradually darkening sky, his eyes grew somber.
*Did we get it wrong?*
The information Honglan had passed on from the Lower District Sect pointed to five locations in total.
But even after searching thoroughly above and below the water, they had found no trace of the Dongting Fisherman’s secret refuge.
After coming up empty-handed one place after another, it was only natural to wonder whether the information had been wrong from the beginning.
Taekyung thought for a moment, then shook his head.
*No. It’s too early to decide that.*
One final place remained. Of the five locations suspected of concealing the Dongting Fisherman’s secret refuge, it was the deepest and most treacherous.
It might even have been more important than the other four combined.
If it really was the Dongting Fisherman’s refuge—and if they encountered him there...
*It’ll be a life-and-death duel. We’ll have to fight with our lives on the line.*
Against a Supreme Peak master, giving everything they had was only natural. But if at all possible, they needed to capture him alive.
The true reason they were searching for the Dongting Fisherman was to reach the larger body behind him.
Dark Heaven was like a three-headed, six-armed monster. Killing the Dongting Fisherman would merely cut off one of its arms. Capturing him would give them a chance to strike at its body.
“The body. The body, huh...”
His quiet mutter scattered into the wind.
Without realizing it, Taekyung touched the silver hairpin holding back his hair and suddenly thought of one person.
He also remembered the hundreds of corpses that had filled the clear waters of Dongting Lake, and the wails of those left behind.
“I’m going to catch you, you bastards. No matter what.”
A faint fragrance drifted from the silver hairpin and lingered at the tip of his nose. The bow of the ferryboat cut forcefully through the river as its waters began turning black.
Donghu Stronghold.

The largest water stronghold in Hubei, which had once wielded tremendous influence under the command of the outstanding Supreme Peak master Hwang Chung, the Yangtze One Saber, had been crowded with unfamiliar visitors for the past two days.
“Pull when I count to three. One, two. Heave!”
Some were tying logs together to make a temporary path across the river. Elsewhere, middle-aged men dressed in neat scholar’s robes were writing on bamboo slips.
A young Daoist in a robe approached one of them and asked,
“Excuse me, sir. Has the search of the left cliff already been completed?”
“About half of it. I can stake our family name on the fact that we haven’t found any trace of a Formation so far. How is Wudang doing?”
“The search is progressing smoothly. We are also maintaining a strict watch in case anything unexpected happens, so you need not worry.”
They were disciples of the Zhuge Clan, known collectively as Divine Mechanism Zhuge, and Daoists from Wudang who had accompanied Perfected Being Hyeongong to Donghu Stronghold.
These unfamiliar visitors, who had been nowhere to be seen two days ago, had formed groups to search the cliffs and were devoting all their efforts to finding traces of Dark Heaven.
Yet even the countless eyes and ears spread throughout the area, aided by brightly burning torches, failed to notice one person.
*Swish.*
His movements made no sound and gave off no presence.
The small, lithe figure quietly and stealthily headed toward the cliff. He passed dozens of people at the very least, yet not one of them noticed who he was.
Nor did anyone detect the Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step, wielded by the greatest assassin in history.
*What a nuisance.*
Mungyeong muttered inwardly as he stepped forward.
Treading on empty air, he soared like a bird and swiftly crossed the cliff.
The stealthy search conducted by the young medical apprentice whom no one paid any attention to did not take long.
*Nothing. I’m certain.*
The area containing Donghu Stronghold’s headquarters was vast.
It was an island capable of comfortably housing more than a thousand people. High cliffs surrounded it on every side, with narrow, undeveloped paths running along their upper reaches.
But that was all.
Nowhere could he sense any trace of human presence or the remnants of a Formation known as a Moving Formation.
That was the conclusion reached after two days of searching by a Supreme Peak master who had surpassed Returning to Simplicity and reached the realm of Returned to Youth.
Mungyeong trusted his judgment. At the same time, he realized there was still one place they had not searched.
*That’s right. One place remains.*
The river visible from the cliff was unusually wide and deep.
Deep enough that even he had no desire to enter it.
*...I suppose I have no choice.*
It was a way to prevent an even greater sacrifice.
The face of the old disciple he had parted from on an unnamed hill overlooking the Sichuan Tang Clan flashed before his eyes.
*All right, you rascal.*
Mungyeong quietly threw himself into the air.
His figure slipped deep into the river as though melting into the water, then glided smoothly toward the depths.

chapters.title: Chapter 463
paragraphs: Deep within a dark cave where only a faint light seeped in, a small old man sat cross-legged in quiet contemplation.
Energy like the sun raced through hundreds of acupoints and into the Eight Extraordinary Meridians. It took on physical form, rising to envelop the old man’s entire body.
Then the changes began.
*Whoooooosh.*
Three flower buds bloomed above the old man’s snow-white hair, then vanished.
As the buds formed, the energy they scattered took on a new shape: five rings radiant with dazzling, multicolored light.
It was a phenomenon that could only be displayed by one of the chosen few among Supreme Peak masters who had reached the realm of Five Qi Returning to Origin.
But the changes surrounding the old man did not end there.
*Fwoosh. Hissssss!*

The five rings symbolizing Five Qi Returning to Origin turned red. Tremendous fire qi erupted from the rings of internal energy brimming with Scorching Yang Qi, coiling around the old man before taking on a blue hue.
Furnace Fire Pure Blue.
When the fire in a furnace grew hot enough, it turned blue. The realm of martial arts the old man had attained was no different.
It was no exaggeration to say that the internal energy and insight he had accumulated over more than a hundred years had already reached the ultimate.
And yet...
*Is this as far as I go?*

The old man, Fire King Jeok Cheongang, withdrew his internal energy. His cross-legged figure descended from where it floated in midair, and the moment he touched the ground, the strange phenomena surrounding him vanished without a trace.
Only Jeok Cheongang’s hollow chuckle remained in the silent cave.
“Heh heh.”
Why could he not break through the wall before him and advance any farther?
He knew the reason better than anyone. He nodded in acknowledgment, yet he could not help regretting that the wall refused to budge. He even resented the heavens for it.
But rather than furrow his brow, Jeok Cheongang soothed his bitterness with a laugh.
*What is there to resent? This old man brought it upon himself.*
Martial arts grew stronger through ceaseless training, while insight came only when one emptied the heart.
But Jeok Cheongang had been unable to clear away the dregs that had accumulated in his heart over the past several decades.

Anything left to pile up and stagnate would eventually rot. His rotting heart filled with worldly anguish, inviting an inner demon—and once that inner demon took hold, he could no longer ward off the infirmities of old age.
“If I hadn’t met that brat... I’d probably be smearing shit on the walls by now. Heh heh.”
Jeok Cheongang laughed heartily.
One.
If he could attain just one small insight, he might reach the realm of Returned to Youth.
But he knew that desire was greed as well. Proof that he had not completely emptied his heart.
He looked up. The sky was visible through a small opening in the cave, and Jeok Cheongang addressed someone unseen beyond it.
“Does this mean I should be satisfied with what I have? Is that it?”
No answer came.
Or perhaps he had already received one.

He had taken a born killer as his disciple and caused innocent people to die. Yet thanks to his second disciple, he had at least managed to preserve his sanity. The answer was that he should no longer cling to anything more.
No one had spoken, but Jeok Cheongang heard the answer within his own heart.
“What a fucking joke. After all the fiends this old man has dealt with, this is how I’m treated?”
Jeok Cheongang sighed in complaint, lowered his head, and continued.
“Don’t you think so?”
A man stood where his gaze came to rest. Crouching Dragon Guest Zhuge Feng waved his folding fan as he answered.

“When I was nine, my grandfather once sat me beside him and said something similar. ‘I don’t know what bastard is up there, but he must have a truly god-awful temper.’ You are saying the same thing now, Senior.”
Jeok Cheongang nodded.
“Zhuge Gonghu did occasionally say something right.”
“He was a wise man.”
“He was also smarter than you. At least he didn’t have the bad manners to wave a fan in front of someone old enough to be his grandfather. Fold that thing before I break it.”
“It will not break easily. I had two nyang of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron worked into it.”
“Is your skull made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron too?”
“Ah, I see. Thank you for the lesson.”
Zhuge Feng promptly folded his fan, then looked around the cave.
“But what brings you here? The search is already over, and no one comes here anymore.”
“That is precisely why I came. This old man knows nothing about mechanisms and formations, so I have to prepare in my own way.”
At the word *prepare*, Zhuge Feng’s eyebrows rose slightly.
“You believe there will be a battle.”
“A martial artist should always be prepared for a fight. Besides, those Dark Heaven bastards are brutal and persistent. This will not end here.”
Jeok Cheongang’s voice was heavy.
Dark Heaven had taken the life of his close friend, Dharma King Hong Dao.
The countless deaths caused by the bloodshed in Henan and Sichuan were more than enough to remind him of the Great Faction War.
“I assume you know that the Heavenly Power Demon was imprisoned in the underground prison beneath the Sichuan Tang Clan.”
“Of course. I also know that before his death, he told Jin Taekyung that Dark Heaven was the successor to the Demonic Cult.”
The Great Faction War, fought for supremacy over the world, had ended in victory for the orthodox faction. But it had not been a sweeping victory. It was a victory that left nothing but wounds.
Had the orthodox faction retained enough strength at the time, it would have pursued the retreating forces of the Demonic Cult and torn out every last root.

But the Heavenly Demon Divine Cult and the orthodox faction—the dragon and tiger—had both lost most of their strength when the war ended. The long interval of more than fifty years had given the defeated survivors ample time to rise again.
Under a new name.
Dark Heaven.
“So much time has passed before we knew it. The wheel has turned, and troubled times have come again.”
At Jeok Cheongang’s quiet words, Zhuge Feng looked up.

The sky visible through the cracks in the cave ceiling was dark and chaotic. Even if the black clouds vanished tomorrow and the blue sky emerged, the heavenly patterns had already fallen into such disarray that no diviner in the world could read them.
*Troubled times.*
After completing its long circle, an age of turmoil had returned. An era of calamity was already upon them.
Blood would flow in rivers, and corpses would pile up like mountains.
Death and destruction would run rampant. Orphans who had lost their parents would wander the world, while plague and famine spread because there would be no one to dispose of the rotting bodies.
*What is happening now is only a small part of it.*
As Zhuge Feng realized that once more, a chill ran down his spine.
But Dark Heaven was not the only reason.
“I see you already had a guest.”
A voice pierced his ears.
Zhuge Feng froze as though someone had dumped ice water over his head.
*How?*
Though he had not reached the Supreme Peak realm, Zhuge Feng was still a master standing at the very edge of Peak.
Yet he had sensed no presence. Heard no sound.
Even though he had left three guards who followed him like shadows at the entrance to the cave, he had noticed no sign of anything.
That meant the owner of the voice was at least a Supreme Peak master.
*If he’s that powerful...*
Aside from Jeok Cheongang, the only possibility was Perfected Being Hyeongong of Wudang.
But the voice was far too young and clear.
It sounded like a boy’s.
*Ah.*
Insight flashed through Zhuge Feng’s mind, and he spun around.
The moment he saw the young medical apprentice he had encountered several times in passing, the fog in his mind dispersed, and a sobriquet slipped from his lips.
“The Slaughter Saint.”
The young medical apprentice, Mungyeong, twitched an eyebrow.
“You already knew?”
“I did not. Not until just now.”
Zhuge Feng continued excitedly.

“But I have always wondered why the greatest assassin in history disappeared. I also wondered why an extraordinary healer known as the Divine Physician appeared only after the Great Faction War had ended.”
“Not bad.”
“I watched you closely once, but I never imagined that you had reached the realm of Returned to Youth.”
Almost nothing was known about the Slaughter Saint. He was a figure shrouded in mystery.
Zhuge Feng stared at Mungyeong with gleaming eyes, then suddenly hesitated.
“But why would you deliberately reveal yourself to me... Unless?”
“You’re quick. Worthy of the Zhuge bloodline.”
“Blood will tell, after all. He may be a little strange, but the boy is clever. Zhuge Gonghu raised his grandson well. Now, putting that aside...”
Jeok Cheongang shrugged and fixed his gaze on Mungyeong.
“What brings you here? Why has an old man who’s been playing at being a child, despite it not suiting him in the slightest, come rushing over?”
“I’ll keep it short. You must leave this place immediately.”
“What?”
As promised, Mungyeong’s answer was extremely brief.
And for Jeok Cheongang, it was nowhere near reason enough to brave that godforsaken Tianling Falls.
“What kind of bullshit is—”
“I should make it even shorter.”
Mungyeong continued in a low, grave voice.
“Your disciple is in danger. No—perhaps everyone is.”
The moment he heard those words, Jeok Cheongang realized that he needed no further reason.
He turned toward Zhuge Feng. Blue flames had already kindled in his aged eyes.
“Launch the boat. Right now.”

There wasn’t water in every direction. Small islands were easy enough to find, as were flat stretches of land formed by mud and sand carried in from tributaries of the Yangtze.
*If a battle breaks out, fighting on land will put us at a much greater advantage.*
None of us had mastered water arts.

“Hmm. That would probably be better.”

“Captain.”

Cheongpung nodded.

*Splash!*
The familiar sensation washed over me as a System notification rang out.
The Title’s effect activated. Transparent webbing formed between my fingers and toes, and breathing became easy.
*Deeper. Farther in.*
I pressed onward without stopping.
I swam swiftly through the cold water, passing countless fish.
Then I spotted something in the distance.
*What’s that...?*

sentences.text: Deep within a dark cave where only a faint light seeped in, a small old man sat cross-legged in quiet contemplation.
Energy like the sun raced through hundreds of acupoints and into the Eight Extraordinary Meridians.
It took on physical form, rising to envelop the old man’s entire body.
Then the changes began.
*Whoooooosh.*
Three flower buds bloomed above the old man’s snow-white hair, then vanished.
As the buds formed, the energy they scattered took on a new shape: five rings radiant with dazzling, multicolored light.
It was a phenomenon that could only be displayed by one of the chosen few among Supreme Peak masters who had reached the realm of Five Qi Returning to Origin.
But the changes surrounding the old man did not end there.
*Fwoosh.
Hissssss!*
The five rings symbolizing Five Qi Returning to Origin turned red.
Tremendous fire qi erupted from the rings of internal energy brimming with Scorching Yang Qi, coiling around the old man before taking on a blue hue.
Furnace Fire Pure Blue.
When the fire in a furnace grew hot enough, it turned blue.
The realm of martial arts the old man had attained was no different.
It was no exaggeration to say that the internal energy and insight he had accumulated over more than a hundred years had already reached the ultimate.
And yet...
*Is this as far as I go?*
The old man, Fire King Jeok Cheongang, withdrew his internal energy.
His cross-legged figure descended from where it floated in midair, and the moment he touched the ground, the strange phenomena surrounding him vanished without a trace.
Only Jeok Cheongang’s hollow chuckle remained in the silent cave.
“Heh heh.”
Why could he not break through the wall before him and advance any farther?
He knew the reason better than anyone.
He nodded in acknowledgment, yet he could not help regretting that the wall refused to budge.
He even resented the heavens for it.
But rather than furrow his brow, Jeok Cheongang soothed his bitterness with a laugh.
*What is there to resent?
This old man brought it upon himself.*
Martial arts grew stronger through ceaseless training, while insight came only when one emptied the heart.
But Jeok Cheongang had been unable to clear away the dregs that had accumulated in his heart over the past several decades.
Anything left to pile up and stagnate would eventually rot.
His rotting heart filled with worldly anguish, inviting an inner demon—and once that inner demon took hold, he could no longer ward off the infirmities of old age.
“If I hadn’t met that brat...
I’d probably be smearing shit on the walls by now.
Heh heh.”
Jeok Cheongang laughed heartily.
One.
If he could attain just one small insight, he might reach the realm of Returned to Youth.
But he knew that desire was greed as well.
Proof that he had not completely emptied his heart.
He looked up.
The sky was visible through a small opening in the cave, and Jeok Cheongang addressed someone unseen beyond it.
“Does this mean I should be satisfied with what I have?
Is that it?”
No answer came.
Or perhaps he had already received one.
He had taken a born killer as his disciple and caused innocent people to die.
Yet thanks to his second disciple, he had at least managed to preserve his sanity.
The answer was that he should no longer cling to anything more.
No one had spoken, but Jeok Cheongang heard the answer within his own heart.
“What a fucking joke.
After all the fiends this old man has dealt with, this is how I’m treated?”
Jeok Cheongang sighed in complaint, lowered his head, and continued.
“Don’t you think so?”
A man stood where his gaze came to rest.
Crouching Dragon Guest Zhuge Feng waved his folding fan as he answered.
“When I was nine, my grandfather once sat me beside him and said something similar.
‘I don’t know what bastard is up there, but he must have a truly god-awful temper.’ You are saying the same thing now, Senior.”
Jeok Cheongang nodded.
“Zhuge Gonghu did occasionally say something right.”
“He was a wise man.”
“He was also smarter than you.
At least he didn’t have the bad manners to wave a fan in front of someone old enough to be his grandfather.
Fold that thing before I break it.”
“It will not break easily.
I had two nyang of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron worked into it.”
“Is your skull made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron too?”
“Ah, I see.
Thank you for the lesson.”
Zhuge Feng promptly folded his fan, then looked around the cave.
“But what brings you here?
The search is already over, and no one comes here anymore.”
“That is precisely why I came.
This old man knows nothing about mechanisms and formations, so I have to prepare in my own way.”
At the word *prepare*, Zhuge Feng’s eyebrows rose slightly.
“You believe there will be a battle.”
“A martial artist should always be prepared for a fight.
Besides, those Dark Heaven bastards are brutal and persistent.
This will not end here.”
Jeok Cheongang’s voice was heavy.
Dark Heaven had taken the life of his close friend, Dharma King Hong Dao.
The countless deaths caused by the bloodshed in Henan and Sichuan were more than enough to remind him of the Great Faction War.
“I assume you know that the Heavenly Power Demon was imprisoned in the underground prison beneath the Sichuan Tang Clan.”
“Of course.
I also know that before his death, he told Jin Taekyung that Dark Heaven was the successor to the Demonic Cult.”
The Great Faction War, fought for supremacy over the world, had ended in victory for the orthodox faction.
But it had not been a sweeping victory.
It was a victory that left nothing but wounds.
Had the orthodox faction retained enough strength at the time, it would have pursued the retreating forces of the Demonic Cult and torn out every last root.
But the Heavenly Demon Divine Cult and the orthodox faction—the dragon and tiger—had both lost most of their strength when the war ended.
The long interval of more than fifty years had given the defeated survivors ample time to rise again.
Under a new name.
Dark Heaven.
“So much time has passed before we knew it.
The wheel has turned, and troubled times have come again.”
At Jeok Cheongang’s quiet words, Zhuge Feng looked up.
The sky visible through the cracks in the cave ceiling was dark and chaotic.
Even if the black clouds vanished tomorrow and the blue sky emerged, the heavenly patterns had already fallen into such disarray that no diviner in the world could read them.
*Troubled times.*
After completing its long circle, an age of turmoil had returned.
An era of calamity was already upon them.
Blood would flow in rivers, and corpses would pile up like mountains.
Death and destruction would run rampant.
Orphans who had lost their parents would wander the world, while plague and famine spread because there would be no one to dispose of the rotting bodies.
*What is happening now is only a small part of it.*
As Zhuge Feng realized that once more, a chill ran down his spine.
But Dark Heaven was not the only reason.
“I see you already had a guest.”
A voice pierced his ears.
Zhuge Feng froze as though someone had dumped ice water over his head.

Though he had not reached the Supreme Peak realm, Zhuge Feng was still a master standing at the very edge of Peak.

Aside from Jeok Cheongang, the only possibility was Perfected Being Hyeongong of Wudang.

Not until just now.”

chapters.title: Chapter 464
paragraphs: Dongting Lake was unquestionably a lake, but it covered a thousand *li*, and even at its shallowest, the water was easily more than ten *zhang* deep.
The place I was swimming through now was one of the deepest parts of Dongting Lake. Naturally, the water was much deeper here, and the current raged like waves.
Finding a small underwater cave under these conditions was nothing short of heaven-sent luck.
*That’s...*
Amid the countless schools of fish, I spotted a gap barely wide enough for a grown man to squeeze through.
A thrill ran down my spine.
*I found it.*
Cliffs rooted deep in a riverbed naturally split apart over the years through sedimentation and erosion. I had seen it several times at the four places we had already visited.
But this time was different.
My reason and instinct, which usually went their separate ways, were whispering the same thing.
*The Dongting Fisherman’s secret refuge.*
Everything left traces.
The difference was subtle and well concealed, but my accumulated experience and keen eyesight told me that human hands had touched the entrance slowly drawing closer.
*The edges are smooth. Someone definitely worked on them.*
There was no need to ask who.
I heightened every one of my senses to the limit and cut through the current.
Slowly. Carefully.
It would be stupid to announce my presence to an enemy with whom I would soon be locked in a life-and-death duel.
If he prepared himself, the situation would become even more unfavorable.
*Fortunately, there’s still plenty of time left on the Title’s effect. No need to rush.*
I had seen more than a few people try to save ten minutes and end up leaving this world fifty years early.
Whether someone lived or died depended on their will and perseverance. I didn’t rush. I let the current carry me along.
*Swish.*
The brightly colored fish that noticed me seemed to hesitate, then cautiously brushed past.
I was barely moving, so they must not have taken me for a threat.
*Good.*
If I could fool fish this close to me, that was enough. I suppressed my presence even further and approached the cave.
At the entrance, which was barely wide enough for a grown man to squeeze through, I took a small breath and slipped inside.
Another submerged passage lay hidden beyond it.
*No sign of anyone so far.*
The passage was as narrow as the entrance and much deeper and longer than I had expected.
I sharpened my senses more than ever and searched for any trace of another presence. Only once I was certain there was none did I begin moving again.
I passed several strange-looking fish and clusters of aquatic plants. I had no idea how far I had gone when a faint light appeared in the distance.
*Wait. Light?*
This was underwater in Dongting Lake, but it was also a passage running through the inside of a cliff. How could there suddenly be light?
The passage did slope upward, but there was no way its structure could have let light leak in.
*Then...*
I swam smoothly toward the light, searched my surroundings once more, then shot upward through a small opening in the ceiling of the passage.
*Splash!*
I sucked in a breath.
Damp air filled my lungs.
At the same time, I felt the transparent gills that had formed around my throat disappear.
The next moment, I climbed out of the water and finally saw the source of the faint light. My eyes widened.
*Night-shining pearls.*
It was a cave.
A narrow, dark path stretched into the distance. Large and small night-shining pearls had been embedded at regular intervals in the ceiling, which was barely high enough for me to straighten my back.
*A submerged passage and a cave carved inside a cliff. Night-shining pearls, too... You’d have to be an idiot not to figure it out by now.*
The Lower District Sect’s information had been correct. This was unquestionably the Dongting Fisherman’s secret refuge.
My heart pounded with the thrill of finally finding him and the tension of the battle to come.
No. Those weren’t the only reasons.
*What’s that?*
I followed an unfamiliar smell that pricked my nose and turned my head.
A charred piece of wood lay on the waterlogged cave floor, and oil floated on the pooled water.
*A torch? Well, it’s not like he has an unlimited supply of night-shining pearls.*
The night-shining pearls embedded in the ceiling were obviously low quality, but that did not mean they were cheap.
I had never heard that the Dongting Fisherman was fabulously wealthy, so torches must have been essential for lighting such a long cave.
And that half-burned torch told me something important.
*It hasn’t been out for long.*
A faint warmth still lingered in the wood. It wasn’t difficult to deduce that the torch had fallen for some reason no more than one or two *shichen* ago.
And that pointed to one conclusion.
*The Dongting Fisherman is definitely here!*
Ultimately, I wasn’t looking for a place. I was looking for a man. Finding his secret refuge would mean nothing if the Dongting Fisherman wasn’t inside.
But through the torch, the Dongting Fisherman had revealed his presence.
Even if I were in his position, I would never have expected an intruder to enter a secret refuge hidden this well.
*That’s your mistake.*
I rose to my feet and began walking slowly along the path ahead.
I had plenty of excellent equipment—White Flame, my favored weapon, along with the Fire Dragon Armor and the Myriad-Poison Ring—but now wasn’t the time to bring any of it out.
It would be better to let my opponent see my empty hands and lower his guard, then exploit the advantage my Inventory gave me.
*Drip. Drip-drop.*
Listening to the irregular patter of water from the ceiling, I walked on with my presence suppressed as much as possible.
The path had been straight at first, but it soon began to twist and turn, sloping upward in some places and downward in others. I never let down my guard.
*But... what are these marks?*
It didn’t take long for me to realize something was strange.
My sharp eye was part of it, but the passage itself was in an alarming state.

Sections of the walls had been shattered here and there, leaving jagged rocks jutting out. Unlike the rest of the passage, which was covered in green moss, the freshly broken surfaces stood out unmistakably.
*Crackle.*
The moment I touched one, part of the wall crumbled away.
*This couldn’t have happened unless someone deliberately used considerable force.*
The entire cave was formed from solid rock that had accumulated over at least several hundred years.
Damaging it would require a blow carrying a significant amount of internal energy. But why would the Dongting Fisherman destroy his own precious refuge?
*Was there a battle here...? No. This is clearly the work of one person.*

I was still far from having the insight to discern the nature and roots of martial arts, but having reached the Supreme Peak realm, I had little trouble inferring what had happened from the traces left throughout the passage.
I furrowed my brow and thought for a moment, then shook my head.
*Focus on the Dongting Fisherman first. I can’t afford to grow careless or let the tension overwhelm me.*
I kept repeating that to myself as I walked.
Then it happened.
*Splash! Whoosh!*
The sudden noise jolted me alert as if someone had dumped cold water over my head.
My fully extended senses analyzed the sound and sent the new information straight to my brain.
*Fifty-odd zhang ahead. Closer than I expected.*
The sound also echoed with unusual depth and volume. That meant there was a larger space ahead, beyond this narrow cave passage.
*Swish.*
One step. Then another.
I focused every nerve in my toes as they touched the damp cave floor.

It was a blessing that I had used my Scorching Yang Qi beforehand to dry the water that had soaked me through. If water dripping from my body had struck the floor and made a sound, the Dongting Fisherman would have discovered me.
*I have to finish this inside the cave. Fighting underwater would make things much harder.*
My opponent was a Supreme Peak master of water arts, one of the finest in the world.
I was confident in my own martial prowess, but if I fought the Dongting Fisherman underwater, I would have to bear the full twenty-percent reduction in power the System had warned me about.
Here, however, I had solid ground beneath my feet. This was land, and naturally, the debuff was gone.
*I can’t let this opportunity slip away.*
The fifty-odd *zhang* between us rapidly dwindled.
*Splish. Splaash.*
The strange sounds continued, serving as perfect markers of distance and direction. As I approached a bend in the cave passage, I relaxed every muscle in my body.
I was already prepared.
Dozens of possibilities flashed before my eyes—how I would move, how I would end it.
If the Dongting Fisherman proved too formidable, I would use everything I had to kill him. If not, I would capture him and use him to draw out the larger body behind him.
*I’ll finish it in a single stroke, like a bolt of lightning.*
With a short breath, I awakened the fire dragon sleeping deep within my dantian.
The three *jiazi* of Scorching Yang Qi I had continually replenished through circulation surged into every limb and bone.
Searing heat flooded hundreds of acupoints and the Eight Extraordinary Meridians, driving every physical ability to its limit.
And then...
*Pop!*
One step was enough.
I planted a foot lightly against the slanted wall and shot forward.
The passage opened into a chamber some thirty *zhang* in radius, presumably the heart of the cave.
At its center, a white-haired old man crouched with his back to me.
*The Dongting Fisherman!*
The silent cry rang through me.
It was hard to believe that this small, shabby old man had harmed so many people. The anger I had buried for a time surged up as a cold flame.
*Inventory open. Summon!*
As the world slowed, the unknown power of the System covered my entire body as I charged toward the Dongting Fisherman.
*Swish. Clack.*
Red armor wrapped around my bare upper body.
The Fire Dragon Armor.

Then a cluster of light visible only to me brushed my finger and transformed into the divine artifact known as the Myriad-Poison Ring. At the same time, a spear with a transparent blade appeared in my grasp.
The next moment, three *jiazi* of Scorching Yang Qi flooded into them all.
*Whoooooosh!*
The damp air vanished. The river water pooled across the floor vanished. Even the droplets falling from overhead vanished.
No—they evaporated.
Blue-white Force blazed like wildfire across White Flame’s transparent spear blade, burning through everything in its path.
And one man stood directly in the path of that searing, destructive concentration of power.
*Die.*
The arrow had already been loosed. The bird resting in its nest could not escape.
To me, the Dongting Fisherman was no different from that bird.
A bird that had believed its nest was safe.
Even if it realized the truth too late, it could not stop an arrow that had already been fired.
Even if it hurriedly spread its wings, it could not avoid death or injury.
Just like the Dongting Fisherman, who was turning his body very slowly right now.
*It’s already too late.*
But in the next instant, I realized my mistake.
I had been too quick to assume.
*Boom!*
A snow-white streak of light flew in from somewhere and slammed into White Flame’s spear blade.
