I followed an unfamiliar smell that pricked my nose and turned my head.
A charred piece of wood lay on the waterlogged cave floor, and oil floated on the pooled water.
*A torch?
Well, it’s not like he has an unlimited supply of night-shining pearls.*
The night-shining pearls embedded in the ceiling were obviously low quality, but that did not mean they were cheap.
I had never heard that the Dongting Fisherman was fabulously wealthy, so torches must have been essential for lighting such a long cave.
And that half-burned torch told me something important.
*It hasn’t been out for long.*
A faint warmth still lingered in the wood.
It wasn’t difficult to deduce that the torch had fallen for some reason no more than one or two *shichen* ago.
And that pointed to one conclusion.
*The Dongting Fisherman is definitely here!*
Ultimately, I wasn’t looking for a place.
I was looking for a man.
Finding his secret refuge would mean nothing if the Dongting Fisherman wasn’t inside.
But through the torch, the Dongting Fisherman had revealed his presence.
Even if I were in his position, I would never have expected an intruder to enter a secret refuge hidden this well.
*That’s your mistake.*
I rose to my feet and began walking slowly along the path ahead.
I had plenty of excellent equipment—White Flame, my favored weapon, along with the Fire Dragon Armor and the Myriad-Poison Ring—but now wasn’t the time to bring any of it out.
It would be better to let my opponent see my empty hands and lower his guard, then exploit the advantage my Inventory gave me.
*Drip.
Drip-drop.*
Listening to the irregular patter of water from the ceiling, I walked on with my presence suppressed as much as possible.
The path had been straight at first, but it soon began to twist and turn, sloping upward in some places and downward in others.
I never let down my guard.
*But... what are these marks?*
It didn’t take long for me to realize something was strange.
My sharp eye was part of it, but the passage itself was in an alarming state.
Sections of the walls had been shattered here and there, leaving jagged rocks jutting out.
Unlike the rest of the passage, which was covered in green moss, the freshly broken surfaces stood out unmistakably.
*Crackle.*
The moment I touched one, part of the wall crumbled away.
*This couldn’t have happened unless someone deliberately used considerable force.*
The entire cave was formed from solid rock that had accumulated over at least several hundred years.
Damaging it would require a blow carrying a significant amount of internal energy.
But why would the Dongting Fisherman destroy his own precious refuge?
*Was there a battle here...?
No.
This is clearly the work of one person.*

I was still far from having the insight to discern the nature and roots of martial arts, but having reached the Supreme Peak realm, I had little trouble inferring what had happened from the traces left throughout the passage.
I furrowed my brow and thought for a moment, then shook my head.
*Focus on the Dongting Fisherman first.
I can’t afford to grow careless or let the tension overwhelm me.*
I kept repeating that to myself as I walked.
Then it happened.
*Splash!
Whoosh!*
The sudden noise jolted me alert as if someone had dumped cold water over my head.
My fully extended senses analyzed the sound and sent the new information straight to my brain.
*Fifty-odd zhang ahead.
Closer than I expected.*
The sound also echoed with unusual depth and volume.
That meant there was a larger space ahead, beyond this narrow cave passage.
*Swish.*
One step.
Then another.
I focused every nerve in my toes as they touched the damp cave floor.
It was a blessing that I had used my Scorching Yang Qi beforehand to dry the water that had soaked me through.
If water dripping from my body had struck the floor and made a sound, the Dongting Fisherman would have discovered me.
*I have to finish this inside the cave.
Fighting underwater would make things much harder.*
My opponent was a Supreme Peak master of water arts, one of the finest in the world.
I was confident in my own martial prowess, but if I fought the Dongting Fisherman underwater, I would have to bear the full twenty-percent reduction in power the System had warned me about.
Here, however, I had solid ground beneath my feet.
This was land, and naturally, the debuff was gone.
*I can’t let this opportunity slip away.*
The fifty-odd *zhang* between us rapidly dwindled.
*Splish.
Splaash.*
The strange sounds continued, serving as perfect markers of distance and direction.
As I approached a bend in the cave passage, I relaxed every muscle in my body.
I was already prepared.
Dozens of possibilities flashed before my eyes—how I would move, how I would end it.
If the Dongting Fisherman proved too formidable, I would use everything I had to kill him.
If not, I would capture him and use him to draw out the larger body behind him.
*I’ll finish it in a single stroke, like a bolt of lightning.*
With a short breath, I awakened the fire dragon sleeping deep within my dantian.
The three *jiazi* of Scorching Yang Qi I had continually replenished through circulation surged into every limb and bone.
Searing heat flooded hundreds of acupoints and the Eight Extraordinary Meridians, driving every physical ability to its limit.
And then...
*Pop!*
One step was enough.
I planted a foot lightly against the slanted wall and shot forward.
The passage opened into a chamber some thirty *zhang* in radius, presumably the heart of the cave.
At its center, a white-haired old man crouched with his back to me.
*The Dongting Fisherman!*
The silent cry rang through me.
It was hard to believe that this small, shabby old man had harmed so many people.
The anger I had buried for a time surged up as a cold flame.
*Inventory open.
Summon!*
As the world slowed, the unknown power of the System covered my entire body as I charged toward the Dongting Fisherman.
*Swish.
Clack.*
Red armor wrapped around my bare upper body.
The Fire Dragon Armor.
Then a cluster of light visible only to me brushed my finger and transformed into the divine artifact known as the Myriad-Poison Ring.
At the same time, a spear with a transparent blade appeared in my grasp.
The next moment, three *jiazi* of Scorching Yang Qi flooded into them all.
*Whoooooosh!*
The damp air vanished.
The river water pooled across the floor vanished.
Even the droplets falling from overhead vanished.
No—they evaporated.
Blue-white Force blazed like wildfire across White Flame’s transparent spear blade, burning through everything in its path.
And one man stood directly in the path of that searing, destructive concentration of power.
*Die.*
The arrow had already been loosed.
The bird resting in its nest could not escape.
To me, the Dongting Fisherman was no different from that bird.
A bird that had believed its nest was safe.
Even if it realized the truth too late, it could not stop an arrow that had already been fired.
Even if it hurriedly spread its wings, it could not avoid death or injury.
Just like the Dongting Fisherman, who was turning his body very slowly right now.
*It’s already too late.*
But in the next instant, I realized my mistake.
I had been too quick to assume.
*Boom!*
A snow-white streak of light flew in from somewhere and slammed into White Flame’s spear blade.

chapters.title: Chapter 465
paragraphs: *Boom!*
The impact knocked White Flame’s spearhead aside.
The streak of light that had flown in along a bizarre trajectory writhed like a living creature, then rained down over my head.
*Shh-shh-shh-shing!*
A downpour of Force.
As that destructive power lit the dark cave in an instant, I twisted smoothly out of its path.
*Swish. Boom-boom-boom!*
My shoulder, neck, waist, chest...
The streak of light swept within a hair’s breadth of the vital acupoints throughout my body before piercing and smashing through the solid cave floor.
Had I reacted even a moment later, the attack would have killed me instantly.
But the Dongting Fisherman’s attack failed to touch even a single hair on my body, and that moment of danger turned into an opportunity.
Just like now.
*Whoom!*
White Flame’s spearhead, knocked off course by the earlier impact, changed direction sharply in midair and swept toward the Dongting Fisherman’s throat.
His grayish-white eyes widened as he turned, and the snow-white streak hurriedly moved to block the spearhead.
But...
*That won’t be enough.*

If the Dongting Fisherman was an old monster who had accumulated enormous internal energy over his long life, then I was a monster who had surpassed those long years through System rewards and countless battles on the edge of death.
Even if our internal energy was equal, my body held the strength of a giant who had surpassed the limits of humanity.
*Boom!*
The instant the blue-white flames struck the streak of light, a thunderous crash rang out as though the sky itself had split apart, and the Dongting Fisherman was sent flying.
The small old man smashed through solid rock and crashed into the wall. The cave shook, and enormous stalactites came tumbling down.
I glared into the grayish-white eyes visible beyond the falling debris and enunciated every word.
“Get up. Drop the pathetic act.”
*Crack-crack-crack.*
His limbs, limp as a corpse’s only moments ago, moved with sudden vigor.
The Dongting Fisherman pulled himself from the hollow his body had left in the wall and cracked his neck from side to side.
Bones ground against one another as he started forward. A long fishing rod had somehow appeared in his wrinkled hand.
*The black-wood fishing rod.*
It could not compare to Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, but this was the Dongting Fisherman’s signature weapon, said to be as strong as meteorite iron and extraordinarily flexible.
Despite being partially damaged, it was still one *zhang* long. A fishing line and hook with a faint sheen hung from its tip.
*That’s...*
I had never seen it before, but I had heard of it.
Heavenly Silkworm Thread—a rare treasure said to rival the Sichuan Tang Clan’s Soul-Severing Thread.

It was strange enough that a mere silkworm cocoon was treated as a spiritual creature, as though the grand name Heavenly Silkworm were not enough. But even that was less astonishing than the thread itself, which was said to be so tough and sharp that not even steel could cut it.
The line attached to the black-wood fishing rod was that very Heavenly Silkworm Thread.
*I’ll have to be careful.*
Caution couldn’t hurt. Even if the Fire Dragon Armor was a divine weapon, it wasn’t invincible armor capable of blocking everything.
I opened my mouth while staring at the Dongting Fisherman, who had stopped three *zhang* away.
“You have two choices. First, you die by my hand right here. Second, you tell me everything you know without leaving out a single detail, then atone to your victims. Which will it be?”
Instead of answering, he stared blankly at me through hazy grayish-white eyes.
There was no emotion in that gaze. A chill ran up my spine as I looked into eyes I could hardly believe belonged to a human being.
*...What is this feeling?*
Everyone had emotions.
But the Dongting Fisherman was different. He was clearly breathing, and I could sense life within him, yet he seemed like an empty object.
*What the hell is this...?*
I had no time to dwell on it. The next moment, I flinched and tightened my grip on the spear shaft.
A nameless fish had suddenly moved only a few steps away.
Its bones were exposed, and the flesh around its belly had been torn away. It thrashed several times, then went still.
Clear teeth marks scarred its body where someone had bitten into it.
*No way.*
I narrowed my eyes at the Dongting Fisherman.
Red blood and glinting scales clung to the wrinkles around his mouth.
Only then did I realize what had made the sounds I’d heard on my way here—and what he had been doing until moments ago.
*He was ripping into it and eating it raw. While it was still alive.*
What kind of lunatic old man was this?
A classic fantasy movie that cable channels used to rerun whenever they had an empty time slot suddenly flashed through my mind.
Now that I looked at him, he did resemble the monster from that movie. The small frame, the hunched back, even the sparse hair.
I clicked my tongue softly and addressed the Dongting Fisherman.
“This changes the genre... The divine artifact you people are looking for isn’t a ring, is it?”
“Fine, don’t answer. I was planning to question you while plucking out the few hairs you have left, one by one.”
“Guh.”
“Oh, shit. What was that?”
My eyes widened at the Dongting Fisherman’s sudden reaction.
I’d just blurted out the first thing that came to mind. Had I actually hit a balding man’s sore spot?
But I couldn’t tell whether the Dongting Fisherman had reacted to the threat against his hair roots or for some other reason.
Before I could say another word, his old grayish-white eyes bulged, and a tremendous roar burst from his throat.
“GRAAAAAH!”
*Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
This was no shout from the old man who screamed on the hill behind the neighborhood every morning at dawn.
The roar, infused with immense internal energy, traveled through the air and hammered the cavern. Everything around us shook and burst apart—the floor, the walls, everything.
And before the shock wave could even spread, the Dongting Fisherman shot toward me, leaving a pale afterimage behind.
*Whoooooosh!*
His eyes had turned pitch-black.
As he charged alongside that streak of light, I spoke in a low, heavy voice.
“Turn down the volume, you fucking bastard.”
*Fwoosh! Boom!*
Blue-white flames enveloped the transparent spearhead as I stepped forward.
*Pop!*
Three *zhang* was by no means a short distance.

But the Dongting Fisherman and I were superhumans who had set foot in the realm of Supreme Peak. The moment we shot toward each other, distance lost all meaning. The gap vanished, and the air exploded.
White Flame’s spearhead, carrying unimaginable heat, and the Heavenly Silkworm Thread, writhing like a living creature as it carried several *jiazi* of internal energy, tore through space.
*Shh-shh-shh-shh-shing!*
The speed deserved to be called extreme swiftness.
The Heavenly Silkworm Thread extending from the tip of the black-wood fishing rod surged like a wave.
Its bizarre, unfathomable movements were unlike anything I had encountered among the countless weapons I’d faced.
The scars left on the countless corpses scattered throughout Donghu Stronghold flashed before my eyes.
*He used this martial art to kill weak, innocent commoners.*

I wasn’t especially sensitive, nor was I a *junzi*. I had no reason to defend the bandits of the Yangtze River Channel League. They were river bandits who had gathered to plunder, and they had undoubtedly taken other people’s lives and property.
It might seem as though I had taken lives too, but the difference between me and them was that they had not killed to survive. They had done it because it served their purposes.
But...
*People should never have died like that.*
Hundreds had been trampled like ants and cut down like livestock. Hundreds more had been drowned in the middle of Dongting Lake.
And most of them hadn’t been martial artists. They were commoners who didn’t know so much as a single form of martial arts. There had even been children who couldn’t write their own names.
People like that should never have died that way.
No human being should kill another like that.
“You get it, you son of a bitch?”
In the slowed world, my voice vanished beneath the raging wind.
Power flooded the hand gripping the spear shaft. As the mighty Scorching Yang Qi boiled throughout my body, I brought the spearhead down at an angle.
*Fwoosh. Shhk!*
A single tongue of flame blossomed in the air.
At the same moment, the streak of light scattered.
A section of the Heavenly Silkworm Thread, severed along the path of my spearhead, fluttered away.
The Dongting Fisherman, whose form had been countered so easily, let out a strange scream and swung the black-wood fishing rod again.
*Shing. Shh-shh-shh-shh-shing!*
Streaks of light split the air in every direction.
The Heavenly Silkworm Thread, filled with Force, sliced through space, piercing and cutting everything in its path.
But I evaded every attack and silently swung my spear.
*Shhk! Shhk! Shhk!*
I could see it all clearly.
I could tell where that strange fishing-rod weapon would move and how the Heavenly Silkworm Thread attached to it would come for me.
My half-lidded eyes took in every detail, and my wide-open senses read each attack before it came.
*If this had been me before my Middle Dantian opened, I would’ve struggled.*
When the place where you stand changes, the scenery you see changes as well.
Opening my Middle Dantian had expanded my senses and granted me a new field of vision I hadn’t even known existed. The results were unfolding before my eyes.
*Here it comes.*

Unusual weapons like the black-wood fishing rod were difficult to master. But once their advantages were fully exploited and paired with the proper martial arts, they became extremely troublesome to face.
Even so, I predicted the oncoming trajectory with perfect accuracy and swung my spear.
*Shhk!*
“GRAAAAAAAH!”
Another fast, razor-sharp strike severed the Heavenly Silkworm Thread.

The line had once stretched five *zhang*, but I’d reduced it by nearly half without allowing it to inflict any meaningful damage. An even more ferocious aura erupted from the Dongting Fisherman’s entire body.
“Now that’s more like a person.”
But martial arts displayed greater power when the mind and body were stable.
When the mind wavered, the body lost its balance. Movements grew wider and rougher.
And finding a gap in that loosened net wasn’t difficult for me.
*Whoooooosh!*
*Flamefire Path.*
A single streak of fire raced across the damp cave floor.
Its internal energy consumption was tremendous and its trajectory simple, but like most of the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts, Flamefire Path had two great advantages.
*It’s fast and destructive.*
*Boom!*
The air grew scorching hot, and every trace of moisture around us evaporated.
I stepped onto the ground, now dry and crumbly as desert sand, and shot forward like an arrow.
*Swish!*
I turned my head, and the Heavenly Silkworm Thread aimed at the back of my neck swept past.
Having missed, the Dongting Fisherman hurriedly redirected the thread and tried to wrap it around my entire body.
But I kicked off the ground half a beat faster.
*Boom! Shhk!*
Something as cold as ice traveled through the tip of my foot, then quickly turned hot as fire.
The flesh at the tip of my bare big toe had been sliced clean away.
The pain was severe enough to make an ordinary person scream, but I accepted it without a flicker.
*This is nothing.*
I’d endured countless injuries and unimaginable pain while traveling between the modern world and Murim.
There had been times when I writhed in agony as though every bundle of nerves in my body were being severed, times when I had genuinely wanted to die.
Compared to that, an injury like this was nothing.
No—it was an absurdly cheap toll.
In exchange for losing only part of my big toe, I’d gained an opportunity to decide the outcome of this life-and-death duel.
*Now!*
My hands and feet obeyed the command from my brain, moving like flowing water.
Faster and cleaner than ever, without the slightest wasted motion.
I drew back the spear shaft, then hurled it forward with all my strength.
*Whoooooosh—thud!*
A strike like a flash of lightning.
White Flame left my hand, smashed through the Dongting Fisherman’s shoulder as he sensed the danger and tried to retreat, then buried itself deep in the wall.
“GRAAAAAAAH!”
As his scream of pain filled the cave, I raised my fist toward him.
“I told you to turn down the volume.”
*Thud!*

Something as cold as ice traveled through the tip of my foot, then quickly turned hot as fire.
The flesh at the tip of my bare big toe had been sliced clean away.
The pain was severe enough to make an ordinary person scream, but I accepted it without a flicker.
*This is nothing.*
I’d endured countless injuries and unimaginable pain while traveling between the modern world and Murim.
There had been times when I writhed in agony as though every bundle of nerves in my body were being severed, times when I had genuinely wanted to die.
Compared to that, an injury like this was nothing.
No—it was an absurdly cheap toll.
In exchange for losing only part of my big toe, I’d gained an opportunity to decide the outcome of this life-and-death duel.
*Now!*
My hands and feet obeyed the command from my brain, moving like flowing water.
Faster and cleaner than ever, without the slightest wasted motion.
I drew back the spear shaft, then hurled it forward with all my strength.
*Whoooooosh—thud!*
A strike like a flash of lightning.
White Flame left my hand, smashed through the Dongting Fisherman’s shoulder as he sensed the danger and tried to retreat, then buried itself deep in the wall.
“GRAAAAAAAH!”
As his scream of pain filled the cave, I raised my fist toward him.
“I told you to turn down the volume.”
*Thud!*

chapters.title: Chapter 466
paragraphs: Even without using internal energy—and though I’d held back—I had already far surpassed human limits through pure physical strength alone.
*Boom!*
My fist struck him square in the face, and the Dongting Fisherman’s entire body jerked. To him, it must have felt like being hit with an iron club.
His pitch-black pupils trembled. Blood-soaked yellow teeth tumbled from his gaping mouth.
*One more.*
*Thud!*
The Dongting Fisherman, blood pouring from his mouth and nose like a waterfall, staggered and waved his hand.
It was only a small movement, but my sharpened senses took in everything happening around me with perfect clarity.
*Swish!*
Something sliced faintly but sharply through the air, aiming for my back.
I already knew what it was.
*The Heavenly Silkworm Thread.*
Instead of dodging, I twisted the wrist of the hand gripping the Dongting Fisherman’s black-wood fishing rod.
*Crack!*
His bones broke. The black-wood fishing rod slipped from his powerless grasp, and the Force-infused Heavenly Silkworm Thread fluttered limply through the air.
“What the fuck are you trying to pull, you son of a bitch? Who do you take me for, a sucker?”
The answer that came back was a heavy sound splitting the air.
*Whoom!*
The Dongting Fisherman’s palm strike shot toward me with terrifying momentum. But I was already prepared. Without hesitation, I thrust out my own palm to meet it.
*Boom!*
The swift, concise first form of the Flame Divine Palm.
Two Forces—one white, one blue—collided in midair, sending razor-sharp winds whipping around us.
Through my wildly tossing hair, I stared coldly at the Dongting Fisherman.
“What are you doing, you bald bastard?”
I didn’t need an answer.
I already knew what I had to do, and the tip of my foot was already lashing out at the Dongting Fisherman’s knee with lightning speed.
*Thud!*
His bones crunched. His body staggered, and blood spilled from the corner of his mouth.
The heavy impact momentarily disrupted the flow of his internal energy, and the Palm Force gathered in the palm still pressed against mine began to fade.
“All right. As of today, we’re officially a thing.”
The scales had already tipped in my favor. I laced my fingers tightly through his, then twisted with all my strength.
*Crack!*
Sibu-leol. I’d never even held a woman’s hand in my life, yet here in Murim, I’d interlocked fingers with enough men to fill a truck.
Of course, an affectionate finger-lock fueled by the pent-up rage of a man who’d been single all his life never failed to deliver.
Just like now.
“Gyaaaaaaah!”
A scream of agony finally burst from the Dongting Fisherman’s mouth.
I clenched my fist and punched him again and again as he stared at me with his pitch-black eyes wide open.
*Thud! Thud! Thud-thud-thud!*
Under the unceasing rain of fists and palms, the Dongting Fisherman’s movements slowly weakened.
Or so I thought.
“Gueeeeeegh!”
What was it?
Had I let my guard down because I thought victory was assured? Had I grown too confident that I could capture him alive?
Whatever the reason, I hadn’t been thorough.
And that created an opening.
*Splaaash!*
My vision turned completely red.
The sticky blood the Dongting Fisherman vomited drenched my face and froze my body for an instant.
And the counterattack of a Supreme Peak master fighting for his life was fiercer than I’d expected.
*Boom!*
With a sound like compressed air exploding, a stream of internal energy seemed to pass straight through the surface of the Fire Dragon Armor and slammed into my upper body.
My vision blurred.
As the scenery flashed past, a thought crossed my mind.
*Damn it. Inner-Family Heavy Hand.*
He still had this much strength left?
I swallowed the blood surging up my throat and drew on my internal energy.
I’d taken an unexpected blow, but compared to the Dongting Fisherman’s condition, this was nothing.
That I had suffered only a minor internal injury despite being caught off guard by the Inner-Family Heavy Hand was proof enough.
*Whoooosh!*
I sent the flow of internal energy, interrupted for only an instant, coursing through every limb and acupoint in my body.
The acupoints damaged by the Inner-Family Heavy Hand throbbed slightly, but that was all.
A carp didn’t die just because someone scooped a bowlful of water from its pond.
Neither would I.
*I’ll finish this.*
I twisted around in midair while hurtling backward. The opposite wall of the cave rushed toward me. I planted my foot against it lightly, then detonated the internal energy flowing through my toes.
*Boom!*
With a roar like the sky splitting apart, the unyielding rocks in the wall exploded.
Hundreds—thousands—of fragments tore through the air in every direction, but I was already gone.
*Whoooooosh!*
Heavier than a rock, faster than the wind.
My entire body cleaved through the air several times faster than when I’d been thrown back, carrying the weight of ten thousand *geun*.
“Dongting Fisherman!”
My shout shook the vast cavern. Several *jiazi* of Scorching Yang Qi carried in my voice pressed down the water and pushed the rocks aside.
And at the end of it all stood one man.
The Dongting Fisherman had just pulled White Flame from his shoulder and the rock wall behind him when he spotted me. His eyes flew wide.
His blackened pupils trembled, flashing a sliver of white.
His mouth quivered open, and his one remaining front tooth trembled pitifully.
“D-d-d-don’t...”
Don’t come any closer?
Fuck off.
I had no idea why the man who’d been acting like a lunatic only moments ago was suddenly trembling like that, but my mind was already made up.
*I was going to bring you back in one piece if possible... but that’s not happening now.*
It was too late for regret. The Dongting Fisherman should have regretted his actions long ago.
Before joining hands with Dark Heaven. Before brutally slaughtering innocent commoners and children.
That was when he should have regretted his actions and repented.
Now that we’d come this far, there was no need for repentance.
All that remained was punishment for his crimes.
*You’re fucking dead.*
I didn’t care if I crushed all four of his limbs. As long as he kept breathing, I could tear out every last strand of hair and every tooth, then drive a stalactite up his ass.
I would take his life only after he’d spat out everything he knew about Dark Heaven.
I’d leave him just alive enough to breathe.
Only until my anger at what he had done had diminished, even slightly.
With exactly that much force behind me, I shot toward him and extended my fist through the slowed world.
*Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.*
*Whoooooosh!*
Fiercely blazing blue-white hellfire swallowed the palm strike the Dongting Fisherman thrust out with his broken hand.

His Palm Force, now as murky as muddy water, shattered and evaporated beneath the Scorching Yang Qi. Beyond the ceaseless whirlwind and flashes of light, my flame-wreathed fist smashed through the Body-Protecting Qi surrounding him.
*Crack! Booooom!*
Every blood vessel in the Dongting Fisherman’s bulging eyes burst. He vomited blood as he was driven into the wall.
Fine, spiderweb-like cracks spread across the hard rock of the cavern wall. Soon, they widened into a massive fissure that reached all the way to the ceiling.
*Rumble. Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
The ceiling collapsed, and the ground split apart.
The rocks that had endured tremendous water pressure deep beneath the vast freshwater lake of Dongting Lake began collapsing one after another. Streams of water surged up from every direction.
*Collapse.*
This space, created at some unknown point in the past, would soon come crashing down.
Just like its owner, who would never return to his secret refuge.
*I have to hurry.*
*Rattle-rattle!*
I pressed the Dongting Fisherman’s acupoints to stop the bleeding. Then, in case anything happened, I sealed him with Pressure-Point Strikes so he could not move even a hair.
I hoisted the small old man onto my back, then punched forward without hesitation.
*Boom! Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
A raging current was visible through the sinkhole-like opening in the floor.
I took a deep breath and leaped into the violent water.
*Splash!*
Cold water closed around my body, and a familiar message rang in my ears.

**System** Title effect activated: Water Rescue Worker Special Skill embedded in the Title applied. Water Rescue Worker’s Webbed Feet generated. Water Rescue Worker’s Gills generated. **Remaining duration:** 18 hours, 43 minutes, 32 seconds
I had plenty of time.
I moved my body powerfully with the current.
Before long, I noticed the Dongting Fisherman constantly blowing bubbles from his mouth and nose. The sight reminded me of something I’d momentarily overlooked.
*What the... Ah.*
Even a master of water arts needed enough internal energy and awareness to use those techniques.
He didn’t breathe through gills like I did. If he remained underwater too long, he might die.
*Wait. If that’s the case...*
A flash of insight struck me.
At the same time, I began swimming with all my strength.
Interlocking fingers was one thing, but I wasn’t about to give up my first kiss too.
Especially not to a crazy old man who was nearly a hundred!
*Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
A vibration that began somewhere deep underwater grew so powerful that it reached the people on the surface.
At the sudden anomaly, the old boatman shrank into himself with fear in his eyes, while the other three men’s faces stiffened.
“Um, I think...”
“It seems it’s finally begun. Or perhaps it has already ended.”
Gung Gibang answered Cheongpung’s murmur in a grave voice.
Hyuk Mujin, who had been anxiously watching the trembling cliff and river, abruptly spoke.
“We have to go.”
Gung Gibang furrowed his brow.
“What?”
“It’s certain that something happened to our Captain. I have a bad feeling.”
“But Jin Taekyung, that bastard...”
“He told us not to move and to wait here. I know.”
“Then why?”
“I’ve always been terrible at listening to people.”
“Damn. You sound proud of it.”
“Isn’t it better than sitting here sucking our fingers?”
At Hyuk Mujin’s words, Gung Gibang gnawed at his lower lip.
He, too, had been uneasy for some time.
He didn’t know exactly when it had begun, but his heart was pounding violently, and every one of his senses was on edge.
*What’s wrong with me? Did something really happen to that bastard?*
A face flashed before his eyes.
The Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.
No—the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Taekyung.

The kind of bastard who looked capable of crawling back alive even if he were thrown into the deepest pit of the underworld. More vicious than A-Gwi and strong enough to beat Yama himself into the ground.
*I’ve never once imagined that bastard dying... But nothing is absolute. Surely not?*
Gung Gibang hadn’t dismissed what Jin Taekyung had said before entering the river. After traveling with him for so long, he knew there was always a reason behind the man’s words and actions.
But this time, he couldn’t help wavering.
*Goddammit. The weather’s gone completely to shit too. What the hell am I supposed to do?*
*Rumble. Crash!*
Just as the old boatman had warned a couple of *shichen* earlier, even calling the current weather on Dongting Lake the worst imaginable would have been an understatement.
A raging storm. Lightning crashing down from the sky.
Gung Gibang looked around with conflicted eyes and finally opened his mouth.
Or rather, he was just about to when—
“It’s all right.”
“Huh?”
“What?”
Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin turned their heads at the same time.
Someone was smiling brightly in their field of view.
At the edge of the small island where they stood, Cheongpung had been lying facedown, listening to something. He brushed the sand from his ear and grinned.
“Benefactor is coming.”
And then—
*Splaaash!*
A figure shot from the water atop a towering spray and landed heavily on the sandy shore.
A muscular young man with a small old man slung over his back.
It was Jin Taekyung.
“Captain!”
“You’re back!”
“Benefactooor!”
“Stay back, you dickheads. If any of you tries to hug me, all three of you are getting murdered today.”
After stopping the three men charging toward him with cries of joy, Jin Taekyung continued in a grave voice.
“We don’t have time, so I’ll get straight to the point. Raise your hand if you’ve ever kissed someone. Or if you want to try it. Hands up.”
Two of them caught on quickly.
One was hopelessly oblivious.
As Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin quietly backed away, one hand shot into the air amid a bright, innocent shout.
“Me! Me! I’ve never kissed anyone before!”
“Fuck. Thank God.”
“Huh?”
Beaming from ear to ear, Jin Taekyung held the Dongting Fisherman out toward the bewildered Cheongpung.
“Your wish just came true.”
*Rumble. Crash!*
Thunder and lightning shook the entire world.

paragraphs: I’ve always been the kind of person who thinks the process matters just as much as the result.
But sometimes, I deliberately look away from the process.
Not every process has to be perfect and beautiful, after all.
*What matters is the result. The result.*
Yeah, that’s all I’m saying.
And behind the process that everyone—including me—had chosen to ignore, an excellent result finally revealed itself.
*Cough! Splash!*
Water spilled between the Dongting Fisherman’s cracked lips as he coughed.
Cheongpung, who had shown a moving spirit of self-sacrifice against the Dongting Fisherman, opened his mouth with a strange expression.
“It feels weird.”
I exchanged glances with Hyuk Mujin, Gung Gibang, and the old boatman, then answered solemnly.
“It’s always like that the first time.”
“Did you feel the same way, Benefactor?”
“...Of course.”
I’d never done it before, but even if I did, I wouldn’t feel the way Cheongpung did. No, I shouldn’t.
I subtly averted my eyes as I answered. Cheongpung nodded, then took a deep breath.
“But I really don’t understand this.”
“You’re excited. That’s all.”
“It smelled strange, too. Like fish.”
*What a nose.*
I remembered the Dongting Fisherman tearing into a raw fish before our fight and answered.
“You’re imagining it.”
“My stomach feels sick.”
“That’s because your body is releasing hormones. Kissing is good for your immune system and helps relieve stress too...”
“What?”
“Nothing.”
“My stomach just feels really nauseous. I want some sweets.”
Hyuk Mujin patted Cheongpung’s shoulder guiltily.
“I’ll buy you some later, Young Hero Cheong.”
“You will, Hyuk Mujin?”
“Yes. I’ll find some way to feed you until your stomach bursts.”
“But you’re poor too, Hyuk Mujin. Last time, I saw you picking up silver nyang at the ferry landing...”
“My father is rich.”
Hyuk Mujin only seemed poor because following me around had put him through all sorts of hardship. His family business was thriving more by the day, so he was still the son of a wealthy household.
At the proud declaration of a second-generation rich kid planning to bleed his father dry, the other two men, who had been watching Cheongpung with sad eyes, joined in.
“Cheongpung, I’ll contribute too, even if I have to beg for the money.”
“This old man is willing to lower your fare a little as well.”
“Wow! Really?”
A pang of guilt stabbed at my heart.
But it couldn’t be helped. It had definitely been his choice.
After doing my best to justify myself, I checked the Dongting Fisherman’s condition.
“How is he?”
At Hyuk Mujin’s question from over my shoulder, I nodded.
“He’s fine.”
“Uh... He doesn’t look particularly fine.”
I was momentarily speechless as I looked down at the Dongting Fisherman.
Both arms were twisted at bizarre angles, and countless wounds showed through his clothes, which had been torn to shreds.
Those were merely the injuries visible to the naked eye. The severe internal injuries were a bonus.
“What on earth happened?”
I gave them a brief summary of what had happened inside the underwater cave.
“I was on guard in case anything happened, but he was weaker than I expected, so I beat the shit out of him and dragged him back.”
After a brief silence, Hyuk Mujin spoke.
“But the Dongting Fisherman is a master of incredible water arts.”
“That’s why I beat him on land. Turns out there was a cave in there.”
“You have an incredible talent for making extremely difficult things sound easy.”
“It wasn’t extremely easy, but it wasn’t extremely difficult either.”
“The important thing is that he’s still breathing.”
“The fact that he’s still breathing looks like a miracle.”
“Considering what that old man has done, he deserves to die right now.”
“That’s true. Either way, it’s fortunate. I was worried about the Dongting Fisherman, of course, but I was also worried that Dark Heaven’s other bastards might be there with him.”
That was something I had considered as well.
According to Honglan’s testimony, the Dongting Fisherman had been the sole culprit behind the tragedy on Dongting Lake.
But slaughtering Yangtze One Saber and so many others at Donghu Stronghold would have required at least two Supreme Peak masters, if not more.
*Mungyeong said the same thing.*
No matter how rapidly I had grown, taking on two or more Supreme Peak masters at once was... hard to say.
Even among people who had reached the same realm, ability varied wildly.
*The Dongting Fisherman was a step below me.*
I’d been lucky. If the Dongting Fisherman had been working with another of Dark Heaven’s powerhouses, I might have been the one to go down instead.
Of course, I wouldn’t have started a fight with such slim odds in the first place.
“But shouldn’t this old man be waking up by now? Why isn’t he moving at all? Did he swallow too much water?”
At Gung Gibang’s question, Cheongpung, who was rinsing his mouth with lake water, answered.
“He’s been hit with Pressure-Point Strikes. Right, Benefactor?”
“Yeah. Exactly.”
At present, the Dongting Fisherman’s Paralysis, Mute, and Sleep Acupoints had all been struck.

Even if the seal on his Sleep Acupoint wore off and he woke from his forced sleep, his body would remain paralyzed, and he wouldn’t be able to move his lips. Forget resisting—he couldn’t even squirm like a grub.
“What do you intend to do now?”
“We’ve accomplished our objective, so we’re going back.”
We were not the only ones who knew the location of this place. If Dark Heaven had caught wind of it and sent reinforcements, we could easily have ended up trapped instead.
*If a monster like the Western Heaven Demon Lord showed up, we might have to prepare ourselves to die.*
There were clear limits to what Cheongpung and I could do alone.
Dark Heaven was unquestionably involved in the string of incidents across Hubei Province. The biggest problem was that we knew neither where they were nor who their members were.
But if we could force the Dongting Fisherman to talk, we could uncover every last detail about them and launch a counterattack.
The Fire King and the Slaughter Saint—two peerless Supreme Peak masters—would commit their full strength, as would Wudang and the Zhuge Clan, the undisputed rulers of Hubei Province.
“We’re leaving. Right now.”
But an obstacle I hadn’t considered stood in our way.
“Um, Great Hero.”
The old boatman had suddenly spoken. After hesitating for a moment, he continued, his face stiff.
“I beg your pardon, but in this old man’s humble opinion, it simply can’t be done.”
“What?”
“As you know, Great Hero, Dongting Lake right now...”
*Rumble-rumble-rumble! Crash!*
Thunder booming from all directions swallowed the rest of the boatman’s words.
He hunched his shoulders as though frightened, then pointed around us with anxious eyes.
“Look. How can we possibly launch a boat in conditions like these?”
He had good reason to be trembling.

The sky had turned pitch-black, and lightning struck at irregular intervals. Heavy rain had begun pouring down at some point, noticeably swelling the waters of Dongting Lake. Violent whirlpools battered the cliffs and rocks.
*Of all times for this to happen.*
It hadn’t been this bad when we entered the Dongting Fisherman’s secret refuge. Yet in less than a single shichen, the situation around us had rapidly deteriorated toward the worst possible outcome.
But...
“We have to go.”
“G-Great Hero.”
“I understand that you’re afraid, but it’s possible. You saw with your own eyes how we got here.”
I had suffered a minor internal injury, but I was still in good shape.
On top of that, we had Cheongpung, a Supreme Peak master, and Gung Gibang, who possessed exceptional martial arts. Hyuk Mujin could also lend a hand in an emergency.
No matter how bad the weather or how violent the current, it wasn’t enough to declare the journey impossible.
The old boatman thought differently.

“I’ve held an oar on Dongting Lake for more than forty years. Today was the first time I’ve ever ferried great masters like you, but it was also the first time I’ve ever launched a boat in weather this vicious.”
The old boatman struggled to get the words out, his voice trembling.
“All I know how to do is read the water and row a boat. I’m an unremarkable old man, but I’ve spent more than half my life on Dongting Lake. If it can’t be done, it can’t be done.”
“Boatman.”
Gung Gibang stepped forward, but before he could say anything, the boatman shook his head repeatedly.
“I know what you’re going to say. But no matter how skilled you are, it’s clear you won’t make it very far.”
“Why do you think that?”
“The boat won’t hold up.”
At the boatman’s firm declaration, everyone—including me—stared with wide eyes.
He was right. No matter how sturdy it was, a ferryboat was still a ferryboat.
To find the Dongting Fisherman’s secret refuge, the boat had needed to be light and small. It had been perfect for that purpose, but those same advantages were now its greatest weaknesses.
*Even by the shortest route, it’ll take at least two shichen to reach land... What if the boat sinks before then?*
The answer to my own question came back immediately.
*No.*

*Even if I used my internal energy to perform Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water, the distance left is too great. And that was before the weather became like this. The boatman is right. The boat won’t hold.*
Even at a glance, I could see patches where wood had been torn from the surface of the ferryboat pulled up onshore.
Like its white-haired owner, the ferryboat was showing its age, and today’s currents and voyage had been especially rough.
*Damn it.*
This wasn’t something I could solve by persuading the boatman.
I could use the Water Rescue Worker Title’s effect, which still had plenty of time remaining, or try the same method of using the Inventory that I had used at Dongting Lake before.
But no matter how I considered the situation, the risk was too great.
“Captain.”
At Hyuk Mujin’s voice, I raised my head and saw everyone looking at me.
Under their gazes, I thought for a moment, then bit my lip.
“What about the route leading in?”
“Pardon?”
I spoke clearly to the old boatman, who had hunched his shoulders at another peal of thunder.
“If it’s difficult to get out, wouldn’t it also be difficult to get in? Especially in conditions like these.”

“Ah, of course it would. The passage is so narrow that nothing but a ferryboat like mine could enter, and with these insane currents, getting in would be several times harder than getting out. Launching a boat on Dongting Lake in weather like this is madness to begin with.”
Then that was even better.
It meant the weather would naturally prevent any possible incursion by Dark Heaven as well.
*We should wait here until the weather settles down.*
I had just finished that thought and was about to give the order when—
*Jerk. Jerk-jerk-jerk!*
Someone nearby suddenly began to move.
I and the others turned our heads toward its source and opened our eyes wide at the same time.
*What the hell?*
The small old man who had been lying motionless as though dead—the Dongting Fisherman—was twitching.
Even as we watched, the trembling running through his body grew faster and stronger.
“He was definitely under Pressure-Point Strikes... How?”
Cheongpung muttered the words like a groan.
As the person who had struck the Dongting Fisherman’s pressure points, I could not easily accept what was happening either.
But my surprise lasted only a moment.
Before my mind could fully process the situation, my body was already moving.
*Swish!*
I shot forward like a gust of wind and thrust out my hand at top speed.
First, the Sleep Acupoint.
Next, the Paralysis Acupoint.
Finally, the Mute Acupoint.
The instant I finished striking his pressure points again, I realized something I hadn’t expected.
*His acupoint seals had never come undone in the first place. This was simply... the Dongting Fisherman’s body reacting independently of his will.*
I faltered in confusion.
*Grab!*
A hand seized my wrist, which had been left hanging in midair.
The Dongting Fisherman was staring at me, his eyes wide open.
Unlike in the cave, his pupils looked like those of an ordinary person.
They were filled with fear.
And then a hollow voice, empty as though his soul had left his body, pierced my ears.
“Run.”
*What?*
I had no time to form a question.
I wasn’t given a chance to react.
The moment every sense in my body went taut, an enormous roar erupted behind me.
*Kaboom—!*

paragraphs: *Rumble-rumble-rumble, crash!*
It was a storm unlike anything anyone had ever experienced.
Every time thunder boomed alongside the lightning, the rain grew heavier, and the river thrashed like a violent dragon.
And one ship was trying to fight its way against it all.
“Hard to port!”
The ship rocked like a willow leaf amid the raging waves. At Ship-Fire Boy Mu Song’s shout from the stern, the river bandits of Water Dragon Stronghold gritted their teeth.
“Grrrrgh!”
“Keep rowing! Put your asses into it and row!”
“Anyone who slacks off from this moment on had better watch out! What was it called again? Right! I’ll sentence you to the dip-and-taste punishment!”
“Aaaaaah!”
Every one of them was a seasoned, highly skilled sailor.

But despite Mu Song’s experienced commands and the river bandits’ efforts to summon every last ounce of strength, the worst weather they had ever encountered refused to let the ship advance any farther.
*Crash! Boom!*
The sail, swollen almost to the point of tearing, was driven back by the force of the wind. Rocks large and small flew in from every direction and slammed into the deck.
Disbelief flashed through Mu Song’s eyes at the impossible sight.
*What in the world is this?*
Martial arts were not the only thing he had learned from his Master, the Seafaring King.
If anything, he had first learned how to steer all sorts of ships, predict the weather, and read the currents—before he had learned martial arts.
Mu Song had been a sailor before he was a Murim martial artist, and no river bandit would follow an incompetent captain.

The little boy who had once yearned for the Yangtze had grown into a captain skilled enough to earn the respect of even old sailors. Even his coldhearted Master, who had not shown his Disciple the slightest hint of affection, had once said:
“It’s a shame. If your grit and martial talent had been even half as good as your skill with ships, you might have taken your Senior Brother’s place.”
There could not be two masters of the Yangtze River Channel League.

The Seafaring King had already chosen his Senior Disciple as his successor, so he sent Mu Song to Sichuan. After founding Water Dragon Stronghold, Mu Song soon distinguished himself and seized control of Sichuan’s stretch of the Yangtze at a young age.
Yet even Mu Song had never seen anything like this.
His Master, the Seafaring King, and the old river bandits who had spent their entire lives as sailors before retiring had probably never seen it either.
*It wasn’t like this when we left the Yangtze tributary. So how...?*
The reason was simple.
The weather had changed with shocking speed.
And they were currently on none other than Dongting Lake.

After receiving Zhuge Feng’s sudden summons, Mu Song had selected his most capable subordinates, crossed Tianling Falls, and immediately headed for Dongting Lake after asking around for Jin Taekyung’s whereabouts.
Not long afterward, they had run into a storm more suited to the middle of the sea.
*Is this even possible? On Dongting Lake?*

Hubei Province’s climate was generally warm. Its annual rainfall was fairly consistent, and although the Yangtze occasionally flooded, the flooding was rarely severe. In fact, it was one of the reasons the region had become such a fertile breadbasket.
Dongting Lake? It was certainly one of the three largest lakes under heaven, but it was still only a lake.
No matter how bad the weather became, it should not have been worse than the Yangtze’s currents. Compared to the unpredictable whirlpools of the sea, it should have been laughable.
That was what he had believed.
At least until two *shichen* ago.
*It wasn’t this bad when we first launched the ship.*

He had not been particularly worried. Since Dongting Lake was not connected to the Yangtze or the sea routes, there was no way to bring a swift ship here. They had borrowed a small merchant vessel instead and headed for the place where Jin Taekyung’s group was said to have gone.
Or rather, they had tried to.
Unlike at the beginning, the weather had grown steadily worse the closer they came to their destination.
It was as though they had crossed some invisible line. Strange phenomena that should not have been possible on a lake were appearing everywhere.
*Whoooooosh.*
A waterspout rose with a chilling howl of wind.
It towered to a dizzying height, blocking the narrow waterway as it advanced toward the merchant vessel. A groan slipped between Mu Song’s clenched teeth.
“What the fucking hell is this...?”
If they were caught in that, it was over. Even if they managed to get past the waterspout, a merchant vessel this flimsy would not survive for long.
Torn between concern for his subordinates’ safety and his desire for revenge against Dark Heaven, which had killed Yangtze One Saber, Mu Song finally spoke.
“I’m sorry, but I’m afraid this is as far as we can go.”
An old voice answered him.
“That’s enough.”
And then—
*Swish!*
Behind Mu Song, a small figure that had remained perfectly balanced leaped from the mast.
He shot toward the waterspout through the driving rain and wind, then clenched his fist.
*Hooooong.*
A single stream of wind wrapped around the fist mottled with age spots. The air stopped moving, and not a single drop of rain dared approach.
At the tip of that fist, hellfire capable of burning everything took shape.
“Get the hell out of my way.”
With a voice like boiling lava, Fire King Jeok Cheongang threw a punch.
*Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.*
*Whoooooosh!*
The next moment, Mu Song and the river bandits saw it clearly.
The flames rising from the fist transformed into a fire dragon and bit into the waist of the waterspout.

The churning water collapsed in an instant beneath the overwhelming Scorching Yang Qi, every trace of moisture evaporating. The waterspout, which had been bearing down on the merchant vessel with the force of ten thousand *geun*, became a dense cloud of steam that spread around them like fog.
Then—
*Boom!*
The heavy sound of something splitting the air scattered the steam.
Jeok Cheongang stood tall in midair, looking down at the merchant vessel. His voice, more deeply subdued than usual, drifted from his lips.
“What are you waiting for? Hurry up and follow me.”
He was not speaking to Mu Song or the river bandits under his command. Their roles had been decided from the beginning, and they had more than fulfilled them.
Only true masters belonged on the battlefield ahead.
And as everyone watched, one person stepped forward.
“Single Reed Crossing the River. Even Master Bodhidharma of Shaolin used a reed leaf to cross a river. From now on, you’d better come down instead of wasting your internal energy for no reason.”
Not a trace of emotion could be found in the flat, dry voice.
The bright, warm boy who had been caring for the sick as a medical apprentice only a short while ago was nowhere to be found.
As Mu Song and the river bandits flinched and moved aside, Mungyeong clicked his tongue inwardly.
*Dong Feng. You foolish Disciple. In the end, things turned out exactly as you wanted.*
He had lived as a medical apprentice for more than forty years.
With hands that had taken more than a thousand lives, he had treated and cared for the sick.
Instead of fiends, he had hunted the bastard called plague. He had gained the undeserved reputation of being a Divine Physician, but he had never once accepted wealth or sought fame.
It had merely been atonement.
And a vow.
But now, the stone pagoda he had built deep within his heart over decades of living as a medical apprentice had come crashing down.
No—perhaps it had collapsed the day he boarded the swift ship leaving Sichuan.
*This too is the path this old man chose. How could I blame anyone else?*
With a dry chuckle, he stepped forward. Behind him appeared a middle-aged man in disheveled scholar’s robes.
“This junior will go with you, Seniors.”
At the words of Zhuge Feng, the current Family Head of the Zhuge Clan and the Crouching Dragon Guest, Mungyeong answered in a dry voice.
“Of course you should. Why else would I bring a burden like you?”
“You certainly have a talent for embarrassing people.”
Mungyeong made a show of frowning. He had no intention of listening to Zhuge Feng ramble, especially when the man was no more than a babe compared to him.
“Enough nonsense. Get on my back.”
“You underestimate this junior. My enlightenment may not match that of the other Family Heads of the Five Great Families, but when it comes to internal energy alone...”
“There’s a reason I brought you here. If I had prioritized martial arts, I would have brought that youngster Hyeongong of Wudang instead. But shouldn’t someone remain back there?”
Perfected Being Hyeongong was a master whose seniority placed him alongside the Sect Leaders of the Nine Sects and One Gang.

Mu Song and the river bandits had been unable to determine Mungyeong’s identity beyond knowing that he was a Returned to Youth master. They were shocked to hear him refer to Perfected Being Hyeongong, a respected elder throughout Murim, as a child.
“Gasp!”
“Who in the world is that man...?”
But Mungyeong had neither the time nor the inclination to answer.
He extended a hand, and Zhuge Feng’s body came sliding toward him.
After seizing none other than the current Family Head of the Zhuge Clan with Seizing an Object Through Empty Space, Mungyeong lightly pushed off the deck and soared like a bird.
*Swish!*
A movement technique both stealthy and impossibly elusive.
Not a single person left aboard the ship could recognize the Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step at its pinnacle.
Leaving the stunned men behind, Mungyeong’s body shot forward as though folding space.
“Is this the right direction?”
*Splash!*
Two—no, three figures sped forward, their feet stepping across the water.
Zhuge Feng, dangling from Mungyeong’s hand, answered Jeok Cheongang.
“According to what Ship-Fire Boy told us, we only need to keep heading straight from here.”
“Are you certain?”
“Of course. However...”
“However?”
After hesitating for a moment, Zhuge Feng continued.
“We still don’t know whether Jin Taekyung is there.”
“He is. Without a doubt.”
Jeok Cheongang immediately shook his head. His tone was nearly one of certainty.

sentences.text: *Rumble-rumble-rumble, crash!*
It was a storm unlike anything anyone had ever experienced.
Every time thunder boomed alongside the lightning, the rain grew heavier, and the river thrashed like a violent dragon.
And one ship was trying to fight its way against it all.
“Hard to port!”
The ship rocked like a willow leaf amid the raging waves.
At Ship-Fire Boy Mu Song’s shout from the stern, the river bandits of Water Dragon Stronghold gritted their teeth.
“Grrrrgh!”
“Keep rowing!
Put your asses into it and row!”
“Anyone who slacks off from this moment on had better watch out!
What was it called again?
Right!
I’ll sentence you to the dip-and-taste punishment!”
“Aaaaaah!”
Every one of them was a seasoned, highly skilled sailor.

But despite Mu Song’s experienced commands and the river bandits’ efforts to summon every last ounce of strength, the worst weather they had ever encountered refused to let the ship advance any farther.
*Crash!
Boom!*
The sail, swollen almost to the point of tearing, was driven back by the force of the wind.
Rocks large and small flew in from every direction and slammed into the deck.
Disbelief flashed through Mu Song’s eyes at the impossible sight.
*What in the world is this?*
Martial arts were not the only thing he had learned from his Master, the Seafaring King.
If anything, he had first learned how to steer all sorts of ships, predict the weather, and read the currents—before he had learned martial arts.
Mu Song had been a sailor before he was a Murim martial artist, and no river bandit would follow an incompetent captain.
The little boy who had once yearned for the Yangtze had grown into a captain skilled enough to earn the respect of even old sailors.
Even his coldhearted Master, who had not shown his Disciple the slightest hint of affection, had once said:
“It’s a shame.
If your grit and martial talent had been even half as good as your skill with ships, you might have taken your Senior Brother’s place.”
There could not be two masters of the Yangtze River Channel League.
The Seafaring King had already chosen his Senior Disciple as his successor, so he sent Mu Song to Sichuan.
After founding Water Dragon Stronghold, Mu Song soon distinguished himself and seized control of Sichuan’s stretch of the Yangtze at a young age.
Yet even Mu Song had never seen anything like this.
His Master, the Seafaring King, and the old river bandits who had spent their entire lives as sailors before retiring had probably never seen it either.
*It wasn’t like this when we left the Yangtze tributary.
So how...?*
The reason was simple.
The weather had changed with shocking speed.
And they were currently on none other than Dongting Lake.

After receiving Zhuge Feng’s sudden summons, Mu Song had selected his most capable subordinates, crossed Tianling Falls, and immediately headed for Dongting Lake after asking around for Jin Taekyung’s whereabouts.
Not long afterward, they had run into a storm more suited to the middle of the sea.
*Is this even possible?
On Dongting Lake?*
Hubei Province’s climate was generally warm.
Its annual rainfall was fairly consistent, and although the Yangtze occasionally flooded, the flooding was rarely severe.
In fact, it was one of the reasons the region had become such a fertile breadbasket.
Dongting Lake?
It was certainly one of the three largest lakes under heaven, but it was still only a lake.
No matter how bad the weather became, it should not have been worse than the Yangtze’s currents.
Compared to the unpredictable whirlpools of the sea, it should have been laughable.
That was what he had believed.
At least until two *shichen* ago.
*It wasn’t this bad when we first launched the ship.*
He had not been particularly worried.
Since Dongting Lake was not connected to the Yangtze or the sea routes, there was no way to bring a swift ship here.
They had borrowed a small merchant vessel instead and headed for the place where Jin Taekyung’s group was said to have gone.
Or rather, they had tried to.
Unlike at the beginning, the weather had grown steadily worse the closer they came to their destination.
It was as though they had crossed some invisible line.
Strange phenomena that should not have been possible on a lake were appearing everywhere.
*Whoooooosh.*
A waterspout rose with a chilling howl of wind.
It towered to a dizzying height, blocking the narrow waterway as it advanced toward the merchant vessel.
A groan slipped between Mu Song’s clenched teeth.
“What the fucking hell is this...?”
If they were caught in that, it was over.
Even if they managed to get past the waterspout, a merchant vessel this flimsy would not survive for long.
Torn between concern for his subordinates’ safety and his desire for revenge against Dark Heaven, which had killed Yangtze One Saber, Mu Song finally spoke.
“I’m sorry, but I’m afraid this is as far as we can go.”
An old voice answered him.
“That’s enough.”
And then—
*Swish!*
Behind Mu Song, a small figure that had remained perfectly balanced leaped from the mast.
He shot toward the waterspout through the driving rain and wind, then clenched his fist.
*Hooooong.*
A single stream of wind wrapped around the fist mottled with age spots.
The air stopped moving, and not a single drop of rain dared approach.
At the tip of that fist, hellfire capable of burning everything took shape.
“Get the hell out of my way.”
With a voice like boiling lava, Fire King Jeok Cheongang threw a punch.
*Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.*
*Whoooooosh!*
The next moment, Mu Song and the river bandits saw it clearly.
The flames rising from the fist transformed into a fire dragon and bit into the waist of the waterspout.
The churning water collapsed in an instant beneath the overwhelming Scorching Yang Qi, every trace of moisture evaporating.
The waterspout, which had been bearing down on the merchant vessel with the force of ten thousand *geun*, became a dense cloud of steam that spread around them like fog.
Then—
*Boom!*
The heavy sound of something splitting the air scattered the steam.
Jeok Cheongang stood tall in midair, looking down at the merchant vessel.
His voice, more deeply subdued than usual, drifted from his lips.
“What are you waiting for?
Hurry up and follow me.”
He was not speaking to Mu Song or the river bandits under his command.
Their roles had been decided from the beginning, and they had more than fulfilled them.
Only true masters belonged on the battlefield ahead.
And as everyone watched, one person stepped forward.
“Single Reed Crossing the River.
Even Master Bodhidharma of Shaolin used a reed leaf to cross a river.
From now on, you’d better come down instead of wasting your internal energy for no reason.”
Not a trace of emotion could be found in the flat, dry voice.
The bright, warm boy who had been caring for the sick as a medical apprentice only a short while ago was nowhere to be found.
As Mu Song and the river bandits flinched and moved aside, Mungyeong clicked his tongue inwardly.
*Dong Feng.
You foolish Disciple.
In the end, things turned out exactly as you wanted.*
He had lived as a medical apprentice for more than forty years.

chapters.title: Chapter 469
paragraphs: Everyone saw it. They could see it.
Amid the blackened sky and the violent wind and rain, a shower of strangely shaped rocks came crashing down.
*Rumble-rumble-rumble, crash!*

When a massive boulder struck the lake, spray erupted several *jang* into the air. Birds that had lost their nests tumbled from the collapsing cliff with shrill cries, while torrential rain and lightning battered the world without pause.
And as everything collapsed around them... one being alone reared up.
*Whoooooosh!*
Water cascaded down its body like a waterfall.
Far below, the humans reduced to tiny dots gazed up at the being that had finally revealed itself, their eyes filled with stunned disbelief.
It was enormous.
Even that word felt inadequate, yet no other came to mind.
Only one question filled everyone’s thoughts.
*What is that?*
Scales gleamed with an ominously beautiful black sheen. Its body was so thick that ten burly men with their arms outstretched could barely have encircled it.
Their gazes traveled up the long, sinuous body, more than thirty *jang* of it visible above the surface, until they reached two horns jutting from its forehead.
And beneath them, its eyes.
Blood-red pupils stretched into long vertical slits. As the scales around its mouth slowly parted, they revealed saw-edged teeth and a maw like a dark cavern.
*Grrrrr.*
The vicious growl echoing down from far above sent a chill deep into the bones of Crouching Dragon Guest Zhuge Feng.
*What in the world...?*
Zhuge Feng had been called the greatest genius in his clan since infancy.

He possessed an extraordinary mind that never forgot anything he had seen, along with an insatiable thirst for knowledge. Over the years, he had devoured tens of thousands of books and made the vast knowledge of the world his own.
The river of knowledge within Zhuge Feng was endlessly broad and deep.
Or so he had thought.
Until he saw that.
*This cannot be.*
For the first time in his life, he felt the fear of confronting the unknown.
At that moment, Zhuge Feng realized that all the knowledge and information he had accumulated had turned to foam.
He also realized that fragments of the countless myths and legends he had dismissed as nonsense now stood before his eyes.
*Could those absurd stories... truly have been real?*
Zhuge Feng had always placed absolute faith in the power of knowledge.

He was a martial artist, but first and foremost, he was the Family Head of the distinguished Zhuge Clan, and he had used reliable information and knowledge to protect his many clansmen and his family’s power.
To a man like him, unverified superstition was not even worth considering. Believing in an illusion no one had ever seen was simply foolish.
But someone a hundred *jang* away from Zhuge Feng was different.
Unlike Zhuge Feng, he was not a Family Head responsible for an entire household. He was merely an old boatman who had survived by relying on his own experience and a single ferryboat.
The old boatman stared into the sky with trembling eyes.
A colossal being stood tall amid the collapse of everything around it. The sight alone made his legs buckle, while unbearable awe and fear pressed down on his shabby shoulders.
The cry that the crushing pressure kept him from voicing echoed only in his heart.
*It’s the divine spirit. The divine spirit of Dongting Lake has revealed itself!*
The world was filled with more superstitions than anyone could count, and Hubei Province was no exception.
An old man told a child, and when that child grew old, he told another child. Stories passed from mouth to mouth for hundreds of years.
The old boatman was no different.
A native of Hubei Province who had spent his entire life on the water, he knew the identity of the being he called a divine spirit.
The Two-Horned Beast of Dongting Lake.
The Water God Dragon.
The true master of Dongting Lake.
*Ah... ahhh...*
The old boatman trembled violently. His entire body shook beneath an emotion he could not understand, and something swelled within his chest.
It was an emotion only he, among everyone present, could feel.
Awe and fear too profound to put into words.
A boatman to the marrow of his bones, he could not believe that he had come face-to-face with the master of Dongting Lake. The aura flowing from that being left him struggling to breathe.
*The divine spirit is angry. All of this happened because the divine spirit was enraged!*
The old boatman realized that his guess had been correct.
The countless deaths that had occurred one after another over the past month. He did not know why, but the divine spirit had certainly been angered beyond measure.
And in the end, it would punish him just as it had punished the others.
With death!
He could not die like this. Somehow, he had to calm the divine spirit’s anger.
A cracked cry burst from the old boatman’s mouth as he stood there, entranced.
“D-Divine Spirit! This humble one has committed no sin!”
The silence that had settled over everyone shattered. The old boatman’s cry scattered into the wind and rain.
Before the others, frozen rigid by the colossal being’s appearance, could stop him, the old boatman ran toward the water on trembling legs.
“Divine Spiriiit!”
*Tap-tap-tap, splash!*
The instant the old boatman’s shabby straw sandals touched the water of Dongting Lake—
*Swish.*
In a world that had slowed to a crawl, a gigantic pair of eyes turned toward him.
The old boatman’s reflection appeared in those blood-red vertical pupils. As the creature registered the tiny, insignificant human, the light in its eyes blazed crimson.
*Whoooooosh!*
A chilling aura erupted in every direction from the thirty-*jang* body.
Birds in flight lost their strength and plummeted. Thousands of fish fleeing in schools through the depths of Dongting Lake floated belly-up to the surface.
An aura as immense as its body, an aura akin to death.
Neither insignificant creatures nor even humans could remain unharmed before it.
Before that invisible aura even reached him, the old boatman’s entire body had already stiffened like a stone statue.
His mouth hung open, his eyes bulged wide. Just as his pupils began to roll white beneath the grip of terror—
*Whoosh! Thud!*
A sharp whistle cut through the air, and the old boatman crumpled where he stood.
A young man gently caught his frail body, then raised his head and stared at the enormous being.
“Hey, you fucking eel bastard.”
At the clear voice, the enormous being’s pupils swelled as though it had realized something.
Different.
Every other human on the ground had frozen from shock and fear, but this young man was different. He was neither stunned nor trembling.
Fear of the unknown came from confronting something incomprehensible.
But that young man was free from it all. More than fearless, he almost seemed accustomed to this.
Just like now.
“Can’t you open those eyes properly?”
With that offhand remark from the young man, Jin Taekyung, a streak of light tore through the air.
*Whoooooosh! Bam!*
When I first saw the thing, only one thought flashed through my mind.
*Am I seeing things?*
I could hardly have thought otherwise. A monster I had seen somewhere before had appeared right in front of me—not in the modern world, but in Murim.

If it had merely been an illustration in some fantasy novel, that would have been one thing. Unfortunately, I recognized it from the *Monster Encyclopedia*, compiled over the past several decades by countless leading scholars and Hunters who had fought in the Great Cataclysm.
*Could that be...?*

Although the monsters I had fought most often during my Hunter career had been low-level creatures like goblins, the section I had looked at most in the *Monster Encyclopedia* was the one covering the highest-level monsters.
And that thing was one of the monsters given a particularly large entry.
*...A Sea Serpent.*
As its name suggested, a Sea Serpent was a marine monster.

In the early days of the Great Cataclysm, a Sea Serpent had announced its existence to the entire world by sinking a US carrier battle group. For some reason, it vanished shortly after the Great Cataclysm.
No, let me correct that.
At least, that had been true until a moment ago.
*A Sea Serpent in Murim? What the hell is going on...?*
I had frozen in shock, but I soon noticed something strange.
*Wait. Something’s different.*
In the modern world where I had been born and raised, the Sea Serpent was not some fictional monster that appeared only in mythology.
It was one of the highest-level monsters serving the Demon King Asmodeus, as well as one of the major culprits responsible for inflicting terrible damage on humanity.
Naturally, there were high-resolution photographs showing exactly what it looked like, along with preserved video recordings of its battles.
But the monster before me was clearly different from the Sea Serpent depicted in the *Monster Encyclopedia*.
*The Sea Serpent looks more like an actual sea snake, but that thing is closer to an Eastern dragon.*
The more closely I looked, the more certain I became. There were subtle differences in the size and length of its body, as well as the shape of its face.
But these two similar yet different monsters did share one crucial trait.
*Whoooooosh!*
It was that.
An inherently ferocious aura possessed only by monsters—fundamentally different from what martial artists called killing intent.
*Fear.*
Fear was exactly what it sounded like: terror and dread.
Every monster possessed it, but the stronger the monster, the more powerful its Fear became.
It shackled an enemy’s body by instilling fear and terror, then shattered the enemy’s mind.
*Just like the Dongting Fisherman.*
The scattered puzzle pieces in my head began falling into place.
The Dongting Fisherman’s state, which had seemed almost insane. His clear eyes returning only after all his strength had drained away.
*He must have encountered that thing before we did.*
Even a Supreme Peak master with immense martial prowess and an unshakable mind could be overwhelmed by the terror of confronting the unknown for the first time.
When it came to resisting Fear, an S-rank Hunter was probably far better equipped than even a Supreme Peak martial artist.
And...
*That goes for me too.*
*Ding.*
**System** You resisted **Fear**! A powerful mind overcomes terror!
*Whoosh, thud!*
I caught the old boatman’s collapsing body as I struck his pressure points.
One second. No, even a quarter of a second later, and the poor old man might have gone mad from Fear—or simply died.
I raised my head and looked at the enormous being towering in the distance.
*Damn. It’s huge.*
I had never fought a Sea Serpent, but this thing was clearly no pushover.
It had just taken a spear I had hurled with all my strength and still hadn’t fallen.
*Bam!*
With a heavy impact, the colossal body, more than thirty *jang* long, swayed slightly.
It was like watching a small mountain move. I bit my lip.
*I couldn’t pierce its scales.*
I could tell from the sound alone. Even after pouring all my strength into the iron spear I had pulled from my Inventory and hurled, I had failed to inflict any meaningful damage.
If I had used White Flame, forged from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, I could have dealt a more decisive blow.
But if I could not finish it in One Strike, that would be a foolish move.
It was more urgent to act before the enormous monster recovered from its confusion.
I turned and drew a deep breath as I pulled internal energy up from my dantian.
“Cheongpung! Hyuk Mujin! Gung Gibang!”
“Hup!”
“Urgh!”
A thunderous shout erupted from my mouth, so loud I could scarcely believe it had come from me. The three men, frozen like stone statues, flinched.
No.
Not three. Two.
Unlike Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin, whose eyes looked as though half their souls had fled their bodies, Cheongpung was staring at me in surprise.
“You startled me. What is it, Benefactor?”
*What the hell is this guy?*
Anyone would freeze after seeing a monster like that. I was the exception because I had grown up in the modern world, surrounded by monsters until I was sick of them.
But Cheongpung had been born and raised in Murim. The fact that he could overcome Fear so easily was astonishing.
“Cheongpung. Are you really all right?”
“Huh? About what?”
“I mean, that thing over there...”
“Oh, right. I was really surprised.”
Cheongpung threw both arms wide and exclaimed emphatically.
“It’s huge! Really huge! I’ve never seen anything like that in my life!”
*I hadn’t thought that through.*
*Cheongpung had been out of his mind from the beginning.*
