chapters.title: Chapter 474
paragraphs: *Kwadeudeuk!*
The instant Jin Taekyung ripped out dozens of whiskers at once, the Mutated Water God Dragon opened wide its one remaining eye.
—Krrrrrk...!
It could not believe it.
That tiny, insignificant human had torn out its whiskers—with his bare hands, without even a weapon.
It was impossible. It should have been impossible. Even for the Water God Dragon, which had lived for hundreds of years, this was a shocking first.
Then, in the next moment, the Water God Dragon realized something.
The human who had ripped out its whiskers through sheer physical strength was completely fucking insane.
“Baldy!”
*Pop!*
“Baldy!”
*Pop-pop!*
“Smooth, shiny baldy!”
*Pop-pop-pop-pop-pop!*
—Gwooooooooooar!
A scream rose from the depths of its soul.
The Mutated Water God Dragon thrashed and howled in agony. For some inexplicable reason, the pain and sorrow surging through it were dozens of times worse than when it had first lost its eye.
It had to get this mad human off it as quickly as possible.
No—before every last whisker was torn out, it had to save at least one!
—Kroaaaaaah!
But despite the Water God Dragon’s desperate wish, Jin Taekyung had no intention of stopping.
*Puhuk!*
Jin Taekyung drove the spearhead between the scales covering the bridge of its nose, anchoring himself in place, and spoke in a sinister voice.
“Hey, know why you can’t walk?”
—Krrk...?
“Because you don’t have two feet.”
*Pop-pop-pop-pop-pop!*
—Gwooooooar!
“Multiply the number of hairs on every spiritual creature in the world together and you still get zero. Because you don’t have any hair. You just don’t. You don’t have a single goddamn hair!”
*Kwadeudeudeuk!*
Jin Taekyung’s methods were more ruthless than ever.

Whenever the whiskers flew at him in a tangled mass, he caught them with one hand and yanked them out like weeds. Iron-hard skin split open, and the whiskers—tougher and sharper than Heavenly Silkworm Thread—were ripped out by the roots.
Every last one of them. Not a single strand remained.
—Uooh, uwooooooar!
Even through its reason, now as murky as a sky smothered by storm clouds, the Mutated Water God Dragon was consumed by overwhelming rage and sorrow.
What kind of whiskers were these?
Those whiskers had grown alongside it for hundreds of years. They were companions to its very soul.
They were excellent weapons for destroying intruders who harbored impudent thoughts, and symbols of its power and majesty.
And now they were gone. They had been pulled out as helplessly as weak, useless seaweed.
By the hands of a human far smaller and more insignificant than itself!
—Kyaaaaaaaaaow!
A savage roar shook heaven and earth.
As the master that had ruled Dongting Lake and the Yangtze for hundreds of years radiated its baleful presence, everything around it held its breath.
No. Everything changed in response to its fury.
*Krrrrrung! Kwa-gwang!*

It was a truly frightening and bizarre sight. Lightning struck without pause from a sky shrouded in unusually thick black clouds, while rain poured down in a deluge unlike anything seen in the past fifty years.
Swollen several times over by the abnormal weather of the past several shichen, the river formed whirlpools large and small that circled the Water God Dragon.
*Kwaaaaaaaaa!*
And in the middle of that landscape, which resembled a minor catastrophe, stood an enormous body towering like a steel tower.
At the sight of the monster, its eye glowing bloodred, the people on the ground groaned quietly.
“Good heavens.”
“Damn it. This old man really has lived a long time. I never thought I’d see something so absurd.”
Jeok Cheongang and Mungyeong stared at the unbelievable scene in astonishment.
They had long known that beings called spiritual creatures and evil creatures possessed astonishing power, but what was unfolding before them lay far beyond anything they had imagined.
A monster as large as a small mountain.
When it swung its tail, cliffs collapsed. When it roared, the world shook in every direction.
And that was not all. Mountains, rivers, plants, and trees held their breath beneath its surging baleful presence, while lightning and water responded to its fury.
Something that belonged in an old, faded legend was happening in reality.
At that moment, a single thought arose in the minds of the two old masters.
*Supernatural powers.*
Things of the strange, prodigious force, rebellion, and ghosts.
Everything embodied by that four-character phrase was unfolding before them.
An inexplicable being and phenomena beyond the understanding of even two men who had spent long years in the Murim were appearing before their eyes.
But the words *supernatural powers* did not belong to only one being.
*Kwadeuk!*
The sound of flesh tearing rang out clearly even amid the thunder and lightning.
The next moment, scales drenched in dark-blue blood poured down over Jeok Cheongang and Mungyeong’s heads.
One, two, three...
Soon, dozens of scales pattered down like a sudden shower.
With eyesight like birds of prey, the two men saw what was happening high above and were rendered speechless.
“Flesh! Let’s see the flesh underneath!”
*Kwadeudeudeuk!*
A young man shouted like a lunatic as his hands moved furiously.
One hand gripped the shaft of his spear with all his strength. The other held no weapon at all as his bare fingers seized a scale.
Then he yanked hard.
The scale tore free helplessly, trailing dark-blue blood.
—Kwoooooooooar!
The Mutated Water God Dragon thrashed its enormous body and let out a savage cry, but it was useless.

Whenever Jin Taekyung caught a hint of an attack, he darted like a ghost into the gaping hollow where its eye had melted away. Once the monster’s rampage ended, he popped his head back out and resumed his work.
He even threw in a few furious punches for good measure.
“You fucking bastard!”
*Kwaang! Kwang! Kwajijik!*
The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, one of the five most destructive techniques among the Fire Gate Clan’s various secret arts, combined with strength tremendous enough to call him superhuman.
The monster’s head, nearly the size of an average ship, shook violently as shattered scales rained down.
—Kyaaaaaaaaaow!
The Mutated Water God Dragon was at its wits’ end.
When it still had its whiskers, it had at least been able to attack.
But now that every last one had been pulled out, it had no idea what to do.
Whenever it thrashed to throw him off, he held on with the spear driven into its flesh. Whenever it seemed to calm down, he emerged and tore off more scales.
What the hell was it supposed to do?
Perhaps because it had smashed its head against the cliff so many times, it was even beginning to feel dizzy.
*Kwaang! Kwaaaaaang!*
Mungyeong and Jeok Cheongang could only open and close their mouths as they watched.
*This fucking lunatic...*
*What is he doing? It’s not like he’s pulling radishes out of the ground...*
Both men knew just how durable those scales were, which only made the sight more astonishing.
The crude Sword Energy of someone who had only just entered the Peak realm could barely cut them. Only Force could reliably split the scales and damage what lay beneath.
Those bizarre scales were absurdly hard.
And yet that young whelp had simply smashed them apart and ripped them off.
With nothing but his bare hands.
*Did he draw up every last bit of his internal energy? Even so, a human’s physical strength should be nowhere near enough.*
*What in the... No, wait. That bastard could do it.*
Mungyeong felt as though he were dreaming.
Jeok Cheongang, who had watched Jin Taekyung ever since Shanxi Province, found the whole thing absurd—and astonishing.
“What a goddamn lunatic! Hahahaha!”
It was not enough that Jin Taekyung had torn out every whisker, one of the monster’s weapons. Now he had begun stripping away its scales as well.
For a martial artist, it was like breaking all their weapons and stripping away the armor worn over their martial uniform.
From Jeok Cheongang’s perspective, Jin Taekyung’s current insight into martial arts was clearly inferior to that of both old masters—and even below Cheongpung’s.
But his very foundation was different.
*He’s simply strong.*
As a martial artist, Jin Taekyung was a powerful fighter who had reached the Supreme Peak realm.
Yet even if the internal energy and martial insight he had accumulated over several jiazi vanished, he would still be strong in his own right.
It was as though the power of heaven had taken residence in a human body made of mere flesh.
“Is that truly possible?”
Faint astonishment colored Mungyeong’s voice.
Jeok Cheongang laughed with delight.
It was a question he had asked himself countless times while training in the Fire Gate Cavern. And every time, Jin Taekyung had responded with an infuriatingly shameless answer.
Now it was time to pass that answer on to someone else.
“Yeah. Heavenly Martial Physique.”
“Absurd, isn’t it? Good. Don’t bother trying to understand. That bastard has always been like that.”
Just as Jeok Cheongang shrugged, Cheongpung spoke with a determined expression.
“Come on, let’s go too. Mimi! Strike with lightning! Whip up a whirlwind!”
...*Chirik, chiriririk?*
“Oh. You can’t.”
“...That idiot’s no different.”

Just as Jeok Cheongang threatened to make Cheongpung drink liquor made from a Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake if he spouted one more load of bullshit, an eerie silence and oppressive presence bore down upon everything within a radius of several dozen *jang*.
*Gugugugugung!*
Jeok Cheongang, Mungyeong, and Cheongpung felt a chill run down their spines and raised their heads.
*Goooooooong.*
The air rippled.
By then, the wind and rain that had been pouring down without pause had stopped.
So did the lightning.
Everything held its breath.
Everyone on the ground saw the monster’s bloodred pupil, which had been shedding a crimson aura, slowly turn pitch-black.
At the same time, its enormous maw slowly opened, revealing cavernous darkness, while a sphere of water churned as though being sucked into its depths.
*What is that?*
A single question flashed through everyone’s mind.
Then a shout came from high above.
No—a scream.
“Get out of the way—!”
Before they could even realize that the voice belonged to Jin Taekyung, the three figures shot away like the wind.
Though there were differences between them, great and small, each was a Supreme Peak master and an experienced martial artist with exceptional combat instincts.
They could not discern the true nature of that thing, but they could tell how terrifying the unknown power within it was.
Their prediction proved exactly right.
*Kwaaaaaaaaa—!*
With a deafening roar, the enormous sphere of water shot toward the ground.
There are many different kinds of monsters.
Some are bipedal, with bodies resembling humans. Others are beast-type monsters that walk and run on four legs like animals, yet are hundreds of times stronger than those bipedal monsters.
Their Intelligence varies just as widely from species to species.
Some are simple-minded brutes, but their insane physical abilities have earned them a place among the higher-level monsters.
Others, like goblins, hunt in packs and employ tactics involving poison and ambushes, but are classified among the lowest-level monsters because of their poor physical abilities.
With monsters possessing such diverse traits, arguments are inevitable whenever the subject comes up—both among actual experts and every fucking know-it-all on the internet.
Even so, when people talk about the strongest monsters, there is one type that everyone names first.
*Dragonkin.*
Beings blessed with extraordinary Intelligence and physiques.
And the mighty power granted exclusively to them.
*Breath.*
But why on earth?
Why?
Why?
*Kwaaaaaaaaaah!*
...Why the hell was this bastard using Breath?

Mountains, rivers, plants, and trees held their breath beneath its surging baleful presence, while lightning and water responded to its fury.
Something that belonged in an old, faded legend was happening in reality.
At that moment, a single thought arose in the minds of the two old masters.
*Supernatural powers.*
Things of the strange, prodigious force, rebellion, and ghosts.
Everything embodied by that four-character phrase was unfolding before them.
An inexplicable being and phenomena beyond the understanding of even two men who had spent long years in the Murim were appearing before their eyes.
But the words *supernatural powers* did not belong to only one being.
*Kwadeuk!*
The sound of flesh tearing rang out clearly even amid the thunder and lightning.
The next moment, scales drenched in dark-blue blood poured down over Jeok Cheongang and Mungyeong’s heads.
One, two, three...
Soon, dozens of scales pattered down like a sudden shower.
With eyesight like birds of prey, the two men saw what was happening high above and were rendered speechless.
“Flesh!
Let’s see the flesh underneath!”
*Kwadeudeudeuk!*
A young man shouted like a lunatic as his hands moved furiously.
One hand gripped the shaft of his spear with all his strength.
The other held no weapon at all as his bare fingers seized a scale.
Then he yanked hard.
The scale tore free helplessly, trailing dark-blue blood.
—Kwoooooooooar!
The Mutated Water God Dragon thrashed its enormous body and let out a savage cry, but it was useless.
Whenever Jin Taekyung caught a hint of an attack, he darted like a ghost into the gaping hollow where its eye had melted away.
Once the monster’s rampage ended, he popped his head back out and resumed his work.
He even threw in a few furious punches for good measure.
“You fucking bastard!”
*Kwaang!
Kwang!
Kwajijik!*
The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, one of the five most destructive techniques among the Fire Gate Clan’s various secret arts, combined with strength tremendous enough to call him superhuman.
The monster’s head, nearly the size of an average ship, shook violently as shattered scales rained down.
—Kyaaaaaaaaaow!
The Mutated Water God Dragon was at its wits’ end.
When it still had its whiskers, it had at least been able to attack.
But now that every last one had been pulled out, it had no idea what to do.
Whenever it thrashed to throw him off, he held on with the spear driven into its flesh.
Whenever it seemed to calm down, he emerged and tore off more scales.
What the hell was it supposed to do?
Perhaps because it had smashed its head against the cliff so many times, it was even beginning to feel dizzy.
*Kwaang!
Kwaaaaaang!*
Mungyeong and Jeok Cheongang could only open and close their mouths as they watched.
*This fucking lunatic...*
*What is he doing?
It’s not like he’s pulling radishes out of the ground...*
Both men knew just how durable those scales were, which only made the sight more astonishing.
The crude Sword Energy of someone who had only just entered the Peak realm could barely cut them.
Only Force could reliably split the scales and damage what lay beneath.
Those bizarre scales were absurdly hard.
And yet that young whelp had simply smashed them apart and ripped them off.
With nothing but his bare hands.
*Did he draw up every last bit of his internal energy?
Even so, a human’s physical strength should be nowhere near enough.*
*What in the...
No, wait.
That bastard could do it.*
Mungyeong felt as though he were dreaming.
Jeok Cheongang, who had watched Jin Taekyung ever since Shanxi Province, found the whole thing absurd—and astonishing.
“What a goddamn lunatic!
Hahahaha!”
It was not enough that Jin Taekyung had torn out every whisker, one of the monster’s weapons.
Now he had begun stripping away its scales as well.
For a martial artist, it was like breaking all their weapons and stripping away the armor worn over their martial uniform.
From Jeok Cheongang’s perspective, Jin Taekyung’s current insight into martial arts was clearly inferior to that of both old masters—and even below Cheongpung’s.
But his very foundation was different.
*He’s simply strong.*
As a martial artist, Jin Taekyung was a powerful fighter who had reached the Supreme Peak realm.
Yet even if the internal energy and martial insight he had accumulated over several jiazi vanished, he would still be strong in his own right.
It was as though the power of heaven had taken residence in a human body made of mere flesh.
“Is that truly possible?”
Faint astonishment colored Mungyeong’s voice.
Jeok Cheongang laughed with delight.
It was a question he had asked himself countless times while training in the Fire Gate Cavern.
And every time, Jin Taekyung had responded with an infuriatingly shameless answer.
Now it was time to pass that answer on to someone else.
“Yeah.
Heavenly Martial Physique.”
“Absurd, isn’t it?
Good.
Don’t bother trying to understand.
That bastard has always been like that.”
Just as Jeok Cheongang shrugged, Cheongpung spoke with a determined expression.
“Come on, let’s go too.
Mimi!
Strike with lightning!
Whip up a whirlwind!”
...*Chirik, chiriririk?*
“Oh.
You can’t.”
“...That idiot’s no different.”

Just as Jeok Cheongang threatened to make Cheongpung drink liquor made from a Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake if he spouted one more load of bullshit, an eerie silence and oppressive presence bore down upon everything within a radius of several dozen *jang*.
*Gugugugugung!*
Jeok Cheongang, Mungyeong, and Cheongpung felt a chill run down their spines and raised their heads.
*Goooooooong.*
The air rippled.
By then, the wind and rain that had been pouring down without pause had stopped.
So did the lightning.
Everything held its breath.
Everyone on the ground saw the monster’s bloodred pupil, which had been shedding a crimson aura, slowly turn pitch-black.
At the same time, its enormous maw slowly opened, revealing cavernous darkness, while a sphere of water churned as though being sucked into its depths.
*What is that?*
A single question flashed through everyone’s mind.
Then a shout came from high above.
No—a scream.
“Get out of the way—!”
Before they could even realize that the voice belonged to Jin Taekyung, the three figures shot away like the wind.
Though there were differences between them, great and small, each was a Supreme Peak master and an experienced martial artist with exceptional combat instincts.
They could not discern the true nature of that thing, but they could tell how terrifying the unknown power within it was.
Their prediction proved exactly right.
*Kwaaaaaaaaa—!*
With a deafening roar, the enormous sphere of water shot toward the ground.
There are many different kinds of monsters.
Some are bipedal, with bodies resembling humans.
Others are beast-type monsters that walk and run on four legs like animals, yet are hundreds of times stronger than those bipedal monsters.
Their Intelligence varies just as widely from species to species.
Some are simple-minded brutes, but their insane physical abilities have earned them a place among the higher-level monsters.
Others, like goblins, hunt in packs and employ tactics involving poison and ambushes, but are classified among the lowest-level monsters because of their poor physical abilities.
With monsters possessing such diverse traits, arguments are inevitable whenever the subject comes up—both among actual experts and every fucking know-it-all on the internet.
Even so, when people talk about the strongest monsters, there is one type that everyone names first.
*Dragonkin.*
Beings blessed with extraordinary Intelligence and physiques.
And the mighty power granted exclusively to them.
*Breath.*
But why on earth?
Why?
Why?
*Kwaaaaaaaaaah!*
...Why the hell was this bastard using Breath?

chapters.title: Chapter 475
paragraphs: The Mutated Water God Dragon.
When you got right down to it, this bastard was a dragon too.
It might have been closer to an *imugi* than a true dragon, considering it could neither roam beneath the azure heavens nor wield a dragon pearl.
But there was one problem...
This bastard with its murky identity knew how to use Breath.
And not just any Breath. A fucking powerful one.
*Kwaaaaaaaaaah!*
I stared with my mouth hanging open as an enormous sphere of water spread across a radius of several dozen *jang*.
The ground, built up layer upon layer over centuries by sediment flowing from the Yangtze, collapsed by nearly half in an instant.
*This is insane.*
A force far beyond ordinary water pressure.
That was not merely an enormous quantity of water gathered together and fired all at once.
With the Mutated Water God Dragon’s immense qi infused into the sphere, it was only right to call it Water Breath from now on.
*Water Breath in the Murim.*
It would have been more natural if some insane undead monster had insisted it was from Atlanta, Georgia, in the United States.
I stared in horror as the Water Breath vomited by the Water God Dragon pulverized everything in its path.
At the same moment, three figures shot away from the ground being reduced to a wasteland.
“Mimi, blow up the water orb!”
“...You’re completely insane. I felt murderous intent for a moment there without even realizing it.”
“That’s normal. This old man has wanted to kill you about five times already.”
One lunatic pestering a horned snake. One rejuvenated old man. And one old man who could hardly look any older.
Once I confirmed that all three were safe, a sigh of relief escaped me.
*Thank goodness they dodged it.*
If they took a direct hit from Breath with that level of destructive power, even a Supreme Peak master could not escape unharmed.
The Water Breath fired by the Mutated Water God Dragon was that powerful. It contained qi that far surpassed the Breath of the Black Wyvern I had personally killed in the past.
*What the hell? It was strong before, but I don’t remember it being this strong...*
Was it the effect of Berserk? Or had it only now drawn out all the power lying dormant within it?
I did not know the exact cause, but it unquestionably had something to do with its pupil suddenly turning black.
And my goal right now was to bring this bastard down by any means necessary.
—Krrrrrrk.
Its pitch-black pupil gleamed.
The monster let out a low growl at the humans who had dodged its attack with the speed of a streak of light, then opened its maw again.
*Goooooong.*
Along with an immense flow of qi, the waterspouts circling it surged upward as though being sucked into its gaping jaws.
*Already...?*
A second Water Breath.
Even wyverns, the modern world’s quintessential dragonkin monsters, could not use Breath this quickly or this frequently.
This thing was on an entirely different level.
Before the Water Breath could be completed, I swung with all my strength and slammed my fist into the bridge of its nose as its jaws slowly opened.
“You gaping bastard!”
*Kwaang!*
The enormous head shook with a deafening boom.
The sudden jolt made the rapidly forming sphere of water falter. But despite accomplishing what I had intended, my expression hardened.
*It’s different.*
That punch had carried all my strength.
Yet the resistance I felt through my fist was nothing like it had been only moments earlier.
Breath was not the only change that had occurred in the Mutated Water God Dragon. Its body had grown stronger as well.
To put it simply, it felt as if a punch that should have smashed through ten pine boards had stopped after breaking only five.
I clenched my teeth.
*Damn it.*
I should have adapted my approach to the situation, but I had been too complacent. I grabbed White Flame, which I had shoved between the dragon’s scales.
*Store in Inventory. Open. Summon.*
*Shhk!*
In the blink of an eye, White Flame vanished as though dissolving into empty space, passed through my Inventory, and reappeared in my grasp.
Every movement had been pared down to the absolute minimum. It was something impossible without the System, and even I had only recently begun to master this application.
The moment White Flame’s shaft settled into my hand, all my preparations were already complete, and I brought it down in a single strike.
*Fwoosh!*
Blue-white flames rose over the transparent spearhead, burning the air and evaporating the moisture filling the surroundings.
The flames sliced through the dense, foglike steam toward the black-scaled bridge of the monster’s nose.
“Shut your mouth.”
Heavenly Strike.
*Kwaaaaaaaaaah—schk!*
The immense flames summoned by burning internal energy split the scales. They burned through flesh and shattered bone.
Even flesh of astonishing toughness could not stop a strike that fused Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron with Force.
Behind everything cleaved apart to either side of the spearhead was the nearly completed sphere of water.
*Cut.*
The centuries-old Water God Dragon’s Water Breath met the fire dragon’s claw plunging down like a lightning bolt from the heavens.
No.
They collided head-on.
*Gooooooong—*
Along with a deafening boom that numbed my ears, red and blue flashes filled my vision.
That day, those present at the scene were not the only ones who heard the mysterious roar.
Everyone staying near Dongting Lake heard it.
*Gugugugugung!*
Mountains, rivers, and trees bowed beneath a tremendous boom unlike any peal of thunder.

Commoners who had shut themselves indoors to avoid the ominous atmosphere flung themselves facedown in shock, while government troops roaming near Dongting Lake to investigate the incident dropped their spears and fled in terror.
Elderly men patted their sobbing grandchildren and gazed worriedly at the sky as they muttered,
“It’s the divine spirit. The divine spirit has grown angry and brought heavenly punishment down upon someone. What is going to become of this wretched world...?”
They were half right and half wrong.
The divine being passed down by word of mouth for hundreds of years, from the distant past to the present day, had indeed existed.

But the spirit beast once worshiped as a divine spirit had degenerated into a hideous evil beast, and the heavenly punishment delivered by the enraged Mutated Water God Dragon had been blocked by a single human.
Deep in a part of Dongting Lake that no one ever visited, the battle between that human and the evil beast continued even now.
—Kroaaaaaaaaah!
A pained roar shook heaven and earth in every direction.
The monster, its maw torn open, writhed and threw its body onto the waters of Dongting Lake.
*Kwa-gwa-gwa-gwa!*
The river water, mixed with dark-blue blood, surged to a distant height in an instant.
Waves fit for the distant open sea rose and crashed in every direction. Three figures no larger than specks beside the monster’s enormous body darted just ahead of them.
*Shweeeeeek!*
Three figures shot through the air like arrows.
But one of them chose a direction completely opposite to the other two.
Seeing Jeok Cheongang charge alone toward the monster instead of dodging, Mungyeong sent a Sound Transmission.
“Fire King!”
But rather than answer, Jeok Cheongang thrust one palm toward the oncoming wave.
*Poom!*
With a heavy crack of displaced air, a hole burst through the center of the enormous wave about to swallow his small, aged body, and the water evaporated into steam.
A second and third wave soon came rolling in, driven by the monster’s ceaseless, pain-filled thrashing.
But the next moment, they were cleanly sliced apart.
*Shraak!*
A pure-white streak of light had severed the waves through their middles.
Then Cheongpung’s scattered Sword Energy mingled with the spray and reduced the pebbles flying through it to dust. Mungyeong shook the water from his short sword and spoke to Jeok Cheongang.
“There are a few things I want to ask. Did you happen to learn water arts since we last saw each other?”
Jeok Cheongang glanced at Mungyeong and answered bluntly.
“Do you know what this old man hates most in the world?”
“First, getting wet. Second, setting a mountain on fire. And third—the last one—watching a mountain burn while I’m soaking wet. Those three things.”
“What does that have to do with—”

“It was about fifty years ago. I’d just finished taking a bath I didn’t want in a nearby valley, and when I came out, Mount Jiuhua was going up in flames. In the end, I hunted down and killed every last one of those sons of bitches.”
It was a story every martial artist knew.
After that day, an old man who had been practicing martial arts deep in the mountains of Mount Jiuhua gained the name Fire King.

“Well, things worked out well enough, and the people around me started praising me as the Fire King and whatnot. But some insane bastards pointed fingers behind my back. They called me a Killing Ghost of an old man who could kill a thousand people without batting an eye.”
Mungyeong frowned at Jeok Cheongang’s attitude. The old man was not even looking at him, simply saying whatever he pleased.
“I have no idea what you’re talking about. What kind of nonsense is—”

“It’s nothing. To put it simply, this old man liked Mount Jiuhua. I liked it even more because it was the first home I could call my own. During the Great Faction War, I drilled it into every bastard under heaven that I’d crush anyone who touched what belonged to me, no matter what it took. But...”
Jeok Cheongang walked toward the writhing monster, his eyes blazing as he continued,
“That damned bastard doesn’t seem to know that. Then again, if it had known, it wouldn’t have touched my Disciple without a shred of fear.”
“You really do whatever you please. So after all that, you never learned water arts.”
“Damn it. We’ll manage somehow.”
“We’re hardly friends, but even I feel compelled to tell you to be careful.”
“Do water arts really matter when dealing with one lousy eel? I’ll hunt it down and crush it by any means necessary.”
Cheongpung joined in with an innocent voice.
“Wow. Do eels really get that big? Are they all about fifty *jang* long?”
“I feel the urge to kill rising.”
“If you’re going to kill him, ask the Sword Saint for permission and do it quietly. Of course, lend us a hand first.”
Mungyeong lightly adjusted his grip on his short sword, then suddenly spoke.
“Did Jin Taekyung happen to learn water arts?”
“I vividly remember training him in the deep valleys of Mount Jiuhua. I’ve never seen anyone so bad at swimming in my life.”
“...Then we’ll have to drag that monster onto land immediately.”
“I agree. I don’t want to lose my Disciple twice.”
If the battle took place underwater, it went without saying that the Water God Dragon would have the advantage.
But there was no other choice.
If they did not step in, Jin Taekyung would drown.
Just as Jeok Cheongang and Mungyeong exchanged determined looks, Cheongpung suddenly spoke.
“Huh? That’s not right. Benefactor is really good at swimming.”
“It’s true. On the way here, Benefactor... Uh, what was it again? Oh, right. He asked me to call him Aguaman.”
What the hell was that supposed to mean?
The two old masters stopped short, confusion rising in their eyes.
At that very moment—
—Gwoooooooooar!
*Shraaaaaaaaaah!*
Along with a roar echoing from deep beneath the river, a human figure shot up through the surface.
Jeok Cheongang’s jaw dropped when he recognized the familiar face amid the spray exploding in every direction.
“You, you...”
“Pwah! Form up!”
“W-What did you say?”
There was no time to resolve his confusion.
The instant the words left his mouth, a huge shadow rippled across the rolling surface.
At the same time, a thunderous shout burst from Jin Taekyung’s lips as he landed on the ground.
“Form an attack formation!”
What burned in his eyes was not the look of a martial artist.
It was the look of a seasoned Hunter.

Along with a roar echoing from deep beneath the river, a human figure shot up through the surface.
Jeok Cheongang’s jaw dropped when he recognized the familiar face amid the spray exploding in every direction.
“You, you...”
“Pwah!
Form up!”
“W-What did you say?”
There was no time to resolve his confusion.
The instant the words left his mouth, a huge shadow rippled across the rolling surface.
At the same time, a thunderous shout burst from Jin Taekyung’s lips as he landed on the ground.
“Form an attack formation!”
What burned in his eyes was not the look of a martial artist.
It was the look of a seasoned Hunter.

chapters.title: Chapter 476
paragraphs: *When was it?*
I once saw a line like that in an old wuxia film whose title I no longer remember.
“Martial arts are only vertical and horizontal. In the end, one of us falls and the other remains standing.”
It was true. The countless battles I had fought in Murim had always ended in one of two ways.
*Either I knocked them down, or they knocked me down.*
Except for the Blood Lord, who had escaped even after losing an arm, the outcome had always been one or the other—and it had never been me who fell.
But when I plunged into the deep river while clinging to the Mutated Water God Dragon, I remembered another possibility I had briefly forgotten.
*What if this bastard runs?*
He had effectively been the master of Dongting Lake and the Yangtze for hundreds of years.
They said even a mutt had half the battle won in its own yard. If the bastard decided to run, there was no way I could stop him.
At the same time, I realized that I had been laboring under a serious misconception.
*This shouldn’t have been a battle. It should have been a hunt.*
This was not a life-and-death duel between two martial artists.
To bring down the monster before me, I had to do whatever it took, by any means necessary.
I had lived as a Hunter for seven solid years, yet without realizing it, I had been pretending to be some hidebound martial artist. I couldn’t help laughing quietly at myself.
*What a stupid thing to do.*
Hunter and martial artist. Martial artist and Hunter.
Both were part of my identity. I was the one and only modern martial artist—and Murim’s Hunter.
Standing once more on the blurred boundary between them, a line that had nearly faded away, I reminded myself of that fact.
*That’s right. This is it.*
It felt as though I had awakened from a very long sleep. I landed lightly on the shore and let out a thunderous shout.
“Form an attack formation!”
The flow of the air changed in an instant, and three pairs of eyes widened. Of the three, Jeok Cheongang and Mungyeong stared at me with trembling eyes before speaking.
“I coddle you a little, and now a greenhorn still wet behind the ears dares speak casually to this old man?”
“The Fire King made a complete mess of training his Disciple.”
“...I apologize. It slipped out.”
I’d forgotten who was standing here.
I must have lost my head after getting swept up in the moment.
Unlike the two old men glaring at me with their eyes blazing, Cheongpung responded enthusiastically.
“Benefactor, that was so cool! Mimi! Form an attack formation!”
*Chirik!*
“I swear to heaven and earth that one day, I will turn that snake bastard into liquor—”
Jeok Cheongang’s oath never reached its conclusion.
The enormous shadow wavering across the rolling surface finally burst through the water and revealed itself.
—Kroaaaaaaaaah!
A roar more savage than any before shook heaven and earth.
Overwhelming qi exploded from its body, as large as a small mountain, and bore down on everything around it. The air trembled beneath the Fear it released.
At the center of it all, dozens of *jang* above us in the distant sky, was a pitch-black pupil looking down at us.
When that single eye, formed from darkness without even a speck of light, gleamed, a groan escaped someone’s lips.
Fear of the unknown.
Everyone except Cheongpung and me remained at least partly vulnerable to the Fear emitted by the Mutated Water God Dragon.
Even Supreme Peak masters counted among the greatest in the world were no exception.
But...
*I’m here.*
I was a veteran Hunter who had fought monsters until I was sick of them. That was who I was.

I had stood my ground against an undead army numbering in the tens of thousands, rotten flesh dangling from their bodies as they charged. I had no reason to tremble in fear just because one eel the size of an aircraft carrier had joined the fight.
“Now that I look at you again, you’re practically a fairy.”
The words had barely left my mouth before the back of my head began to prickle. From the listener’s perspective, it probably sounded like complete madness.
But what I had just said was one hundred percent sincere.
*It’s true that this bastard is powerful, but the Arch Lich was much harder to deal with—and much stronger.*
If the Skeleton King hadn’t helped me back then, I would have died without question.
But the important thing was that I had survived and brought the bastard down. The fear I had felt while facing the Arch Lich had become experience, carved into my body and mind in its entirety.
*And I’m a fast learner.*
Good or bad, every experience became part of me. Over the past seven years, I had learned how to survive and how to win.
I drew a deep breath and raised White Flame’s shaft high into the air.
Then I slammed the end down with all my strength. A level of internal energy never seen before rode the shaft.
*Goooooong!*
The wave of qi that shot outward with the deafening boom pushed back the Fear radiating from the dragon.
The crushing pressure that had completely surrounded us dissipated as though an invisible pane of glass had shattered.
“This is...”
Jeok Cheongang and Mungyeong stared at me in astonishment. I kept my eyes fixed on the dragon and spoke.
“First. Don’t get scared for no reason.”
Everyone carried fears, great and small, inside their hearts. Fear was a force that preyed upon those fears and turned them into terror.
But once that fear was stripped away, we could finally recognize something we had forgotten.
—Krrrrrrrr.
The enormous monster letting out that low growl was not as powerful or frightening as we had imagined.
I stared straight into its gleaming, pitch-black pupil and continued.
“Second. From this point on, follow my instructions and beat the shit out of that bastard without mercy.”
Mungyeong’s dry voice pierced my ears.
“I do not particularly care for the process, but the result sounds rather pleasant.”
“You don’t dislike it because of that, do you?”
“What do you take me for?”
“That was a stupid question.”
The Slaughter Saint.
The greatest assassin, past or present, in Murim’s long history.
To an assassin who eliminated a target by any means necessary, the process did not matter. Only the result did.
“Old Master.”
“As far as this old man remembers, I never taught you how to deal with an evil beast like that... We can discuss it after we finish the bastard off.”
*Tssssss!*
After Jeok Cheongang’s curt reply, Cheongpung answered with purple Sword Force instead of words.
It was a nightmare of a party composition: nothing but DPS, without a healer or a tank. Even so, there could not have been a more powerful raid team.
*Four Supreme Peak masters.*
A lineup impressive enough to make even a five-star Jangsu stone bed weep.
Compared to the enormous body of the Mutated Water God Dragon, we were no more than ants. But inside each of us crouched a giant carrying an unprecedented power.
And now, the four giants were going to hunt a colossal monster.
“You’re dead now.”
As if it understood me, the Mutated Water God Dragon raised its enormous body from beneath the surface and roared.
—Gwooooooooooar!
*Krrrrung, kwaaaaaaaaaang!*
With a single roar, dozens of waterspouts rose and came crashing toward us. Between them, the dragon’s ragged maw split wide.
*Gooooooooong—!*
The air vibrated faster and more powerfully than before.
But before the third Water Breath could take shape, a shout burst from my lips and pierced the wind and rain to reach everyone’s ears.
“Spread out!”
*Shwish-shwish-shwish-shwish!*
As though following a prearranged signal, four figures shot away in different directions and took positions around the dragon.
At last, it was time for the hunt.
Raid.
When the unreal invaded reality and Hunters and monsters began fighting one another to the death, this word—once used only in fantasy games—became something even a three-year-old child knew.

But none of the billions of people who had survived the Great Cataclysm could have imagined that another raid was taking place somewhere beyond time and space, against a strange monster resembling a dragon.
Nor could they have imagined that a familiar face was caught up at the center of it all.
*Tat-tat, shweeeeeek!*
A solidly built figure bounded off fragments of flying rock and shot skyward.
A massive tail passed within a hair’s breadth, smashing into a half-collapsed cliff and unleashing a blast of wind.
Through his streaming hair, the eyes of the young man—Jin Taekyung—gleamed.
*If I cut that tail now... No. Don’t.*
Jin Taekyung restrained the hand that instinctively wanted to swing his spear.
He knew exactly what mattered most in this raid.
He had to block the Mutated Water God Dragon’s escape, lure it as far onto land as possible, and dispatch it in a flash.
If he struck back and wounded it before then, he might only put the monster on guard.
Of course, someone watching the scene had a slightly different opinion.
“You fucking piece of—!”
*I can’t lose the Disciple I only managed to gain in my old age like this!*
But Jeok Cheongang’s movement as he prepared to launch a palm strike at the monster, accompanied by a thick curse, abruptly stopped at the shout that rang out the next moment.
“Old Master!”
*Fwoosh, kwaaaaaaaaaang!*
The Scorching Yang Qi hastily veered aside and burned the innocent ground.
For the briefest instant, puzzlement passed through the dragon’s pitch-black eye. Then it changed into the eye of a savage beast.
—Gwoooooooooar!
*Whoom, bang!*
With a roar, its enormous tail swept across the ground like a broom.
Jeok Cheongang leaped into the air at the last instant to evade the attack and exploded in frustration.
“How long are you planning to make us retreat!”
*Kwaang!*
Far above the ground, Jin Taekyung dodged the monster’s body as it came crashing toward him and answered.
“I told you I’d give the signal!”
“And when is that going to be?”
“I’ll handle it when the time comes, so please stop shitting all over the place! There’s only so much trolling I can take! Do what you’re told like everyone else!”
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes trembled.
Some of the strange words prevented him from understanding exactly what Taekyung meant, but he had heard one thing perfectly clearly.
*A dump? This old man is taking a dump?*

Until recently, he had been worried that his infirmities of old age might progress to the point where he started smearing feces on the walls. Now the boy he considered his Disciple was saying something that vile to him.
The shout that followed jolted Jeok Cheongang out of his shock.
“Old Master, now! Fall back thirty *jang*! Cheongpung, move behind the bastard! Mungyeong, take the flank!”
“Yes, Benefactor!”
“What a strange fellow. I agreed to follow your lead, not to let you speak casually to me.”
“For fuck’s sake, I really can’t stand ranged-DPS assholes who refuse to communicate. Just listen to me!”
Seeing Mungyeong struck speechless, clamp his mouth shut, and silently do as he was told improved Jeok Cheongang’s mood slightly.
*At least he calls me Old Master.*
He should have been angry. But seeing Mungyeong addressed by his bare name like some nobody from next door made Jeok Cheongang grateful that Taekyung had not simply called him Cheongang.
At the same time, he thought he understood Mungyeong’s feelings as he moved without another word.
*What is this strange feeling?*
How should he put it?
Jin Taekyung was radiating an almost absurd air of command.
And in Jeok Cheongang’s estimation, it was not the overwhelming presence or bearing of a Supreme Peak master.
It was more like...
*A veteran. Yes, exactly. A battle-hardened veteran.*
Jeok Cheongang had lived his entire life as a martial artist. He had never had any connection to the authorities, nor had he ever been a soldier.
Yet for some reason, he felt as though he understood what it was like for a fresh recruit on the battlefield to stand before a battle-hardened veteran.
“What an incredibly strange fellow, no matter how many times I look at him...”
“Hey, Jeok Cheongang! Snap out of it!”
The corner of Jeok Cheongang’s eye twitched. But before he could unleash his anger, the words he had been waiting for finally rang out.
“Now—strike!”
*Shwish-shwish-shwish-shwish!*
The four giants shot forward at the same time toward the Water God Dragon, which had finally left the waters of Dongting Lake and climbed onto land.

paragraphs: *Shwish-shwish-shwish-shwish!*
Front, back, left, right.
The instant the Mutated Water God Dragon noticed four figures shooting toward it from every direction, its one remaining eye widened.
—Krrk!
*When did they...?*
Even in Berserk Status, the Mutated Water God Dragon could tell the situation was turning against it.
But rage had paralyzed its reason, and the immense power contained within its large, beautiful body led the strange and terrifying evil beast to underestimate its opponents.
Then someone shouted.
That was enough to sever the last thread of reason that had barely registered the danger.
“Even if everyone else curses you, I believe you’re a good guy. Because you don’t have a single rough edge.”
—Krrrrrr...!
A murderous light flashed in its pupil, which was nearly as large as a grown man.
It did not matter what that tiny, insignificant human was babbling about.
All that mattered was that he was the one who had ripped out every last whisker—the dragon’s pride, its finest weapon, and practically its soulmate for hundreds of years.
*Kill him.*
*No matter what it takes, I will kill that fucking human!*
*Whooooooosh!*
Its enormous tail, filled with murderous intent, blasted apart everything in its path.
At the end of that path, one man’s lips curled into a faint smile.
“Got you, you son of a bitch.”
*What?*
A chill swept through the Mutated Water God Dragon’s entire body, but it was already too late.
With that much force and speed behind it, pulling its tail back was as impossible as recalling an arrow after it had been fired.
*Whoom, boom!*
Everything was crushed beneath the violently swinging tail.
The cliff that had barely been holding together collapsed completely, and the resulting roar swallowed every other sound.
But what awaited the Mutated Water God Dragon was not the thrill of crushing its enemy.
It was searing pain.
*Fwoosh, thk!*
No.
It was not imagining things.
The next moment, the Mutated Water God Dragon saw it clearly.
Through the slowly dispersing wind, rain, and clouds of dust, a spear wreathed in blue-white flames had pierced straight through its large, beautiful tail.
And the fucking human gripping that spear was smiling.
“Got you.”
My mother had always been lenient when it came to raising her children.

She never believed studying was the only path to success. Even when she saw my high school report card—sevens in every subject, like I’d hit the slot-machine jackpot—she ended her lecture with one short remark.
“Amazing, my son...”
Hmm. Now that I thought about it, she may already have given up on me halfway by then.
In any case, even she made me read books when I was young.
I think it was in elementary school. She saw me folding paper airplanes out of an English workbook and flying them around, so she handed me a book and told me to read that instead.
The title was...
Oh, right.
*Gulliver’s Travels.*
Even though I had no talent for studying, I enjoyed novels like that. Sometimes, I even reenacted memorable scenes from them with Hayeon.
For example, the scene where the Lilliputians tied Gulliver down with ropes.
“Mom! Look! I caught Hayeon! She’ll be quiet now!”
“Waaaaaah! Mommy!”
“No! Hayeon! My daughter!”
Of course, my curiosity did not end particularly well.

When my mother saw her young daughter bound from head to toe in blue packing tape, she screamed. Then she used a *hyojason* to beat the calves of the son who had just proven himself decidedly unfilial.
But with a tenacity unusual for an elementary schooler, I did not shed a single tear.
I did, however, reflect on where I had gone wrong.
“Next time, I need to tape her mouth shut too, so she can’t scream!”
Ah, what fond memories.
The vicious elementary schooler who had bound his much younger sister in blue packing tape was long gone, but the memory of that day remained vivid.
Along with the ambition I had held as a child: to tie up Gulliver just like in the novel.
*Thk!*
That’s right.
Just like now.
Remembering the childhood dream I had thought would never come true, I spoke.
“Got you.”
My method was more brutal than the one the Lilliputians had used on Gulliver, but it was undeniably effective.
I had predicted that the bastard would swing its tail. I dodged just before the enormous, hideous thing lashed across my body, then drove my spearhead in with all my strength.
White Flame, the sturdy, transparent divine weapon, became a massive nail that pierced through both the monster’s tail and the ground beneath it.
*What about a hammer?*
Obviously, that would be my fist.
And I still had plenty of nails left.
*Open Inventory. Summon.*
*Thk-thk-thk-thk-thk!*
It all happened in an instant.
I summoned five spears from my Inventory in a flash and drove them into the bastard’s tail. Then I brought my fist down in place of a hammer.
*Boom! Boom! Booooom!*
*Anchoring complete.*
My powerful punch struck the ends of the spear shafts. The sharp spearheads sank deep into the ground and trembled.
*Hayeon, are you watching?*
I trembled with satisfaction at the sight.
The Mutated Water God Dragon screamed in agony.
—Gwoooooooooar!
But its scream seemed a little premature to me.
Three people who had been waiting for this exact moment were just about to unleash attacks with everything they had.
The fastest among them arrived first and swung his sword at the dragon’s waist.
*Shk—!*
Ghostlike movement.
Speed too great for even my eyes to follow completely.
Nothing could stop the dazzling flash that burst from that gray-white shadow.
Not even scales hardened further by Berserk Status.
Not even flesh and bone as tough as iron.
It was none other than the Slaughter Saint’s sword strike.
*Shrrk!*
A clear sound of cutting pierced through the confusion of battle and reached my ears.
Mungyeong’s figure, having dealt a devastating blow with the fastest and most concise sword strike in existence, vanished in a blur.
Dark blood erupted like a waterfall, and a scream of agony burst from the monster’s maw.
—Kuaaaargh!
The attack had not severed its torso completely, but a single strike had sliced through nearly one-fifth of its thickness.
Of course it screamed.
But there was one thing I wanted the bastard to know.
This was not over yet.
“Two more strikes.”
Before I had even finished speaking, purple Force resembling the glow of sunset shot forward and lit the darkness.
*Shwish-shwish-shwish-shwish!*
Dozens of red plum blossoms appeared amid the swirling wind and rain.
That was no illusion.
I instantly recognized the trails drawn by the purple Force infused with the Zaha Divine Technique, known as the essence of Huashan.
*The Plum Blossom Sword Technique.*
If Mungyeong’s sword was a razor-sharp guillotine that severed its target in a single blow, Cheongpung’s Plum Blossom Sword Technique was a dagger that slashed and carved dozens of times.
Now that dagger had taken the shape of plum blossoms and was plunging into the split wound.
*Thk-thk-thk! Shrrk!*
Bringing down an enormous opponent was surprisingly simple.
Either hit it with one tremendous blow powerful enough to knock it flat, or keep pounding the same spot.
And make it hurt like hell.
Before the Mutated Water God Dragon could unleash yet another scream, someone came rushing in to deliver a blow that combined both methods.
“Can’t you just fucking die, you motherless evil-beast bastard!”
A streak of flame tore across the battlefield, accompanied by a filthy insult about the bastard’s parents that was wildly unbecoming of his age.
*The Fire King.*
The illegal resident of Mount Jiuhua.
The firebug of the Great Faction War.
A national-level thug who had dominated the Murim with seniority as insane as Bodhidharma’s skull water and martial arts even more explosive.
Just looking at him made my heart race and my eyes burn.
*Ah, fuck it.*
Whatever happens, happens. I’d already dropped the formalities anyway.
Once you were riding a tiger, there was nothing left to be afraid of.
Feeling my blood boil, I shouted at the top of my lungs.
“Go, Fire King! Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist!”
“You fucking little—!”
I could not tell who he was cursing, because the enormous boom that followed drowned him out.
*Fwoosh, kwaaaaaaang!*
Flames erupted from his fist and shot forward, vaporizing every trace of moisture in their path.
Hellfire carrying unimaginable heat tore into the gaping wound created by the previous two attacks, burning and devouring everything inside.
—Kraaaaaaaaaah!
I remembered hearing somewhere that death by fire was the most painful death in the world.
Anyone who saw this scene would have no choice but to agree completely.
Heat filled the air on every side, hot enough to conjure visions of a fiery hell, along with the thick, acrid stench of burning flesh.
And in the middle of it all, a gigantic monster writhed, engulfed in hellfire.
A terrible scream unlike anything we had heard before shook the ground and drove back the waters of Dongting Lake.
Its agony made it thrash so violently that even I, gripping the embedded spears with all my strength, could no longer hold on.
*Thk, thud-thud-thud!*
When Gulliver came to his senses and broke free of the ropes the Lilliputians had bound him with, what had they thought as they stared up at the giant rising above them?
I could not know for certain.
But at least I was neither shocked nor flustered.
“Well, look at you.”
It made no difference anyway.
The three hardcore ranged-DPS addicts—or rather, three Supreme Peak masters—had followed my orders perfectly, and the Mutated Water God Dragon had suffered devastating damage.
Even if it pulled out the spears embedded in its tail and gathered Water Breath now, nothing would change.
*Shiiiiing, tap!*
*Seizing an Object Through Empty Space.*
Like the other spears, White Flame had been torn free by the force of the dragon’s tail and sent spinning through the air.
Then it was sucked into my hand.
I raised White Flame’s spearhead, slick with dark-blue blood, and pointed it at the bastard.
“From now on... hack apart anything you can reach.”
My voice came out as hot as lava.
The three people who had grown accustomed to waiting for my orders sprang into action like beasts freed from their leashes.
*Snap!*
Jeok Cheongang, Mungyeong, Cheongpung—and me.
The first and strongest raid team in the history of the Murim shot toward the enormous body of the monster writhing in agony.
*Shweeeeeek!*
Four superhumans stepped out toward four different points.
And four streaks of Force carried unprecedented power.
*Shwish-shwish-shwish-shwish! Shrrk!*
*Fwoosh, kwaaaaaaang!*
East, west, south, north.
Above, below, left, right.
There was no opening through which the dragon could escape and no direction in which it could dodge.
They were everywhere.
And nowhere.

Its body, as large as a small mountain, was the largest target imaginable. Its mangled tail could overturn river and earth alike, but it could not touch the figures flashing around it like streaks of light.
The Mutated Water God Dragon.
The greatest advantage of this corrupted being, which had spent hundreds of years growing to its immense size, had now become its greatest weakness.
—Kroooooooooar!
There was no shield that could not be broken.
No door that could not be opened.
In a span too brief to even call a moment, dozens of streaks of Force carved the monster’s body apart and left it in a horrifying state.
Its dangerously beautiful jet-black scales shattered into pieces.
Its flesh and bones, so tough that ordinary blades could not even scratch them, had long since been slashed and crushed beyond recognition.
*Craaaack, shaaaaaah!*
Dark-blue blood gushed from its wounds and soaked the earth.
The thunder and lightning that had struck without pause began to fade.
The storm winds and driving rain slowly died away.
And so did the life of one being.
*Shrrk!*
—Krrk...!
Pain struck the Mutated Water God Dragon once more.
Its body writhed feebly, and then a figure appeared in the pupil of its eye.
A young human with a familiar face.
Its mortal enemy.
The one it absolutely had to kill.
—Gwoooooooooar!
And the presence of one man alone—Jin Taekyung—roused the monster’s last fading reserves of strength.
*Gooooooong—!*
At the very moment a massive sphere of water, what someone called Water Breath, was about to be completed after the dragon poured out every last bit of its strength...
Then the young human vanished from before its eye.
The next moment, the Mutated Water God Dragon heard a low, steady voice.
“You’ve worked hard.”
*Thk!*

—Krrk!
*When did they...?*
Even in Berserk Status, the Mutated Water God Dragon could tell the situation was turning against it.
But rage had paralyzed its reason, and the immense power contained within its large, beautiful body led the strange and terrifying evil beast to underestimate its opponents.

Its enormous tail, filled with murderous intent, blasted apart everything in its path.

Everything was crushed beneath the violently swinging tail.
The cliff that had barely been holding together collapsed completely, and the resulting roar swallowed every other sound.

She never believed studying was the only path to success.
Even when she saw my high school report card—sevens in every subject, like I’d hit the slot-machine jackpot—she ended her lecture with one short remark.
“Amazing, my son...”
Hmm.
Now that I thought about it, she may already have given up on me halfway by then.
In any case, even she made me read books when I was young.
I think it was in elementary school.
She saw me folding paper airplanes out of an English workbook and flying them around, so she handed me a book and told me to read that instead.
The title was...
Oh, right.
*Gulliver’s Travels.*
Even though I had no talent for studying, I enjoyed novels like that.
Sometimes, I even reenacted memorable scenes from them with Hayeon.
For example, the scene where the Lilliputians tied Gulliver down with ropes.
“Mom!
Look!
I caught Hayeon!
She’ll be quiet now!”
“Waaaaaah!
Mommy!”
“No!
Hayeon!
My daughter!”
Of course, my curiosity did not end particularly well.
When my mother saw her young daughter bound from head to toe in blue packing tape, she screamed.
Then she used a *hyojason* to beat the calves of the son who had just proven himself decidedly unfilial.
But with a tenacity unusual for an elementary schooler, I did not shed a single tear.
I did, however, reflect on where I had gone wrong.
“Next time, I need to tape her mouth shut too, so she can’t scream!”
Ah, what fond memories.
The vicious elementary schooler who had bound his much younger sister in blue packing tape was long gone, but the memory of that day remained vivid.
Along with the ambition I had held as a child: to tie up Gulliver just like in the novel.
*Thk!*
That’s right.
Just like now.
Remembering the childhood dream I had thought would never come true, I spoke.
“Got you.”
My method was more brutal than the one the Lilliputians had used on Gulliver, but it was undeniably effective.
I had predicted that the bastard would swing its tail.
I dodged just before the enormous, hideous thing lashed across my body, then drove my spearhead in with all my strength.
White Flame, the sturdy, transparent divine weapon, became a massive nail that pierced through both the monster’s tail and the ground beneath it.
*What about a hammer?*
Obviously, that would be my fist.
And I still had plenty of nails left.
*Open Inventory.
Summon.*
*Thk-thk-thk-thk-thk!*
It all happened in an instant.
I summoned five spears from my Inventory in a flash and drove them into the bastard’s tail.
Then I brought my fist down in place of a hammer.
*Boom!
Boom!
Booooom!*
*Anchoring complete.*
My powerful punch struck the ends of the spear shafts.
The sharp spearheads sank deep into the ground and trembled.
