chapters.title: Chapter 478
paragraphs: I hadn’t been aiming for that spot from the beginning.
No. I hadn’t even known it was there.
It was like trying to find a squirrel hidden in a dense forest.

The Mutated Water God Dragon’s body was simply too enormous for me to spot it, and I had never imagined there could be such a gap in a part of its body it had guarded so thoroughly throughout the battle.
But...
*That.*
There it was.
A weakness capable of severing the windpipe of this gigantic monster.
And I did not let the perfect opportunity to finish the fight slip away.
*Thk!*
—Krrk...!
Living creatures were truly remarkable. They constantly evolved, adapting to their surroundings and compensating for their weaknesses.
If even humans, whose average life span was only now approaching a hundred years, could do that, then surely this exalted being, which had lived for centuries, was no different.
*Was it coincidence? Or fate?*
Either way, it didn’t matter.
The only thing that mattered now was that a gap exactly one scale wide had been left in the monster’s neck, which was otherwise covered in its toughest scales.
And I hadn’t missed it.
“You’ve worked hard.”
Those final words of encouragement were a privilege only the victor could enjoy.
I had driven my spearhead precisely into the underside of its neck—where a human’s Adam’s apple would have been. Tightening my grip on the shaft, I shoved it deeper.
*Thk—!*
The dragon’s scaled jaw trembled with a short groan, as though it were trying and failing to draw breath.
Then its jet-black pupil quivered, and the sphere of water on the verge of completion inside its wide-open maw began to disperse.
*Shhhhhhh!*
An incomplete Water Breath was nothing more than ordinary water.
I did not avoid the deluge pouring down over my head. I let it hit me full-on.
The unusually cold water of Dongting Lake soaked me from head to toe, calming my mind.
*I won.*
At the same time, a thrill surged up my spine.
The end of a long, brutal battle.
Once again, I had survived and buried my spearhead in the neck of a powerful enemy. And as always, the end of a life-or-death battle came down to two words.
Vertical and horizontal.
The victor standing tall and the loser collapsing.
Even an evil beast that had lived for an unfathomable span of time was no exception to that absolute law of the jungle.
*Whoooooosh. Splash!*
The body that had once possessed such immense strength and resilience gave way and toppled onto the waters of Dongting Lake.
Through the spray rising high into the air, I saw its eye blink slowly and its snout tremble faintly.
No.
I heard it.
—You are just as I remember.
The moment someone’s voice echoed inside my head, the strength drained from the hand that had been about to drive the spear in again and finish the job.
As though bewitched, I stared into the Mutated Water God Dragon’s enormous eye and felt my body lock in place.
*What the hell...?*
The jet-black gleam and murderous aura that had made it look like a monster born beneath an ill-fated star were nowhere to be found.
Like dark clouds parting after a day of driving rain, an eye as clear and deep as the blue sky gazed back at me.
—There is no need to be surprised. After five hundred years or so, one naturally acquires abilities like this.
“Sound Transmission?”
—Perhaps it would be more accurate to call it mental intent.
The Mutated Water God Dragon—or rather, the divine being also known as the Two-Horned Beast of Dongting Lake—calmly sent its thoughts into my mind.

—You do not know me, but I know you. You look exactly as you did when I saw you in a dream long ago. I dismissed it as an idle dream and forgot all about it... Yes. This, too, must be part of the natural order.
A dream? The natural order?
*Damn it, what the hell is going on?*
“This is... I mean...”
—Hah.
My fumbling for words must have struck it as amusing. A growling laugh rumbled from the blood-soaked corner of the Water God Dragon’s mouth.
—You cannot understand, so do not try. These are merely the ramblings of an old imugi whose cultivation proved insufficient to ascend. My only regret is that I have no time left.
The Water God Dragon’s words were true. Its body had already reached its limit and stood on the verge of death, while the light was gradually fading from its deep eyes.
*Damn it.*
It was too late for regrets.
I bit my lip.
Part of me mourned the Water God Dragon’s impending death. To be coldly honest, another part simply regretted the loss.
This mystical being had regained its senses moments before death. It was an important key to solving the mystery.
*Dark Heaven.*
There was no way a divine and wise imugi had turned into a mad evil beast that slaughtered humans for no reason.
Someone must have interfered. And if so, I could hardly leave Dark Heaven off the list when it stood at the very top of the suspects behind everything currently happening in the Murim.
“Who did this to you? And how?”
The question was brief, but it contained everything.
The Water God Dragon’s reply went far beyond anything I had expected.
—See for yourself.
“Excuse me?”
The Water God Dragon answered by blinking.
*Srrk.*
Blue liquid welled in its enormous eye. The liquid everyone called tears slid slowly down its scales, and the moment it touched me, I understood what the Water God Dragon had meant.
*Ding.*

**System Water God Dragon** wishes to convey a portion of its memories to you. **Memory Fragment Acquired**. The power contained within **Memory Fragment** is leading you into the Water God Dragon’s memories.
As the System notification rang in my ears, the Water God Dragon’s tear unfurled like a curtain before my eyes.
*Shhhhhhh.*
A cool sensation washed over me.
Then the world stopped.
It was exactly what its name suggested: a fragment of memory.
It held the five hundred years the Water God Dragon had lived, but perhaps because of the mutation, parts of it had broken away. Some memories were blurred, while others remained perfectly clear.
And everything began with its birth.
—Guruk?
Somewhere deep beneath the waters of Dongting Lake, a tiny newborn creature looked around in bewilderment.
Aquatic plants swayed as though dancing, and countless underwater creatures had gathered around it.
The subjects who sensed the birth of a divine being swam joyfully through the currents.
It was an auspicious day—the birth of a new master of Dongting Lake and the occasion of a grand enthronement ceremony.
—Guruk? Guk!
The new master of the river tilted its head with all the curiosity of a puppy, then began to swim with its tiny body.
The moment this being, gifted with dazzling wisdom and power at birth, began to move, countless creatures followed behind it, and even the river parted to make way.
*Shhhhhhh!*
As it cut through the waters of Dongting Lake with supple, powerful movements, its body gradually grew larger.
Silver scales sprouted across its once-small, soft pink body, and imposing whiskers grew long beneath its snout.
It was probably around then.
Those who caught sight of this divine being once every few decades—or even less often—gave it a new name out of reverence.
A name I knew well.
*Water God Dragon.*

Perhaps because of the two horns on its forehead, it was also called the Two-Horned Beast. But most people were reluctant to call such a beautiful and mysterious being a mere beast. Instead, they worshiped it as the divine spirit of Dongting Lake.
And the imugi, having received a new name from humanity, would occasionally perform deeds that truly seemed divine.
It rescued sailors on the verge of drowning and carried them to remote stretches of dry land. It also used its innate power to calm violent currents on countless occasions.
And that wasn’t all. The Water God Dragon was also the one that defeated an evil beast that had once stained the Yangtze with blood.
After a fierce battle, it slew the turtle-shaped evil beast and came to rule both Dongting Lake and the Yangtze.
Time flowed like water.
Over the course of more than five hundred years, the Water God Dragon grew beyond all comparison to what it had once been.
It was a benevolent imugi possessed of tremendous power and profound wisdom, and an excellent ruler who cared for its subjects.
Yet even the Water God Dragon had one concern.
—Huh. Fighting never ends in the Lower Realm.
The horrors it had witnessed over its long life were truly appalling.
Humans constantly fought among themselves, and whenever they did, blood and countless corpses were scattered across the waters.
Two empires fell and war followed war. The Water God Dragon grew troubled and weary.
—I have already spent an unfathomable span of time in the Lower Realm. When will I finally be able to ascend?
No matter how people worshiped it as the divine spirit of Dongting Lake and called it a dragon, the Water God Dragon was, in truth, still an imugi that had yet to become one.
For the Water God Dragon, ascension was practically a destiny determined at birth.
But its cultivation progressed so slowly that it came to resent the heavens, and enlightenment remained stubbornly out of reach.
Then a school of fish brought news that was more than enough to stir the weary Water God Dragon’s curiosity.
—You say a human has appeared? But no one has visited that place in decades.
An uninvited visitor had entered the deepest and most secluded part of Dongting Lake—a treacherous place where no human had set foot in a very long time.
Its curiosity piqued, the Water God Dragon headed for the place it had once used as its dwelling.
The moment it arrived, it realized something was terribly wrong.
—What is this...!
The Water God Dragon of the past was not the only one shocked by the sight.
Watching through the fragment of memory, I was just as stunned.
*That can’t be...*
A clammy, sickening sensation crept slowly up my spine.
Overcome by disbelief, doubt, and the sheer shock of being blindsided, I muttered blankly.
*...A Gate.*
There was no doubt.
I had passed through Gates hundreds—no, thousands—of times. I was certain.
The black energy pouring in streams through the cracks between the enormous rocks was unmistakably magical power.
*What the fucking hell...!*
My vision swam, and every curse I knew echoed through my head.

If I had not been trapped inside the Water God Dragon’s memories—if I had been able to move and shout freely—I would have smashed everything around me. I would have screamed until my throat tore open.
*Fuck, a Gate. Magical power!*
My head felt ready to burst from the flood of thoughts. The scream I could not release died on the tip of my tongue.
Eyes wide with shock and fury, I stared at the scene unfolding before me.
—Stop! I said stop!
The master of the lake used its entire body to hold back the countless subjects charging toward it.
The teeth of the fish exposed to demonic qi were sharper than saw blades, and their scales had turned completely jet black.
—Please, stop!
But its desperate thoughts could no longer reach the fish mutated by demonic qi, and the Water God Dragon was forced to make a terrible decision.
If those unnaturally powerful and violent fish escaped, all of Dongting Lake and the Yangtze would be stained with blood.
A sacrifice had to be made for the greater good.
—...I am sorry.
The battle in the deepest waters of Dongting Lake naturally ended in the Water God Dragon’s victory.
But it was not even given time to grieve.
The wise imugi, which had lived for centuries, understood what it had to do. It placed its own body over the enormous rift that ceaselessly poured out its ominous energy.
—I do not know what you are, but you will not have your way.
*Rumble, rumble, rumble!*
It was the longest and fiercest struggle of the Water God Dragon’s entire life.

For seven days and nights, the two powers remained locked in a stalemate. The waters of Dongting Lake and the Yangtze churned violently, and the people on land trembled in fear, believing the divine spirit had grown angry.
And I already knew how that struggle ended.
—Krrr...
The Water God Dragon, its dazzling intelligence lost as it fell into corruption and became an evil beast, let out a low growl.
It had protected its territory and subjects by absorbing most of the demonic qi, but it could not contain all that power.
*Hissss.*
Its eyes slowly turned red.
Yet its last remaining grain of reason drove the Water God Dragon to surge out of the water.
It was the will of an old imugi determined to find the culprit behind this terrible atrocity.
*Shhhhhhh!*
On a dark night, the blackened waters parted.
The Water God Dragon rose as though ascending to heaven, and its red pupil reflected a person sitting on a moss-covered rock and splashing their feet in the water.
“The energy here is lovely. Coming all this way was worth it.”
A clear, gentle voice.
A dazzlingly white nape.
And a silver hairpin securing long black hair twisted into a knot.
*...Honglan.*
The moment that name surfaced in my mind, the entire world around me shattered into pieces.

sentences.text: I hadn’t been aiming for that spot from the beginning.
No.
I hadn’t even known it was there.
It was like trying to find a squirrel hidden in a dense forest.

The Mutated Water God Dragon’s body was simply too enormous for me to spot it, and I had never imagined there could be such a gap in a part of its body it had guarded so thoroughly throughout the battle.
But...
*That.*
There it was.
A weakness capable of severing the windpipe of this gigantic monster.
And I did not let the perfect opportunity to finish the fight slip away.
*Thk!*
—Krrk...!
Living creatures were truly remarkable.
They constantly evolved, adapting to their surroundings and compensating for their weaknesses.
If even humans, whose average life span was only now approaching a hundred years, could do that, then surely this exalted being, which had lived for centuries, was no different.
*Was it coincidence?
Or fate?*
Either way, it didn’t matter.
The only thing that mattered now was that a gap exactly one scale wide had been left in the monster’s neck, which was otherwise covered in its toughest scales.
And I hadn’t missed it.
“You’ve worked hard.”
Those final words of encouragement were a privilege only the victor could enjoy.
I had driven my spearhead precisely into the underside of its neck—where a human’s Adam’s apple would have been.
Tightening my grip on the shaft, I shoved it deeper.
*Thk—!*
The dragon’s scaled jaw trembled with a short groan, as though it were trying and failing to draw breath.
Then its jet-black pupil quivered, and the sphere of water on the verge of completion inside its wide-open maw began to disperse.
*Shhhhhhh!*
An incomplete Water Breath was nothing more than ordinary water.
I did not avoid the deluge pouring down over my head.
I let it hit me full-on.
The unusually cold water of Dongting Lake soaked me from head to toe, calming my mind.
*I won.*
At the same time, a thrill surged up my spine.
The end of a long, brutal battle.
Once again, I had survived and buried my spearhead in the neck of a powerful enemy.
And as always, the end of a life-or-death battle came down to two words.
Vertical and horizontal.
The victor standing tall and the loser collapsing.
Even an evil beast that had lived for an unfathomable span of time was no exception to that absolute law of the jungle.
*Whoooooosh.
Splash!*
The body that had once possessed such immense strength and resilience gave way and toppled onto the waters of Dongting Lake.
Through the spray rising high into the air, I saw its eye blink slowly and its snout tremble faintly.
No.
I heard it.
—You are just as I remember.
The moment someone’s voice echoed inside my head, the strength drained from the hand that had been about to drive the spear in again and finish the job.
As though bewitched, I stared into the Mutated Water God Dragon’s enormous eye and felt my body lock in place.
*What the hell...?*
The jet-black gleam and murderous aura that had made it look like a monster born beneath an ill-fated star were nowhere to be found.
Like dark clouds parting after a day of driving rain, an eye as clear and deep as the blue sky gazed back at me.
—There is no need to be surprised.
After five hundred years or so, one naturally acquires abilities like this.
“Sound Transmission?”
—Perhaps it would be more accurate to call it mental intent.
The Mutated Water God Dragon—or rather, the divine being also known as the Two-Horned Beast of Dongting Lake—calmly sent its thoughts into my mind.
—You do not know me, but I know you.
You look exactly as you did when I saw you in a dream long ago.
I dismissed it as an idle dream and forgot all about it...
Yes.
This, too, must be part of the natural order.
A dream?
The natural order?
*Damn it, what the hell is going on?*
“This is...
I mean...”
—Hah.
My fumbling for words must have struck it as amusing.
A growling laugh rumbled from the blood-soaked corner of the Water God Dragon’s mouth.
—You cannot understand, so do not try.
These are merely the ramblings of an old imugi whose cultivation proved insufficient to ascend.
My only regret is that I have no time left.
The Water God Dragon’s words were true.
Its body had already reached its limit and stood on the verge of death, while the light was gradually fading from its deep eyes.
*Damn it.*
It was too late for regrets.
I bit my lip.
Part of me mourned the Water God Dragon’s impending death.
To be coldly honest, another part simply regretted the loss.
This mystical being had regained its senses moments before death.
It was an important key to solving the mystery.
*Dark Heaven.*
There was no way a divine and wise imugi had turned into a mad evil beast that slaughtered humans for no reason.
Someone must have interfered.
And if so, I could hardly leave Dark Heaven off the list when it stood at the very top of the suspects behind everything currently happening in the Murim.
“Who did this to you?
And how?”
The question was brief, but it contained everything.
The Water God Dragon’s reply went far beyond anything I had expected.
—See for yourself.
“Excuse me?”
The Water God Dragon answered by blinking.
*Srrk.*
Blue liquid welled in its enormous eye.
The liquid everyone called tears slid slowly down its scales, and the moment it touched me, I understood what the Water God Dragon had meant.
*Ding.*
**System Water God Dragon** wishes to convey a portion of its memories to you. **Memory Fragment Acquired**.
The power contained within **Memory Fragment** is leading you into the Water God Dragon’s memories.
As the System notification rang in my ears, the Water God Dragon’s tear unfurled like a curtain before my eyes.
*Shhhhhhh.*
A cool sensation washed over me.
Then the world stopped.
It was exactly what its name suggested: a fragment of memory.
It held the five hundred years the Water God Dragon had lived, but perhaps because of the mutation, parts of it had broken away.
Some memories were blurred, while others remained perfectly clear.
And everything began with its birth.
—Guruk?
Somewhere deep beneath the waters of Dongting Lake, a tiny newborn creature looked around in bewilderment.
Aquatic plants swayed as though dancing, and countless underwater creatures had gathered around it.
The subjects who sensed the birth of a divine being swam joyfully through the currents.
It was an auspicious day—the birth of a new master of Dongting Lake and the occasion of a grand enthronement ceremony.
—Guruk?
Guk!
The new master of the river tilted its head with all the curiosity of a puppy, then began to swim with its tiny body.
The moment this being, gifted with dazzling wisdom and power at birth, began to move, countless creatures followed behind it, and even the river parted to make way.
*Shhhhhhh!*
As it cut through the waters of Dongting Lake with supple, powerful movements, its body gradually grew larger.
Silver scales sprouted across its once-small, soft pink body, and imposing whiskers grew long beneath its snout.
It was probably around then.
Those who caught sight of this divine being once every few decades—or even less often—gave it a new name out of reverence.
A name I knew well.
*Water God Dragon.*
Perhaps because of the two horns on its forehead, it was also called the Two-Horned Beast.
But most people were reluctant to call such a beautiful and mysterious being a mere beast.
Instead, they worshiped it as the divine spirit of Dongting Lake.
And the imugi, having received a new name from humanity, would occasionally perform deeds that truly seemed divine.
It rescued sailors on the verge of drowning and carried them to remote stretches of dry land.
It also used its innate power to calm violent currents on countless occasions.
And that wasn’t all.
The Water God Dragon was also the one that defeated an evil beast that had once stained the Yangtze with blood.
After a fierce battle, it slew the turtle-shaped evil beast and came to rule both Dongting Lake and the Yangtze.
Time flowed like water.
Over the course of more than five hundred years, the Water God Dragon grew beyond all comparison to what it had once been.
It was a benevolent imugi possessed of tremendous power and profound wisdom, and an excellent ruler who cared for its subjects.
Yet even the Water God Dragon had one concern.
—Huh.
Fighting never ends in the Lower Realm.
The horrors it had witnessed over its long life were truly appalling.
Humans constantly fought among themselves, and whenever they did, blood and countless corpses were scattered across the waters.
Two empires fell and war followed war.
The Water God Dragon grew troubled and weary.
—I have already spent an unfathomable span of time in the Lower Realm.
When will I finally be able to ascend?
No matter how people worshiped it as the divine spirit of Dongting Lake and called it a dragon, the Water God Dragon was, in truth, still an imugi that had yet to become one.
For the Water God Dragon, ascension was practically a destiny determined at birth.
But its cultivation progressed so slowly that it came to resent the heavens, and enlightenment remained stubbornly out of reach.
Then a school of fish brought news that was more than enough to stir the weary Water God Dragon’s curiosity.
—You say a human has appeared?
But no one has visited that place in decades.
An uninvited visitor had entered the deepest and most secluded part of Dongting Lake—a treacherous place where no human had set foot in a very long time.
Its curiosity piqued, the Water God Dragon headed for the place it had once used as its dwelling.
The moment it arrived, it realized something was terribly wrong.
—What is this...!
The Water God Dragon of the past was not the only one shocked by the sight.
Watching through the fragment of memory, I was just as stunned.
*That can’t be...*
A clammy, sickening sensation crept slowly up my spine.
Overcome by disbelief, doubt, and the sheer shock of being blindsided, I muttered blankly.
*...A Gate.*
There was no doubt.
I had passed through Gates hundreds—no, thousands—of times.
I was certain.
The black energy pouring in streams through the cracks between the enormous rocks was unmistakably magical power.
*What the fucking hell...!*
My vision swam, and every curse I knew echoed through my head.
If I had not been trapped inside the Water God Dragon’s memories—if I had been able to move and shout freely—I would have smashed everything around me.
I would have screamed until my throat tore open.
*Fuck, a Gate.
Magical power!*
My head felt ready to burst from the flood of thoughts.
The scream I could not release died on the tip of my tongue.
Eyes wide with shock and fury, I stared at the scene unfolding before me.
—Stop!
I said stop!
The master of the lake used its entire body to hold back the countless subjects charging toward it.

chapters.title: Chapter 479
paragraphs: The world collapsed, then rebuilt itself once more.
The ferocious red pupil, the surging river, and the beautifully crafted silver hairpin all vanished. In their place came reality beyond the memory.
*Whoooooosh.*
I slowly blinked. The curtain of water surrounding my body scattered, and my changed surroundings came into focus.
At the same time, time itself—frozen as though someone had pressed pause—began moving again.
Then, in the next instant, the chill in the air and a flood of System notifications crashed over me like a dam bursting all at once.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*

**System Memory Fragment** has ended! The Quest information has been updated because the **Mutated Water God Dragon** has regained its reason! In accordance with the updated Quest information, the mission has been recognized as successful! Surprise Quest, **Corrupted Spirit Beast**, has been successfully completed! You have gained a tremendous amount of EXP and Fame! **Level Up! Level Up!**
With the Level Up notifications, a mysterious power breathed new vitality into my exhausted body and replenished my depleted internal energy.
And yet, for some reason, I could barely breathe.
*Honglan. It was Honglan.*
Yes. It had been her.
The Lower District Sect member who had survived the tragedy at Dongting Lake alongside Ju Wongong. A breathtaking beauty capable of swaying an entire nation.

The owner of the hairpin in my hair was the one who had corrupted a benevolent imugi and stained Dongting Lake and the Yangtze with blood—the culprit behind every incident that had occurred in Hubei Province.
*Why hadn’t I realized it? Where had the lies begun, and where had the truth ended?*
*Gate. Magical power. Honglan. Dark Heaven.*
Countless questions and thoughts flashed through my mind in a single instant. My overloaded brain felt ready to burst.
As I trembled at the unbelievable reality, I spotted three figures shooting toward me.
Jeok Cheongang was in the lead, his face contorted with fury.
“You bastard, how dare you—!”
Thinking about it, the scene was easy to misread.

My conversation with the Water God Dragon and the time I had spent inside the Memory Fragment had both taken place within an incredibly brief instant. To everyone else, I had been standing there perfectly fine before suddenly starting to act strangely.
Jeok Cheongang’s furious bellow snapped me back to reality, and I shouted like a bolt of lightning.
“Old Master!”
We could understand each other’s intentions with nothing more than a glance.
The moment Jeok Cheongang recognized the emotion in my shout, an exclamation mark appeared in his eyes. At the same time, the fist he had been driving forward forcefully changed direction.
*Whoom, kwaaaaaang!*
It missed by no more than a hair.
The Fist Force narrowly avoided the Water God Dragon and slammed into the surface of the now-calm lake.
The heat carried by the Scorching Yang Qi was so intense that every trace of moisture within a radius of several jang evaporated in an instant.
The Water God Dragon was already at death’s door.
If that attack had struck it, there would not even have been time for a final conversation.
“You bastard, why—!”
—Were you worried about your Disciple? A fine master indeed.
“Gasp!”
It was obvious that the mental intent the Water God Dragon had sent out had not reached me alone.
Jeok Cheongang sucked in a short breath and stepped back. Mungyeong and Cheongpung arrived immediately afterward, both looking as though they had seen a ghost.
“What in the world was that just now?”
“Uh, even Mimi can’t do anything like that.”
...*Shlick.*
Our reflections appeared in the Water God Dragon’s deep, clear eyes. Jeok Cheongang asked in a trembling voice,
“What... What in the world are you?”
—Some call me a divine spirit. Others call me a monster. You must find the answer to that question for yourself.
*Grrr.*
The Water God Dragon exhaled with difficulty and continued sending its mental intent.
—Before the end, I should thank you. Had you not intervened, I would have remained a hideous evil beast until my final breath...
The mental intent that had rung clearly inside our minds gradually faded.
The light was already draining from the Water God Dragon’s clear eyes.
*It’s dying? Just like this?*
I looked at Mungyeong with the last of my hope, but the man who also bore the sobriquet Divine Physician merely shook his head, his expression grim.
“It’s already too late. Even a Great Firmament Immortal couldn’t stop it now.”
—You speak the truth, one who walks between life and death.
One who walks between life and death.
Mungyeong’s neatly shaped brows twitched at the words that had seen straight through his identity.
“You... know me?”
—Though I failed to ascend to the heavens, I cultivated for many long years. I saw every one of you here in my dreams.
What exactly had been happening in the dreams the Water God Dragon claimed to have?
It was an imugi that had lived for five hundred years. Even now, with all its strength exhausted and death close at hand, it possessed a depth and mystery beyond anything I could fathom.
As though gazing at something beyond human understanding, the Water God Dragon stared into the empty air over our shoulders and sent out its mental intent.
—Unfortunately, this is as far as I am permitted to go. Though I cannot speak of the heavenly patterns... yes, I suppose I may leave one gift behind before I depart.
*A gift?*
None of us had time to voice the question.
In the next instant, my eyes widened at the faint cluster of light emerging from the blood-soaked corner of the Water God Dragon’s mouth.
*Shhhhhhh.*
It was a pearl, glowing softly.
As though lifted by an invisible hand, it slipped free of the Water God Dragon’s mouth and floated into the air. Then it began to tremble.
*Whoom.*
A vibration traveled through the air.
At the same time, the black stain covering much of the pearl melted away. Each time part of it vanished, the pearl visibly shrank.
*This is...*
What I could see was only part of it.
I could feel the sheer magnitude and depth of the qi contained within the pearl, and the sight unfolding before me brought a single word to mind.
*Purification.*
At last, when the transformation was complete, an irrepressible gasp escaped someone’s lips.
“Ah.”
*Shhhhhhh.*
The pearl now shone with a radiance far brighter than before.
Although it had shrunk to roughly the size of an ordinary pill, the crystal of qi, cleansed of every impurity, contained power of immeasurable clarity and depth.
*So pure.*
It was an incredibly powerful crystal of qi.
As all of us stared at it in awe—
*Slither.*
The crystal of energy slowly drifted through the air and stopped in front of me. At the same time, the Water God Dragon’s mental intent rang out.
—This is my Origin Essence. Humans call it an inner core.
—Though it is insignificant compared to what it once was, it will surely become a great source of strength. Please use it where it is needed.
I had no reason to refuse.
I stared at the crystal with trembling eyes, then reached out and took it.
*Ding.*
**System Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence** acquired!
The System notification rang in my ears.
Having given me everything it possessed, the Water God Dragon slowly blinked.
A faint smile lingered in its eyes as it gazed up at the clear sky.
—So this is where it ends...
*Grrr.*
Along with the fading mental intent, the final breath of the imugi that had failed to become a dragon escaped from its blood-soaked mouth.
Then everything stopped, and silence descended.
I reached out and closed the Water God Dragon’s eyes, which had grown cold and stiff.
*You’ve worked hard.*
I had witnessed the Water God Dragon’s life through the Memory Fragment.
It had been a mysterious being far beyond any ordinary spiritual creature, and a benevolent one that had sacrificed itself to prevent an even greater disaster.
So at least in its final moment, it deserved the right to meet death on its own terms.
Not as a sacrifice for someone else’s Level Up, but as a natural death.
But there was one person—no, one bitch—who was the exception, no matter what.
*...Honglan.*
I pulled the silver hairpin from my hair.
It gave off a scent so faint that even my keen sense of smell could barely detect it. I stared at it in silence, then turned to the still-confused Jeok Cheongang.
“Want to go catch a snake?”
“First tell me what the hell is going on... What? A snake?”
“Yes. A flower snake.”
A clear peal of laughter rang across the deck of the military vessel, drawing everyone’s attention.
Though the laughter was not the only reason they were looking.
Every man with eyes had been stealing glances at her since before they boarded the vessel. She was that beautiful.
“Good heavens. Even her laughter is beautiful.”
When a middle-aged man in a military uniform muttered wistfully, the colleague beside him scolded him.
“Your wife should have seen you just now.”
“Don’t say such unlucky things. I’d rather lock eyes with Yama.”
“You’re old enough to know better, and you have five children as cute as rabbits. Are you seriously acting like this?”
“What about you?”
“I don’t have any children yet.”
“You have a wife.”
His fellow soldier solemnly declared,
“Not for much longer.”
“...You’ve completely lost your mind. Are you serious?”
“What’s wrong with me? A man ought to try his luck at least once.”
“I guarantee you won’t get the chance.”
“Are you trying to jinx me before I’ve even started?”
“No. Someone much younger, better-looking, and more capable than you has already made the first move.”
He was telling the truth. A military officer with striking, handsome features was already striding confidently toward the woman.
“Young Lady. I assume something pleasant has happened?”
Officer Song, who was in charge of the military vessel, flashed his white teeth in a broad grin.

He came from a wealthy family and was handsome to boot. The woman before him might be a breathtaking beauty the likes of whom he would see only once or twice in his life, but he still had confidence in himself.
*She isn’t some young lady from a prestigious household. She’s only a singing courtesan.*
The very next moment, that confidence crumbled without a trace.
“Yes. Something very pleasant.”
Her voice was so pure it seemed to cleanse the soul, and her smile was like hydrangeas in full bloom.
Her beauty was seductive yet pristine, pristine yet so lofty that no one dared approach.
Officer Song began to stammer without realizing it.
“I-is, is that so?”
At his flustered appearance, the woman—Honglan—covered her mouth and laughed.
Her eyes curved like half-moons, drawing anguished groans from the officers who had been stealing glances at her.
*How dare those bastards.*
Officer Song glared at his subordinates, then spoke over the pounding of his heart.
“What a shame. If only I could share that pleasure with you, Young Lady...”
Honglan smiled faintly at his deliberately trailing words.
“I’m not sure. I’m hesitant to say anything careless in case I unsettle our Officer Song’s heart.”
*Our dear Officer Song?*
There was no doubt about it. This was the green light that supposedly appeared between a man and a woman who had feelings for each other.
Emboldened, Officer Song bellowed,
“On my ancestors’ honor, that will absolutely never happen!”
“Oh my, how brave. Then I’ll let only you in on it, Officer Song. Bring your ear a little closer...”
“Yes, yes!”
Officer Song leaned his ear toward Honglan, his heart pounding.
Then her sweet, warm breath tickled his ear.
“The truth is, I used the imugi living in Dongting Lake to kill a great many people.”
“What?”
“But that imugi just died. I’m sorry to see it go, but at the same time, I’m delighted.”
Officer Song slowly lifted his head and stared blankly at Honglan.
He had no idea what the woman before him was talking about, or what he had just heard.
“Young Lady, what does that—”
“It’s exactly what you heard. I believe you’ll understand me, Officer Song.”
For some reason, Honglan’s languid voice made Officer Song’s expression go hazy.
This was no mere infatuation. It was an irresistible pull, a chain that seized a person’s emotions and soul.
“Isn’t that right, Officer Song?”
“...Of course. Naturally.”
“That’s wonderful.”
Honglan watched with satisfaction as Officer Song nodded like a man under a spell, then turned her gaze toward the broad river.
And to the man who had become her captive, she made a request—or rather, issued her first command.
“Shall we change our destination?”

You must find the answer to that question for yourself.
*Grrr.*
The Water God Dragon exhaled with difficulty and continued sending its mental intent.
—Before the end, I should thank you.
Had you not intervened, I would have remained a hideous evil beast until my final breath...
The mental intent that had rung clearly inside our minds gradually faded.
The light was already draining from the Water God Dragon’s clear eyes.
*It’s dying?
Just like this?*
I looked at Mungyeong with the last of my hope, but the man who also bore the sobriquet Divine Physician merely shook his head, his expression grim.
“It’s already too late.
Even a Great Firmament Immortal couldn’t stop it now.”
—You speak the truth, one who walks between life and death.
One who walks between life and death.
Mungyeong’s neatly shaped brows twitched at the words that had seen straight through his identity.
“You... know me?”
—Though I failed to ascend to the heavens, I cultivated for many long years.
I saw every one of you here in my dreams.
What exactly had been happening in the dreams the Water God Dragon claimed to have?
It was an imugi that had lived for five hundred years.
Even now, with all its strength exhausted and death close at hand, it possessed a depth and mystery beyond anything I could fathom.
As though gazing at something beyond human understanding, the Water God Dragon stared into the empty air over our shoulders and sent out its mental intent.
—Unfortunately, this is as far as I am permitted to go.
Though I cannot speak of the heavenly patterns... yes, I suppose I may leave one gift behind before I depart.
*A gift?*
None of us had time to voice the question.
In the next instant, my eyes widened at the faint cluster of light emerging from the blood-soaked corner of the Water God Dragon’s mouth.
*Shhhhhhh.*
It was a pearl, glowing softly.
As though lifted by an invisible hand, it slipped free of the Water God Dragon’s mouth and floated into the air.
Then it began to tremble.
*Whoom.*
A vibration traveled through the air.
At the same time, the black stain covering much of the pearl melted away.
Each time part of it vanished, the pearl visibly shrank.
*This is...*
What I could see was only part of it.
I could feel the sheer magnitude and depth of the qi contained within the pearl, and the sight unfolding before me brought a single word to mind.
*Purification.*
At last, when the transformation was complete, an irrepressible gasp escaped someone’s lips.
“Ah.”
*Shhhhhhh.*
The pearl now shone with a radiance far brighter than before.
Although it had shrunk to roughly the size of an ordinary pill, the crystal of qi, cleansed of every impurity, contained power of immeasurable clarity and depth.
*So pure.*
It was an incredibly powerful crystal of qi.
As all of us stared at it in awe—
*Slither.*
The crystal of energy slowly drifted through the air and stopped in front of me.
At the same time, the Water God Dragon’s mental intent rang out.
—This is my Origin Essence.
Humans call it an inner core.
—Though it is insignificant compared to what it once was, it will surely become a great source of strength.
Please use it where it is needed.
I had no reason to refuse.
I stared at the crystal with trembling eyes, then reached out and took it.
*Ding.*
**System Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence** acquired!
The System notification rang in my ears.
Having given me everything it possessed, the Water God Dragon slowly blinked.
A faint smile lingered in its eyes as it gazed up at the clear sky.
—So this is where it ends...
*Grrr.*
Along with the fading mental intent, the final breath of the imugi that had failed to become a dragon escaped from its blood-soaked mouth.
Then everything stopped, and silence descended.
I reached out and closed the Water God Dragon’s eyes, which had grown cold and stiff.
*You’ve worked hard.*
I had witnessed the Water God Dragon’s life through the Memory Fragment.
It had been a mysterious being far beyond any ordinary spiritual creature, and a benevolent one that had sacrificed itself to prevent an even greater disaster.
So at least in its final moment, it deserved the right to meet death on its own terms.
Not as a sacrifice for someone else’s Level Up, but as a natural death.
But there was one person—no, one bitch—who was the exception, no matter what.
*...Honglan.*
I pulled the silver hairpin from my hair.
It gave off a scent so faint that even my keen sense of smell could barely detect it.
I stared at it in silence, then turned to the still-confused Jeok Cheongang.
“Want to go catch a snake?”
“First tell me what the hell is going on...
What?
A snake?”
“Yes.
A flower snake.”
A clear peal of laughter rang across the deck of the military vessel, drawing everyone’s attention.
Though the laughter was not the only reason they were looking.
Every man with eyes had been stealing glances at her since before they boarded the vessel.
She was that beautiful.
“Good heavens.
Even her laughter is beautiful.”
When a middle-aged man in a military uniform muttered wistfully, the colleague beside him scolded him.
“Your wife should have seen you just now.”
“Don’t say such unlucky things.
I’d rather lock eyes with Yama.”
“You’re old enough to know better, and you have five children as cute as rabbits.
Are you seriously acting like this?”
“What about you?”
“I don’t have any children yet.”
“You have a wife.”
His fellow soldier solemnly declared,
“Not for much longer.”
“...You’ve completely lost your mind.
Are you serious?”
“What’s wrong with me?
A man ought to try his luck at least once.”
“I guarantee you won’t get the chance.”
“Are you trying to jinx me before I’ve even started?”
“No.
Someone much younger, better-looking, and more capable than you has already made the first move.”
He was telling the truth.
A military officer with striking, handsome features was already striding confidently toward the woman.
“Young Lady.
I assume something pleasant has happened?”
Officer Song, who was in charge of the military vessel, flashed his white teeth in a broad grin.
He came from a wealthy family and was handsome to boot.
The woman before him might be a breathtaking beauty the likes of whom he would see only once or twice in his life, but he still had confidence in himself.
*She isn’t some young lady from a prestigious household.
She’s only a singing courtesan.*
The very next moment, that confidence crumbled without a trace.
“Yes.
Something very pleasant.”
Her voice was so pure it seemed to cleanse the soul, and her smile was like hydrangeas in full bloom.
Her beauty was seductive yet pristine, pristine yet so lofty that no one dared approach.
Officer Song began to stammer without realizing it.
“I-is, is that so?”
At his flustered appearance, the woman—Honglan—covered her mouth and laughed.
Her eyes curved like half-moons, drawing anguished groans from the officers who had been stealing glances at her.
*How dare those bastards.*
Officer Song glared at his subordinates, then spoke over the pounding of his heart.
“What a shame.
If only I could share that pleasure with you, Young Lady...”
Honglan smiled faintly at his deliberately trailing words.
“I’m not sure.
I’m hesitant to say anything careless in case I unsettle our Officer Song’s heart.”
*Our dear Officer Song?*
There was no doubt about it.
This was the green light that supposedly appeared between a man and a woman who had feelings for each other.
Emboldened, Officer Song bellowed,
“On my ancestors’ honor, that will absolutely never happen!”
“Oh my, how brave.
Then I’ll let only you in on it, Officer Song.
Bring your ear a little closer...”
“Yes, yes!”
Officer Song leaned his ear toward Honglan, his heart pounding.
Then her sweet, warm breath tickled his ear.
“The truth is, I used the imugi living in Dongting Lake to kill a great many people.”
“What?”
“But that imugi just died.
I’m sorry to see it go, but at the same time, I’m delighted.”
Officer Song slowly lifted his head and stared blankly at Honglan.
He had no idea what the woman before him was talking about, or what he had just heard.
“Young Lady, what does that—”
“It’s exactly what you heard.
I believe you’ll understand me, Officer Song.”
For some reason, Honglan’s languid voice made Officer Song’s expression go hazy.
This was no mere infatuation.
It was an irresistible pull, a chain that seized a person’s emotions and soul.
“Isn’t that right, Officer Song?”
“...Of course.
Naturally.”
“That’s wonderful.”
Honglan watched with satisfaction as Officer Song nodded like a man under a spell, then turned her gaze toward the broad river.
And to the man who had become her captive, she made a request—or rather, issued her first command.
“Shall we change our destination?”

chapters.title: Chapter 480
paragraphs: “Ugh.”
The wrinkled skin around the old man’s eyes twitched. He tossed and turned with a groan, then finally opened his eyes after a long while.
*Where am I...?*
Instead of damp, yellow-stained wallpaper, he saw a ceiling so starkly white that it was almost oppressive.
He lay there blankly, unable to make sense of the situation, until a calm voice reached his ears.
“Are you awake?”
It wasn’t hard to find the source of the voice.
The old man sat up with a start and saw a young man seated before a small brazier, watching him.
“Wh-who might you be?”
“There are ultimately only two kinds of people in a clinic: medical apprentices and patients. Since you still belong to the latter category, you should lie back down.”
“Ah.”
Only then did the old man realize that this unfamiliar place was a clinic. He also realized the identity of the young man, who looked barely more than a boy.
“So you’re a medical apprentice, sir. But why am I in a clinic... Ow.”
As he spoke in bewilderment, a sudden headache made him groan.
Only now did he realize that his aged body ached everywhere. He was drenched in sweat and trembling uncontrollably.
*Good heavens. What on earth happened?*
The young medical apprentice crossed the room and came to his aid.
“I’m going to insert a few needles now. Calm yourself and breathe slowly. All right. One. Two...”
*Tap.*
“Wha—?”
The old man’s eyes went round. The crown of his head prickled as though an ant had bitten him, and then his headache vanished as if it had been washed away.
Holding a slender needle, the young medical apprentice smiled faintly at the old man’s astonished stare.
“Are you all right?”
“Pardon? Yes.”
“Then lie back down. From what I’ve observed over the past two days, fortunately, there doesn’t seem to be anything seriously wrong... but you still shouldn’t be moving around yet.”
“Ah, I-I understand.”
His medical skills were nothing short of miraculous, and something about his presence inexplicably put both body and mind at ease.
Up close, he looked much younger than expected, yet he seemed more seasoned than even an elderly medical apprentice.
“I’ll help you. Relax and lie down slowly.”
“Yes, yes.”
The old man lay back down as though entranced. The young medical apprentice raised several fingers.
“I need to perform a simple check. Elder, how many fingers am I holding up?”
“It looks like three.”
“And now?”
“Two.”
“Correct. Where do you live, and what is your name and age?”
“...Do I have to tell you that too?”
“I need to make sure your mind is completely clear.”
“Hmm. Let me think.”
Unlike the earlier questions, these required some thought.
The old man had only just awakened, and his condition was still unstable. Feeling a faint headache, he slowly opened his mouth.
“I’ve lived my whole life around Wuhan and Dongting Lake. My name is Gwak Bongchul. No one kept proper track when I was growing up, so I don’t know my exact age, but I reckon I must be past seventy.”
“So you’re Elder Gwak. You’re remarkably fit for your age. What do you do?”
“I... Well, I...”
The old man frowned and hesitated until his occupation came back to him.
“I row a boat.”
“You’re a boatman.”
“Yes. When I was young, I worked as a deckhand on a merchant ship. After I bought my own boat, I mostly carried passengers around Dongting Lake and showed them the sights.”
Before long, the old man—no, the elderly boatman—was delving into old memories and talking without prompting. Each time, the young medical apprentice encouraged him with a gentle smile and a nod.

“There was an older fellow I used to work with. He put it into my head that a man with his own boat was bound to find himself a woman. So I took the plunge and bought a sleek little beauty made by Baekchu.”
“Is that so?”

“I don’t know if you’ve heard of Baekchu, sir. These days, boats like that are common at the Wuhan ferry docks, but when I was young, a man who sailed a Baekchu vessel was considered a first-rate husband prospect. That, or an Audi. You know, the one with four circles on the bow.”
“That sounds somewhat like Five Qi Returning to Origin.”
“Huh? What’s Five Qi Returning to Origin?”
“It’s something. Let’s move on.”

“Anyway, that boat I bought was sleek and beautiful. It attracted plenty of women, too. Once, a widow from the neighboring village came to me late at night and asked me to show her the Baekchu. Then, all of a sudden, she yanked her dress ties open...!”
“...Let’s skip a little farther ahead.”
The young medical apprentice listened with patience far beyond his years. As the story continued, the solid dam blocking the boatman’s memories slowly began to crumble.
Then, while the boatman cheerfully rambled on, his aching body forgotten, one particular memory suddenly resurfaced.
He froze like a stone statue.
It was a bolt of lightning.
A nightmarish memory.
*Rumble. Boom!*
*Graaaaaaah!*
The crash of thunder and a furious roar rang vividly in his ears.
He blinked slowly, and the image of a colossal being silhouetted against the black sky flashed before his eyes.
“Gah!”
The boatman sprang upright without realizing it and stared blankly into the air.
“W-wait. Wait a moment.”
His voice trembled, and his eyes were wide open.
Perhaps because he had exerted himself so suddenly, every part of his body began aching again. But the boatman paid no attention to any of it.
The memories flooding back through the broken dam consumed his thoughts.
“Me-medical apprentice! What did you say to me earlier?”
“What are you referring to?”
“Two days! Didn’t you say two days had passed?”
*Grab!*
A grip far too strong for a man over seventy clamped around the medical apprentice’s slender wrist.
But the young medical apprentice did not so much as twitch an eyebrow as he calmly replied,
“That is correct.”
“Good heavens. How could this happen?”
“Calm yourself, Elder.”
“T-this is no time to be calm. We must tell the people and report this to the higher-ups at once!”
The boatman was half out of his mind.
His entire body was drenched in sweat and trembling without his realizing it, while his unfocused eyes darted anxiously in every direction.
It was as though something might devour him at any moment.
“We have to run as quickly as possible. Hurry!”
That was when the young medical apprentice reached toward the patient, who was shouting as though in the throes of a fit.
*Swish.*
A smooth white hand without a single callus touched the boatman’s slightly hunched back. Warmth flowed from it and filled his body.
The inexplicable phenomenon finally calmed the boatman, and he gasped for breath.
“Wh-what was that?”
“Think of it as a miscellaneous technique I’ve practiced from time to time. And, Elder.”
“Gasp.”
The boatman met the medical apprentice’s deep, clear gaze, and for reasons he could not explain, the words caught in his throat.
The young medical apprentice studied him for a moment before slowly continuing.
“The thing you’re worried about will never happen. Do you understand?”
“Pardon?”

“It’s simple. Erase everything you saw, heard, and experienced from your mind. Two days ago, you were summoned to Dongting Lake with the government troops, but you collapsed because you were unwell. You woke up today.”
“P-please wait a moment.”
“Everything I’m telling you is true. It must become true. That day, you carried no passengers, and you never saw the divine spirit of Dongting Lake.”
The boatman shuddered as though he had been struck by lightning.
The young medical apprentice’s words were that shocking.
“D-does that mean you saw the Mountain Spirit too, sir...?”
“That may be the case, or it may not. But there is one thing you must remember... You must forget everything you remember about those events.”
The boatman swallowed hard at the young man’s gentle yet blade-cold voice.
Then the suffocating silence in the room was broken by the last bit of courage a man over seventy could muster.
“D-do you intend to kill me?”
“Me? No.”
The young medical apprentice slowly shook his head and continued.
“But someone else may think differently. For example... the City Lord of Hubei Province, who would not want ominous rumors spreading.”
“T-the City Lord!”
The City Lord of Hubei Province.
An official who governed a city by order of the Son of Heaven—a man who, at least within Hubei Province, was as good as a king.
The boatman cried out reflexively at the unexpected appearance of such a high-ranking person. Then he realized his mistake, and his vision went dark.
*What a stupid fool! What if someone heard me?*
Unlike him, however, the young medical apprentice’s expression remained relaxed.
It was the composure of the person who had ensured that none of their conversation could leave the room.
No—even if their words did leak out, the young medical apprentice would not bat an eye.
The precaution was solely for the sake of the boatman’s life.
Unaware of that, the boatman spoke again in a tightly hushed voice.
“I-I want to live. Why on earth would the City Lord want to kill an insignificant boatman like me?”

“When floods come, droughts strike, and plagues spread, people die in every direction, and wars break out everywhere. Then the rebels who dream of becoming kings and high officials speak with one voice. They say that the will of Heaven has left the Son of Heaven. That we should overthrow this rotten country.”
The young medical apprentice clicked his tongue softly, stood up, and tossed out one final remark.
“Even disasters beyond human power lead to such things. So what do you suppose would happen if the divine spirit of Dongting Lake, a creature as vast as a mountain, went mad and ran wild?”

“Thousands died. The Yangtze and Dongting Lake were filled with corpses and blood, and streets that once blazed through the night fell dark. Now, with the frightened people watching Hubei Province, what do you think would happen if everyone learned what you saw and heard?”
He left the rest unsaid, but in the suffocating silence, the boatman found the answer himself.
*I’d die. Without a doubt.*
He had been born into a poor tenant farmer’s family and lived his entire life illiterate, but he had not spent more than seventy years with his eyes and ears closed.
If anything, ferrying countless passengers had taught him how the world worked through the conversations he overheard.
*If I so much as breathe a word about what I know...*
It would be the end of him.
Neither the Son of Heaven seated upon the throne nor the City Lord of Hubei Province would want people to learn that the mad divine spirit of Dongting Lake had killed thousands.
No, perhaps they would eliminate everyone involved in the matter immediately.
A martial artist from a prestigious sect might be another matter, but an old boatman past seventy could be disposed of without anyone ever knowing.
“Good heavens. Oh, good heavens...”
As the boatman exhaled like a man whose soul had left his body, a lifeline was extended to him.
“Erase it all from your memory. Sell your boat, keep your mouth shut, and live out the rest of your days. Do that, and nothing will happen.”
“W-will that really be enough?”
“That is all I have to say.”
The young medical apprentice rose from his seat. The boatman stared dazedly at his departing back, then hurriedly called out.
“A-are you really a medical apprentice, sir?”
“Of course.”
The young medical apprentice, Mungyeong, answered without hesitation and released the doorknob.
Then he pointed to the brazier still burning in the corner of the room and the kettle slowly boiling atop it.
“I boiled that decoction myself. Three times a day. After meals. Make sure you take it.”
Caring for a patient until the very end was a medical apprentice’s duty.

He left the rest unsaid, but in the suffocating silence, the boatman found the answer himself.
*I’d die.
Without a doubt.*
He had been born into a poor tenant farmer’s family and lived his entire life illiterate, but he had not spent more than seventy years with his eyes and ears closed.
If anything, ferrying countless passengers had taught him how the world worked through the conversations he overheard.
*If I so much as breathe a word about what I know...*
It would be the end of him.
Neither the Son of Heaven seated upon the throne nor the City Lord of Hubei Province would want people to learn that the mad divine spirit of Dongting Lake had killed thousands.
No, perhaps they would eliminate everyone involved in the matter immediately.
A martial artist from a prestigious sect might be another matter, but an old boatman past seventy could be disposed of without anyone ever knowing.
“Good heavens.
Oh, good heavens...”
As the boatman exhaled like a man whose soul had left his body, a lifeline was extended to him.
“Erase it all from your memory.
Sell your boat, keep your mouth shut, and live out the rest of your days.
Do that, and nothing will happen.”
“W-will that really be enough?”
“That is all I have to say.”
The young medical apprentice rose from his seat.
The boatman stared dazedly at his departing back, then hurriedly called out.
“A-are you really a medical apprentice, sir?”
“Of course.”
The young medical apprentice, Mungyeong, answered without hesitation and released the doorknob.
Then he pointed to the brazier still burning in the corner of the room and the kettle slowly boiling atop it.
“I boiled that decoction myself.
Three times a day.
After meals.
Make sure you take it.”
Caring for a patient until the very end was a medical apprentice’s duty.

paragraphs: *Creak. Click.*
Mungyeong closed the door, leaving the boatman alone, and thought,
*That should be enough.*
Perhaps because he had lived so long, the boatman was far quicker on the uptake than Mungyeong had expected.
He would have to spend the rest of his life under the authorities’ watch, but that was still a hundred times better than turning up dead without anyone knowing how.
The deal with the City Lord of Hubei Province had already been struck. As long as the boatman kept his mouth shut, he could live out the remainder of his days in peace.
Besides, even if he did talk, everyone would dismiss him as a senile old madman.
*And he won’t have to worry about money anymore. All things considered, it’s not a bad arrangement for him.*
Mungyeong wondered what expression the boatman would make when he discovered the money pouch beside the brazier. He also recalled what the person who had asked him to deliver it had said.
“He came along for no good reason and nearly died. The least we can do is give him hazard pay and workers’ compensation.”
Workers’ compensation?
It was a bizarre term Mungyeong had never heard before, but then again, Jin Taekyung had always been like that.
A brat so young he was practically yellow instead of merely green—and one who never stopped surprising him.
*I can’t make sense of him at all.*
Mungyeong could have listed his peculiarities forever, but after everything that had happened, that impression had only grown stronger.
He recalled how Jin Taekyung had not shrunk back before that enormous, unprecedented monster. If anything, he had rampaged even more wildly. Mungyeong’s brow furrowed.
*Natural courage? Perhaps. But there was something else... Yes. He looked accustomed to it. Like a battle-hardened veteran who had survived countless battles.*
Had fighting Dark Heaven made Jin Taekyung accustomed to the bizarre phenomena known as supernatural powers?
Or did Jin Taekyung possess some secret no one else knew?
Mungyeong was walking along, lost in thought, when voices reached him.
“Physician Song, I heard they caught those bastards who deserve to die.”
“Good heavens. ‘Bastards who deserve to die’? Hyang, you’re a medical apprentice. How can you use such harsh language...?”
In the busy courtyard of the clinic, an older, middle-aged medical apprentice was scolding a young female medical apprentice who did not even look twenty. She pouted.
“A medical apprentice is still a person, isn’t she? Besides, those men deserve to die.”
“Ahem. Watch your words. You may be right, but I’m afraid someone might hear you.”
“You’re only saying that because of that gentleman, aren’t you? What does it matter? He’s too far away to hear us anyway.”
Contrary to the young woman’s carefree assumption, Mungyeong heard and saw everything happening around him without missing a thing.
That included their conversation.
“What do you think, Physician Song?”
“About what?”
“Oh, come on. Don’t pretend you don’t know. What else could I mean but the dark-path figures of Murim who committed those heinous crimes at Dark Heaven’s instigation?”
“What could a mere medical apprentice like me possibly say? I’m simply grateful the culprits have finally been captured. All I can do is devote myself to my duties.”

“But don’t you think it’s strange? The Sea Serpent Society’s ship sinking at Red Cliffs, the tragedy at Dongting Lake, even all the deaths involving the river bandits beyond Tianling Falls... They’re saying those men were responsible for everything.”
“Strange? In what way?”
“Well, it’s just... Hmm. You know Sister Hwang, right?”
“You mean Medical Apprentice Hwang?”
“Yes. She told me something. Um...”
The young medical apprentice trailed off and glanced around. Then she rose onto her toes and whispered.
It still sounded as loud as thunder to Mungyeong.

“She said the patient she’s looking after is a pretty famous wandering martial artist, and when he heard the story, he snorted. He said that no matter how many dark-path figures there were, they’d never be a match for the Yangtze One Saber.”
“The Yangtze One Saber?”

“That’s the name—or rather, the sobriquet—of the river bandit chief who suffered a disaster this time. Apparently, his martial arts are so powerful that there isn’t a martial artist anywhere who hasn’t heard of him.”
“According to what the wandering martial artist said, the authorities rounded up so many dark-path figures this time to cover something up.”
Mungyeong gave a silent, derisive laugh. The middle-aged medical apprentice’s face stiffened.
“Hyang, have you told anyone else about this?”
“No. I’d only just heard it when Physician Song called for me, so I came straight here.”
“What about Medical Apprentice Hwang? Did anyone else hear it besides you?”
“Why are you suddenly acting like this, Physician Song?”
“Answer me.”
The genial-looking medical apprentice’s face hardened as he questioned her. The young woman replied in a tiny voice.
“No one else was there. It was just the two of us. And I was the first person Sister Hwang told.”
“Phew. That’s fortunate, at least.”
“Did I do something wrong?”
“No. You and Medical Apprentice Hwang were merely careless because you’re both still young. But from now on, it would be best not to discuss this matter. Do you understand?”
“Ah. Yes.”
“Hyang.”
The middle-aged medical apprentice gently patted the cowed young woman on the head and continued in a kindly voice.

“Those dark-path mongrels who committed such heinous crimes will be executed at noon tomorrow—some by beheading, others by being torn apart by chariots. Their severed limbs will roll through the streets of Wuhan, and the ground will run red with blood.”
“What?”

“This is all thanks to the City Lord, who acted on the orders of His Majesty the Emperor, and to Great Hero Jin Taekyung of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, who personally exterminated the culprits. So don’t be swayed by false rumors. All you need to do is praise them.”
“Yes, yes.”
“No, not like that. Repeat after me. May His Majesty the Emperor live ten thousand years! A thousand years to the City Lord! A thousand years to Great Hero Jin Taekyung!”
“L-long live His Imperial Majesty the Emperor...”
“Louder!”
*Is he insane?*
Mungyeong stared at the middle-aged medical apprentice in disbelief and clicked his tongue inwardly.
If even a medical apprentice who could be considered educated acted like this, then the reaction of ordinary people was obvious.
*They’ll praise the Son of Heaven without a shred of doubt. It’s only been two days, so the report on this incident probably hasn’t even reached the imperial palace yet.*
A fabricated lie. A hidden truth.
The world never changed.
Mungyeong gave a small shake of his head and continued walking.
After leaving the clinic, which stood within the vast Hubei provincial government compound, he headed straight for a large estate among the many pavilions, one reserved for honored guests.
There, he found a master and Disciple proudly displaying the depth of their affection for each other.
“Say that again. What was that? ‘Jeok Cheongang’? ‘Take a shit’?”
“Old Master, please calm down...”
“I’ll pin your limbs down and shit on your face.”
“Whoa. Is that your thing?”
“You fucking piece of—”
“Dormammu, I’ve come to take a shit. Ah, sorry. It slipped out on instinct.”
“I swear on the ancestors of our sect, I’ll stuff shit into your mouth!”
“Waaah! Somebody save me!”
“Get over here this instant!”
*Swish! Swish! Swish! Whoooosh!*
As he watched the fierce chase unfold, a thought occurred to Mungyeong.
*What an affectionate—and filthy—master-and-Disciple relationship.*
Fortunately, Jeok Cheongang did not end up shitting in my mouth.
Of course, that didn’t mean things ended peacefully or normally.
*Bam!*
“Ah, wait. That hit bone...”
*Boom!*
“Ugh!”
*Goddamn it. Isn’t using Flame Divine Palm going too far?*

He had drastically reduced its power, presumably because he possessed at least a shred of human conscience. But still—how could he use Flame Divine Palm against his Disciple? No, against me, who was practically his Disciple?
*My insides are getting nice and warm.*
Who needed gukbap? One bowl of Flame Divine Palm, and I already felt full.
As I groaned and clutched my chest, Jeok Cheongang spoke in a sinister voice.
“Stop whining and get up.”
“Is it... over?”
“It’s nowhere near over. How dare you speak so casually to a master as high as the heavens...”
“Master?”
“Ahem. Not merely a master as high as the heavens, but this old man, who is even higher than the heavens. Do you think I raised you so I could be treated like this?”
“...My mother raised me, though. Why are you taking credit, Old Master?”
“You insolent brat!”
Just as Jeok Cheongang’s eyes began blazing, a lifeline descended from heaven.
“That’s enough.”
Someone had entered without making a sound. At Mungyeong’s single remark, Jeok Cheongang frowned.
“If you came in, you should have quietly watched. Why interfere?”
“It seemed excessive, so I stepped in. Is there a problem?”
*Damn. He’s got so much charisma. No wonder all his targets ended up dead when he was an assassin.*
I gazed at Mungyeong with emotion welling in my eyes.
“Oh, what a saint...”
“Look at this brat. He’s babbling nonsense again. I suppose he’ll need to be beaten for quite a while before he comes to his senses.”
Jeok Cheongang ominously rolled up his sleeves, but Mungyeong shook his head.
“Stop. This is excessive.”
“You’ve been getting on my nerves for a while now. Why do you keep meddling in other people’s business...?”
“No matter how I look at it, this is excessive. Shouldn’t I get a turn too?”
“Ah. Fair point.”
*Goddamn it. So that’s what he meant.*
The moment Jeok Cheongang graciously yielded his place to the next batter, a brilliant silver streak lashed out like a whip.
*Swish. Shhk!*
A chill ran down my spine, and cool air slipped through the gap in my severed clothes.
I swallowed hard as my shirt split cleanly into two halves, falling open to either side.
*Crazy.*
It had missed by a hair’s breadth.
I stood there with my heart pounding while Mungyeong gazed impassively at me.
“You didn’t dodge.”
“I couldn’t sense any killing intent.”
“You could still have dodged.”
“What would’ve been the point? If I dodged, I’d only get hit twice instead of once. You weren’t planning to kill me anyway, were you?”
“As expected, you’re strange. Strange enough to put me in a bad mood.”
*Really? For someone who’s in a bad mood, your expression is pretty ambiguous.*
Jeok Cheongang, on the other hand, looked unmistakably pissed off.
“How dare you swing a sword at my Disciple?”
“Disciple?”
At Mungyeong’s questioning repetition, Jeok Cheongang hastily corrected himself.
“How dare you swing a sword at that bastard who isn’t even fit to be called my Disciple?”
“Is that really something you can say after beating him like a dog with martial arts?”
“Whether I beat him like a dog or drive him like an ox, I’m the only one allowed to do it! And use your fists! Not a sword!”
I knew he was trying to look out for me, but somehow, that only made me feel sad.
Mungyeong narrowed his eyes as he listened to Jeok Cheongang’s utterly incoherent argument.
“I can feel my innate qi draining away just standing here. Enough. I didn’t come for this pointless exchange.”
Before Jeok Cheongang could say anything else, I hurriedly spoke up.
“Are you coming back from the clinic?”
“Yes. I went to check on the Dongting Fisherman and meet the boatman.”
“How are they?”
“The boatman has regained consciousness. There are no unusual symptoms, and he’s sharp enough to understand what he’s told. The Dongting Fisherman, on the other hand... isn’t doing well.”
I nodded gravely.
The boatman had been knocked unconscious by a Pressure-Point Strike before he was properly exposed to Fear.
The Dongting Fisherman was the exact opposite. This was only my guess, but he must have encountered the mutated Water God Dragon at Donghu Stronghold and been severely exposed to Fear.
“He must be in pretty bad shape. Though I suppose it’s only natural that he’s not in his right mind...”
“His injuries are severe.”
“What?”

“All four of his limbs were crushed, and his internal injuries are considerable. He’s a Supreme Peak master, and the City Lord gave him an elixir, so he should recover quickly. But that imugi must have gotten him good.”
“What’s wrong?”
“...Nothing. It’s nothing.”
It seemed I had forgotten to tell him.
I had truly, genuinely forgotten.
I’d had plenty of chances to mention it over the past two days, but I had forgotten anyway.
*I was pretty preoccupied, to be fair.*
Of course, that was because I had been tracking one person.
Honglan.
The culprit behind this entire incident.
The woman who had corrupted the imugi that had guarded the Yangtze and Dongting Lake for more than five hundred years and caused countless deaths.
And the woman I had never managed to find.
*Where the hell did she run off to?*
I pulled out the silver hairpin without realizing it and stared down at it, lost in thought.
*Bang!*
Someone burst onto the grounds, throwing open the main gate as if he meant to tear it down.
Gung Gibang must have raced here using his movement technique at full speed. He struggled to catch his breath before speaking.
“Huff. Hah... I found Honglan’s trail.”
