chapters.title: Chapter 482
paragraphs: “We found a trace of Honglan.”

Gung Gibang’s announcement did not agitate only me. Immediately after the battle with the Water God Dragon ended, Jeok Cheongang and Mungyeong—both of whom already knew what we had learned about Honglan’s identity—reacted as well.
“You found that goddamned bitch?”
“What happened?”
After Jeok Cheongang’s blunt question and Mungyeong’s shameless question, asked while he was still concealing his identity, I spoke grimly.
“A trace?”
The result was what mattered.
Gung Gibang had not said they had found Honglan. He had clearly said they had found *a trace of Honglan*, and the implication was obvious.
“You didn’t find her.”
Gung Gibang had finally caught his breath. He nodded.
“Not yet. But I’ve sent messenger pigeons to our disciples, Wudang, the Zhuge Clan, and the government troops, so soon—”
“No. You won’t find her.”
I answered firmly and continued.
“If she were that easy to catch, we would’ve picked up her trail long ago.”
The government troops were idiots with nothing but numbers on their side. The Beggars’ Sect, Wudang, and the Zhuge Clan were at least reliable, but the chances of them finding Honglan...
Slim, no matter how I looked at it.

Even setting aside my gut feeling that there was no way she would be caught this easily, if she had a Moving Formation hidden nearby, we would all be like dogs left staring at the roof after the chicken got away.
“What kind of trace did you find, and where? Tell me everything.”
“A military vessel was found at Red Cliffs.”
“Don’t tell me it was...”
“That’s right. The very vessel where Honglan was last seen. The authorities have already confirmed it.”
Two days ago, shortly after we left to find the Dongting Fisherman, the government troops had attempted to take Honglan to the Hubei provincial government.

She was the only survivor besides Ju Wongong, a member of the Huang tribe. On the surface, she was also one of the chief contributors to his rescue, alongside me. From the authorities’ perspective, taking her with them had been the obvious choice.
*Though that was the last time anyone saw her.*
After that, the military vessel Honglan had boarded vanished like a ghost.
So did the roughly one hundred government troops and sailors aboard it.
And now Gung Gibang had brought us news that the same vessel had been found.
“...And? What happened?”
In truth, I already knew the answer before I asked.
*They’re probably all dead.*
I had already heard that the people who boarded the vessel with Honglan were ordinary men with no connection to Dark Heaven.
There was no way Honglan had tossed them a few coins for their trouble, waved goodbye, and gone peacefully on her way.
The grim expression on Gung Gibang’s face only supported my guess.
Except—
“Ninety-four in total. Every one of them committed suicide by stabbing themselves in the throat.”
“What?”
That, I had not expected.
I blinked silently, then somehow managed to force out my voice.
“All those people... committed suicide together?”

“Without a doubt. They stabbed themselves in the throat with the daggers they carried as standard equipment. When the bodies were examined, they were said to have died with smiles on their faces. Of course, Honglan was nowhere to be found.”
“What the hell?”
I would not have been this shocked if Honglan had simply killed them herself.
But this was a kind of death far beyond anything I had imagined.
A mass suicide.
And they had been smiling?
For a moment, I could not speak. Then Mungyeong and Jeok Cheongang opened their mouths almost simultaneously.
“This is...”
“Yeah. It has to be the Soul-Seizing Technique. And an extremely powerful one.”
The Soul-Seizing Technique.
As the name suggested, it was one of the monstrous martial arts and supreme techniques that bewitched and controlled an opponent’s soul.
I knew what it was because it had often appeared in the wuxia novels I had read, but this was the first time I had encountered it since coming to Murim.
“Wait. That actually exists?”
Jeok Cheongang stared at me as if I had said something absurd.
“Is that something the man who took down a five-hundred-year-old imugi should be saying?”
“...Well, when you put it that way, I don’t really have a response.”

“For untold ages, the Demonic Cult has stood at the heart of the Thousand-Year Demonic Path. Dark Heaven is the successor to that very Demonic Cult. It would hardly be strange for people who use the Soul-Seizing Technique to be running wild.”
“But you said before that the Soul-Seizing Technique was nothing special.”
“That’s only true against this old man. The reason that wretched witch Honglan didn’t use it on you from the beginning is likely much the same.”
“Because I’m a Supreme Peak master?”
“To break through the wall means that one’s body and mind have reached a supreme realm. And how much more resistant would you be, with your Middle Dantian awakened?”
Jeok Cheongang paused, then suddenly frowned and added,
“No. Perhaps what that bitch wanted was for you to fight the imugi.”
“Either way, what matters is that the culprit is a master of the Soul-Seizing Technique and has vanished like a ghost.”
Mungyeong quietly joined the conversation, but Gung Gibang shook his head.
“There’s one more thing.”
“...What?”
“The investigation found that there were ninety-six people aboard the military vessel in total. Even excluding Honglan, that leaves one person.”
“Wait. Then...”
“There’s one survivor. The officer who commanded the military vessel, attached to the Hubei provincial government.”
A survivor?
Everyone, myself included, stared wide-eyed at Gung Gibang. He swallowed hard before continuing.
“He’s on his way here now.”
A brief silence followed.
Then Jeok Cheongang spoke, his expression stiff.
“By the way, is speaking informally to this old man a trend among young people these days?”
“...I-I wasn’t speaking to you, Great Hero Jeok.”
“You won’t come to your senses until you’ve been beaten like a dog on slaughter day. Get down.”

“His name is Song Ho. He is the son of a prominent merchant family in Hubei Province, and thanks to his father’s efforts, he was summoned by the City Lord of Hubei Province. Two days ago, the City Lord dispatched him with orders to bring in the culprit.”
The middle-aged man, whose looks must have broken plenty of women’s hearts in his youth, continued anxiously.

“He was a womanizer and had been involved in several scandals, but he showed talent in both literary and martial pursuits from a young age. The City Lord kept him close not merely because of his father’s influence, but because he was sharp and dependable when it came to getting things done.”
I didn’t know what he had been like before, but he certainly didn’t seem that way now.
I half listened to the middle-aged man—the Hubei Branch Leader of the Lower District Sect—and studied the young officer sitting before us, bound with rope.
His skin was dry and rough. His eyes were unfocused, as though he had been possessed by a ghost, and clear saliva dripped from the corner of his open mouth.
*Drip. Drip.*
Jeok Cheongang watched the young officer drool vacantly and furrowed his brow.
“He’s been completely ensnared by the Soul-Seizing Technique. He’s already lost his mind.”
I agreed with Jeok Cheongang completely.
There was no trace of reason left in the young man before us. Instead of a promising military officer, a doll with its soul pulled out was sitting there.
“How is his condi—how is he?”
At my hurried correction, Mungyeong slowly shook his head.
“It’s hopeless. I cannot say what prolonged observation might reveal, but for now, there does not appear to be even the slightest chance of recovery.”
“If there’s no hope, how bad is he?”
“To lose one’s soul is no different from dying. In this state, he will be unable to speak or act on his own.”
His condition was far worse than I had expected.
Jin Wikyung, who had hurried over after hearing that the sole survivor had been escorted here, spoke up.
“Would another renowned physician have a different opinion?”
“No matter who examines him, they will reach the same conclusion. If their opinion differs from mine, they are probably a quack.”
“Good heavens. Even if the Divine Physician examined him?”
*Hyung. That’s the guy.*

I swallowed the words rising in my throat. The Hubei Branch Leader of the Lower District Sect—who had briefly been treated as an agent of Dark Heaven after mistaking Honglan’s identity—bowed repeatedly and withdrew.
Then, just as the room fell silent—
“Ah... uh... oh.”
A cold chill raced up my spine.
Everyone around me, myself included, stared at the young officer with our eyes wide open.
His eyes remained hazy and unfocused. In contrast, his slack mouth began to twitch, and a voice slowly seeped out.
“Uh... ah.”
“...That’s impossible.”
Mungyeong muttered in disbelief.

He had cared for and treated countless patients. With medical skill worthy of the title Divine Physician and the martial prowess of a Supreme Peak master, Mungyeong’s confident diagnoses were practically absolute laws.
Or at least they had been until a few seconds ago.
“What is this?”
Mungyeong rarely raised his voice, but now he did as he swiftly took the officer’s pulse.
His expression grew as complex and subtle as it had been when he looked at the Water God Dragon.
“His condition is completely unchanged. Then why?”
And in the next moment, everyone present heard the voice that flowed from between the officer’s lips.
“Nothing is absolute, and nothing remains unchanged forever. You’d think you would have learned that by now. Don’t you agree?”
It was unmistakably a man’s voice—the officer’s own.
But Gung Gibang and I both recognized the echo of someone else within it. Our eyes met, and we shouted the same name at the same time.
“Honglan!”
It felt as though a bolt of lightning had pierced the crown of my head.
If Hyuk Mujin and Cheongpung had been here, they would have reacted the same way.
I looked at the young officer—or rather, at Honglan, confronting me from some distant place through the officer’s body—with a sunken gaze and spoke.
“Where are you, you fucking bitch?”
“Oh my. Our young master has a rougher mouth than I expected. Men who swear at women aren’t very popular, you know.”
“Fuck off. I’ve never been popular anyway.”
“I didn’t expect that answer. You really are a masterpiece.”
“Cut the bullshit and tell me where you are. I’ll leave you in tatters.”
“You’re cuter than I’d heard. And funny, too.”
Her familiar, clear laughter slipped out through the officer’s lips.
The corners of his mouth remained the same, yet her voice continued to flow from it. The sight was enough to raise goose bumps.
Even then, I did not miss one important phrase.
“...Than you’d heard?”
“You already know, don’t you? We have many eyes and ears. Blood Lord did most of the talking.”
“Dark Heaven. Yeah, I figured.”
Even a 99.9 percent possibility was still only a guess without that final 0.1 percent.
Honglan had revealed her identity without the slightest hesitation. She continued brightly.

“I was surprised. You’ve become much stronger than Blood Lord said you were. Then again, if that were still all you amounted to, the Western Heaven Demon Lord would have killed you before the imugi got the chance.”
Why was this happening?
My anger showed no sign of fading, yet my mind and voice were growing calmer instead.
Unlike before, I asked in a remarkably composed voice,
“Who are you?”
It was a genuine question.
Even as I asked, I did not expect her to answer willingly.
But Honglan shattered my expectations with a single word.
“The Southern Heaven Demon Empress.”
“The Southern... Heaven Demon Empress?”
*These fucking bastards are really screwing around in every direction—east, west, south, and north.*

chapters.title: Chapter 483
paragraphs: “Southern Heaven... Demon Empress?”
Honglan—or rather, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, inhabiting the body of a young military officer—spoke in a lighthearted tone.
“It’s embarrassing to hear someone else say that sobriquet aloud.”
“Embarrassing my ass. You bastards are raising hell in every direction—east, west, south, and north. So is the eastern one the East Virgin Forever-Alone, and the northern one North Korea’s Kim?”
“The sobriquets are different, but you came surprisingly close. You’re smarter than I expected.”
“...Damn it.”
Western Heaven Demon Lord and Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
Even Mimi-chan could tell that those sobriquets had been created with the four directions in mind.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord was already a monster I had barely managed to defeat after several brushes with death. And there were at least three more like him?
But an even more important question remained.
I stared at the military officer’s vacant face.
“How did you do it?”
“Oh my. What could possibly have our young Great Hero so curious?”
“You know what I’m talking about.”
A strange light suddenly flashed through the officer’s slack eyes.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress gazed at me through someone else’s eyes, then casually tossed out a question.
“You saw it, didn’t you?”

“There’s no way you could have found it in only two days. So I suppose a spiritual creature really is a spiritual creature. Then again, a five-hundred-year-old imugi would certainly qualify as a divine being.”
Having grasped everything in an instant, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress smoothly added,
“Then you must also know that I won’t answer you.”
It was all still vivid. The traces of the Gate I had glimpsed through fragments of memory. And the sight of the Water God Dragon being tainted by the demonic qi that had flowed from it.
That was something that could not—and should not—have happened.
At least not here in Murim. It was an incomprehensible phenomenon that should never have appeared in this world.
Yet the Southern Heaven Demon Empress and Dark Heaven had dragged the impossible into reality. It was enough to make me wish it were all a lie.
“What the hell are you people after?”
“After?”
The next moment, clear laughter flowed between the officer’s lips. It carried genuine amusement, not something feigned.
After laughing aloud for a while, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress continued.
“Child. I am merely a lowly servant who moves according to orders. No one can presume to fathom that person’s will.”
That person.
Everyone present knew whom those two words referred to.
Jeok Cheongang muttered in a voice that seemed to boil like lava.
“Lord of Heaven.”
*Crack.*
With the sound of bones shifting, the officer’s head turned toward Jeok Cheongang like a creaking wooden puppet.
“I’ve heard that a crazed old monster lives on Mount Jiuhua. Fire King Jeok Cheongang, you are correct. It is indeed that person. The greatest and noblest of all...”
“You mean a fucking bastard who wouldn’t be worth the satisfaction of burning alive. How dare you wag that wicked tongue before this old man?”
A brief silence followed Jeok Cheongang’s words, which carried a cold flame.
Then the officer’s tightly closed lips slowly parted, and a subdued voice flowed out.
“You’d best choose your words more carefully if you wish to cling to that stubborn life of yours a little longer.”
“My life?”
Jeok Cheongang snorted and turned to me.
“You tell her. What happened to everyone who came after this old man’s life?”
“They died. Every last one of them.”
“Then how would you feel about this old man adding a bitch instead of a bastard to his kill list?”
There was no question about it. I thrust up a thumb.
“You’re a true feminist of this era.”
“Femibista? What’s that?”
“It means you’re fair. You beat the shit out of everyone equally, regardless of sex or age.”
“Is that some word young people use these days? Whatever the case, I like the meaning.”
Jeok Cheongang nodded in satisfaction, then glared at the Southern Heaven Demon Empress inhabiting the officer’s body.
“You heard that? This femibista intends to punish you and that Lord of Heaven fellow, or whatever his name is. So wash your neck and wait.”
*Uh. Should I stop him now, before the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist turns into the Feminist Fist?*
Still, I felt much better. The confusion in my head seemed to have cleared completely.
*Yeah, fuck it. We just need to beat the shit out of all of them.*
Wasn’t that the Fire Gate Clan’s motto, anyway? Smash, break, and burn anyone we decided was an enemy.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress was never going to answer my questions. In that case, no matter what Dark Heaven tried, all I had to do was keep moving forward and smash through it.
*I don’t have a choice anyway.*
Once I had climbed onto the back of a raging tiger, there were only two paths left.
And rather than be thrown from its back, I would end this insane struggle even if I had to smash the tiger’s skull to do it.
No. I had to.
“Phew...”
I exhaled the breath I had been holding, then leaned close to the military officer. Looking through the soul-less eyes at some distant place, I spoke.
“When we meet again... you’re going to die.”
The officer’s lips twitched.
“Yes. I, too, look forward to that day. And when it comes, no one here will survive.”
His head slowly turned. His unfocused, milky eyes swept over everyone in the room one by one.
But no one avoided that chilling gaze. Mungyeong was no exception.
“You should put an end to this futile killing. A blade always turns back on its wielder in the end.”
His voice and tone were polite, mindful of the others around him. But hidden within them was a blade only a handful of people could detect.
It was the true face of the greatest assassin of all time—the supreme martial artist known as the Slaughter Saint, who had walked a path stained with nothing but blood.
“...What an unusual child. Unusual enough to make me curious about this Divine Physician.”
But the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, borrowing someone else’s body, did not seem to have grasped Mungyeong’s true identity.

She might have known his public identity as the Divine Physician’s Disciple, but the connection between the Slaughter Saint who had vanished forty years ago and a young medical apprentice was far too tenuous.
And before the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s suspicions about Mungyeong could deepen, Jin Wikyung spoke in a heavy voice.
“I swear on the name of the Jin Family of Taiyuan that you will never touch so much as a hair on our youngest’s head.”
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan. Can that paltry family and its feeble martial arts truly protect that child?”
“Even a sewer rat will fight a tiger for the sake of its young. If you’re curious, come and see for yourself. I’ll have no choice but to show you.”
Even in the face of a bizarre phenomenon far beyond the bounds of common sense, Jin Wikyung did not lose his composure.
No sooner had he finished, calm yet resolute, than Gung Gibang scratched his matted hair.
“Great Hero Jin, it would hurt my feelings if you left our Sect out.”
“I forgot the Beggars’ Sect. Will you join us?”

“My Master used to say that one dog-beating stick can only beat a neighborhood cur, but a hundred can beat even a tiger to death. So what do you think would happen if a hundred thousand Beggars’ Sect disciples gathered?”
The true strength of the Beggars’ Sect lay in its overwhelming numbers.
Their forces were so vast that no one could object to calling them the hundred-thousand-strong Beggars’ Sect.
Gung Gibang, the Successor Beggar who stood only one step from the summit of the Beggars’ Sect, bared his yellow teeth in a grin.
“You were such a lovely young lady. It’s a shame to see you like this. But what can we do? Don’t resent me too much if I smash that pretty face of yours with my club.”
“Resent you?”
The corner of the officer’s mouth slowly curled upward.
Through his mouth, now twisted into a grotesque smile that threatened to split his skin, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress addressed everyone.
“There’s no need to be so impatient. It won’t be long now...”
Her voice faded like a dying campfire.
By then, dark red blood was already flowing from between the officer’s lips. Without hesitation, I seized his wrist and felt for his pulse.
*Whoosh.*
Internal energy surged from my dantian and poured into his body, but the death that had already begun could not be reversed.
Things that outlived their usefulness were discarded.
Perhaps that was why the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had kept the officer alive.
*A puppet whose body she could borrow for a while.*
Blood gushed from his mouth, then spilled in a stream.
And it wasn’t only his mouth.
Dark red blood poured from his eyes, nose, and ears—from the seven apertures of the human body.
A death that could not be stopped by several jiazi of internal energy or even a Pressure-Point Strike loomed before the officer’s eyes.
“It’s too late.”
At that exact moment, Mungyeong’s voice rang in my ears.
Along with a flood of blood, one final sentence slipped from the officer’s slowly parting lips.
“Everything shall be as that person wills.”
*Slump. Thud.*
That was the end.
The officer’s head drooped as the last of his vitality drained away, and his breathing stopped.
As silence descended with one man’s death, the presence approaching the estate stopped outside the door.
“Um... may I come in?”
The voice was familiar.
A young man cautiously poked his head through the slowly opening door.
“Benefactor, Great Hero Zhuge Pong is looking for you.”
“Not Zhuge Pong. Zhuge Feng.”
“Yes. Great Hero Zhuge Pong.”
“...I should just stop talking.”
I sighed and rose to my feet.
I didn’t ask where Crouching Dragon Guest Zhuge Feng was, where I needed to go, or why he was looking for me.
After all, I was the one who had told them about *that place* in the first place.
“So, did you find it?”
“Yes.”
Cheongpung’s eyes lit up.
“It’s exactly the place you described, Benefactor.”
That place was the very location from the Water God Dragon’s memories.
Yeah. The damn Gate.
Honglan—or rather, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—opened her eyes.

She lifted the silk curtain of the gently swaying four-horse carriage. Beyond the lattice window, dense undergrowth stretched into the distance, while the Escort Bureau’s men sweated in the hot, humid weather of the southern regions.
“Hmm.”
With her chin resting in her hand as she gazed out the window, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress looked like a painting all by herself.
Then a furious shout thundered over the heads of the Escort Bureau men stealing entranced glances at her.
“Stop gawking and focus on the delivery! Unless you want to get yourselves killed by the Miao people we’ll meet in a few days!”
Despite the rough language, the speaker was a woman of dazzling beauty.
Beneath the bamboo hat pulled low to block the sunlight, her long, straight nose was sharp as a blade, and her lightly tanned skin was pleasing to the eye.
*A female escort? You don’t see that every day.*
It did not take long for the female escort, who had spent quite some time berating the rough men, to notice the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s gaze.
She eased the reins, drew alongside the carriage, and addressed her through the window.
“Is there a problem?”
“Not at all. Thanks to all your hard work, I’m traveling quite comfortably.”
“Then why are you looking at me like...?”
“Just because.”
“Pardon?”
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress smiled sweetly.
“You’re so young and pretty. I couldn’t help looking.”
“Ah, thank you.”
The female escort, the Young Bureau Head of a small-to-medium Escort Bureau, was flustered but did her best to hide it.

The fact that the woman complimenting her was beautiful enough to make even other women fall for her was one thing. More importantly, she was a passenger who had paid a considerable sum, so the Young Bureau Head’s reaction was only natural.
But at the next words, she could no longer conceal her bewilderment.
“I covet it. Enough to want to take it and put it on my own face.”
“I’m joking. Just joking.”
Her bright laughter rang out. The Southern Heaven Demon Empress continued in an amused voice as the female escort froze.
“So, how much farther is it to Yunnan?”
At that moment, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress could barely contain her delight.
Delight at the screams and deaths that would soon be heard in another place.
And delight at having met a new face.

Demon Empress?”
Honglan—or rather, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, inhabiting the body of a young military officer—spoke in a lighthearted tone.
“It’s embarrassing to hear someone else say that sobriquet aloud.”
“Embarrassing my ass.
You bastards are raising hell in every direction—east, west, south, and north.
So is the eastern one the East Virgin Forever-Alone, and the northern one North Korea’s Kim?”
“The sobriquets are different, but you came surprisingly close.
You’re smarter than I expected.”
“...Damn it.”
Western Heaven Demon Lord and Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
Even Mimi-chan could tell that those sobriquets had been created with the four directions in mind.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord was already a monster I had barely managed to defeat after several brushes with death.
And there were at least three more like him?
But an even more important question remained.
I stared at the military officer’s vacant face.
“How did you do it?”
“Oh my.
What could possibly have our young Great Hero so curious?”
“You know what I’m talking about.”
A strange light suddenly flashed through the officer’s slack eyes.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress gazed at me through someone else’s eyes, then casually tossed out a question.
“You saw it, didn’t you?”
“There’s no way you could have found it in only two days.
So I suppose a spiritual creature really is a spiritual creature.
Then again, a five-hundred-year-old imugi would certainly qualify as a divine being.”
Having grasped everything in an instant, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress smoothly added,
“Then you must also know that I won’t answer you.”
It was all still vivid.
The traces of the Gate I had glimpsed through fragments of memory.
And the sight of the Water God Dragon being tainted by the demonic qi that had flowed from it.
That was something that could not—and should not—have happened.
At least not here in Murim.
It was an incomprehensible phenomenon that should never have appeared in this world.
Yet the Southern Heaven Demon Empress and Dark Heaven had dragged the impossible into reality.
It was enough to make me wish it were all a lie.
“What the hell are you people after?”
“After?”
The next moment, clear laughter flowed between the officer’s lips.
It carried genuine amusement, not something feigned.
After laughing aloud for a while, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress continued.
“Child.
I am merely a lowly servant who moves according to orders.
No one can presume to fathom that person’s will.”
That person.
Everyone present knew whom those two words referred to.
Jeok Cheongang muttered in a voice that seemed to boil like lava.
“Lord of Heaven.”
*Crack.*
With the sound of bones shifting, the officer’s head turned toward Jeok Cheongang like a creaking wooden puppet.
“I’ve heard that a crazed old monster lives on Mount Jiuhua.
Fire King Jeok Cheongang, you are correct.
It is indeed that person.
The greatest and noblest of all...”
“You mean a fucking bastard who wouldn’t be worth the satisfaction of burning alive.
How dare you wag that wicked tongue before this old man?”
A brief silence followed Jeok Cheongang’s words, which carried a cold flame.
Then the officer’s tightly closed lips slowly parted, and a subdued voice flowed out.
“You’d best choose your words more carefully if you wish to cling to that stubborn life of yours a little longer.”
“My life?”
Jeok Cheongang snorted and turned to me.
“You tell her.
What happened to everyone who came after this old man’s life?”
“They died.
Every last one of them.”
“Then how would you feel about this old man adding a bitch instead of a bastard to his kill list?”
There was no question about it.
I thrust up a thumb.
“You’re a true feminist of this era.”
“Femibista?
What’s that?”
“It means you’re fair.
You beat the shit out of everyone equally, regardless of sex or age.”
“Is that some word young people use these days?
Whatever the case, I like the meaning.”
Jeok Cheongang nodded in satisfaction, then glared at the Southern Heaven Demon Empress inhabiting the officer’s body.
“You heard that?
This femibista intends to punish you and that Lord of Heaven fellow, or whatever his name is.
So wash your neck and wait.”
*Uh.
Should I stop him now, before the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist turns into the Feminist Fist?*
Still, I felt much better.
The confusion in my head seemed to have cleared completely.
*Yeah, fuck it.
We just need to beat the shit out of all of them.*
Wasn’t that the Fire Gate Clan’s motto, anyway?
Smash, break, and burn anyone we decided was an enemy.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress was never going to answer my questions.
In that case, no matter what Dark Heaven tried, all I had to do was keep moving forward and smash through it.
*I don’t have a choice anyway.*
Once I had climbed onto the back of a raging tiger, there were only two paths left.
And rather than be thrown from its back, I would end this insane struggle even if I had to smash the tiger’s skull to do it.
No.
I had to.
“Phew...”
I exhaled the breath I had been holding, then leaned close to the military officer.
Looking through the soul-less eyes at some distant place, I spoke.
“When we meet again... you’re going to die.”
The officer’s lips twitched.
“Yes.
I, too, look forward to that day.
And when it comes, no one here will survive.”
His head slowly turned.
His unfocused, milky eyes swept over everyone in the room one by one.
But no one avoided that chilling gaze.
Mungyeong was no exception.
“You should put an end to this futile killing.
A blade always turns back on its wielder in the end.”
His voice and tone were polite, mindful of the others around him.
But hidden within them was a blade only a handful of people could detect.
It was the true face of the greatest assassin of all time—the supreme martial artist known as the Slaughter Saint, who had walked a path stained with nothing but blood.
“...What an unusual child.
Unusual enough to make me curious about this Divine Physician.”
But the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, borrowing someone else’s body, did not seem to have grasped Mungyeong’s true identity.

She might have known his public identity as the Divine Physician’s Disciple, but the connection between the Slaughter Saint who had vanished forty years ago and a young medical apprentice was far too tenuous.
And before the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s suspicions about Mungyeong could deepen, Jin Wikyung spoke in a heavy voice.
“I swear on the name of the Jin Family of Taiyuan that you will never touch so much as a hair on our youngest’s head.”
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan.
Can that paltry family and its feeble martial arts truly protect that child?”
“Even a sewer rat will fight a tiger for the sake of its young.
If you’re curious, come and see for yourself.
I’ll have no choice but to show you.”
Even in the face of a bizarre phenomenon far beyond the bounds of common sense, Jin Wikyung did not lose his composure.

chapters.title: Chapter 484
paragraphs: It wasn’t difficult to find our destination. The boatmen had already made one round trip and learned the waterways, so they guided the vessel forward with practiced ease.
*Whoosh...*
It was hard to believe that a storm had raged only two days ago. The river was calm, and the breeze was cool.
Sitting at the bow beneath the pouring sunlight, I spotted something familiar in the passing scenery.
*That’s right. It was around here.*
The *Memory Fragment* contained the memories left in the Water God Dragon’s mind, and I had seen and felt everything from its perspective.
Naturally, that included the way to *that place*.
“Wait. Cheongpung, are we sure this is the way?”
At my sudden question, Cheongpung tilted his head.
“It is. Why do you ask?”
“It looks a little different from what I remember. Especially that cliff over there...”
“Oh, that? There were some circumstances.”
“What circumstances?”
“Well, we followed the route you told us about, but the gap was so narrow that only a hand could fit through.”
“Oh.”
So that was why no one had set foot there for so many years. As countless years passed and sediment accumulated, the cliff had eventually blocked the passage.
That hadn’t been a problem for the Water God Dragon. It could simply swim underneath instead of passing through the cliff.
Humans, however, were a different story.
“So?”
“We cut through it.”
“...You cut through it?”
“Yes. The Wudang grandpa and I snipped it apart with our swords.”
*What the hell? He’s talking about cutting through a cliff like it’s a piece of paper.*
But with Origami Man—no, Perfected Being Hyeongong, the Supreme Peak master Wudang was so proud of—and Cheongpung, it wasn’t impossible.
Even I could have managed it without much trouble.
“Anyway, we carved straight through. It wasn’t that hard. I heard the others who arrived with the second group cleaned up the rest.”
“...Uh. Right.”
Sometimes I forgot that I was surrounded by monsters.
And that I was one of them.
Jeok Cheongang, who had been listening to our conversation, poked Mungyeong in the ribs.
“Has the world gone mad? I don’t remember things being like this when we were young. Those two are just monsters, right?”
“Don’t lump me in with you. It’s insulting.”
“So how old were you when you became a Supreme Peak master?”
“They’re the monsters.”
“Yes. That must be it. Hah. Perhaps the heavenly patterns have grown clouded. Murim has changed. It certainly has.”
As Jeok Cheongang lamented, the vessel continued between cliff walls cut so perfectly straight that the sight sent a chill down my spine.
Then a new landscape—and new people—gradually came into view.
*Whoosh! Splash!*
Peak masters swept down using the exquisite movement technique known as Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water. They stepped across the river’s surface and blocked the vessel with imposing auras.
“Stop! Everyone aboard must state their names and sobriquets. Once the identity verification process is complete—”
Jeok Cheongang, already on edge after his recent aquatic lifestyle, stuck his head out with a fiendish expression.
“This old man is the Fire King.”
“Gasp!”
“Stop us and you die.”
“Y-yes, sir!”
“O-open the way! No one stop them!”
*Whoosh!*

Gung Gibang watched the figures vanish at twice the speed with which they had appeared and muttered, “Was Wudang’s movement technique always this impressive? The Beggars’ Sect will have to stay on its toes.”
No. They had probably realized how completely fucked they were and fled for their lives.

Either way, everything proceeded smoothly after that. The vicious Fire Pokémon Jeok Cheongang needed no explanation, and my face was famous enough that anyone who failed to recognize me might as well have been working for Dark Heaven. Besides, Cheongpung and Gung Gibang were with me.
“Oh, did someone just recognize me?”
“Of course. You’re the only beggar who travels with me.”
“Wow! Someone recognized me just now, too!”
“Of course. You’re the only person who travels around with a horned water snake.”
“Okaaay...”
I ignored the dejected Gung Gibang and Cheongpung and focused on the scene ahead.
Archers had somehow climbed to the tops of the towering cliffs and stood ready to fire. I could also sense masters concealed all around us.
*Wudang, the Zhuge Clan, and it looks like the Beggars’ Sect is here too.*
The security was formidable.
But considering the weight and importance of the situation, that was only natural.
“Has the City Lord of Hubei Province decided to bury this matter completely?”
Jin Wikyung nodded gravely.
“For now. The common people would hardly welcome the news that a five-hundred-year-old imugi had gone mad and run amok.”
“That’s true.”
Public support was a double-edged sword.

Under normal circumstances, the simple folk would revere the Son of Heaven, but the moment a flood or earthquake struck, they would pull a Hyuk Mujin-level about-face and declare it an omen of the nation’s ruin.
And if a plague came along as part of a buy-two-get-one-free deal, the people of this era would grab the pickaxes they used to till their fields and charge out to overturn the country.
How much worse would it be if an imugi, worshiped by countless people as a divine creature, suddenly went mad and killed several thousand people?
The City Lord of Hubei Province would want to hide that truth as much as possible.
“He does agree, at least in part, that Dark Heaven is an extremely dangerous organization.”
“...He agrees *in part*? Even after all this?”
I took back what I had just said.
Concealing the Water God Dragon’s existence was one thing, but how many people had died because of this incident? And he only agreed *in part*?
He clearly still hadn’t come to his senses.
“It is a delusion born of arrogance. He believes Murim is merely Murim and that it poses no threat to their ability to govern the country. I tried my best to persuade him, but it was of little use.”
Jeok Cheongang abruptly cut in with a disgruntled voice.

“Those idiot government officials haven’t changed at all. They were exactly the same during the Great Faction War. When the Demonic Cult pushed down through Sichuan, they sat on their hands. Only after the civilian casualties mounted did they scramble to gather troops.”
“What happened then?”

“What do you think happened? By then, the Demonic Cult had already been defeated and withdrawn, and some bastard calling himself a Great General came strutting over to take credit. He said it was all thanks to His Imperial Majesty’s grace and whatnot. Since the Emperor was the master of the country, it didn’t really matter who won, but congratulations on your victory. That sort of bullshit.”
“You showed remarkable restraint. For you, Old Master, that was practically the patience of a Buddha.”
Jeok Cheongang looked at me as if I were talking nonsense.

“Why would this old man have put up with that? I tried to beat him to death. If Hong Dao hadn’t stopped me, it wouldn’t have been the Great Faction War. It would have been the Great Government War, or something like that.”
“...Ah. Right.”
“In any case, don’t expect much from the government officials. We should be satisfied that they at least turned the dark-path figures who had been sitting quietly into Dark Heaven’s lackeys.”
Jin Wikyung answered with a bitter smile.
“Yes. Fortunately, the people’s anger and wariness toward Dark Heaven have been soaring ever since.”
“They had nothing to do with this incident, but what can we do? They aren’t exactly innocent, either. They’re dark-path figures, so using this opportunity to uproot them wouldn’t be a bad idea.”

After negotiating with Murim, the government had crushed Hubei Province’s dark-path figures as scapegoats to appease the people’s anger. Both sides had gotten what they wanted, so it was a kind of give-and-take.
Of course, our reputations had skyrocketed once again in the process.
*Whether the government would actually step in even if Dark Heaven ran wilder than it already had was another question.*
As I thought about that, the vessel that had been charging forward finally came to a stop.
We docked at a temporary pier built against the cliff, and gazes poured toward us.
“That’s Great Hero Jeok Cheongang.”
“The Successor Beggar is beside him, too. I was wondering where the Huashan Divine Dragon had gone.”
“Wait. Isn’t that young man the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon?”
“Did you hear? There’s talk among the leaders that the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon was the one who took down the imugi...”
They thought they were whispering, but I could hear every word.
*You idiots.*
Annoyed by the muttering, I deliberately scowled. The area fell silent in an instant.
Then a shout broke the silence.
“Oh, you’re here!”
The middle-aged man running toward us was drenched from head to toe in mud and river water. Unfamiliar aquatic plants were tangled in his disheveled hair.
I muttered inwardly as I watched him approach.
*That man is the Family Head of the Zhuge Clan?*
It was something I was only now fully appreciating, but Crouching Dragon Guest Zhuge Feng was unquestionably an eccentric even by Murim standards.
“Family Head, I normally wouldn’t say anything, but there are outsiders present. Please show some decorum...”
“Ah, please move aside, Uncle.”
“Family Heaaad!”
He had clearly stuffed his dignity into a mailbox and left it there.
Zhuge Feng ruthlessly brushed aside the family elder trying to stop him, hurried over, and spoke with his face flushed.
“We found it. We really found it!”
“Yes, I know. Cheongpung told me—”
“At first, I wondered what kind of bullshit you were talking about, but it was sitting right there in the place you described!”
Wasn’t that a little too honest?
I had explained everything so earnestly, and he had dismissed it as bullshit?
Seeing my expression, Zhuge Feng continued with an appropriately solemn look.
“Our ancestor, Zhuge Wuhou, once said that one should tap even a stone bridge before crossing it. Don’t take it too personally.”
Was trotting out their ancestor whenever it suited them a Zhuge Clan motto, or was it hereditary?
I stared suspiciously at Zhuge Feng.
“...Did Zhuge Wuhou really say that? As far as I know, that’s a proverb from another country.”
“He must have said it at least once in his life. Is that important right now?”
*Unbelievable.*
Whether it was the Chinese over there or the Chinese over here, they were astonishingly good at copying other people’s work.
Before I could respond, Zhuge Feng spun around and started walking ahead of us.
“Follow me.”
Jeok Cheongang, who had been trembling with delight at finally being able to set foot on even a temporary pier, narrowed his eyes.
“‘Follow me’? Was that directed at this old man?”
“...I wasn’t speaking to you, Senior.”
“Then watch your mouth from now on. Straighten out that folded tongue before this old man splits you in half.”
“Yes, sir.”
“And why are you walking so slowly? This old man’s grandmother would be faster than you.”
“Hyah!”
What was with the sudden battle cry?

As alert and disciplined as the model trainee in position one, Zhuge Feng activated his movement technique and raced ahead. Not long afterward, I encountered a bizarre sight that hadn’t appeared even in the *Memory Fragment*.
“What is that...?”
“I invented that device when I was nine. Bringing it here over the last two days was quite an ordeal. What do you think?”
I nodded as I stared at the enormous stone wall standing in the river like a barrier.
“Wow. That’s incredible.”

“It’s impossible to investigate underwater for long, so we used stone cut from the cliff to seal off all four sides, then drained the water from inside. If ordinary laborers had done this, it would have taken several months at the very least.”
The mechanism Zhuge Feng had invented had played a major role, but without martial artists, no one would have even considered building something like this in two days.
“Would everyone clear out for a moment?”
The moment we descended beneath the stone wall, Zhuge Feng uttered those words, and the people who appeared to be formation experts from the Zhuge Clan withdrew like the receding tide.
Only then could I see it.
A towering cliff that must have stood in the same place for countless years—and an enormous fissure running directly across its center.
*Swish.*
The instant I instinctively reached out and touched the fissure—
**System Beep.*
**System Beep-beep.*
An utterly ominous System notification pierced my ears.

Humans, however, were a different story.
“So?”
“We cut through it.”
“...You cut through it?”
“Yes.
The Wudang grandpa and I snipped it apart with our swords.”
*What the hell?
He’s talking about cutting through a cliff like it’s a piece of paper.*
But with Origami Man—no, Perfected Being Hyeongong, the Supreme Peak master Wudang was so proud of—and Cheongpung, it wasn’t impossible.
Even I could have managed it without much trouble.
“Anyway, we carved straight through.
It wasn’t that hard.
I heard the others who arrived with the second group cleaned up the rest.”
Right.”
Sometimes I forgot that I was surrounded by monsters.
And that I was one of them.
Jeok Cheongang, who had been listening to our conversation, poked Mungyeong in the ribs.
“Has the world gone mad?
I don’t remember things being like this when we were young.
Those two are just monsters, right?”
“Don’t lump me in with you.
It’s insulting.”
“So how old were you when you became a Supreme Peak master?”
“They’re the monsters.”
“Yes.
That must be it.
Hah.
Perhaps the heavenly patterns have grown clouded.
Murim has changed.
It certainly has.”
As Jeok Cheongang lamented, the vessel continued between cliff walls cut so perfectly straight that the sight sent a chill down my spine.
Then a new landscape—and new people—gradually came into view.
*Whoosh!
Splash!*
Peak masters swept down using the exquisite movement technique known as Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water.
They stepped across the river’s surface and blocked the vessel with imposing auras.
“Stop!
Everyone aboard must state their names and sobriquets.
Once the identity verification process is complete—”
Jeok Cheongang, already on edge after his recent aquatic lifestyle, stuck his head out with a fiendish expression.
“This old man is the Fire King.”
“Gasp!”
“Stop us and you die.”
“Y-yes, sir!”
“O-open the way!
No one stop them!”
*Whoosh!*
Gung Gibang watched the figures vanish at twice the speed with which they had appeared and muttered, “Was Wudang’s movement technique always this impressive?
The Beggars’ Sect will have to stay on its toes.”
No.
They had probably realized how completely fucked they were and fled for their lives.
Either way, everything proceeded smoothly after that.
The vicious Fire Pokémon Jeok Cheongang needed no explanation, and my face was famous enough that anyone who failed to recognize me might as well have been working for Dark Heaven.
Besides, Cheongpung and Gung Gibang were with me.
“Oh, did someone just recognize me?”
“Of course.
You’re the only beggar who travels with me.”
“Wow!
Someone recognized me just now, too!”
“Of course.
You’re the only person who travels around with a horned water snake.”
“Okaaay...”
I ignored the dejected Gung Gibang and Cheongpung and focused on the scene ahead.
Archers had somehow climbed to the tops of the towering cliffs and stood ready to fire.
I could also sense masters concealed all around us.
*Wudang, the Zhuge Clan, and it looks like the Beggars’ Sect is here too.*
The security was formidable.
But considering the weight and importance of the situation, that was only natural.
“Has the City Lord of Hubei Province decided to bury this matter completely?”
Jin Wikyung nodded gravely.
“For now.
The common people would hardly welcome the news that a five-hundred-year-old imugi had gone mad and run amok.”
“That’s true.”
Public support was a double-edged sword.

Under normal circumstances, the simple folk would revere the Son of Heaven, but the moment a flood or earthquake struck, they would pull a Hyuk Mujin-level about-face and declare it an omen of the nation’s ruin.
And if a plague came along as part of a buy-two-get-one-free deal, the people of this era would grab the pickaxes they used to till their fields and charge out to overturn the country.
How much worse would it be if an imugi, worshiped by countless people as a divine creature, suddenly went mad and killed several thousand people?
The City Lord of Hubei Province would want to hide that truth as much as possible.
“He does agree, at least in part, that Dark Heaven is an extremely dangerous organization.”
“...He agrees *in part*?
Even after all this?”
I took back what I had just said.
Concealing the Water God Dragon’s existence was one thing, but how many people had died because of this incident?
And he only agreed *in part*?
He clearly still hadn’t come to his senses.
“It is a delusion born of arrogance.
He believes Murim is merely Murim and that it poses no threat to their ability to govern the country.
I tried my best to persuade him, but it was of little use.”
Jeok Cheongang abruptly cut in with a disgruntled voice.
“Those idiot government officials haven’t changed at all.
They were exactly the same during the Great Faction War.
When the Demonic Cult pushed down through Sichuan, they sat on their hands.
Only after the civilian casualties mounted did they scramble to gather troops.”
“What happened then?”
“What do you think happened?
By then, the Demonic Cult had already been defeated and withdrawn, and some bastard calling himself a Great General came strutting over to take credit.
He said it was all thanks to His Imperial Majesty’s grace and whatnot.
Since the Emperor was the master of the country, it didn’t really matter who won, but congratulations on your victory.
That sort of bullshit.”
“You showed remarkable restraint.
For you, Old Master, that was practically the patience of a Buddha.”
Jeok Cheongang looked at me as if I were talking nonsense.
“Why would this old man have put up with that?
I tried to beat him to death.
If Hong Dao hadn’t stopped me, it wouldn’t have been the Great Faction War.
It would have been the Great Government War, or something like that.”
Right.”
“In any case, don’t expect much from the government officials.
We should be satisfied that they at least turned the dark-path figures who had been sitting quietly into Dark Heaven’s lackeys.”
Jin Wikyung answered with a bitter smile.
“Yes.
Fortunately, the people’s anger and wariness toward Dark Heaven have been soaring ever since.”
“They had nothing to do with this incident, but what can we do?
They aren’t exactly innocent, either.
They’re dark-path figures, so using this opportunity to uproot them wouldn’t be a bad idea.”
After negotiating with Murim, the government had crushed Hubei Province’s dark-path figures as scapegoats to appease the people’s anger.
Both sides had gotten what they wanted, so it was a kind of give-and-take.
Of course, our reputations had skyrocketed once again in the process.
*Whether the government would actually step in even if Dark Heaven ran wilder than it already had was another question.*
As I thought about that, the vessel that had been charging forward finally came to a stop.
We docked at a temporary pier built against the cliff, and gazes poured toward us.
“That’s Great Hero Jeok Cheongang.”
“The Successor Beggar is beside him, too.
I was wondering where the Huashan Divine Dragon had gone.”
“Wait.
Isn’t that young man the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon?”
“Did you hear?
There’s talk among the leaders that the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon was the one who took down the imugi...”
They thought they were whispering, but I could hear every word.
*You idiots.*
Annoyed by the muttering, I deliberately scowled.
The area fell silent in an instant.
Then a shout broke the silence.
“Oh, you’re here!”
The middle-aged man running toward us was drenched from head to toe in mud and river water.
Unfamiliar aquatic plants were tangled in his disheveled hair.
I muttered inwardly as I watched him approach.
*That man is the Family Head of the Zhuge Clan?*
It was something I was only now fully appreciating, but Crouching Dragon Guest Zhuge Feng was unquestionably an eccentric even by Murim standards.
“Family Head, I normally wouldn’t say anything, but there are outsiders present.
Please show some decorum...”
“Ah, please move aside, Uncle.”
“Family Heaaad!”
He had clearly stuffed his dignity into a mailbox and left it there.
Zhuge Feng ruthlessly brushed aside the family elder trying to stop him, hurried over, and spoke with his face flushed.
“We found it.
We really found it!”
“Yes, I know.
Cheongpung told me—”
“At first, I wondered what kind of bullshit you were talking about, but it was sitting right there in the place you described!”
Wasn’t that a little too honest?
I had explained everything so earnestly, and he had dismissed it as bullshit?
Seeing my expression, Zhuge Feng continued with an appropriately solemn look.
“Our ancestor, Zhuge Wuhou, once said that one should tap even a stone bridge before crossing it.
Don’t take it too personally.”
Was trotting out their ancestor whenever it suited them a Zhuge Clan motto, or was it hereditary?
I stared suspiciously at Zhuge Feng.
“...Did Zhuge Wuhou really say that?
As far as I know, that’s a proverb from another country.”
“He must have said it at least once in his life.
Is that important right now?”
*Unbelievable.*
Whether it was the Chinese over there or the Chinese over here, they were astonishingly good at copying other people’s work.
Before I could respond, Zhuge Feng spun around and started walking ahead of us.
“Follow me.”
Jeok Cheongang, who had been trembling with delight at finally being able to set foot on even a temporary pier, narrowed his eyes.
“‘Follow me’?
Was that directed at this old man?”
“...I wasn’t speaking to you, Senior.”
“Then watch your mouth from now on.
Straighten out that folded tongue before this old man splits you in half.”
“Yes, sir.”
“And why are you walking so slowly?
This old man’s grandmother would be faster than you.”
“Hyah!”
What was with the sudden battle cry?
As alert and disciplined as the model trainee in position one, Zhuge Feng activated his movement technique and raced ahead.
Not long afterward, I encountered a bizarre sight that hadn’t appeared even in the *Memory Fragment*.
“What is that...?”
“I invented that device when I was nine.
Bringing it here over the last two days was quite an ordeal.
What do you think?”
I nodded as I stared at the enormous stone wall standing in the river like a barrier.
“Wow.
That’s incredible.”
“It’s impossible to investigate underwater for long, so we used stone cut from the cliff to seal off all four sides, then drained the water from inside.
If ordinary laborers had done this, it would have taken several months at the very least.”
The mechanism Zhuge Feng had invented had played a major role, but without martial artists, no one would have even considered building something like this in two days.
“Would everyone clear out for a moment?”
The moment we descended beneath the stone wall, Zhuge Feng uttered those words, and the people who appeared to be formation experts from the Zhuge Clan withdrew like the receding tide.
Only then could I see it.
A towering cliff that must have stood in the same place for countless years—and an enormous fissure running directly across its center.
*Swish.*
The instant I instinctively reached out and touched the fissure—
**System Beep.*
**System Beep-beep.*
An utterly ominous System notification pierced my ears.

chapters.title: Chapter 485
paragraphs: Thump. Thump.
My heartbeat thundered inside me.
One step, then another. The closer I drew to *it*, the harder my heart pounded.
My mouth felt gritty, as though I had chewed a handful of sand. My eyes had gone wide without me realizing it, and they felt dry and stiff.
Then, the moment my hand finally touched the fissure in the cliff, I learned the true source of that ominous feeling.
*Beep.*
**System This Gate has already lost most of its functions! - Entry into the Gate is impossible! - The **Gate Conquest** Quest cannot be generated!
The notification drilling into my ears, the holographic window filling my vision, the gazes of everyone watching me...
Faced with all of it, I slowly uttered a single word.
“...Fuck.”
*Crunch.*
Without realizing it, I had clenched my hand hard enough for my fingers to dig into the cliff.
The faintest trace of demonic qi seeped from the fissure—or rather, the Gate—and made my vision swim.
*I’d hoped until the very end that it wasn’t this.*
That damn Gate. It really was a Gate.
How? Why?
Those unanswerable questions stayed with me for a long time afterward.

My thoughts were a mess. I had suspected as much ever since seeing it through the *Memory Fragment*, but now that I was face-to-face with a reality so difficult to believe, I found myself at a loss for words.
*A Gate in the Murim.*
This was an enormous rift—a sign that the laws governing this world were collapsing, and the first step toward disaster.
*Dark Heaven.*
Their true nature was far deeper and darker than I had ever imagined.
Standing apart from the others, I gazed out over the blackened waters of Dongting Lake. Then I picked up a loose stone and tossed it into the water.
*Splash.*
*The bloodshed at Shaolin led to Sichuan, and eventually reached this place.*
The past several months had been one continuous sea of corpses and blood.
While the Star-Array Grand Banquet was taking place in Henan, Shaolin—the Mount Tai and Northern Dipper of the orthodox Murim—had been attacked, and the flames of Dark Heaven had spread to Sichuan.
More importantly, inexplicable phenomena had occurred along the way.
*The Blood Lord, the Western Heaven Demon Lord, and the Moving Formation.*
I could still vividly recall the sight of the Blood Lord recovering even after being struck by Jeok Cheongang’s Dance of the Fire God and Demon—a technique that staked his life itself.
*No. It wasn’t even accurate to call that recovery.*
That was right. What the Blood Lord had shown was closer to regeneration than recovery.
New flesh had sprouted as if time itself were reversing. Bones had slid back into place. Everything charred pitch-black like ash had regenerated in an instant.
As I watched that unbelievable sight, one very familiar creature had come to mind.
*A Troll. Yeah, he was just like a Troll.*
Or maybe a potion...
Damn it. A Troll and a potion? It was my own idea, but it sounded insane.
What was even crazier was that it might actually have been true.
I picked up another stone and sent it flying even farther.
*Splash.*

And that wasn’t the only strange phenomenon the Blood Lord had displayed. When the Sword Saint’s arrival put him on the defensive, hadn’t he cried out for the Lord of Heaven before vanishing without a trace?

At the time, everyone had concluded that it was one of the monstrous martial arts and supreme techniques born of demonic, heterodox arts. But now that I had confirmed the existence of the Gate, things looked different.
*Teleport.*
It might have differed slightly from the Teleport I had experienced through Magic Johnson, but if that wasn’t Teleport, I’d use Hyuk Mujin’s palm as a griddle.
*Come to think of it, more than one thing hadn’t added up about the Western Heaven Demon Lord.*
During the Sichuan Blood Tragedy, the Western Heaven Demon Lord had sacrificed one arm to defeat the Poison King.
But when I confronted him in the underground prison beneath the Sichuan Tang Clan, he already had a new one.
No matter how many angles I considered or how many possibilities I went through, only two explanations could account for that.
Either the Western Heaven Demon Lord was a living model kit, or some unknown power had been at work.
Naturally, the former was impossible.
Though personally, I would have preferred it.
*The Moving Formation was the same.*
The Moving Formation. A wondrous formation capable of transporting hundreds of Dark Heaven’s black-robed men at once.
Dark Heaven was called the successor to the Demonic Cult. If the Demonic Cult had possessed anything like that, they would have put it to use more than fifty years ago.

Then the Great Faction War would have ended in victory for the Demonic Cult, and instead of becoming the Third Young Master of the Jin Family of Taiyuan, I would have become the Third Young Master of the Black Dragon Gang—or some other dark-path sect.
*Why hadn’t I realized it?*
Even I, the sole outsider in this world of Murim, had failed to predict the truth.

The faint suspicion that had occasionally crossed my mind had been buried beneath talk of monstrous martial arts and supreme techniques from the Thousand-Year Demonic Path, then erased by the power the Western Heaven Demon Lord had called supernatural powers.
But things were different now.
I had confirmed the existence of the Gate. I had realized that the common sense and laws of the Murim, which had gradually become familiar to me, were collapsing.
And I had realized that the strange abilities of Dark Heaven—which martial artists called monstrous martial arts and supernatural powers—could be explained with a single word.
*Magic.*
At the single word filling my mind, my vision brightened, and my forehead, which had been burning hot, slowly cooled.
At the same time, the title of another being who had yet to reveal himself slipped from between my lips.
“...Lord of Heaven.”
The one who reigned at the summit of Dark Heaven.
A being so overwhelming that people like the Blood Lord, the Western Heaven Demon Lord, and the Southern Heaven Demon Empress called themselves his lowly servants.
*What the hell are you?*
Just thinking about the Lord of Heaven made all the blood in my body run cold.
If—just if—that bastard called the Lord of Heaven was the very being that had surfaced in my mind...
*Splash!*
Water sprayed high into the air, sending ripples across the surface.
I snapped out of my thoughts as if I’d been doused in cold water. When I turned, a familiar face came into view. I hadn’t even noticed him approach.
“What are you spacing out for?”
His voice was gruff, but the eyes peering out from between the deep wrinkles on his face were filled with concern.
I let out a quiet laugh at Jeok Cheongang’s expression and opened my mouth.
“You startled me. What brings you here?”
He dropped heavily into the seat beside me.
“You’d been gone for so long that I came to see what you were doing.”
“If you were coming, you could’ve come quietly. Why throw a rock out of nowhere?”
“Watching you fiddle with pebbles like a seven-year-old was getting on this old man’s nerves. Do you have a problem with that?”
“What if I do?”
*Whoosh!*
Before the words had even left my mouth, I ducked. A vicious rush of air brushed my hair and tore through the space where my head had been.
Jeok Cheongang smacked his lips after his attack on the back of my head failed.
“You’ve got remarkably sharp instincts.”
“Do you think this is the first time? I can dodge you with my eyes closed now.”
“Close them.”
“...I’d rather not.”
“You insolent brat. Then why were you so distracted earlier? Spacing out like that in the Murim is a good way to get yourself killed.”
“So you were planning to kill me?”
“Of course. If that’s what you want, this old man can certainly oblige.”
“Then you’ll have to find another Disciple. Oh, wait. Since I’m not actually your Disciple, I guess it doesn’t matter.”
“Ahem. Ahem-ahem!”
Jeok Cheongang forced out several fake coughs before abruptly asking,
“So what has an idiot with nothing but shit in his head so troubled?”
“I was wondering where to take a shit.”
*Smack!*
Damn it. I couldn’t dodge that one.
Jeok Cheongang had even used a grappling technique to make sure he landed the blow on the back of my head. He glared at me.
“Do you want to shit blood?”
“Why? You said my head was full of shit, and I said I was thinking about shit. What’s the problem?”
“Answer me properly before I switch your mouth and ass around.”
“Ah. Yes, sir.”
Rubbing the back of my throbbing head, I thought for a moment before speaking.

“The truth is, I’m not from this world. And I think an evil power from the world I originally came from is deeply connected to Dark Heaven. You know that imugi that went berserk this time? That was all their doing. The rift in the cliff is a Gate. If it ever fully breaks open, monsters will come pouring out.”

“When that happens, it’s all over. Completely over. And it’s probably not true, but there’s a bastard called Demon King Asmodeus. If he’s still alive and has his sights set on the Murim, then we’re all completely fucked—”
“I understand.”
I swallowed the rest of my words at Jeok Cheongang’s response.
It was a ridiculous story that no one would believe anyway. I had been spilling everything without restraint, but his reaction left me speechless.
“Excuse me?”
“I said I understand.”
“I understood every word. There’s no need to say any more.”
What was with that reaction?
I was beyond bewildered. At the same time, an indescribable emotion surged up from deep within my chest.
*He believes me? He believes this ridiculous story? No... he believes me?*
As Jeok Cheongang silently gazed at me, my chest swelled and my throat tightened.
A little over a year. Short by some measures, long by others.
We had shared more hardships and joys than anyone else, and the emotion in the old man’s eyes was something that could only be called absolute trust.
*...He trusted me that much.*
Sometimes an inexplicable emotion would seize me and leave me unable to speak—unable even to figure out what I should say.
But at that moment, I realized it was time to say the word I had been turning over in my heart for so long.
“Old Master. No...”
After a long hesitation, I finally forced the words out.
As I opened my mouth, my heart trembling, Jeok Cheongang smiled kindly and nodded.
“I understood you perfectly. You sure take a long time to say that you want to die.”
“M—yes?”
“What do you mean, ‘yes,’ you damn bastard.”
*Whap-whap-whap!*
What the fuck?
My brain ground to a halt. I stared blankly, mouth hanging open and both hands clutching the back of my head, as his furious voice rang out.
“Do you take this old man for an idiot? What? You’re not from this world? ‘I Was a Mere Civilian in Another World, but Now I’m a Supreme Peak Master in the Murim.’ Is that it?”
“That title’s surprisingly trendy and pretty good—no, that’s not the point. Just hear me out.”
“I already did. Those were your last words.”
“Whoa, whoa. Hold on!”
“‘Hold on’? After all the times I’ve beaten you, you still haven’t come to your senses, and now you’re talking to me like an equal again, you insolent little...!”
*Whap-whap-whap!*
Dozens of palm shadows filled my vision and battered every inch of my body.
As searing heat burrowed into me, I thought,
*Master, my ass. Fuck.*
I was an idiot for getting moved, even for a moment.
“If you ever spout that kind of bullshit again, I’ll tear you in half and kill you. Understood?”
At Jeok Cheongang’s murderous warning, Jin Taekyung—who had been beaten mercilessly for fifteen minutes—groaned.
“Ugh, hold on. I think I’m actually going to die.”
“Quiet. You’re slower than this old man’s grandmother!”
“...Old Master, since we’re on the subject, you don’t sneak out a smartphone and use it whenever you go take a leak, do you?”
*Smack!*
After delivering one final blow to Jin Taekyung, who had once again spouted something incomprehensible, Jeok Cheongang clicked his tongue and walked away.
The murderous aura radiating from his entire body made everyone swallow hard and clear a path.
Step. Step.
He walked toward somewhere.
Now alone, Jeok Cheongang wore a complicated expression that was impossible to decipher.
*...That brat. Spouting such incomprehensible nonsense.*
Still, who knew?
Jeok Cheongang had never believed in rumors or superstitions—not even a little—in his entire life. But if Jin Taekyung was the one saying it, things were different.
That brat was more special to him than anyone else.
*Come to think of it, he seemed about to say something beginning with “Ma...”*
Could it be?
No. Of course not.
Jeok Cheongang sighed and looked up at the moon hanging over the cliff.
Beneath the brilliant moonlight, he saw someone in much the same position as himself standing nearby, gazing out over the water.
“Can we talk for a moment?”
At Jeok Cheongang’s words, Mungyeong answered,
“No. Get lost.”
