*Earn Mungyeong’s recognition.*
At this point, I would rather run around with iron balls hanging from me.
At least then I would have a clear objective and be able to check my progress.
But this was basically the crime of getting on someone’s bad side.
Didn’t it mean I had to keep getting put through the wringer until he decided he liked me?
*This feels like it’ll take a while.*
I didn’t know what Mungyeong’s training methods would be like, but one thing was certain: earning his recognition wouldn’t be easy.
Objectively speaking, it would be strange if it were.
*It’s probably going to be brutal, but I’ll have to endure it.*
The man I was dealing with wasn’t some ordinary martial artist.
He was the Slaughter Saint, a Supreme Peak master counted among the greatest in the world.
Being taught secret martial arts by someone of that caliber was a fortuitous encounter in itself.
And when I thought about it, I had already experienced two such fortuitous encounters.
The first was, without a doubt, the System.
And the second...
*The Old Master.*
There was no way I could leave Jeok Cheongang out of it.

If I hadn’t met him—if I hadn’t learned the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts, passed down to only one person in each generation—then even with the System, I probably wouldn’t have attained my current strength or position.
As that train of thought continued, Jeok Cheongang’s face suddenly flashed through my mind.
*Still, I should go see him.*
Of course, Jeok Cheongang and I had never formally entered into a Master-Disciple relationship.
But just because we didn’t call each other Master and Disciple didn’t mean ours was merely a relationship of convenience.
We were the kind of people who understood each other without speaking.
Jeok Cheongang and I quietly turned the words *Master* and *Disciple* over in our hearts.
Or maybe not.
I’m suddenly not so sure.
Jeok Cheongang might think differently, but that was how I saw it.
And it was obvious that Jeok Cheongang must be troubled after swallowing his pride and personally asking Mungyeong to teach someone who was practically his Disciple.
*He’s probably off somewhere moping by himself again.*
Other people whispered that Jeok Cheongang was nothing more than a hot-tempered, impossibly eccentric old man.
But the Jeok Cheongang I knew was tenderhearted.
He might scold and grumble, but beneath it all, his heart was practically soggy with affection for the people he cared about.
I glanced up at the bright moon and started walking.
*I’ll find him soon enough.
There are plenty of people around.*
That comfortable thought vanished without a trace less than half an hour later.
“You haven’t seen him?”
“No, sir.
I haven’t seen him for a while.”
“If you’re lying to me...”
“Why would I lie to the Captain?
If I didn’t want to get beaten to death, I’d make up things that never happened and tell you.”
“Cheongpung?
You haven’t seen him either?”
“No, Benefactor.
Why?
Is something wrong?”
Never mind.
It’s nothing.
Get back to what you were doing.”
“Oh!
If nothing’s wrong, would you like to see Mimi?
She ate ten Blood Fish, so her belly is incredibly round!”
“Yeah.
Great.”
This place wasn’t even that large.
Where on earth had he disappeared to?
I searched everywhere for the missing Jeok Cheongang, but no matter whom I stopped and asked, the answers were never helpful.
“Hey, you beggar passing by.
Come here.”
“No.”
“You haven’t been beaten enough lately.”
“Damn it.
I have a reputation to maintain too.
No matter how much of a Supreme Peak master you are, if you treat me, the Successor Beggar, like some stray dog you’re calling over from the street, what will the Sect’s disciples think?”
“Two silver nyang.”
“Are you seriously treating me like a beggar...”
“Ten nyang.”
*Fwoosh!*
“Hm.
One cannot ignore a friend’s summons.
What is it?”
“Our Old Master—no, our Master.
Do you know where he is?”
“Sir Jeok?
No idea.
I haven’t seen him once since he arrived here.”
“Can you ask the other Beggars’ Sect disciples?”
“Well, we’re all busy with our assigned tasks.
Still, you never know.
I’ll make a round and let you know if I hear anything.”
“Yeah, thanks.”
“What are friends for?”
“Then get to it.”
“...What about the silver?”
“I’ll pay you later.
But if you find my Master’s location, I’ll give you double.”
“T-Twenty nyang!
Beggerrr!”
But even Gung Gibang, who had become a slave to capitalism and run off enthusiastically, ultimately failed to find Jeok Cheongang.
I tossed him five silver nyang, then continued making the rounds.
The answers I received were always more or less the same.
“Sir Zhuge, have you perhaps seen my Master?”
“Oh, you came at the perfect time.
I’m testing our clan’s formation, and I think that with a little more refinement, I can suppress the energy leaking from this fissure—”
“That’s great.
Good luck.”
“Great Hero Jin!
I saw him!”
“Really?
Where?”
“About two shichen ago, he was over by the water, beating someone senseless.”
“The person getting beaten was me.”
“Great Hero Jin!
Great Hero Jin!”
“Yes.
You there, with your hand raised.
Where did you see him?”
“If you mean Sir Jeok, I haven’t seen him.”
“No, then why are you—”
“Would you sign this martial robe for me?
My son dreams of becoming a fine martial artist like Great Hero Jin.
He says he’ll have no regrets if he can get your autograph...”
“...What’s your son’s name?”
“Zhuge Sopyeong.
Please write something telling him to practice his martial arts diligently and not be a picky eater.
Especially when it comes to green onions.”
“Wait.
Then may I ask for your autograph too?”
“I got here first.
Get in line!”
“What?
Why are you suddenly lining up?
Move to the back!
Don’t line up!
Ah, this is driving me crazy.”
About an hour later, after completing my grand tour, I returned to the temporary private tent that had been set up for me.
By then, it was already past midnight.
After signing autographs with inspirational messages for Zhuge Sopyeong, Changwoo, Myoryeong, Jinsu, and the other budding talents, I was completely drained.
“...So where the hell is the Old Master?”
This wasn’t even the Liaodong Plain.
How could he simply vanish into thin air?
At this point, he had clearly made up his mind to stay hidden.
He had probably predicted that I would come looking for him and deliberately disappeared.
*I’ll be seeing him soon enough anyway.
For him to avoid me this much...*
He must have been even more troubled than I had imagined.
I let out a small sigh, picked up the water pitcher from the wooden table in the corner of the tent, and gulped down the water.
I had been walking around and talking all day, so my throat was parched.
But why did the water taste like this?
*Did they scoop it straight from the river?
It’s a little salty.*
Even if Murim hadn’t suffered from environmental pollution yet, I couldn’t help feeling uneasy.
That was when it happened.
*Beep.*
**System You have been poisoned by **Potent Paralysis Powder**.

Potent Paralysis Powder** is a type of anesthetic that clouds the mind and stiffens the body. - You feel your consciousness becoming hazy! - Your **Scorching Yang Qi** resists the poison! - If you do not take action quickly, the Status condition **Full-Body Paralysis** will activate!
No, fuck.
What the hell was this?
Forgetting that my body was slowly becoming paralyzed, I stared blankly at the System window.
Then a brief memory flashed through my mind like lightning.
*You’ll naturally find out tomorrow.*
*It’s already the hour of the Pig.
It’ll be midnight soon.
Can’t you just tell me and get it over with?*
*It’s late.
Don’t forget.
We begin tomorrow.*
Mungyeong, you son of a bitch!
My blood seemed to surge backward with rage.
At the same time, the blood carrying the paralysis powder raced through my body, and my vision began to fade.
I sucked in a startled breath, hurriedly raised my internal energy, and shouted a command in my mind.
*Inventory Open, Summon!*
At once, a ring appeared on my finger.
I normally kept the Myriad-Poison Ring in my Inventory to avoid attracting attention, but now it gleamed with a strange luster.
*Ding.*
**System The usage conditions for the **Myriad-Poison Ring** have been met. - Special Skill **Poison Absorption** has activated!
Potent Paralysis Powder** resists!
*Hissss!*
I could feel it.
Deep inside my body, two energies with entirely different purposes collided.
But the Myriad-Poison Ring was a divine artifact of the Sichuan Tang Clan, one that had even absorbed Jeok Cheongang’s Formless Ultimate Poison.
And once my Scorching Yang Qi—the natural counter to poison—joined in, the paralysis powder had no choice but to collapse helplessly.
*Ding.*
**System Detoxification** complete! - All traces of **Potent Paralysis Powder** have disappeared from your body! - All Status conditions have been cleared!
“...Phew.
You crazy old man.”
I muttered the curse as I released the breath I had been holding.
He had set a trap like this the moment midnight passed.
I never imagined that “we begin tomorrow” would mean this.
*Damn it.
He really is an assassin.*
At first, I had thought it was an ambush by Dark Heaven.
Was this what he meant by turning me into a true Murim martial artist?
I was already exhausted, and the sudden attack had sent my heart pounding and made my legs go weak.
With a deep sigh, I collapsed onto the bed.
*Phut-phut!*
*Beep.*
**System You have been poisoned by **Potent Soul-Bewitching Powder**!
Slaughter Saint, you fucking bastard.

chapters.title: Chapter 491
paragraphs: “Hey, Captain. You haven’t slept—?”
Hyuk Mujin entered my temporary tent in the dim light before dawn, then fell silent as if he’d seen a ghost.
“Why?”
“Uh, well...”
“Say it.”
“It’s nothing. You just look unusually tired today.”
Tired? Tired. Was that all I could call this?
I glared at the bronze basin of wash water. My hair was a mess, and my eyes were bloodshot. When I looked up, I saw that the entire tent was in shambles.
Hyuk Mujin belatedly noticed the same thing, and his pupils began quaking.
“What in the world happened here?”
“Yeah. Something happened.”
My voice sounded so unfamiliar it might have belonged to someone else. I rubbed my haggard face and muttered, “That fucking assassin...”
I’d said it quietly, but not quietly enough. Mujin jumped at the word *assassin*.
“Pardon? An assassin?”
“What?”
“You just said ‘assassin.’ I heard you.”
“You heard wrong.”
“I heard it with my own ears.”
“I said you heard wrong.”
Of course, it was true.

Some vicious assassin bastard had installed a dozen or so hidden weapons inside the tent, and I had managed to trigger every single one of them. With a one-hundred-percent success rate, I had been reduced to a bloody rag.
The maddening part was that I couldn’t tell anyone.
“C-Captain...”
“I said you heard wrong!”
“That’s not it. You’re bleeding from your butt.”
Fuck. No wonder my ass had felt warm.
As I cursed silently and pressed a hand to the wound, Mujin gave me a dubious look.
“I still think it was an assassin.”
“I got hurt training.”
“Really?”
I nodded weakly.
This counted as training. I had no idea what kind of training involved staying awake all night doing nothing but detoxifying poison, but it counted.
“It really was training. I swear on both your balls.”
“As I’ve told you repeatedly, please don’t swear on my balls. And if an assassin is threatening you right now, blink twice.”
“...Mujin. If you’re going to ask me that, shouldn’t you at least use Sound Transmission?”
“I can’t use Sound Transmission yet.”
“Then write it down.”
“Oh. Right.”
“Are you insane?”
Then again, this was Hyuk Mujin. What had I expected?
I let out a long sigh and looked him up and down. He’d dressed neatly in his martial robes and come to see me this early, so he clearly wanted something.
“Anyway, what’s going on?”
“Ah, Sir Zhuge is looking for you. Everyone’s gathered.”
“Everyone? Why?”
“You know.”
Mujin glanced around for no reason, then mouthed a few words before finally lowering his voice to a whisper meant only for me.
“The imugi. The dead one.”
“Ah.”
“Only a handful of us are going, and we’re keeping it quiet. Perfected Being Hyeongong of Wudang is waiting too.”
“Even Perfected Being Hyeongong? Ah, of course.”
He was the only Supreme Peak master involved in this incident who had remained at Donghu Stronghold.

He was also the Wudang Sect Leader’s Junior Brother and a respected elder of the Murim. He was more than qualified to attend as Wudang’s representative. However closely we guarded the Water God Dragon’s existence, we couldn’t keep it secret from Wudang.
*Though for something this important, wouldn’t the Sect Leader himself come? Why Hyeongong?*
The question occurred to me, then vanished as I thought of someone else.
“Hey, is anyone else going with us—”
I was about to finish the question, half hoping I was wrong, when a quiet voice came from outside the tent.
“Young Master Jin. Everyone is waiting.”
“If you’re ready, please come out.”
The presence outside receded as soon as the words ended. Mujin tilted his head at the sight of me standing frozen.
“What’s wrong?”
“Why is *he* going?”
“Who? Oh, Mungyeong? He is the Divine Physician’s disciple, after all. He should be able to help with the imugi’s anatomy and such. But why?”
Why? Because I had no idea what that lunatic might do.
I swallowed the words rising in my throat and started toward the exit. Then I stopped and turned back to Mujin.
“Mujin.”
“Yes?”
“Go first. I’ll follow right behind you.”
“Pardon?”
I could almost hear a System notification ringing in my ears.
**System You have acquired **Meat Shield**!
When I boarded the small vessel waiting for us, I found several familiar faces.
Perfected Being Hyeongong, dressed in a heavily patched Daoist robe with an old Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword at his waist, greeted me with a gentle smile.
“A young fellow Daoist has arrived. It is good to see you again.”
“Greetings, Perfected Being Hyeongong.”
I gave a fist-and-palm salute, now fairly convincing as a martial artist. Beside him, Zhuge Feng waved his folded fan and cut in.
“But your face...”
“Nothing happened.”
“You don’t look well for someone to whom nothing happened. Don’t you agree, Perfected Being?”
“I agree with Family Head Zhuge. You look as though an assassin tormented you all night.”
“An assassin? Perfected Being, you do make jokes. Ha ha.”
“Ho ho ho.”
Don’t laugh. Don’t even show me your teeth.
Without the Myriad-Poison Ring, I doubted I’d be standing right now.
I had been soaked in so much poison that I had seriously considered whether I should change my sobriquet from the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon to something like Poisoned Pickle.
*Look at him, sitting there shamelessly.*
I glared at Mungyeong, who had already claimed a seat on the swift ship.
The boy noticed my piercing gaze and slowly turned his head.
—Lower your eyes.
If he said lower them, I lowered them.
I quietly looked away, and another Sound Transmission followed.
—Judging by your condition, you must have fallen for every trap from the first day. How pathetic. If you hadn’t had the Myriad-Poison Ring and Scorching Yang Qi, you would have been dead by now.
—...How do you know whether I would have died or survived?
—Want me to tell you?
—I misspoke.
He wasn’t wrong. Every hidden weapon he’d set was coated with powerful poison.

I had once heard that medicine and poison shared the same source. I didn’t know who had said it, but they had been completely right. Somehow, every poison I suffered came with the adjective *potent* attached to it.
Only the Myriad-Poison Ring’s absurd effectiveness and my Scorching Yang Qi—a natural counter to poison—had kept me from suffering anything worse than a few puncture wounds.
Without those two things... Just thinking about it made my blood run cold.
*Medical apprentice, my ass. What kind of Divine Physician is that? He’s a Poison Physician.*
—I know you just insulted me.
“Ghk.”
I sucked in a startled breath before I could stop myself. Kindhearted Hyeongong looked at me with concern.
“What’s wrong, young friend?”
“Ah, nothing. It’s just a habit.”
“That’s a relief. For a moment, I thought an assassin really was threatening you. Didn’t you, Family Head Zhuge?”
“Ha ha ha! You’ll have me splitting my sides, Perfected Being!”
“Ho ho ho.”
I was tempted to tear Zhuge Feng’s navel right out.
While I glared at his stomach, the vessel slipped through the calm water. The departure was so smooth that I noticed it a beat too late.
“Wait. The Old Master—no, my Master isn’t here.”
Zhuge Feng looked puzzled by my sudden objection.
“Hm? Didn’t you hear?”
“Hear what?”
“Senior Jeok decided not to come. He also said not to look for him for the time being, until everything is finished.”
“...Is that so?”
“You didn’t know? That explains why he didn’t pass the message along through his Disciple.”
This was the first I’d heard of it.
Whatever his reason, it stung a little that he hadn’t said a word to me. At the same time, I thought I understood how he felt.
*He must have a lot on his mind.*
I’d never raised a Disciple, but if I found myself in his position someday, I thought I might feel the same way.
Perhaps it was like entrusting a beloved pet—one you’d cared for with love and devotion, almost like family—to someone else.
No, scratch that. That made me Jeok Cheongang’s pet dog.
*His son. Right, let’s go with son.*
While I was settling that with myself, Cheongpung came over with a bright smile and thrust something toward me.
“What’s this?”
“Candy, Benefactor.”
“...I can see that. Where do you keep finding it?”
There were only two possibilities.
Either Cheongpung was a System user with ten metric tons of candy in his Inventory, or there was a tree nearby that grew the stuff.
“Either way, thanks.”

Normally I wouldn’t have given it a second glance, but with so much on my mind, I could use the sugar. I bit into the candy and asked, “Finding candy at a time like this takes some skill. Did you buy it on your last visit to the Zhuge Clan?”
“No. I ate all of that already.”
“Hm? Then where did this come from?”
“Slaugh—no, Mungyeong gave it to me. He told me to give this one specially to you, Benefactor. He’s a really good person!”
The answer came from somewhere else.
*Beep.*

**System You have been poisoned by **Potent Energy-Dispersing Poison**! Energy-Dispersing Poison** temporarily prevents you from using internal energy. - Your **internal energy** is slowly dissipating! Immediate action is required!
Fuck. No wonder the candy had tasted unusually sweet.
I quietly took out the Myriad-Poison Ring.
They say people leave their names behind when they die, while beasts leave their hides.
The same was true of the spirit creature that had ruled Dongting Lake and the Yangtze for five hundred years.
The Water God Dragon’s spirit had already left its body, but the body remained where it had last lain, retaining all the majesty and beauty it had possessed in life.
Even Perfected Being Hyeongong, an old Daoist of profound insight and enlightenment, was lost for words. All he could manage was a single exclamation.
The sight of the Water God Dragon’s body was that overwhelming.
Even Gung Gibang, who had seen it before, stood with his mouth hanging open and kept exclaiming in awe.
“It’s incredible even the second time around. Don’t you think?”
I answered as politely as I could.
“It is. So is your breath. Could you get lost? I think it’s stronger than the Energy-Dispersing Poison.”
“Hm. Easily done. On one condition.”
“What?”
“Of the ten silver nyang you promised me yesterday, I still haven’t received five. I knew you were shameless, but I never thought you’d go so far as to prey on a beggar.”
“I’ll pay you. Just keep it short. I’m starting to see things.”
I could hardly tell whether that was his mouth or a sewer.
Gung Gibang finally got the other five silver nyang out of me, then grumbled.
“Stop exaggerating. And if you mean hallucinations, I’ve had more than enough of those myself. I’ve been having strange dreams for the past few days.”
“Dreams?”
“Yes. Dreams.”
Gung Gibang gave a quiet laugh and pointed at Mungyeong.

“I dreamed Mungyeong was fighting that imugi. Sword Force was flying everywhere, and he kept vanishing and reappearing like a ghost... If someone had told me he was the Slaughter Saint, the greatest assassin of all time, I’d have believed them.”
*He is the Slaughter Saint.*
I continued staring at the Water God Dragon’s body, doing my best to ignore Gung Gibang’s endless chatter.
From head to tail, its enormous body stretched for more than a hundred ja. Its scales, once stained black, now scattered dazzling silver light, while countless wounds were carved across its body.
I ran my hand over one of the gaping wounds and apologized silently.
*I’m sorry.*
Of course I knew the battle had been unavoidable. I had no reason to apologize. If anything, the Water God Dragon had been grateful to us for stopping it, even if this was what it had taken.
But I was apologizing because I couldn’t bury its body as it was.
*The corpse.*
The raid was over. It was time to dispose of the corpse.

He also said not to look for him for the time being, until everything is finished.”
“...Is that so?”
“You didn’t know?
That explains why he didn’t pass the message along through his Disciple.”
This was the first I’d heard of it.
Whatever his reason, it stung a little that he hadn’t said a word to me.
At the same time, I thought I understood how he felt.
*He must have a lot on his mind.*
I’d never raised a Disciple, but if I found myself in his position someday, I thought I might feel the same way.
Perhaps it was like entrusting a beloved pet—one you’d cared for with love and devotion, almost like family—to someone else.
No, scratch that.
That made me Jeok Cheongang’s pet dog.
*His son.
Right, let’s go with son.*
While I was settling that with myself, Cheongpung came over with a bright smile and thrust something toward me.
“What’s this?”
“Candy, Benefactor.”
“...I can see that.
Where do you keep finding it?”
There were only two possibilities.
Either Cheongpung was a System user with ten metric tons of candy in his Inventory, or there was a tree nearby that grew the stuff.
“Either way, thanks.”
Normally I wouldn’t have given it a second glance, but with so much on my mind, I could use the sugar.
I bit into the candy and asked, “Finding candy at a time like this takes some skill.
Did you buy it on your last visit to the Zhuge Clan?”
“No.
I ate all of that already.”
“Hm?
Then where did this come from?”
“Slaugh—no, Mungyeong gave it to me.
He told me to give this one specially to you, Benefactor.
He’s a really good person!”
The answer came from somewhere else.
*Beep.*
**System You have been poisoned by **Potent Energy-Dispersing Poison**!
Energy-Dispersing Poison** temporarily prevents you from using internal energy. - Your **internal energy** is slowly dissipating!
Immediate action is required!
Fuck.
No wonder the candy had tasted unusually sweet.
I quietly took out the Myriad-Poison Ring.
They say people leave their names behind when they die, while beasts leave their hides.
The same was true of the spirit creature that had ruled Dongting Lake and the Yangtze for five hundred years.
The Water God Dragon’s spirit had already left its body, but the body remained where it had last lain, retaining all the majesty and beauty it had possessed in life.
Even Perfected Being Hyeongong, an old Daoist of profound insight and enlightenment, was lost for words.
All he could manage was a single exclamation.
The sight of the Water God Dragon’s body was that overwhelming.
Even Gung Gibang, who had seen it before, stood with his mouth hanging open and kept exclaiming in awe.
“It’s incredible even the second time around.
Don’t you think?”
I answered as politely as I could.
“It is.
So is your breath.
Could you get lost?
I think it’s stronger than the Energy-Dispersing Poison.”
“Hm.
Easily done.
On one condition.”
“What?”
“Of the ten silver nyang you promised me yesterday, I still haven’t received five.
I knew you were shameless, but I never thought you’d go so far as to prey on a beggar.”
“I’ll pay you.
Just keep it short.
I’m starting to see things.”
I could hardly tell whether that was his mouth or a sewer.
Gung Gibang finally got the other five silver nyang out of me, then grumbled.
“Stop exaggerating.
And if you mean hallucinations, I’ve had more than enough of those myself.
I’ve been having strange dreams for the past few days.”
“Dreams?”
“Yes.
Dreams.”
Gung Gibang gave a quiet laugh and pointed at Mungyeong.
“I dreamed Mungyeong was fighting that imugi.
Sword Force was flying everywhere, and he kept vanishing and reappearing like a ghost...
If someone had told me he was the Slaughter Saint, the greatest assassin of all time, I’d have believed them.”
*He is the Slaughter Saint.*
I continued staring at the Water God Dragon’s body, doing my best to ignore Gung Gibang’s endless chatter.
From head to tail, its enormous body stretched for more than a hundred ja.
Its scales, once stained black, now scattered dazzling silver light, while countless wounds were carved across its body.
I ran my hand over one of the gaping wounds and apologized silently.
*I’m sorry.*
Of course I knew the battle had been unavoidable.
I had no reason to apologize.
If anything, the Water God Dragon had been grateful to us for stopping it, even if this was what it had taken.
But I was apologizing because I couldn’t bury its body as it was.
*The corpse.*
The raid was over.
It was time to dispose of the corpse.

chapters.title: Chapter 492
paragraphs: It went without saying that so many people had gathered here for reasons other than praying for the Water God Dragon’s soul.
And one person in particular was showing rather obvious ulterior motives.
“Incredible. Simply incredible.”
Zhuge Feng’s eyes shone with rapture as he stroked the silver scales.
“This strength. This beauty. I can hardly believe it.”
The Water God Dragon had died without ever becoming a true dragon, but it was still a divine imugi that had lived for five hundred years.
Its body had already proven itself in battle. It was both armor and a weapon in its own right.
“This is... a priceless treasure.”
Zhuge Feng wasn’t exaggerating in the slightest.
The scales were harder than steel, and even Sword Energy could not cut clean through them. The bones beneath were harder still.
Even in the modern age, with its advanced Magic-powered forging, material like this would sell for whatever price its owner named. In Murim, its value went without saying.
*It may not be on the level of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, but... it’s an incredible treasure.*
The Water God Dragon’s body stretched for more than a hundred zhang, and every inch of it was made up of treasures like those.
Armor made from those scales would not be pierced even by a crossbow. A weapon made from its bones would be harder and sharper than one made from meteorite iron.
Martial arts manuals, elixirs, and exceptional weapons—the three things every martial artist went crazy for.
It was only natural that greed showed in Zhuge Feng’s eyes, and in several others’.
“If we made a Dog-Beating Staff out of that...”
Hyuk Mujin objected to Gung Gibang’s muttering.
“Why make a Dog-Beating Staff out of the bones? You’d want a sword. A Bone Sword made from an imugi’s bones... Just imagine it.”
“Are you looking down on the Beggars’ Sect?”
“No. Just you, Gung Gibang.”
“Want me to beat you like a dog?”
“Come on, calm down. There’s enough there to make a hundred Dog-Beating Staffs or swords with plenty left over. Why fight about it?”
“Fair point. Then I call one Dog-Beating Staff.”
“And I’ll reserve a sword...”
*Crack! Crack!*
“Ugh!”
“Argh!”
Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin each took a smack to the back of the head. They turned to me and shouted.
“Why’d you hit me?”
“Please tell us why *before* you hit us!”
These bastards still didn’t get it.
I frowned and shook a large fist at them threateningly.
“You two useless bastards couldn’t do a damn thing when we were fighting, and now you’re talking about Dog-Beating Staffs? Swords? Reservations?”
“Well, that’s...”
“A martial artist can’t help...”
“If it weren’t for the Water God Dragon, Hubei Province would’ve been destroyed. It wouldn’t have ended with a few fish going berserk.”
There was no denying that countless people had died because of the Water God Dragon.
But it hadn’t acted of its own free will. And if the Gate had opened completely, Hubei Province would have become a hellscape.
“Of course its body will be put to good use. But if you’re even remotely human, show some gratitude. Got it?”
The two of them flinched at my shout and muttered in voices as tiny as ants.
“Like you do...”
“Honestly, Captain, you don’t have much room to talk. Look what you did to the Dongting Fisherman.”
*Crack! Crack-crack!*
Two more cries followed the blows. I rounded on Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin as they clutched their heads again.
“Is that the same thing? Is it? Huh?”
I had my side of that story too.
Of course I felt bad about wrecking the Dongting Fisherman, but I’d had no choice.
He’d been directly exposed to the corrupted Water God Dragon’s Fear. He’d harmed people while out of his mind, and every piece of evidence at the time had pointed to him as the culprit.
His limbs might have been broken, but at least he was alive. Come to think of it, getting beaten to a pulp by me had freed him from the Fear.
*A fist beat Fear.*
A triumph of humanity...
No, not really. We’d each had our circumstances.
I’d even visited him because I felt bad. He was unconscious, though, so we hadn’t been able to talk.
“Anyway, be grateful. Understand?”
I was still shaking my fist at the two of them when another voice spoke.
“Young Friend Jin is right.”
There was wisdom in the voice alone. Perfected Being Hyeongong of Wudang stepped forward, his expression troubled.
“I had my doubts when I heard what happened, but seeing it with my own eyes, I understand now. It truly is a divine creature blessed by the heavens.”
Jin Wikyung, who was also seeing the Water God Dragon for the first time, nodded solemnly.
“You’re quite right, Perfected Being. It sacrificed itself to prevent even greater bloodshed. This imugi deserves to be called a Divine Dragon.”
“A terrible loss. We owe it so much. Should we not all pray for its soul together?”
Perfected Being Hyeongong was exactly what one would expect from an old Daoist who had cultivated profound Daoist mastery at Wudang, the sacred ground of Daoism.
He was nothing like the human garbage beside me, who couldn’t muster a shred of gratitude.
Overcome by a sudden surge of faith in the Primordial Heavenly Venerable, I quickly clasped my hands together.
“Amen.”
Hyeongong, who had been reciting a Daoist prayer, flinched and turned to me.
“Amen?”
“My mistake. Amitabha.”
“...Repeat after me. Infinite Life Buddha.”
“Ah, sorry. Infinite Life Buddha.”
“Excellent. The Primordial Heavenly Venerable will watch over you, Young Friend Jin.”
“Ah. Yes.”
*Does Wudang have missionaries too?*
Hyeongong smiled like a Civilization player going for a religious victory. After a short prayer, he looked up at the sky.
“You, divine imugi. I pray that you become an Azure Dragon there and soar across the heavens.”
“Just as one would expect of you, Perfected Being.”
Zhuge Feng and Jin Wikyung, each with his own interests at stake, eagerly sang his praises. Hyeongong answered with a kindly smile.
“Ho ho. I merely did what was right. Now then...”
“Yes, Perfected Being?”
What profound words would the old Daoist say next?
Everyone, myself included, bowed their heads and listened reverently.
“Let’s start cutting it up.”
“We still have to do what needs to be done, do we not?”
I raised my head.
Greed for a weapon blazed in Hyeongong’s eyes. His gaze practically shouted what his voice did not.
*I call a Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword! One Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword for me!*
He wasn’t a Daoist. He was a lunatic.
Looking at the man I’d trusted for all of a moment, I was reminded of something.
*Every last one of these Murim bastards is hopeless.*
The raid was over. The fighting wasn’t.
One battle remained, and sometimes it got even fiercer than the raid itself.
*Distribution of the spoils. Final settlement.*
Hunters had to make a living, after all.

Maybe things were different for top Hunters earning several billion to tens of billions of won a year. In a raid party of lower-tier Hunters, though, arguments over byproducts worth a few tens of thousands of won were commonplace. That was why contracts were essential.
And the Water God Dragon’s corpse was a treasure of immense value all by itself.
We’d gone into this raid without drawing up a contract. In the modern world, that would have led to an enormous dispute.
But this was Murim. The people here belonged to the physical school: they preferred settling matters with their bodies to talking things out.
I knew just the word for people like that.
*Suckers.*
I glanced around. Nearly everyone was watching everyone else, waiting to see who would speak first.
Two people were exceptions.
The first was the Family Head of the Zhuge Clan, arguably the wealthiest family in Hubei.
“Ahem.”
Zhuge Feng cleared his throat, then went on as though his proposal were perfectly reasonable.
“Our family will have to make a concession in this matter. The Zhuge Clan will take only ten percent. The rest can go to everyone else...”
“Hold it. Are you dealing from the bottom?”
“What!”
I cut him off with a quiet laugh.
“Ten percent? What did you do to earn ten percent? Take that much without working for it and you’ll get a stomachache.”
“Am I wrong? I respect you, Sir Zhuge, but this isn’t right.”
*Ten percent, when he didn’t do a damn thing? How dare he try to sneak in and rob us blind?*
Zhuge Feng flinched at my glare, then tried again.
“Barely did a thing? Without the information the Zhuge Clan provided, you would have been blind even with your eyes open. You never would have made it here.”
“You have quite a long tongue.”
“Ghk!”

“The conclusion you reached from that information was that the Dongting Fisherman was the culprit. Wasn’t it? You’re telling me that the Dongting Fisherman, lying there injured, suddenly got up, did five somersaults, and then used Stepping on Empty Air to hop all the way here?”
“That... that was...”
Zhuge Feng fell silent. The only other person there who looked at ease gave him a gentle smile.
It was the smile of a man whose skill had brought the Jin Family of Taiyuan to its current standing.
“Sir Zhuge, I apologize for my younger brother’s rudeness.”
“C-Cough!”
“It’s my fault for teaching him so poorly.”
“His words were rather harsh.”
“They must have hurt your feelings. I really shouldn’t have let this happen.”
“It’s all right. At least you seem reasonable, Lesser Family Head, so I’m glad...”
“No. He deserves a proper scolding. Taekyung, you little rascal! Apologize at once!”
At Jin Wikyung’s booming shout, I immediately bowed my head.
“I’m sorry. I spoke too harshly.”
“Even if Sir Zhuge was trying to get something for nothing, there are lines you must not cross!”
“I apologize again.”
“No, wait. Hold on. Lesser Family Head Jin?”
Zhuge Feng seemed to sense something was wrong, but Jin Wikyung’s scolding went on.
“Taekyung, you played the greatest part in defeating the Water God Dragon! You practically saved Sir Zhuge’s life! But he is still the Family Head of a great clan and a respected elder of Murim!”
“Whew. I’ve committed a crime worthy of death.”
“Wait, Lesser Family Head.”

“You may have been raised without manners, but you’re still a youngster! How dare you treat Sir Zhuge, a man renowned throughout Murim, as though he were some shameless bastard? As soon as we return to our family, I’ll...!”
“Lesser Family Head Jiiin!”
Zhuge Feng cried out desperately and waved a hand, looking thoroughly fed up.
“All right. I understand. I understand everything. Just see that I’m taken care of.”
“Then you accept our apology?”
“I’m sorry, Sir Zhuge!”
“Yes, yes, I understand. Now both of you, stop.”
“Thank you. Even if it isn’t ten percent, we’ll make sure the Zhuge Clan gets a share it can be happy with.”
“A consolation cut is the universal rule.”
“...Whew.”
*Game over. Yoshi, grand season.*
Zhuge Feng wilted, worn out in body and spirit. Jin Wikyung and I exchanged satisfied smiles.
I could die and come back to life and still never match Zhuge Feng’s intellect. But you couldn’t learn this kind of negotiation at a desk.
*This was wisdom born of experience.*

I’d thrown a fit during a settlement to get one extra goblin poison dart. Jin Wikyung had spent years mastering the divine art of handling every shitty job the family could dump on him while no one knew whether his father was alive or dead.
If everyone else here was a sucker, we were cardsharps.
*And judging by our contributions, I was obviously the star of the show.*
Those who fight claim the spoils.
This was a battle we couldn’t retreat from—and shouldn’t.
Only by standing our ground against anyone who challenged us could we become true Hunters and true martial artists.
“Ten percent. Hand it over. Or hand over your neck.”
“We’ll hand it over.”
But there were exceptions to every rule.
...Fuck.

chapters.title: Chapter 493
paragraphs: Opportunity isn’t given to everyone equally.
By that measure, Perfected Being Hyeongong had been given more opportunities than most. At just ten years old, he had become a direct Disciple of the Wudang Sect Leader.
His path had been smooth from the start.
Born with martial talent among the best of his generation and an upright nature to match, Hyeongong had always received wholehearted support. Which meant he had never wanted for anything in his life.
And yet...
*I want it.*
Perfected Being Hyeongong’s eyes trembled faintly. It was a material desire he had not felt in a very long time.
*I’ve never felt this way before.*
Gold, wealth, fame, glory—he had no need for any of it. He wore each Daoist robe he received until it fell apart and lived on simple, modest meals.

Elixirs and martial arts manuals were no different. Since reaching the Supreme Peak realm, he had devoted himself to cultivating his mind. Whenever his Senior Brother, the Sect Leader, offered him an elixir, Hyeongong passed it on to his promising grand-disciples. As for manuals, the Wudang techniques he had already mastered were more than enough.
But this. This was different.
“Hoo... Infinite Life Buddha. Infinite Life Buddha.”
Hyeongong ran a rough hand down his beard and recited the invocation. Yet despite his efforts to master himself, his gaze kept returning to the imugi’s corpse.
*They say those bones are incredibly hard.*

Through the split scales and gaping wound, he could see enormous bones giving off a faint glow. Perhaps because they had belonged to a five-hundred-year-old imugi, the bones had a luster unlike anything else. He had heard they were so hard that even ordinary Sword Energy could not cut through them.
*If I made a sword from those bones, it would be incredible... No. What am I thinking? Get a grip, Hyeongong!*
He squeezed his eyes shut. He had just watched the two Jin brothers leave Zhuge Feng in tatters, which made the temptation all the more troubling.

At least Zhuge Feng had been there when the battle took place. Hyeongong had been hundreds of li away, at the Donghu Stronghold headquarters. He had no grounds to demand anything, nor the nerve to set aside his shame and ask.
*Infinite Life Buddha, Infinite Life Buddha. A Daoist, led astray by a desire like this? Get a hold of yourself, Hyeongong.*
While he was struggling in silence, someone spoke.
“Perfected Being. Are you busy?”
“Hm?”
Hyeongong’s eyes flew open. A familiar young man was looking at him with a knowing gaze.
*Jin Taekyung.*

Together with the Sword Saint’s Disciple, Cheongpung—the Huashan Divine Dragon—this young man was at the center of the storm sweeping through Murim. The gossips were already saying that beneath the Ten Kings stood the Two Dragons.
*An extraordinary young man. Almost unbelievably so.*
But Hyeongong had something more pressing on his mind than his opinion of Jin Taekyung.
*Could it be?*
The old Daoist looked at him, his heart quickening with hope.
“What is it, Young Friend Jin?”
Taekyung smiled gently. “If you’re not busy, I was hoping we could talk.”
“Talk? About what?”
“We have to deal with the corpse now, and there’s more of it than we expected.”
“Th-That’s why?”
“You came all the way here in person. Of course you should have something to take home.”
“Oh!”
Hyeongong’s eyes immediately lit up. Jin Taekyung smiled and continued.
“Our Jin Family of Taiyuan has always held the Daoists of Wudang in the highest regard. As fellow martial artists of Murim, we’d be delighted to share a little of what we’ve gained.”
“I-Is that true?”
“Of course. I swear on Hyuk Mujin’s balls. My eldest brother is fully in favor of it too.”
“Good heavens! Infinite Life Buddha!”
Taekyung had gently scratched the itch Hyeongong had been too ashamed to mention. The old Daoist was beside himself with joy.
Hyeongong did not know who Hyuk Mujin was or why Jin Taekyung was swearing on the man’s balls. All that mattered was that he was being given a share.
*How can anyone be this kind?*
Taekyung was nothing like the hypocrites with their fine words. He was a ray of light shining into a cold Murim crawling with shameless people.
Hyeongong could practically see a halo over Jin Taekyung’s head.
“Thank you! May the Primordial Heavenly Venerable protect you and the Jin Family of Taiyuan, young friend! Infinite Life Buddha!”
“Amen.”
Something about that was strange, but Hyeongong didn’t care. He was still beaming when Taekyung continued in his gentle voice.
“There is one small problem, though.”
“Hm? What problem?”
“The corpse is so large that I can’t deal with it alone. And we can’t exactly move it whole.”
“Quite right. Quite right.”

From head to tail, its vast body stretched over a hundred jang. It was questionable whether it could even be moved in one piece. And since doing so would require a great deal of manpower, keeping the matter secret would become even more impossible.
“So I’d like to ask you a small favor, Perfected Being.”
Hyeongong faltered. Suspicion flickered in his eyes.
“Wait. Young Friend Jin. This favor of yours wouldn’t happen to mean...”
“Yes. We need you to lend us a hand. At this rate, it’ll take days.”
*So that’s it! That’s why he was being so generous!*
Hyeongong glared at Jin Taekyung with an expression of betrayal.
“You want me to use Wudang’s sword arts to take that imugi’s corpse apart?”
“Think of it as work.”
“Work? You expect me to think of it as work? I did not train in martial arts for this!”
Reaching the Supreme Peak realm meant devoting most of one’s life—no, one’s entire life—to martial arts.

Hyeongong was no exception. How many years had he spent with a sword as his companion, his beloved? He had even honed his martial arts through secluded meditation, facing a wall in pitch darkness. To him, Taekyung’s request was an insult.
*The nerve of him.*
His expression hardened.
“Infinite Life Buddha. Young friend, you have insulted not only me but the sword arts of the great Wudang Sect.”
“Insulted you? I would never. I’m only asking you to lend a hand.”
“But I cannot use my sword for something as trivial as—”
Just as Hyeongong’s voice began to rise, Taekyung tossed out a remark.
“Now that I look at it, your sword’s pretty worn.”
“What?”
“Seems about time you replaced it. What do you think?”
Hyeongong’s pupils quivered. Before he knew it, he was looking down at the old Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword at his waist.
*It certainly is worn... No! What am I thinking?*
He had carried that sword since he was ten. It was a precious gift from his late master.
Hyeongong hurriedly shook his head to clear it, then opened his eyes wide.
“It is not worn!”
“It is. Look at the hilt. It’s practically falling apart.”
“It does seem a little... No! You’re mistaken!”
“Fine, forget the hilt. The scabbard’s covered in cracks too. Has it been through a drought?”
“Ah! When did those appear...?”
“This is worse than I thought. Could you draw the sword?”
“Why should I?”
*Shing!*
Only after shouting did Hyeongong realize he had drawn it. He stared in horror.
*When did I do that?*
The devil’s whisper went on regardless.
“The blade doesn’t look too good either.”
“My late master gave me this sword!”
Taekyung answered calmly. “My parents gave me this body, but it’s worn down with use. If I could’ve replaced it, I would have done it ages ago.”
“Well, this old Daoist’s joints have been aching lately too. I’ve been yearning for Bone Transformation... What are you trying to pull?”
“I’m just telling you the cold reality. Oh, the edge is still sharp, at least.”
*Get a grip. Get a grip, Hyeongong.*
He steadied his breathing and answered with pride. “Of course it is. The blade was forged with four nyang of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron mixed into it.”
“Good heavens. Four nyang of that precious Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron?”
“Do you see now? This sword may look worn, but it is every bit a treasured sword.”
“Ah. Is that right?”
“Of course! I already own a sword anyone would covet. Why would I need another—”
*Clang!*
“Oh, sorry. My hand slipped and I dropped my spear. Please, go on.”
Hyeongong barely noticed Taekyung’s sheepish smile. His eyes were fixed on the faintly glowing spear, his eyelids trembling.
“Y-Young Friend Jin. Is that, by any chance...”
“Nothing special. It’s made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron too, but it’s nothing compared to your sword.”
It certainly didn’t look that way.
Hyeongong swallowed and asked cautiously, “How many nyang?”
“Solid. The whole thing, from the blade to the shaft.”
“This is fucking insane. Infinite Life Buddha.”
“Sorry? What was that?”
“Ah, nothing. Nothing at all.”
A devil. This was the devil’s whisper.
Yet Hyeongong’s eyes remained fixed on Jin Taekyung’s spear, White Flame, as he recited the invocation as if possessed.
“Light as a feather, incredibly hard, and sharp besides. But...”
Then that soft, tempting voice reached his ears again.
“I think I’d like a weapon made from an imugi’s bones.”
“Infinite Life Buddha. I would not.”
“Think about it carefully. Not just any weapon, but one containing all the qi of a sacred imugi that lived for no less than five hundred years.”
*It would be incredible. I want one so badly.*
Hyeongong barely swallowed the words rising to his lips and shook his head frantically.
“Impossible! I could never abandon the sword my master gave me—”
“Who said anything about abandoning it? You can have both.”
“Fuck, I could do that! Ah, Primordial Heavenly Venerable!”
“Sorry?”
“Stop! That’s enough! Infinite Life Buddhaa!”
“If you help us, we’ll give you a share generous enough that Wudang won’t feel slighted. Do you think I’d settle this with a single sword?”
“I already have a sword made with Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron!”
“Yes. And an imugi’s bones.”
“How could I use another sword when I have the one my master gave me?”
“Yes. The more, the better.”
“I did not learn martial arts for this sort of thing!”
As Hyeongong clung to his last shred of pride and lamented, Jin Taekyung suddenly shouted toward somewhere behind the corpse.
“Hey, Cheongpung! How’s it going?”
A cheerful face popped out from behind the enormous corpse. Cheongpung had been promised a considerable share for fighting alongside them.
“Yes, Benefactor! I’m working on the waist!”
“Really? That part’s especially thick. Giving you trouble?”
“No! The Martial Extremity Grand Unity Sword cuts through it just fine!”
“Good. I’ll be there soon. Keep at it.”
“Yes, Benefactor!”
Taekyung gave the diligent worker a pleased smile, then turned back to Hyeongong.
“Ah, sorry, Perfected Being. I took my eyes off the work for a moment.”
“But what were we talking about? I’ve been forgetting things a lot lately.”
Hyeongong looked from Cheongpung, hard at work, to Taekyung and back again.
Half a shichen later...
*Slash!*
The Taiji Wisdom Sword, Wudang’s finest sword technique, was separating the imugi’s scales from its bones.
“Murim has gone completely mad.”
That was Mungyeong’s brief assessment as he watched the entire situation unfold.

paragraphs: Slash! Shhk-shhk-shhk!
Scales split apart, and huge chunks of flesh were cut into evenly sized pieces.
The enormous bones emerging between them were so clean it hardly seemed possible.
Thud! Slash!
His skill bordered on the supernatural.
As the onlookers stared in a daze, a quiet murmur spread through the crowd.
“Hyuk. I’m asking because I genuinely don’t know, but... Was the Jin Family of Taiyuan originally a family of fishermen?”
“Can I ask the Lesser Family Head that exact question?”
“Of course not, you lunatic. But you’d have to be born with a talent like that. Could he actually be a fisherman...?”
“Lesser Family Head! Do you know what Gung Gibang just said?”
“Hey, hey!”
“Was one of our ancestors a fisherman? How can the youngest one do that?”
“...Lesser Family Head?”
“If Zhuge Wuhou had seen this, he’d have fallen right out of his four-wheeled carriage. Wouldn’t you agree, Perfected Being Hyeongong?”
“Good heavens. Infinite Amen, Avalokiteshvara.”
“...Perfected Being?”
While everyone questioned the roots of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and worked toward religious unification, one person was thinking about something else entirely.
*Huh. Look at this guy.*
Mungyeong’s clear eyes followed Jin Taekyung as he cut and sliced like a man possessed.
*What incredible power. And it’s fast and concise, too.*
You could tell a person’s realm from the smallest movement. By that measure, what Jin Taekyung was doing was astonishing.
*What an achievement. Hard to believe he’s barely past twenty.*

Mungyeong already knew Jin Taekyung defied common sense. Everyone in this dusty martial world knew it. Even the young prodigies of the Nine Sects and One Gang, with all the support they received, struggled to break through to Peak at twenty. Jin Taekyung had reached Supreme Peak and now stood shoulder to shoulder with masters one or even two generations above him.
But that was not the only reason Mungyeong admired him.
*He moves like a veteran of the martial world. That control over his strength, at his age... Not a motion wasted.*
Thump! Slash!
Even the smallest movement was efficient. He might have been conscious of all the people watching, but he showed none of the flashy affectation someone his age might have indulged in.
He simply cut, sliced, and separated, like a traveler quietly following the quickest, easiest path.
*He was the same when he fought the imugi.*
An assassin took in and analyzed everything around him. His profession demanded that he kill his target and find a way out, whatever the circumstances.
And Mungyeong was the Slaughter Saint, called the greatest assassin of all time.
He had watched Jin Taekyung ever since Sichuan—not as the Divine Physician, but through the eyes of the Slaughter Saint.
*The Heavenly Martial Physique... Could it really be true?*

It had been forty years since Mungyeong left Murim. For all that time—long enough for the mountains and rivers to change four times—he had lived as a medical apprentice. He had examined and treated thousands, perhaps tens of thousands, of patients.
Yet even with all that experience, he could not easily explain Jin Taekyung’s body or talent.
*He’s similar to Cheongpung, but there’s a subtle difference.*
Mungyeong glanced at Cheongpung, then looked away.
Cheongpung was the only person who could be compared to Jin Taekyung. In his understanding and application of martial arts, he might even surpass him.
Cheongpung, too, had a remarkable body unlike any Mungyeong had seen. But not quite like Jin Taekyung’s.
*Cheongpung was refined. Jin Taekyung was born this way.*
The shape and size of his muscles, his skeleton, his acupoints—everything was perfect.
The Heavenly Martial Physique.
Mungyeong’s gaze deepened as he watched Jin Taekyung.
*What if that boy made my secret martial arts entirely his own...?*
He pushed the thought aside almost as soon as it came.
*Ridiculous.*
Martial arts were like an endless mountain range. Most martial artists still at its foot might think Mungyeong had reached the summit, but he could see another mountain ahead.
That was how vast and distant the world of martial arts was.

Even Mungyeong had not reached the end of the secret martial arts he practiced. Heavenly Martial Physique or not, Jin Taekyung could hardly achieve anything satisfactory with them in such a short time.
*Especially now.*
War was almost upon them. With countless battles ahead, Mungyeong needed to teach him what mattered most. Too much of anything could become poison.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, must have known that when he entrusted Jin Taekyung to him.
*But... what on earth should I teach that bastard?*
At a loss for the first time in a long while, Mungyeong watched the scene before him.
“Cheongpung! Ready?”
“Yes, Benefactor!”
“Lay into it with the Plum Blossom Sword Technique!”
“Agh!”
“Perfected Being! Where are you?”
“Oh. Here I am!”
“Why are you standing over there instead of working? Can’t you see the rest of us working?”
“I-I was just going to take a short break...”
“Perfected Being, you’re such an individualist! Where’s your teamwork?”
“I-I’m sorry.”
“Show me how sorry you are. Taiji Wisdom Sword, go!”
“I-Infinite Life Buddha!”
Slash! Slash! Slash!
Under Jin Taekyung’s forceful direction, the Water God Dragon’s corpse was dismantled in no time.
The others cried out in admiration. Mungyeong only grew more troubled.
*What am I supposed to teach that bastard?*
At this point, he looked like the kind of person who would grow just fine on his own...
Then Mungyeong made up his mind.
No. Now that he had taken this on, he would see it through to the end. He wanted to stay close and find out just how far that arrogant bastard Jin Taekyung could go.
*First, I need to fix that absurdly complacent attitude of his.*
Mungyeong slipped up beside Hyuk Mujin, who was staring with his mouth open.
“Martial Warrior Hyuk.”
“Holy shit. He cut through that in one go—oh, Mungyeong. What is it?”
“Young Master Jin must be exhausted. Would you take him some water?”
“Huh. You really do think of things the rest of us don’t. I’ll take it right over.”
“Please don’t tell him I gave it to you. I’d be happier if you got the praise.”
“You really are something...!”
Hyuk Mujin looked at Mungyeong with deeply moved eyes and accepted the leather waterskin.
Of course, along with cool water, it contained a deadly poison called Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder—an extreme poison that killed its victim before they could take seven steps.
“...What’s this?”
Immediately after the work was finished, Hyuk Mujin approached me with a leather waterskin. He answered my question with a proud expression.
“Water. I thought you might be tired, Captain.”
“There’s no way you thought of something this considerate.”
“I fetched it myself! Why don’t you trust me?”
Had I been too sensitive lately? He looked so wronged that I felt a little guilty for doubting him.
Besides, after working that long, I really was thirsty.
“Hm. Really?”
“Forget it. If you’re going to be like this, don’t drink it! I’ll drink it myself!”
“Hey, hey. Fine. Leave it here and go. I’ll drink it.”
“I said forget it!”
“That’s enough. You’re starting to piss me off.”
Once Mujin was gone, I carefully pulled the stopper from the waterskin and sniffed it.
*Mm. Smell.*
*Smells normal, at least.*
I still wasn’t letting my guard down. Very carefully, I tilted the waterskin.
A drop of water trickled out slowly and plopped onto my tongue.
*Just in case, I’ll start with one drop...*
Beep.

**System You have been poisoned by **Potent Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder**! Potent Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder** is an extreme poison capable of killing dozens of bulls with a single drop! - Severe **Internal Injury** and organ damage are likely. Very, very urgent treatment is required!
“...Hyuk Mujin, you son of a bitch.”
Fuck. That wasn’t the kind of one drop I’d had in mind.
*Inventory open. Summon!*
I hurriedly put on the Myriad-Poison Ring and raised my Scorching Yang Qi to drive out the poison.
The next System notification told me the poison had been purged. But that wasn’t the end.
Beep.

**System Quick action—but the extreme poison has left aftereffects! - Your **Sinews and Meridians** have suffered slight damage! - Some stats have decreased due to the damage to your **Sinews and Meridians**! Strength** decreased by 5! Agility** decreased by 5! - Status abnormality: **Severe Stomachache**! - Status abnormalities will return to normal once you have fully recovered, but the lost stat points cannot be restored!
“What the hell?”
No, fuck. Had I really lost stat points?
Not one or two, either. A whole ten points between Strength and Agility had vanished.
*Ten points is one level-up!*
Damn it. I knew exactly who was behind this.
I’d gone through hell to raise those stats, and now they were gone. Hot fury surged up from deep in my gut.
Grrrggg.
...Was that fury, or feces?
And of all the shitty status abnormalities to get, I had to get this one. My vision went white with pain, and I hurried off.
“Young Friend Jin, where are you going?”
“Benefactor, where are you going?”
“Move, move. We’re done dismantling it, so all that’s left is sorting. I need to take care of something first...”
“Benefactor, are you going to poop?”
*Don’t say it so loudly, you lunatic. What if Mungyeong hears you?*
Pale-faced, I stumbled on. Only when I got close to a place out of sight did I start to feel relieved.
*Whew. Thank goodness.*
Shitting myself while standing would be humiliating enough. If Mungyeong saw me, I’d be in for it.
Fortunately, he wasn’t among the others, so he must have gone somewhere else...
*Wait. Somewhere else?*
The question crossed my mind just as my foot touched the ground.
Then I heard a faint sound.
Step. Tap.
A chill ran down my spine. I launched myself into the air on instinct.
Shhk-shhk-shhk-shhk!
Four blades whistled through the air.
Four daggers came from the front, back, left, and right. They pierced the edges of my clothes and skimmed my skin. If I hadn’t dodged, they would have lodged in my chest, back, and limbs.
*What the hell...!*
I righted my body and landed on the ground, then glared furiously at the rock wall more than ten zhang away.
“Can we take it down a notch? Huh?”
The rock wall shimmered like a heat haze. A figure emerged and answered in a dry voice.
“I told you clearly. I decide how you train.”
“You put me in this state and then hide over there? You could at least face me—”
“I wasn’t hiding. I was watching.”
“What difference does that make? You got caught.”
“I showed myself just enough for you to notice. If you couldn’t manage even that, you might as well bite down on a blade and die.”
“You?”
Mungyeong. No—the Slaughter Saint.
The moment I met his deep, steady gaze, goose bumps rose on my skin and hot fury surged up again.
Grrrrrrrk. Frrt.
It wasn’t fury. It was feces.

“...Lesser Family Head?”
“If Zhuge Wuhou had seen this, he’d have fallen right out of his four-wheeled carriage.
Wouldn’t you agree, Perfected Being Hyeongong?”
“Good heavens.
Infinite Amen, Avalokiteshvara.”
“...Perfected Being?”

*Huh.
Look at this guy.*
Mungyeong’s clear eyes followed Jin Taekyung as he cut and sliced like a man possessed.
*What incredible power.
And it’s fast and concise, too.*
You could tell a person’s realm from the smallest movement.
By that measure, what Jin Taekyung was doing was astonishing.
*What an achievement.
Hard to believe he’s barely past twenty.*
Mungyeong already knew Jin Taekyung defied common sense.
Everyone in this dusty martial world knew it.
Even the young prodigies of the Nine Sects and One Gang, with all the support they received, struggled to break through to Peak at twenty.
Jin Taekyung had reached Supreme Peak and now stood shoulder to shoulder with masters one or even two generations above him.
But that was not the only reason Mungyeong admired him.
*He moves like a veteran of the martial world.
That control over his strength, at his age...
Not a motion wasted.*
Thump!
Slash!
Even the smallest movement was efficient.
He might have been conscious of all the people watching, but he showed none of the flashy affectation someone his age might have indulged in.
He simply cut, sliced, and separated, like a traveler quietly following the quickest, easiest path.
*He was the same when he fought the imugi.*
An assassin took in and analyzed everything around him.
His profession demanded that he kill his target and find a way out, whatever the circumstances.
And Mungyeong was the Slaughter Saint, called the greatest assassin of all time.
He had watched Jin Taekyung ever since Sichuan—not as the Divine Physician, but through the eyes of the Slaughter Saint.

It had been forty years since Mungyeong left Murim.
For all that time—long enough for the mountains and rivers to change four times—he had lived as a medical apprentice.
He had examined and treated thousands, perhaps tens of thousands, of patients.

*He’s similar to Cheongpung, but there’s a subtle difference.*

But not quite like Jin Taekyung’s.
*Cheongpung was refined.
Jin Taekyung was born this way.*
The shape and size of his muscles, his skeleton, his acupoints—everything was perfect.
The Heavenly Martial Physique.
Mungyeong’s gaze deepened as he watched Jin Taekyung.
*What if that boy made my secret martial arts entirely his own...?*
He pushed the thought aside almost as soon as it came.
*Ridiculous.*
Martial arts were like an endless mountain range.
Most martial artists still at its foot might think Mungyeong had reached the summit, but he could see another mountain ahead.
That was how vast and distant the world of martial arts was.
Even Mungyeong had not reached the end of the secret martial arts he practiced.
Heavenly Martial Physique or not, Jin Taekyung could hardly achieve anything satisfactory with them in such a short time.
*Especially now.*
War was almost upon them.
With countless battles ahead, Mungyeong needed to teach him what mattered most.
Too much of anything could become poison.
The Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, must have known that when he entrusted Jin Taekyung to him.
*But... what on earth should I teach that bastard?*
At a loss for the first time in a long while, Mungyeong watched the scene before him.

Ready?”

“Lay into it with the Plum Blossom Sword Technique!”
“Agh!”

Where are you?”
“Oh.
Here I am!”
“Why are you standing over there instead of working?
Can’t you see the rest of us working?”
“I-I was just going to take a short break...”
“Perfected Being, you’re such an individualist!
Where’s your teamwork?”
“I-I’m sorry.”

Taiji Wisdom Sword, go!”
“I-Infinite Life Buddha!”

Slash!

No.

chapters.title: Chapter 495
paragraphs: When you’re a baby, it would be stranger if you *could* control your bladder.
At seven? You’re still in kindergarten. These things happen. In elementary school, it would be a little embarrassing, but it wasn’t unheard of in the lower grades.
But I was twenty-seven.

The media of the twenty-first century were falling over themselves to call me a new hero, while the martial artists of Murim called me the Fire King’s heir and a rising star destined to change the face of Murim.
And yet...
*Fuck.*
I’d shit myself. At twenty-seven. Not peed myself—shit myself. In front of Mungyeong, no less.
*Ah, ahh. Anastasia!*
“...Take your time cleaning up and come back.”
After a long silence, Mungyeong left me with those words.
He seemed less concerned for me than he was about getting shit on his short sword. That damn old man.
Every time I thought about what had just happened, I wanted to log out and never return to Murim again. To hell with Dark Heaven and everything else.
*Should I just leave Murim altogether?*
I was sitting by the water, seriously considering it, when someone approached with a smile.
“Captain. What are you doing here all by your—”
The moment I recognized him, I swore at him with all my heart.
“Hyuk Mujin, you son of a bitch.”
“Why are you swearing at me all of a sudden?”
“Stay out of my sight for a while. Please.”
“Even if you’re the Captain, that’s going too far. You wouldn’t spit in a smiling man’s face, would you?”
“Khack—ptui!”
“Gah!”
Mujin barely dodged the glob of phlegm. He looked me over as though I’d lost my mind.
“What happened to make you act like this?”
“Nothing happened. So shut up and get out of my sight.”
“That doesn’t quite add up.”
“Want me to put your arms and legs where they don’t belong?”
Because of the water that bastard had brought me, I’d lost both stat points and my dignity.
I was barely keeping my fist to myself because I knew Mungyeong was the real culprit.
Mujin, who had no idea what had happened, looked baffled.
“Good grief. Anyone would think I’d made you shit your pants.”
“What was that reaction?”
“...Nothing. Why are you here?”
He gave me a suspicious look, then pointed toward the people in the distance.
“We’ve mostly finished sorting everything, but something’s odd.”
“Odd? What?”
“There are fewer imugi bones and scales than we expected. I think you’d better come see for yourself.”
“Really?”

“Yes. Perfected Being Hyeongong is furious that there’s so little for an imugi that size. He’s combing the area like he’s hunting for lice. He says if someone stole any, he’ll find the culprit on the Primordial Heavenly Venerable’s honor.”
What was he, Detective Kindaichi?
He must have completely lost his mind after helping with the Taiji Wisdom Sword just to obtain some bones, only to think someone had snatched them away.
The more I listened, the more absurd it seemed, so I asked Hyuk Mujin,
“How could anyone steal it? And it’s not like only a little went missing. It must be well over a thousand geun. How could anyone hide that without us noticing?”
“Exactly. Hardly anyone even knows about this place—”
Mujin broke off and turned to me.
“But how did you know?”
“Hm?”
“How much was missing. You said it must be over a thousand geun.”
“Just a rough guess. They’ve been making a racket over there for a while.”
I answered as calmly as I could, but I felt a sudden stab of guilt.
Because...
*He’s sharp. I need to watch what I say.*
The culprit Perfected Being Hyeongong had sworn to find was me.
Just thinking about the haul piled up in my Inventory made me feel full.
*Come to think of it, I did take a lot.*
It had been easier than lying in bed playing with my smartphone.
The Water God Dragon’s corpse was enormous, and I’d worked on more of it than anyone else, sweeping the choicest parts into my Inventory as I went.
The sharpest tailbone. The unusually hard scales around its neck. Even some flesh, just in case.
Pile up everything I’d smuggled away, and it would dwarf a decent-sized manor.
“...Why are you smiling so contentedly?”
“Me? What smile?”
“Just now. You looked incredibly shady.”
Apparently, my delight at pulling off the perfect crime was written all over my face. I straightened my expression.
“I wasn’t smiling.”
“Anyway, leave them to it. Go get ready.”
“Ready for what?”
“To head back. You want to live here forever?”
People we could trust would move the sorted remains of the Water God Dragon discreetly, a little at a time.
Most of them would go to the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
*That’ll be a huge help in the battles ahead.*
I got to my feet. Mujin was already running off in the distance, almost before I’d finished speaking. Watching his back, I called out inwardly.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
Shhk.
At the command, the Water God Dragon’s bones, scales, and flesh appeared in my hands. I couldn’t help smiling.
*Item appraisal.*
Ding.

**System Item Window Water God Dragon’s Bones Type:** Material **Grade:** Supreme Peak **Restriction:** Only a Master Artisan can forge them. **Description:** The bones of the Water God Dragon, an imugi that lived for countless years. They are exceptionally strong and contain an unknown, mystical qi. A craftsman who has reached the proper realm may be able to draw out their true power.
Although there were slight differences, the System’s description of the scales was similar.
They, too, were Supreme Peak materials of exceptional strength with mystical qi inside them. As for the flesh, eating it regularly over time could increase internal energy and stat points.
*This is like winning the lottery.*
But the real jackpot was something else.
If the bones and scales were Lotto tickets and the flesh an annuity lottery, this was the American Powerball. The prize was on another scale entirely.
My heart pounding, I took *it* out of the Inventory.
*Item appraisal.*
Ding.

**System Item Window Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence Type:** None **Grade:** None **Restriction:** None **Description:** The Origin Essence of the Water God Dragon, an imugi that lived for countless years. Though damaged by magical power, it is a kind of inner core extracted according to the Water God Dragon’s will. It holds an immense quantity of exceptionally pure qi and is unlike any ordinary elixir. However, if you cannot withstand the qi within it... Further details omitted.
*That’s incredible.*
I carefully stroked the **Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence** in my hand.
That last line was ominous, but this was the greatest thing I’d gained from the trip to Hubei.
*Unlike any ordinary elixir... Just how powerful is it?*
Having been contaminated by magical power, it couldn’t contain as much qi as the Water God Dragon had possessed at its peak. Even so, the amount had to be enormous.
The Water God Dragon had lived for over five hundred years. By simple calculation, that meant it had accumulated at least ten jiazi of qi.
From that perspective, the reduction in the Origin Essence’s power was practically a blessing in disguise.
*Pour too much water into a small vessel, and it overflows.*
As the final line of the item description suggested, even I would burst like a balloon if I tried to take in that much qi all at once.
*The question is when and where to use it.*
Several faces came to mind. One old face in particular kept returning.
*Old Master.*
Jeok Cheongang hadn’t come to mind simply because he was old.
Strangely enough, it was because of Mungyeong’s poison.
After Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder had cost me ten precious stat points, and a severe stomachache had made me shit myself, a thought had struck me.
*If Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder did this much... What condition must Old Master be in after being poisoned by the Formless Ultimate Poison?*
Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder was undoubtedly an extreme poison, but it wasn’t enough to threaten the life of a Supreme Peak master.
The Formless Ultimate Poison that had struck Jeok Cheongang in Henan was far more toxic. Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder couldn’t compare.

Even the Luoyang Strange Physician, one of the most renowned physicians in the world, had no answer and had advised us to seek the Divine Physician. And because the poison had already spread so far, we’d needed the Myriad-Poison Ring as well.
*Fortunately, the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng let us finish treating him...*
But had he really recovered without any significant aftereffects?
I stared at the **Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence**, doubt and worry mingling in my mind.
Perhaps this was an item whose purpose had been decided from the very beginning.
“Little Brother!”
*Inventory open. Store.*
I hurriedly put the **Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence** back into my inventory at Jin Wikyung’s shout from behind me, then turned around with an awkward smile.
“Yes, I’m coming!”
Today had been a day of many satisfying gains.
Yet something weighed on my heart, and for some reason, my stomach felt as though it were twisting.
Grrrggg.
“...Sigh.”
Oh. The status abnormality still hadn’t worn off.
Humans were not the only creatures that settled near water. Animals did too.
Birds nested along the cliffs above the broad waters of Dongting Lake. Wild boars, foxes, wolves, and even tigers lived there as well.
If Dongting Lake below the cliffs was territory permitted to humans, then the cliffs above belonged to the animals.
It was a peaceful place untouched by human feet.
So the great tiger, king of that place, was displeased to find an uninvited guest had arrived.
- Grrrrrrr.
Irritation rumbled through its sharp teeth. Its nose flared ceaselessly, following the human scent that still lingered in the air.
Its keen sense of smell soon found the source.
- Grrr.
At the edge of a sheer cliff, the great tiger spotted the intruder and snorted.
It had wondered what sort of creature had the nerve to come here. The answer was smaller and shabbier than it had expected: an old human who hardly looked worth a single bite.
Ssshhk.
Its body, weighing several hundred geun, moved nimbly toward the old man. It was at that very moment.
“So there was a tiger.”
The tiger stopped short in its silent approach.
The old man had risen on his short legs and was staring straight at it.
“You’re old too, I see.”
- Grrr.
The tiger bared its teeth. The old man only gave a short laugh.
“Quiet now. Come here and keep this old man company.”
- Raaaargh!
“You striped mutt, you want to die? I said come here.”
The tiger flinched.
It couldn’t have said why, but every hair on its body stood on end. It approached the old man with uncertain steps.
When the wrinkled hand gently scratched its chin, it felt good despite itself.
- Prrrrr.
Watching the great tiger purr, the old man—Fire King Jeok Cheongang—murmured softly.
“Yes. I’ve already grown old.”
The sky above the cliff was clear. His heart was dark.
