Anyone would think I’d made you shit your pants.”
“What was that reaction?”
“...Nothing.
Why are you here?”
He gave me a suspicious look, then pointed toward the people in the distance.
“We’ve mostly finished sorting everything, but something’s odd.”
“Odd?
What?”
“There are fewer imugi bones and scales than we expected.
I think you’d better come see for yourself.”
“Really?”
“Yes.
Perfected Being Hyeongong is furious that there’s so little for an imugi that size.
He’s combing the area like he’s hunting for lice.
He says if someone stole any, he’ll find the culprit on the Primordial Heavenly Venerable’s honor.”
What was he, Detective Kindaichi?
He must have completely lost his mind after helping with the Taiji Wisdom Sword just to obtain some bones, only to think someone had snatched them away.
The more I listened, the more absurd it seemed, so I asked Hyuk Mujin,
“How could anyone steal it?
And it’s not like only a little went missing.
It must be well over a thousand geun.
How could anyone hide that without us noticing?”
“Exactly.
Hardly anyone even knows about this place—”
Mujin broke off and turned to me.
“But how did you know?”
“Hm?”
“How much was missing.
You said it must be over a thousand geun.”
“Just a rough guess.
They’ve been making a racket over there for a while.”
I answered as calmly as I could, but I felt a sudden stab of guilt.
Because...
*He’s sharp.
I need to watch what I say.*
The culprit Perfected Being Hyeongong had sworn to find was me.
Just thinking about the haul piled up in my Inventory made me feel full.
*Come to think of it, I did take a lot.*
It had been easier than lying in bed playing with my smartphone.
The Water God Dragon’s corpse was enormous, and I’d worked on more of it than anyone else, sweeping the choicest parts into my Inventory as I went.
The sharpest tailbone.
The unusually hard scales around its neck.
Even some flesh, just in case.
Pile up everything I’d smuggled away, and it would dwarf a decent-sized manor.
“...Why are you smiling so contentedly?”
“Me?
What smile?”
“Just now.
You looked incredibly shady.”
Apparently, my delight at pulling off the perfect crime was written all over my face.
I straightened my expression.
“I wasn’t smiling.”
“Anyway, leave them to it.
Go get ready.”
“Ready for what?”
“To head back.
You want to live here forever?”
People we could trust would move the sorted remains of the Water God Dragon discreetly, a little at a time.
Most of them would go to the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
*That’ll be a huge help in the battles ahead.*
I got to my feet.
Mujin was already running off in the distance, almost before I’d finished speaking.
Watching his back, I called out inwardly.
*Inventory open.
Summon.*
Shhk.
At the command, the Water God Dragon’s bones, scales, and flesh appeared in my hands.
I couldn’t help smiling.
*Item appraisal.*
Ding.

**System Item Window Water God Dragon’s Bones Type:** Material **Grade:** Supreme Peak **Restriction:** Only a Master Artisan can forge them. **Description:** The bones of the Water God Dragon, an imugi that lived for countless years.
They are exceptionally strong and contain an unknown, mystical qi.
A craftsman who has reached the proper realm may be able to draw out their true power.
Although there were slight differences, the System’s description of the scales was similar.
They, too, were Supreme Peak materials of exceptional strength with mystical qi inside them.
As for the flesh, eating it regularly over time could increase internal energy and stat points.
*This is like winning the lottery.*
But the real jackpot was something else.
If the bones and scales were Lotto tickets and the flesh an annuity lottery, this was the American Powerball.
The prize was on another scale entirely.
My heart pounding, I took *it* out of the Inventory.
*Item appraisal.*
Ding.

**System Item Window Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence Type:** None **Grade:** None **Restriction:** None **Description:** The Origin Essence of the Water God Dragon, an imugi that lived for countless years.
Though damaged by magical power, it is a kind of inner core extracted according to the Water God Dragon’s will.
It holds an immense quantity of exceptionally pure qi and is unlike any ordinary elixir.
However, if you cannot withstand the qi within it...
Further details omitted.
*That’s incredible.*
I carefully stroked the **Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence** in my hand.
That last line was ominous, but this was the greatest thing I’d gained from the trip to Hubei.
*Unlike any ordinary elixir...
Just how powerful is it?*
Having been contaminated by magical power, it couldn’t contain as much qi as the Water God Dragon had possessed at its peak.
Even so, the amount had to be enormous.
The Water God Dragon had lived for over five hundred years.
By simple calculation, that meant it had accumulated at least ten jiazi of qi.
From that perspective, the reduction in the Origin Essence’s power was practically a blessing in disguise.
*Pour too much water into a small vessel, and it overflows.*
As the final line of the item description suggested, even I would burst like a balloon if I tried to take in that much qi all at once.
*The question is when and where to use it.*
Several faces came to mind.
One old face in particular kept returning.
*Old Master.*
Jeok Cheongang hadn’t come to mind simply because he was old.
Strangely enough, it was because of Mungyeong’s poison.
After Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder had cost me ten precious stat points, and a severe stomachache had made me shit myself, a thought had struck me.
*If Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder did this much...
What condition must Old Master be in after being poisoned by the Formless Ultimate Poison?*
Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder was undoubtedly an extreme poison, but it wasn’t enough to threaten the life of a Supreme Peak master.
The Formless Ultimate Poison that had struck Jeok Cheongang in Henan was far more toxic.
Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder couldn’t compare.
Even the Luoyang Strange Physician, one of the most renowned physicians in the world, had no answer and had advised us to seek the Divine Physician.
And because the poison had already spread so far, we’d needed the Myriad-Poison Ring as well.
*Fortunately, the Thousand-Year Snow Ginseng let us finish treating him...*
But had he really recovered without any significant aftereffects?
I stared at the **Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence**, doubt and worry mingling in my mind.
Perhaps this was an item whose purpose had been decided from the very beginning.
“Little Brother!”
*Inventory open.
Store.*
I hurriedly put the **Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence** back into my inventory at Jin Wikyung’s shout from behind me, then turned around with an awkward smile.
“Yes, I’m coming!”
Today had been a day of many satisfying gains.
Yet something weighed on my heart, and for some reason, my stomach felt as though it were twisting.
Grrrggg.
“...Sigh.”
Oh.
The status abnormality still hadn’t worn off.
Humans were not the only creatures that settled near water.
Animals did too.
Birds nested along the cliffs above the broad waters of Dongting Lake.
Wild boars, foxes, wolves, and even tigers lived there as well.
If Dongting Lake below the cliffs was territory permitted to humans, then the cliffs above belonged to the animals.
It was a peaceful place untouched by human feet.
So the great tiger, king of that place, was displeased to find an uninvited guest had arrived.
- Grrrrrrr.
Irritation rumbled through its sharp teeth.
Its nose flared ceaselessly, following the human scent that still lingered in the air.
Its keen sense of smell soon found the source.
- Grrr.
At the edge of a sheer cliff, the great tiger spotted the intruder and snorted.
It had wondered what sort of creature had the nerve to come here.
The answer was smaller and shabbier than it had expected: an old human who hardly looked worth a single bite.
Ssshhk.
Its body, weighing several hundred geun, moved nimbly toward the old man.
It was at that very moment.
“So there was a tiger.”
The tiger stopped short in its silent approach.
The old man had risen on his short legs and was staring straight at it.
“You’re old too, I see.”
- Grrr.
The tiger bared its teeth.
The old man only gave a short laugh.
“Quiet now.
Come here and keep this old man company.”
- Raaaargh!
“You striped mutt, you want to die?
I said come here.”
The tiger flinched.
It couldn’t have said why, but every hair on its body stood on end.
It approached the old man with uncertain steps.
When the wrinkled hand gently scratched its chin, it felt good despite itself.
- Prrrrr.
Watching the great tiger purr, the old man—Fire King Jeok Cheongang—murmured softly.
“Yes.
I’ve already grown old.”
The sky above the cliff was clear.
His heart was dark.

chapters.title: Chapter 496
paragraphs: “Hmm.”
Hyuk Mujin carefully picked up his brush. The small booklet spread across the table was already packed with entries from the past several days.
**X Month X Day. Weather was shitty, then cleared up.**
I had a nightmare about a monster that looked like a dragon. It scared me so badly I wet myself in my sleep.
As soon as I woke up, I sneaked down to the stream to wash my undergarments and trousers. Gung Gibang was already there, washing shit out of his trousers.
What a filthy bastard. Even among beggars, you’d be hard-pressed to find a worse one.
I have no idea why our Captain insists on dragging around someone who shits his pants.
But why am I in the infirmary?
**X Month X Day. Clear skies.**
The nightmare was real.
According to Mungyeong, the monster was an imugi. Demonic qi had seeped into its very marrow and driven it to commit an atrocity that outraged heaven and humanity.
Fortunately, thanks to the Captain stepping in, I was barely affected by the demonic qi. I was told to keep a diary for the time being and use it to piece my memories back together.
Still, I couldn’t believe all those ridiculous things I’d seen had actually happened.
While Mungyeong was explaining, a question occurred to me. I asked if what I’d seen in the dream—no, what I’d seen there, with him fighting—had been real too.
Mungyeong said no. Gung Gibang joined in asking him about it, but for some reason, I fell asleep right there. I must have been tired.
Then why is there a bruise on my forehead?
I don’t know. I’m going back to sleep.
**X Month X Day.**
I went to deal with the corpse. The imugi’s enormous size nearly made me piss myself once, and the Captain’s butchering skills nearly did it a second time.
I asked him to make me a Bone Sword and got beaten until my skull rang.
I heard the imugi’s corpse would be transported in secret after being divided into bones, scales, and flesh.
Oh, and for some reason, a considerable amount of the sorted remains disappeared.
Perfected Being Hyeongong was furious and declared that he would find the culprit, but that’s ridiculous. We’re not talking about something the size of a fist. Who could steal that much?
We left the little commotion behind and boarded the boat back. Once aboard, I noticed a terrible smell of shit coming from somewhere.
I couldn’t stand it any longer and brought it up. Before I could finish speaking, the Captain pointed at Gung Gibang.
He denied it vehemently, but I saw him washing his shit-stained trousers a few days ago. How could I believe him?
Mungyeong sat beside me with an odd expression the whole time.
He probably wanted to curse Gung Gibang out over the smell but held back to spare his dignity.
What a good kid. Every time I see him, he seems so innocent and easy to like.
**X Month X Day.**
It’s been two days since we dealt with the imugi’s corpse.
I don’t know why, but Sir Jeok hasn’t been around at all, and the Captain looks gaunter by the day.
I joked that he looked like someone being tormented by poison and ambushes day and night. He glared at me as if he wanted to kill me.
He only takes it out on me because I’m an easy target.
Just as I was thinking that, Gung Gibang said the same thing and got beaten too. I felt better.
**X Month X Day.**
This is my first entry in three days. I haven’t written because there was nothing worth writing about.
First Sir Jeok, and now the Captain has become hard to find. Mungyeong keeps wandering off somewhere too.
What else is a martial artist like me supposed to do with his free time? Gung Gibang and I found a decent place to train.
His breath smells like a sewer, but when he keeps his mouth shut and trains, he’s not so bad.
Cheongpung somehow found us. Every bit of advice he gave was useless.
Whenever I asked him about martial arts, I got one of two answers.
“It’s really easy.”
“Why can’t you do it?”
You bastard. If it were that easy, would I still be First Rate?
Maybe he got frustrated, because he demonstrated it for me. I still couldn’t understand a thing.
Every time we train, that water snake called something like Mimi sits beside us swallowing Blood Fish. Maybe that’s why it seems to have grown so much. Its horns too.
No wonder the Blood Fish seemed to have vanished. They must have all gone down that thing’s throat.
**X Month X Day.**
I’ve become fairly friendly with a few martial artists from the Zhuge Clan and Wudang, and they’ve told me some things.
Under the direct supervision of Sir Zhuge Feng, the Crouching Dragon Guest, the Zhuge Clan is testing a formation to seal the gap completely.
Apparently, if they can’t seal it, strange creatures like the Blood Fish will keep appearing. I have no idea what bizarre method those Dark Heaven bastards used to make such a thing.
Meanwhile, Wudang is still hunting the Killing Ghost.
Even with the authorities helping them comb through Hubei Province, they haven’t found him. The bastard must have made an art of running away.
**X Month X Day.**
It has been seven days and nights since I came here. The Captain’s complexion was calm when I saw him again after so long.
Before, he’d been covered in wounds from whatever training he was doing alone, and his face was either pale or tinged blue. He seems to be better now.
His temper has grown sharper instead, and he walks like a ghost.
He gives off so little sign of his presence that he caught Gung Gibang and me bad-mouthing him and beat us within an inch of our lives.
Seriously, how did he hear us from that far away?
Come to think of it, Mungyeong looked pleased while I was getting beaten... I must have imagined it.
“Hmm.”
That was where the diary of what Hyuk Mujin had seen and experienced over roughly ten days ended.
He gazed down at the booklet, lost in thought. Just as he was about to put brush to paper for a new entry, excited shouts came from outside.
“It—it worked!”
“Family Head! We did it!”
“Not you—I did it! As expected, I’m a genius! Zhuge Wuhou!”
Slip! Splotch!
His concentration broke. His hand slipped, and the brush went astray.
Hyuk Mujin’s face contorted. So much for writing with the bearing of a great literary master.
“Which bastard was that?”
A familiar voice slipped into his ear as he raged.
“The bastard you’re talking about sounds like Sir Zhuge Feng. Shall I pass along your words?”
“Go ahead. Then Young Hero Gung dies, and I die right after him.”
Hyuk Mujin answered gruffly and put down his brush as Gung Gibang entered the tent without permission.
“But what on earth is happening outside?”
“Looks like the Zhuge Clan managed to seal the gap completely.”
“With a formation?”
“What else would they use? Rocks?”
“Oh, come on. Why *couldn’t* they use rocks?”
“Because that wouldn’t solve the problem. And if rocks were enough, they’d have sealed it ages ago. Think before you speak.”
“Oh, really? Is thinking too much why you shit yourself?”
“A dog that pissed itself criticizing a dog that shit itself.”
“Pissing is better than shitting. Besides, Young Hero Gung did it twice. Last time, when we went to dispose of the imugi’s corpse...”
“This is driving me crazy. I told you, that wasn’t me!”
Hyuk Mujin clicked his tongue as Gung Gibang thumped his chest.
“There’s only so much you can deny.”
“I’m telling you the truth!”
“If it wasn’t Young Hero Gung, then who was it? Hmm? Surely you don’t think Perfected Being Hyeongong did it?”
“Jin Taekyung! I swear that bastard reeked of shit—gah!”
Gung Gibang broke off with a start and looked around. Only a few days earlier, he had been beaten half to death after having a similar conversation.
“He’s not here, is he?”
Hyuk Mujin swallowed dryly as well.
The Jin Taekyung he knew had a fiery personality. Whoever started the insults, he would happily beat both sides senseless.
“P-probably?”
“You’re sure?”
“How would I know? Anyone who can sense the Captain coming is already a Supreme Peak master. Or a ghost.”
The two of them looked around with every sense on high alert, then let out deep sighs of relief.
Suddenly, the absurdity of their situation struck them. They had become afraid after saying only a few words.
“How long do we have to live like this?”
“Until the Captain dies.”
“What if he undergoes Returned to Youth someday?”
“Then we bite our tongues and kill ourselves. What else can we do?”
“Damn it. That Jin Taekyung bastard is a real monster. How can anyone be like that?”
Hyuk Mujin nodded vigorously. He’d known Jin Taekyung since his days as a delinquent; of course he understood.
“That’s true. And there are two of them, not just one.”

“Cheongpung? Don’t even get me started. After seeing the Drunken Eight Immortals Fist only a few times, he started imitating it pretty closely. If my master found out, he’d try to kill me for leaking our sect’s secret art.”
“Ooh.”
“...I have a fairly good idea what you were just thinking, but keep your mouth shut forever. I’m really going to die.”
“Oooh.”
“You rotten bastard.”
Gung Gibang shook his head, then asked, “What’s your lord doing, anyway? I hardly see him.”
“How would I know? He might be training. Might not. Some days he stays in his tent the whole time.”
“Sir Jin’s always busy with one thing or another. But Sir Jeok’s been gone a long time too.”
Jeok Cheongang had vanished without a trace after their first day there.
Plenty of people wondered where he was. None worried about his safety.
Fire King. Those two words were proof enough of what he could do.
“Who could harm the Fire King?”
“True. Even Dark Heaven wouldn’t dare. If they tried anything, three or four of their pillars would have been ripped out, and the surrounding area would already have been reduced to ashes.”
Gung Gibang nodded in agreement and continued.
“Come to think of it, I haven’t seen much of Mungyeong lately either.”
“Neither have I. Whenever I do see him, he’s with the Captain.”
“Really?”
“Yes. I figured it might be because the Captain got hurt while training...”
“Hmm.”
“What?”
“Nothing. I smell something.”
“Did you shit yourself again?”
“Hyuk Mujin, you lunatic. Not that. I mean there’s something going on between them.”
Gung Gibang frowned in thought.
“Wait. Could it be?”
“Could what?”
“You still don’t get it? Why have those two been together so often lately?”
Hyuk Mujin’s expression changed. Listening to Gung Gibang, he began to see what he meant.
“Then maybe...”
“Exactly what you’re thinking.”
“Good heavens. How can this be?”
“If you think about it, it is strange. The Captain punches us whenever he gets bored, but he hasn’t used so much as a single act of violence against Mungyeong.”
“He hardly even curses at him anymore. And something was suspicious when we went to deal with the imugi’s corpse.”
“When Jin Taekyung disappeared, Mungyeong was gone too.”
“Exactly! The Beggars’ Sect’s future Sect Leader never disappoints!”
“That settles it. Mungyeong...”
Gung Gibang’s face went rigid.
“He must be learning martial arts from that Jin bastard.”
“Ah, Mungyeong! How could you make such a terrible choice?”
Hyuk Mujin was genuinely heartbroken. Mungyeong was like a clean white sheet of paper. The thought of Jin Taekyung’s ink soaking into it made his chest ache.
“What did that child ever do to deserve this?”
“What a tragedy. How can I face the Divine Physician in Sichuan?”
“Not Mungyeong! We can’t let him go down the same path we did!”
“It’s too late. Jin Taekyung is a Fiend. Now that Mungyeong is in that evil bastard’s clutches, there’s nothing we can do.”
“Then by now, Mungyeong must be...”
The two of them sighed in dismay at the same time. Thinking of Mungyeong, who must by now be fighting for his life under Jin Taekyung’s evil clutches, they felt their hearts grow heavy.
*Please survive, Mungyeong.*
*Please, somebody save me.*
Slice!
A gust of wind brushed my neck.
The pain was as cold as ice, then immediately flared hot. A bead of cold sweat ran down my forehead and dropped onto the ground with a soft tap.
Swish, tap!
I righted myself in midair and stared straight ahead.
“That was a little dangerous.”
A voice answered—or rather, a Sound Transmission.
—It was meant to be.
“No, I’m serious. I almost died.”
—Glad to hear it.
*Where the hell is he?*
I looked all around, but I couldn’t see him. There was only that Sound Transmission, coming from nowhere I could pin down.
“Fucking hell.”
—What kind of hell?
I took a deep breath and tightened my grip on White Flame’s shaft.
Toward whoever was watching me from somewhere unseen, I muttered as though spitting the words out.
“This is so fucking shitty I can’t keep doing this.”
Whoosh!
Instead of an answer, a blinding sword strike came flying at me.

Hyuk Mujin swallowed dryly as well.
The Jin Taekyung he knew had a fiery personality.
Whoever started the insults, he would happily beat both sides senseless.
“P-probably?”
“You’re sure?”
“How would I know?
Anyone who can sense the Captain coming is already a Supreme Peak master.
Or a ghost.”
The two of them looked around with every sense on high alert, then let out deep sighs of relief.
Suddenly, the absurdity of their situation struck them.
They had become afraid after saying only a few words.
“How long do we have to live like this?”
“Until the Captain dies.”
“What if he undergoes Returned to Youth someday?”
“Then we bite our tongues and kill ourselves.
What else can we do?”
“Damn it.
That Jin Taekyung bastard is a real monster.
How can anyone be like that?”
Hyuk Mujin nodded vigorously.
He’d known Jin Taekyung since his days as a delinquent; of course he understood.
“That’s true.
And there are two of them, not just one.”
“Cheongpung?
Don’t even get me started.
After seeing the Drunken Eight Immortals Fist only a few times, he started imitating it pretty closely.
If my master found out, he’d try to kill me for leaking our sect’s secret art.”
“Ooh.”
“...I have a fairly good idea what you were just thinking, but keep your mouth shut forever.
I’m really going to die.”
“Oooh.”
“You rotten bastard.”
Gung Gibang shook his head, then asked, “What’s your lord doing, anyway?
I hardly see him.”
“How would I know?
He might be training.
Might not.
Some days he stays in his tent the whole time.”
“Sir Jin’s always busy with one thing or another.
But Sir Jeok’s been gone a long time too.”
Jeok Cheongang had vanished without a trace after their first day there.
Plenty of people wondered where he was.
None worried about his safety.
Fire King.
Those two words were proof enough of what he could do.
“Who could harm the Fire King?”
“True.
Even Dark Heaven wouldn’t dare.
If they tried anything, three or four of their pillars would have been ripped out, and the surrounding area would already have been reduced to ashes.”
Gung Gibang nodded in agreement and continued.
“Come to think of it, I haven’t seen much of Mungyeong lately either.”
“Neither have I.
Whenever I do see him, he’s with the Captain.”
“Really?”
“Yes.
I figured it might be because the Captain got hurt while training...”
“Hmm.”
“What?”
“Nothing.
I smell something.”
“Did you shit yourself again?”
“Hyuk Mujin, you lunatic.
Not that.
I mean there’s something going on between them.”
Gung Gibang frowned in thought.
“Wait.
Could it be?”
“Could what?”
“You still don’t get it?
Why have those two been together so often lately?”
Hyuk Mujin’s expression changed.
Listening to Gung Gibang, he began to see what he meant.
“Then maybe...”
“Exactly what you’re thinking.”
“Good heavens.
How can this be?”
“If you think about it, it is strange.
The Captain punches us whenever he gets bored, but he hasn’t used so much as a single act of violence against Mungyeong.”
“He hardly even curses at him anymore.
And something was suspicious when we went to deal with the imugi’s corpse.”
“When Jin Taekyung disappeared, Mungyeong was gone too.”
“Exactly!
The Beggars’ Sect’s future Sect Leader never disappoints!”
“That settles it.
Mungyeong...”
Gung Gibang’s face went rigid.
“He must be learning martial arts from that Jin bastard.”
“Ah, Mungyeong!
How could you make such a terrible choice?”
Hyuk Mujin was genuinely heartbroken.
Mungyeong was like a clean white sheet of paper.
The thought of Jin Taekyung’s ink soaking into it made his chest ache.
“What did that child ever do to deserve this?”
“What a tragedy.
How can I face the Divine Physician in Sichuan?”
“Not Mungyeong!
We can’t let him go down the same path we did!”
“It’s too late.
Jin Taekyung is a Fiend.
Now that Mungyeong is in that evil bastard’s clutches, there’s nothing we can do.”
“Then by now, Mungyeong must be...”
The two of them sighed in dismay at the same time.
Thinking of Mungyeong, who must by now be fighting for his life under Jin Taekyung’s evil clutches, they felt their hearts grow heavy.
*Please survive, Mungyeong.*
*Please, somebody save me.*
Slice!
A gust of wind brushed my neck.
The pain was as cold as ice, then immediately flared hot.
A bead of cold sweat ran down my forehead and dropped onto the ground with a soft tap.
Swish, tap!
I righted myself in midair and stared straight ahead.
“That was a little dangerous.”
A voice answered—or rather, a Sound Transmission.
—It was meant to be.
“No, I’m serious.
I almost died.”
—Glad to hear it.
*Where the hell is he?*
I looked all around, but I couldn’t see him.
There was only that Sound Transmission, coming from nowhere I could pin down.
“Fucking hell.”
—What kind of hell?
I took a deep breath and tightened my grip on White Flame’s shaft.
Toward whoever was watching me from somewhere unseen, I muttered as though spitting the words out.
“This is so fucking shitty I can’t keep doing this.”
Whoosh!
Instead of an answer, a blinding sword strike came flying at me.

chapters.title: Chapter 497
paragraphs: Half an hour.
That was the longest I could hold out. With the cold edge of a sword against the back of my neck, I muttered under my breath.
“God, this sucks.”
Ssshhk.
A stinging pain ran across my neck, and blood slid down it. The point of the gesture was obvious. I sighed.
“I lost. Let’s stop.”
“Wrong. Again.”
That dry voice was one I hadn’t heard during the fight. I already knew what its owner wanted me to say.
“...I’m dead. Happy?”
The blade that had been slowly digging into my neck stopped. When I felt the cold metal withdraw, I pressed a hand to the cut to stop the bleeding, then turned around.
Mungyeong was sitting on a rock about thirty feet away.
“Do you know how many times you’ve died?”
“Twelve.”

Five times, my Sinews and Meridians had been severed in all four limbs. Three times, I had died from a Pressure-Point Strike to a lethal acupoint. Three more times, my heart had been pierced. And just now, my throat had been cut.
I hadn’t actually died, but I might as well have. I wiped the sticky blood from my neck with my sleeve and looked at Mungyeong.
“It’ll be different next time.”
“That’s the eleventh time I’ve heard that.”
“I mean it this time.”
“That makes twelve.”
*What a memory.*
As I stood there speechless, Mungyeong asked, “Do you know why you died?”
A fight always left a result, and a result gave you something to think about.
I silently replayed our fight in my head, then blurted out an answer.
“Because I fought like an assassin?”
“As expected, you know nothing... Hmm.”
Mungyeong had begun speaking almost at the same time as me, but now he trailed off.
“Am I wrong?”
“Go on.”
“I don’t know exactly when it started, but I found myself imitating you. Your movements and things like that.”
At first, after getting turned into a pickle soaked in poison, I’d begun paying attention to everything around me. Then I’d started copying Mungyeong’s movements bit by bit.
Dueling him two or three times a day, I’d gradually grown used to them. My eyes recognized them, and so did my body.
But...
“That was my mistake.”
“Why?”
“New shoes rub your heels raw. Even more so if they’re too small.”
“Be more specific.”
“I should’ve quit the clumsy imitation and fought my own way. Especially against the Slaughter Saint.”
Mungyeong stared at me for a while, then tossed out a single remark.
“You’re not a complete idiot.”
“Oh, was that a compliment?”
“It means you’ve only just reached the basics.”
“Exactly. Thank you for the compliment.”
Mungyeong frowned.
“Are your ears plugged?”
“Nope. They work fine.”
“...You have a gift for getting on people’s nerves.”
“Either way, reaching the basics means it was a compliment. Why are you so bad at being honest? Are you going through puberty?”
“I said I’m not!”
“Why are you shouting all of a sudden?”
“When did I— I said I’m not!”
“...Now that I think about it, maybe you are.”
*Not going through puberty, my ass.*
But if I talked back one more time, my head looked liable to fly off.
After that outburst, Mungyeong returned to his usual calm, dry tone as though nothing had happened.
“The basics are just that: the basics. There have been plenty of others like you.”
*Others like me?*
I ventured a question.
“Do you have other Disciples?”
“Of course. You met one in Sichuan.”
“Other than Old Man Dong. You know what I mean. Don’t change the subject.”
Silence was as good as an admission. The thought of the Slaughter Saint’s hidden Disciples made me curious.
“Who? Who are they? Do you still keep in touch? Do you all get together for a meal on Teacher’s Day?”
“I have no reason to tell you. And what the hell is Teacher’s Day?”
“You’re awfully difficult.”
“...You grow more insolent by the day. Do you have five lives or something?”
“Considering I’ve died and come back twelve times, I’d say I have about thirteen. So you’re really not going to tell me?”
Mungyeong stared at me, then spoke abruptly.
“I’ll tell you. On one condition.”
A condition from the Slaughter Saint. I answered with complete confidence.
“It’s about time to eat. I’ll be going now.”
“I distinctly remember you eating before you came.”
“I eat five meals a day.”
“Stay and hear the condition. You seemed quite curious.”
“Everyone has a life of their own and secrets they’d rather keep. Who am I to pry? Anyway, I’ll be off.”
“Stop right there if you want to keep your head.”
*Fuck. I shouldn’t have asked.*
My stomach knotted with panic as I turned back around. Fine. Since I was stuck here, I might as well hear the story.
“So you really have other Disciples?”
“Not Disciples. But I did teach several people.”
“That sounds like you’re saying they’re gone.”
“It’s been a very long time. They couldn’t possibly still be alive.”
“Were they, by any chance, in the same line of work as...?”
“They were assassins. They belonged to Salcheonmun with me.”
Even the name smelled of blood.
*So he belonged to a sect, too.*
It made sense when I thought about it. No matter how extraordinary Mungyeong was, he hadn’t been born an assassin.
*Still, a sect the Slaughter Saint belonged to should be fairly well known.*
But no matter how thoroughly I searched my memory, the name Salcheonmun meant nothing to me.
As if he’d read my mind, Mungyeong spoke.
“No use trying to remember it. The sect vanished long ago.”
There was only one way for a sect to vanish. Watching his expression, I carefully said one word.
“Annihilated?”
“Yes.”
“How did that happen? No, before that—weren’t you the Sect Leader?”
“They chose the wrong path and paid the price. That’s all I’ll say.”
Mungyeong finished speaking and rose to his feet. A short sword in his hand already gleamed with a keen blue edge.
“Now it’s time for you to pay.”
“Excuse me?”
“Dodge one sword stroke. That’s the condition.”
Most people would probably think, *How am I supposed to evade that?* But from my perspective, it was worth trying.
I’d lasted half an hour against the Slaughter Saint while doing a lousy imitation of an assassin. Surely I could dodge one stroke.
“If I do, will you tell me more later?”
“Of course.”
“Fine. I can do that.”
Mungyeong added, “Close your eyes.”
“Fuck. Are you kidding me?”
“Then you will die. Not the thirteenth time, but for the first and last time.”
Before he’d finished speaking, Mungyeong’s sleeve fluttered.
By now, I was used to his attacks. I instinctively turned my head, but what came flying toward me wasn’t a hidden weapon. It was something else.
*That’s...*
A powder so fine I could barely make it out even when I strained my eyes to their limit.
It rode the wind blowing toward me. The instant the powder touched the air—
Whoosh!
Darkness swallowed the world.
No. That wasn’t right.
The darkness hadn’t swallowed the world. It had swallowed me.
Beep.
**System** You have been poisoned by **Blindness Powder**! You temporarily lose your eyesight! Rapid **Detoxification** is required! If Detoxification is delayed too long, permanent damage may occur!
Every hair on my body stood on end as the System alert sounded in my ears.
Blindness Powder? The poison itself didn’t matter. I was still wearing the Myriad-Poison Ring.
The problem was that Mungyeong’s sword was coming through the darkness far faster than the ring could detoxify the Blindness Powder.
Ssshhk.
I couldn’t see a thing. But I could feel it clearly.
In a world moving so slowly it felt as though someone had pressed pause, a killing sword approached, erasing the wind in its path.
*This is...*
A move from the greatest assassin of all time.
I felt a killing intent unlike anything I’d ever encountered—so stealthy and chilling that I shuddered.
I stared blankly into the darkness.
And in that suffocating space where I could see nothing, I felt every sense I had awaken.
Slash!
Wudang, the Zhuge Clan, and the Beggars’ Sect.
They had chosen only trustworthy elites to preserve secrecy, but no one could ignore either the standing or the number of those gathered.
Among the several hundred martial artists from prestigious great sects, the figure of a young medical apprentice was bound to stand out wherever he went.
“Oh, it’s you. Just coming out?”
“I’ve just been to see Young Master Jin.”
“You seem to visit him more often these days.”
“Yes. His training has been so rough lately that he keeps getting hurt.”
“Good heavens. Great Hero Jin really is remarkable. He’s younger than my son, but he isn’t content with his current realm. He just keeps working...”
“He must be an incredible master. I don’t know much about Murim myself.”

The Zhuge martial artist standing guard let out a short laugh at the young medical apprentice’s innocent remark. Boredom had led him to bother a child who’d learned nothing but medicine, and now he felt a little guilty.
“He is incredible. No doubt about it. You’ll understand someday, too.”
“Hmm. Is that so?”
“If you’re not involved in Murim, you might not know. Anyway, is his training over for today?”
As though he knew nothing, Mungyeong tilted his head and answered.
“No. He said no one should come near him for the next two shichen.”
“Understood. This is Great Hero Jin we’re talking about—we can’t interrupt his training. I’ll pass that along to the next guards.”
“Yes. Then take care.”
Mungyeong politely bowed at the waist and was about to leave when the martial artist suddenly spoke.
“My, his training must be rougher than I thought.”
“Sorry?”
“The blood on your sleeve. Was Great Hero Jin badly hurt?”
The guard’s follow-up question never reached Mungyeong. He looked down at the bloodstain on his sleeve and murmured, “The basics...?”
“Hmm?”
“Oh, it’s nothing. Young Master Jin is fine, so don’t worry.”
“Ah. Good. All right.”
Leaving the martial artist behind with an uneasy expression, Mungyeong walked away.
Several faces had grown familiar enough to speak to him and acknowledge him as they passed, but the young medical apprentice’s mind held only one person.
*Jin Taekyung. Jin Taekyung...*
He’d thought it couldn’t happen. Yet the boy really had dodged that final sword stroke.
The results of the past several days of testing, and of today, had exceeded Mungyeong’s expectations. No, they had exceeded anything he’d imagined.
*So this can happen.*
Everything he’d told Jin Taekyung was true.
He had once had people who could properly be called Disciples, and every one of them had possessed the “basics.”
But there was one thing he hadn’t mentioned: how long that had taken.
*The fastest of them took a little over a year, if I remember right.*
Jin Taekyung had done it in only seven days and nights.
No one else came close.

Mungyeong didn’t know whether it was because of the boy’s Heavenly Martial Physique or because he was a Supreme Peak master. Whatever the reason, there was something special about Jin Taekyung himself.
“Even so... I never expected this much.”
He murmured too softly for anyone to hear and rolled up his sleeve.
The skin had been cut by something sharp, and beads of blood had formed along the wound. Looking at it, Mungyeong had a sudden thought.
*Now I understand how the Fire King feels.*
But Mungyeong did not realize that a faint smile had formed at the corner of his mouth.

My flicker of unease faded as soon as I spotted the moon shining faintly in the ink-dark sky. I muttered, my voice hoarse, “Shit. You could’ve woken me before you left.”
I’d thought the Blindness Powder was still working. It was just night.
A good deal of time must have passed while I was unconscious. I lay sprawled on my back, staring blankly at the sky, then slowly sat up.
*What the hell happened?*
I had moved almost entirely unconsciously, and since I’d passed out while poisoned by the Blindness Powder, I hadn’t seen what happened at the time. I felt my dirt-covered body all over.
*Nothing else seems to be hurt. I must have stopped it somehow.*
I could guess the result, but I couldn’t picture how I’d done it. How had I moved? No matter how hard I tried to recall the sensation, the memory stayed hazy.
There was one thing I did know.
Beep.

“Agh,” my ass. As someone who had nearly crossed the Jordan River instead of Dongting Lake, I was furious.
*A Follow-up Quest.*

I’d expected something like this, but that didn’t make it any less worrying. Stage 1 had me dodge the Slaughter Saint’s sword stroke with my eyes closed. What kind of fucked-up stunt did they have planned for Stage 2?
At least the rewards were generous.
*I guess putting my body through hell paid off.*
I hadn’t leveled up, but I’d gained a considerable amount of EXP and recovered the points I’d lost after being poisoned by Seven-Step Soul-Chasing Powder.
And...
*Which asshole came up with those titles?*
Deadly Poison Sommelier and Wow, You Survived That. The names pissed me off, but both Achievements were worth having.
The Poison Resistance from the first one was obviously welcome. The second might seem a little vague right now, but it was a huge gift.
*A clue to enlightenment.*

I’d been feeling as though I’d hit a wall lately. Nothing could have been better news. Of course, if I said that out loud after racing through the realms on the Fire Gate Clan’s Supreme Peak martial arts and quarterly helpings of elixirs, Murim would probably declare me a public enemy.
*Still, a wall’s a wall.*

Ask a martial artist stuck at Second Rate or Third Rate what they need, and nine out of ten will say martial arts manuals and elixirs. Ask a master who’s reached Peak or higher, and the answer changes.
*Enlightenment.*

Ten years, twenty years—even longer could pass without it coming. No matter how extraordinary the martial arts you learned or how many elixirs you took, there was a limit to how far they could carry you.

If stuffing yourself with elixirs could make you a Supreme Peak master and return you to youth, who would train until they bled and sweated? People devoted their lives to training because they couldn’t get past that wall any other way.
Gung Gibang had once told me that quite a few martial artists even took opium, hoping to expand the realm of their minds and attain enlightenment.
When I asked why they’d do something so stupid, his answer was simple.
“They know they’ll get addicted to opium if they keep it up.”
“Then why do it?”
“Because they’re martial artists.”
A short answer, but it explained everything.

Martial artists were creatures like that. They were the sort of people who would do anything if it meant becoming stronger. They were more intoxicated by martial arts than by opium, and they had become addicted to power.
And I wasn’t so different.
*I want to be stronger. Stronger still.*

I had more now than I could ever have imagined in the past, and I still wanted more strength. There was one crucial difference between me and other martial artists, though. I didn’t want it so I could gain something. I wanted it so I could protect what I had.
*If I’d been satisfied with where I was, I never would’ve accepted Mungyeong’s training.*
That made the clue to enlightenment an enormous gain.
There was just one tiny problem.
*Doctor, I don’t remember a thing.*
I didn’t even know what I’d done. Fuck.
Seriously, how had I pulled it off? I thought I’d dodged the sword by a hair, but I couldn’t remember what happened after that.
*Maybe I’ll figure it out if I keep training.*
I tried to recapture the sensation, but for now I was groping through fog. I sighed, got to my feet, and began brushing the dirt off my clothes.
That was when it happened.
Ssshhk—boom!
Far away, a streak of blue fire shot into the dark sky and burst in a brilliant flash.
*A signal firework?*
I hurried out of the training area to see what was going on and found the martial artists standing guard.
“What happened?”
“Oh, Great Hero Jin. You’re finally out.”
The Beggars’ Sect disciple shrugged. His patched clothes and the two knots hanging from his waist marked him as a member of the Hubei branch.
“Blue means visitors. We knew they were coming, but they’re later than expected.”
“Visitors?”
*What is this place, a tourist attraction?*

Since the place was being treated as highly classified, I couldn’t immediately think of anyone who might come here. At most, there were the three sects gathered here and the authorities. And if they were sending reinforcements, the guards wouldn’t call them visitors.
“Where from? The Zhuge Clan? Wudang? Oh, did Wudang’s Sect Leader finally arrive?”
“Sorry?”
The Beggars’ Sect disciple and the other martial artists stared at me as if they had never seen such a strange person before.
“Uh... you haven’t heard?”
“Heard what?”
“Who’s coming.”
“What are you talking about...? Is it someone I know?”
The disciple nodded.
“Yes. They’re from the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
From where?
Splash! Splish, splash!
Disciplined footsteps crossed the moonlit river and left fresh tracks in the sand.
Around fifty martial artists moved as one, forming lines on either side. A man walked slowly between them, spotted me, and stopped.
“It’s been a long time.”
His eyes were as sharp as ever, and he had more scars than I remembered. I gave a short laugh at the familiar face I hadn’t seen in a year.
“Your face looks even fiercer. Maybe we should call you Ghost Face instead of Ghost Sword.”
“There were plenty of bastards who needed dealing with. As our family’s reach has grown, all sorts have come crawling out of the woodwork.”
“Just tell me who. I’ll deal with them.”
“There’s no need. They’ve already left for a place beyond anyone’s reach. And...”
His narrowed eyes held a smile, and his voice carried both fondness and joy.
“There’s no need for the Divine Dragon to bother with mere cows and pigs.”
Ghost Sword Wipeng—Jin Wikyung’s right-hand man and the person once charged with knocking some sense into me—gave me a deep martial salute.
“Wipeng, Commander of the Jin Dragon Squad of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan, greets the Third Young Master.”
“Greetings, Third Young Master!”

The shout rang out through the stillness of the deep night. Powerful energy radiated from the bodies of the martial artists standing in lines like iron towers on either side. They were just like the two characters embroidered across every one of their chests: Jin Dragon.
*Wow. When did the Jin Family of Taiyuan get this big?*

It felt like yesterday that we’d sat with our heads together, muttering that we were fucked because we had nowhere near enough First Rate masters for the war against the Mount Heng Sword Sect. Yet the weakest member of the Jin Dragon Squad standing before me was at least First Rate.
*Just looking at them gets me fired up.*

The Jin Family of Taiyuan had been slowly declining: the Family Head had been absent for years, we were desperately short on people, and the Third Young Master liked pleasure houses more than his own home. And that was only part of it.
Seeing how far the family had risen made my chest swell with pride.
*Is this why people build families?*
I was gazing at Wipeng and the Jin Dragon Squad when a voice behind him spoiled the moment.
“Hey, damn it! You startled me. Why are you all shouting in the middle of the night? What if an old man with a weak heart like mine drops dead from the shock?”
That seemed unlikely.
I studied the man’s muscles—hard to believe they belonged to an old man—and finally dredged up the memory.
“Always do Taebo?”
Jang Taebo, former Guild Leader of the Ironcraft Guild, scowled.
“Listen to the mouth on this brat. Am I your friend?”

I’d built up quite a reputation over the past year, but Jang Taebo, a master craftsman who never held back, didn’t seem to care. If anything, that made me even happier to see him. Besides, White Flame, the spear he’d put his heart into forging, had saved my life more than once.
“Seriously, Elder. What brings you here?”
The answer came from someone other than Jang Taebo.
“I asked him to come.”

The people who had hurried over after hearing that the Jin Family of Taiyuan had arrived murmured among themselves and parted to either side. Jin Wikyung came through the crowd, and a shout even louder than before rang out.
“Wipeng, Commander of the Jin Dragon Squad of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan, pays his respects to his lord.”
“Loyalty!”
“That’s enough.”

Under different circumstances, Jin Wikyung would have grabbed Wipeng’s hand and danced a waltz with him, but countless eyes were watching us. Wearing a solemn, dignified expression, he waved a hand and continued in his deep voice.
“Commander of the Jin Dragon Squad. And Old Master Jang. You’ve both had a difficult journey.”
“Not at all, my lord.”
“Don’t concern yourself with this old man, Lesser Family Head.”

Wipeng was obviously a trusted retainer, but even Jang Taebo, who called me this brat and that bastard, was unfailingly respectful toward Jin Wikyung. I’d heard he had retired ages ago. Had he started taking work from the Jin Family of Taiyuan while I was away?
Leaving my question unanswered, Jin Wikyung spoke again.
“The journey must have been tiring. Let’s all move somewhere else first.”
I could tell I was included in that “all.” I could also tell the man running toward us, panting hard, wasn’t.
“Hyuk Mujin, Vice Commander of the Jin Dragon Squad! I’ve just finished my guard duty and returned!”
*Some guard duty.*
*If you’re going to lie, wipe the sleep from your eyes first, you bastard.*

chapters.title: Chapter 499
paragraphs: Spring was in full swing, but the night wind blowing along Dongting Lake’s winding waterways was chilly.
Jang Taebo entered Jin Wikyung’s heavy-cloth tent, claimed the spot in front of the brazier, and sat down to warm himself.
“Whew. Now I feel alive.”
Jin Wikyung smiled and handed him a cup of tea.
“You’ve had a long journey.”
“Good thing I happened to be in Henan. If I’d been in Shanxi, I wouldn’t have come even at your request, Lesser Family Head. Working an old man who’s just waiting to die this hard...”
I looked at Jang Taebo’s threatening muscles and thought,
*He looks plenty capable of hard work...*
Just look at him. He wasn’t merely fit; he was built. While overwork shaved years off other people’s lives, the worst it could do to Jang Taebo was cost him some muscle.
Wipeng seemed to be thinking along the same lines. He glanced from his own forearm to Jang Taebo’s, then spoke.
“I heard everything that happened in Sichuan and Hubei. I came myself to see if all was well and settle the matter in Henan while I was at it. It seems my timing was good.”
Jin Wikyung laughed heartily and patted Wipeng on the shoulder.
“Wipeng. You truly are my Zhang Liang!”
“I’m a martial artist.”
“Oh. Then Han Xin.”
“Han Xin was purged in the end.”
“Xiao He, then.”
“Xiao He was a civil official too.”
Jin Wikyung looked at Wipeng as though he wanted to purge him on the spot, then cleared his throat.
“Ahem. It seems you’ve had a great deal bottled up.”
In an ordinary relationship between lord and retainer, Wipeng would have denied it. But he was one of the few people who could openly give Jin Wikyung a hard time.
“Yes, my lord. Did you not know?”
“I knew, but I didn’t expect you to come all this way to tell me.”
“I didn’t come of my own accord. You summoned me. Do you realize you’ve been away for nearly three months? Not long ago, even Sect Leader Lee came to ask whether something had happened to you.”
“Cough, cough!”
The way Jin Wikyung kept clearing his throat suggested he had plenty to feel guilty about.
Wait. Sect Leader Lee? Wipeng couldn’t mean...
“Are you talking about Young Lady Lee—Lee Seowol?”
Wipeng shook his head.
“Not Young Lady. She is the bona fide Sect Leader of an established sect, Third Young Master.”
“Oh. Right.”
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had once sought to become the dominant power in Shanxi Province, only to collapse after a series of disasters.
However, Lee Seowol, the only surviving blood relative of the Blood Wolf Sword, had survived with my help and sworn loyalty to the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
Vassal or not, a Sect Leader was still a Sect Leader.
*When did I last see her...? Has it been over a year already?*
It was around the time Jeok Cheongang and I left the Jin Family of Taiyuan for Mount Jiuhua. A year had passed in Murim alone. Counting my time in the modern world, it had been even longer.
I could still remember our parting clearly.
“Excuse me, Sect Leader Lee.”
“Young Lady.”
“Pardon?”
“Please call me Young Lady.”
“Ah, yes. Young Lady Lee, then.”
“Go ahead, Young Master Jin.”
“May peace prevail throughout your household.”
“And may your sect prosper too. Whatever you do, I hope it all goes well.”
Hmm. I thought we’d parted on a fairly warm note.

The Lee Seowol I remembered had the resolve you’d expect of a martial family’s daughter. She hadn’t backed down even when Pung Yang came at her with the Red Wind Band. The ruined Mount Heng Sword Sect must have recovered quite a bit by now.
“So, is Young Lady Lee doing well these days?”
Wipeng considered the question.
“In some respects, yes. In others, perhaps not.”
“Why? Is something going wrong?”

“If you’re asking about the sect, the Mount Heng Sword Sect has already completed its reconstruction. Under Sect Leader Lee’s command, it is growing rapidly, and the number of its disciples is increasing every day.”
“Oh.”
“Great Hero Cheol Mubaek, the Tiger of Mount Heng and a friend of her late father, has also ended his seclusion and is taking an active role in the affairs of the Mount Heng Sword Sect.”
“Ohh.”
Then everything was going well, wasn’t it?
Wipeng narrowed his eyes at my puzzled look.
“Third Young Master, forgive me for asking, but have you truly not contacted her once since then?”
“Contacted her? About what?”
“...Hah. Never mind. Pretend you didn’t hear that.”
The mood had turned strange. Jang Taebo clicked his tongue beside me, and a thought flashed through my mind.
*No way. Come on, it can’t be. But what if...? No. That’s not it.*
Jin Wikyung rescued me from my sudden confusion with a single remark.
“I’m glad to hear Sect Leader Lee is doing well. What about my second brother? I haven’t seen him in months.”
Wipeng gave me a look usually reserved for a pill bug, then sighed.
“He’s much the same. He lives on the fasting pills stored in the training hall and hasn’t set foot outside.”
“Mukyung, that fool. What is he trying to do...?”
Jin Wikyung had reason to worry.
Before I left for Mount Jiuhua, Jin Mukyung had lost a duel to Cheongpung. From that day on, he’d shut himself in the training hall and refused to come out.
A year had passed. The Star-Array Grand Banquet had been held, and Dark Heaven’s shadow now hung over Murim. He was still in there.
*He did say he wouldn’t come out until he’d accomplished something great.*
There was a time when all of Murim called Jin Mukyung a once-in-a-millennium genius.

Even the direct disciples of the Nine Sects and One Gang, with their generous supply of exceptional martial arts and elixirs, couldn’t compare to him. Despite being born into a fallen martial family on the fringes, Jin Mukyung had risen to the forefront of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes on the strength of his martial arts alone.
*And then he met Cheongpung.*
For Jin Mukyung, Cheongpung’s existence must have been an enormous shock and an equally enormous stimulus. The fact that he was still training in seclusion more than a year later was proof of it.
*He’ll accomplish something. I’m sure of it.*
The Jin Mukyung I knew was a genius, no question.
He hadn’t had the Sword Saint to teach him, or exceptional elixirs and martial arts handed to him. He’d come this far on his own. I couldn’t imagine what he might be like when he finally emerged.
*The question is when.*
He wasn’t going to emerge when he was nearly sixty, was he?
If he survived on nothing but fasting pills until then, I’d genuinely respect him and treat him as my hyung. Frankly, a full year of eating those tasteless things was impressive enough.
Even Wudang Daoists brought jerky instead of fasting pills when they practiced wall-facing meditation. What did that tell you?
*One bite of a fasting pill, and even the worst vegetarians—the kind who flip over the grill at a barbecue restaurant—would go looking for pork belly.*
While I was thinking about that, the conversation had moved on to Jang Taebo.
“By the way, Lesser Family Head, will you tell this old man why you summoned him?”
In response to Jang Taebo’s grumbling question, Jin Wikyung abruptly tossed out a single phrase.
“Ironcraft Hall. What do you think?”
“I’ve never heard of such a place in the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”
“You wouldn’t have. It was established only a few days ago.”
Jang Taebo frowned.
“It’s a strangely familiar name. It reminds me of the Ironcraft Guild, where this old man once worked.”
“I named it with you in mind, Old Master Jang. Master of Ironcraft Hall. Has a nice ring to it, doesn’t it?”
“Lesser Family Head.”
Jang Taebo sighed.
“I left the Ironcraft Guild long ago.”
“Then perhaps it’s time you came back.”
“I’m old and tired. I haven’t the strength to lift a hammer.”
Jin Wikyung stared meaningfully at Jang Taebo’s threatening muscles, then moved his lips.
“Youngest.”
By now, I knew exactly why he’d summoned Jang Taebo. I tapped White Flame, strapped across my back, and let it fall.
Clang!
“Oh no! I dropped a divine weapon made by a blacksmith too old and tired to lift a hammer!”
“My spear, made from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron! They say it’s incredibly difficult to work. I wonder who made it...”
Jang Taebo glared at me as though he wanted to tear me apart.
“Enough.”
“Why? I wasn’t talking about you, Elder.”
“I made it, didn’t I?”
“What are you talking about? How could someone who can’t lift a hammer make this?”
“...That damned brat.”
Jang Taebo sighed as though the ground itself had collapsed, then looked at Jin Wikyung.
“Was this why you gave me all sorts of help?”
“Of course not. It was a simple kindness to the artisan who made a divine weapon for my beloved youngest brother.”
“Then I’ll answer your proposal.”
“I’m listening.”
“No. That is the only answer this old man can give. It wouldn’t change with a blade at my throat.”
I shot my hand up.
“What about the spear?”
“Shut up before I take it back and snap it.”
“Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron. Special feature: fucking hard.”
“...Why did I ever make a spear for a bastard like you? What riches and glory did I think I’d get out of it?”
“Just become the Master of Ironcraft Hall. I hear you’ve had plenty of help from our family.”
“I’ll repay you with money. Do you think I’m going to put myself through that kind of hell again at my age?”
“Seriously? You really won’t do it?”
“Then what are you going to do? I said I wouldn’t.”
“Then just tell me your conditions. I’ll meet as many of them as I can.”
“Conditions?”
A smug smile appeared on Jang Taebo’s face.
“Remember this time last year? I’ll set the same conditions.”
“The conditions from back then? You can’t mean...”
“The Herb of Eternal Youth, gongcheong seokyu, a dragon’s claw, or a dragon pearl. Bring me any one of those.”

Jang Taebo entered Jin Wikyung’s heavy-cloth tent, claimed the spot in front of the brazier, and sat down to warm himself.
“Whew.
Now I feel alive.”
Jin Wikyung smiled and handed him a cup of tea.
“You’ve had a long journey.”
“Good thing I happened to be in Henan.
If I’d been in Shanxi, I wouldn’t have come even at your request, Lesser Family Head.
Working an old man who’s just waiting to die this hard...”
I looked at Jang Taebo’s threatening muscles and thought,
*He looks plenty capable of hard work...*
Just look at him.
He wasn’t merely fit; he was built.
While overwork shaved years off other people’s lives, the worst it could do to Jang Taebo was cost him some muscle.
Wipeng seemed to be thinking along the same lines.
He glanced from his own forearm to Jang Taebo’s, then spoke.
“I heard everything that happened in Sichuan and Hubei.
I came myself to see if all was well and settle the matter in Henan while I was at it.
It seems my timing was good.”
Jin Wikyung laughed heartily and patted Wipeng on the shoulder.
“Wipeng.
You truly are my Zhang Liang!”
“I’m a martial artist.”
“Oh.
Then Han Xin.”
“Han Xin was purged in the end.”
“Xiao He, then.”
“Xiao He was a civil official too.”
Jin Wikyung looked at Wipeng as though he wanted to purge him on the spot, then cleared his throat.
“Ahem.
It seems you’ve had a great deal bottled up.”
In an ordinary relationship between lord and retainer, Wipeng would have denied it.
But he was one of the few people who could openly give Jin Wikyung a hard time.
“Yes, my lord.
Did you not know?”
“I knew, but I didn’t expect you to come all this way to tell me.”
“I didn’t come of my own accord.
You summoned me.
Do you realize you’ve been away for nearly three months?
Not long ago, even Sect Leader Lee came to ask whether something had happened to you.”
“Cough, cough!”
The way Jin Wikyung kept clearing his throat suggested he had plenty to feel guilty about.
Wait.
Sect Leader Lee?
Wipeng couldn’t mean...
“Are you talking about Young Lady Lee—Lee Seowol?”
Wipeng shook his head.
“Not Young Lady.
She is the bona fide Sect Leader of an established sect, Third Young Master.”
“Oh.
Right.”
The Mount Heng Sword Sect had once sought to become the dominant power in Shanxi Province, only to collapse after a series of disasters.
However, Lee Seowol, the only surviving blood relative of the Blood Wolf Sword, had survived with my help and sworn loyalty to the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
Vassal or not, a Sect Leader was still a Sect Leader.
*When did I last see her...?
Has it been over a year already?*
It was around the time Jeok Cheongang and I left the Jin Family of Taiyuan for Mount Jiuhua.
A year had passed in Murim alone.
Counting my time in the modern world, it had been even longer.
I could still remember our parting clearly.
“Excuse me, Sect Leader Lee.”
“Young Lady.”
“Pardon?”
“Please call me Young Lady.”
“Ah, yes.
Young Lady Lee, then.”
“Go ahead, Young Master Jin.”
“May peace prevail throughout your household.”
“And may your sect prosper too.
Whatever you do, I hope it all goes well.”
Hmm.
I thought we’d parted on a fairly warm note.
The Lee Seowol I remembered had the resolve you’d expect of a martial family’s daughter.
She hadn’t backed down even when Pung Yang came at her with the Red Wind Band.
The ruined Mount Heng Sword Sect must have recovered quite a bit by now.
“So, is Young Lady Lee doing well these days?”
Wipeng considered the question.
“In some respects, yes.
In others, perhaps not.”
“Why?
Is something going wrong?”
“If you’re asking about the sect, the Mount Heng Sword Sect has already completed its reconstruction.
Under Sect Leader Lee’s command, it is growing rapidly, and the number of its disciples is increasing every day.”
“Oh.”
“Great Hero Cheol Mubaek, the Tiger of Mount Heng and a friend of her late father, has also ended his seclusion and is taking an active role in the affairs of the Mount Heng Sword Sect.”
“Ohh.”
Then everything was going well, wasn’t it?
Wipeng narrowed his eyes at my puzzled look.
“Third Young Master, forgive me for asking, but have you truly not contacted her once since then?”
“Contacted her?
About what?”
Never mind.
Pretend you didn’t hear that.”
The mood had turned strange.
Jang Taebo clicked his tongue beside me, and a thought flashed through my mind.
*No way.
Come on, it can’t be.
But what if...?
No.
That’s not it.*
Jin Wikyung rescued me from my sudden confusion with a single remark.
“I’m glad to hear Sect Leader Lee is doing well.
What about my second brother?
I haven’t seen him in months.”
Wipeng gave me a look usually reserved for a pill bug, then sighed.
“He’s much the same.
He lives on the fasting pills stored in the training hall and hasn’t set foot outside.”
“Mukyung, that fool.
What is he trying to do...?”
Jin Wikyung had reason to worry.
Before I left for Mount Jiuhua, Jin Mukyung had lost a duel to Cheongpung.
From that day on, he’d shut himself in the training hall and refused to come out.
A year had passed.
The Star-Array Grand Banquet had been held, and Dark Heaven’s shadow now hung over Murim.
He was still in there.
*He did say he wouldn’t come out until he’d accomplished something great.*
There was a time when all of Murim called Jin Mukyung a once-in-a-millennium genius.
Even the direct disciples of the Nine Sects and One Gang, with their generous supply of exceptional martial arts and elixirs, couldn’t compare to him.
Despite being born into a fallen martial family on the fringes, Jin Mukyung had risen to the forefront of the Ten Dragons and Phoenixes on the strength of his martial arts alone.
*And then he met Cheongpung.*
For Jin Mukyung, Cheongpung’s existence must have been an enormous shock and an equally enormous stimulus.
The fact that he was still training in seclusion more than a year later was proof of it.
*He’ll accomplish something.
I’m sure of it.*
The Jin Mukyung I knew was a genius, no question.
He hadn’t had the Sword Saint to teach him, or exceptional elixirs and martial arts handed to him.
He’d come this far on his own.
I couldn’t imagine what he might be like when he finally emerged.
*The question is when.*
He wasn’t going to emerge when he was nearly sixty, was he?
If he survived on nothing but fasting pills until then, I’d genuinely respect him and treat him as my hyung.
Frankly, a full year of eating those tasteless things was impressive enough.
Even Wudang Daoists brought jerky instead of fasting pills when they practiced wall-facing meditation.
What did that tell you?

chapters.title: Chapter 500
paragraphs: It was still dark when Jang Taebo followed us out, looking as though he’d been led to his execution. The moment he saw the Water God Dragon’s remains, his expression changed.
“Ohhh... Ohhhhh...!”
Talk about a change of attitude.
Trembling like a kindergartener who needed to pee, Jang Taebo threw himself between the mountains of bones and scales.
“Oh, the strength! The color!”
His eyes had gone hazy, and his voice shook. He ran his hands over the scales and stroked the bones, unable to contain his excitement.
“I’d be happy to be buried here and die! No, I want to die here!”
“Get the Old Master out of there! The pile’s about to collapse!”
“Y-yes, sir!”
The Jin Dragon Squad martial artists had been staring blankly at the remains of a gigantic creature unlike anything they had ever seen. Now they rushed forward and dragged Jang Taebo out.
Only then did the old Master Artisan come to his senses. He looked at me with moist eyes.
“So everything you told me was true.”
“It sounds insane, but every word of it was true.”
“I thought I’d had my fill of working meteorite iron fallen from the sky and Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron...”
Jang Taebo wiped at his eyes. He sniffed, tried to compose himself, then seized my shoulder.
“Thank you. Now I can die without regrets.”
I gave him a warm look.
“Don’t say that. Stay healthy and live a long life. Have something nourishing simmered for yourself, too.”
“You little...”
“You still have plenty of Stamina and life left to grind into the forge. Where are you trying to run off to—the afterlife?”
“You little...!”
Same words. Different feeling.
A high-quality slave this hard to acquire deserved to be put to work. Toss him a reward now and then, crack the whip when needed.
Of course, I wasn’t the one holding the whip.
“Well, would you look at that. Even the second time, it’s astonishing. And there’s so much of it.”
“Speak of the whip holder.”
“Hm? What was that, my youngest?”
“Nothing, eldest brother.”
Jin Wikyung tilted his head, then laughed and patted Jang Taebo on the back.
“What do you think, Hall Master Jang? Quite a sight, isn’t it?”
“Hall Master... Jang?”
“Of course. You’re the Master of our family’s Ironcraft Hall now. That makes you Hall Master Jang. Come, let’s hear your opinion.”
The reality Jang Taebo had briefly forgotten began to sink in. His face darkened.
“There’s no question it’s extraordinary. Even at the Ironcraft Guild, with the finest artisans and materials under Heaven gathered in one place, I never saw anything like this.”
“So, can you work with it?”
“I can’t promise anything until I try. But...”
Jang Taebo studied the mountain of remains before continuing.
“The bones are far stronger than meteorite iron, though not quite as strong as Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron. They should be workable.”
“And the hide and scales?”
“I made enough armor in my younger days to get sick of it. None of it was made from an imugi, of course... but I’ll try.”
“Oh!”

“With this much material, there will be enough to arm every martial artist in the Jin Family of Taiyuan—or rather, in our family—and still have some left over. I should be able to show results soon, so I trust you’ll forgive the first few failures.”
“Of course.”
Among artisans, Jang Taebo held a place equal to—or perhaps higher than—the Three Saints did among martial artists.
Jin Wikyung’s face lit up at the high-quality slave’s calm, well-founded confidence.
“I’ve heard that only the finest Master Artisan of his generation can lead the Ironcraft Guild. I’m counting on you, Hall Master Jang. Whatever you need, just say the word.”
“Then assign me some artisans I can rely on, Lesser Family Head.”
“Artisans?”
“I know our family has artisans of its own. If I train them, they may not become the beams that hold up the family, but they could make sturdy pillars. However...”
“That would take time. Am I right?”
“Yes. I have eyes and ears, and I’ve heard what’s been happening across the world. The artisans I still keep in touch with tell me orders for weapons and armor have risen sharply.”
The war had already begun.

From the small and mid-sized sects scattered throughout Murim to the Nine Sects and One Gang, everyone wanted weapons and armor to prepare for the war that had drawn so close. The fires of the forges would not go out until the war ended.
In the current state of Murim, it was not only the flames of war that had begun to blaze fiercely.
“Time is short, Lesser Family Head.”
Jin Wikyung looked up at the sky in silence. Then he spoke.
“Hall Master Jang, how long have you been at this?”
“I started when I was shorter than your sword, Lesser Family Head. I’ve devoted my life to it.”
“Then after all those years in the trade, you must have made many friends.”
“Of course. Every one of them is a renowned artisan in their field.”
“Send messenger pigeons to everyone who comes to mind. I don’t care if it costs a fortune.”
“Everyone has something they value more than money. To an artisan like me, the body of an imugi is worth more than any fortune.”
Jang Taebo stepped back and gave Jin Wikyung a respectful martial salute.
“Jang Taebo, Master of Ironcraft Hall of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan, obeys the Lesser Family Head’s command.”

By then, the darkness had retreated and the sun was rising on a new day. The light spreading from the east looked like the glow of a forge, and the quick footsteps of the Jin Dragon Squad martial artists carrying away the Water God Dragon’s remains beat like hammers.

While fifty Jin Dragon Squad martial artists transported the Water God Dragon’s remains under Wipeng and Jang Taebo’s meticulous direction, Jin Wikyung and I returned to where we were supposed to be. There we found Zhuge Feng beside himself with excitement.
“I did it! I’m telling you, I did it!”
He bounced around like a child, without a trace of the dignity expected of a clan’s Family Head.
But once I saw what he’d done, I couldn’t help nodding.
*He blocked the magical power completely.*
Unlike before, not even a trace of magical power escaped the enormous rift—or rather, the Gate.
The dogs, pigs, fish, and other animals apparently left there for testing showed an interest in it a few times, then went back to what they’d been doing.
“You really did it, Sir Zhuge,” Jin Wikyung said.
A broad smile spread across Zhuge Feng’s exhausted face.

“Of course I did. Even my ancestor Zhuge Wuhou couldn’t have managed this. Come to think of it, he knew a thing or two about mechanisms and formations himself, but Wei still kicked his ass in the end...”
“F-Family Head!”

“What? It’s true! If he really cared about the people and was such a great strategist, he should’ve thrown a resignation letter in that incompetent emperor’s face instead of a campaign memorial, then taken the throne for himself...”
“Family Head, have you lost your mind?”
“No, Uncle. Am I wrong?”
The Zhuge Clan was a mess.
Having smeared shit all over his ancestor’s reputation, the current Family Head shook off his relatives and continued proudly.
“Well? What do you think of the Demon-Sealing Formation now that you’ve seen it?”
“The Demon-Sealing Formation?”
Zhuge Feng nodded, pleased with himself.
“I named it. A formation that seals a demon’s power. Fitting, isn’t it?”
The Demon-Sealing Formation. Considering where that power came from, I couldn’t think of a better name.
Not that the name mattered if the formation worked.
As I carefully examined the Demon-Sealing Formation, Jin Wikyung whispered to me.
“What do you think?”
“Of what?”
“I’m just looking at it. How would I know?”

Murim formations were much like modern magic circles. I’d encountered Magic plenty of times as a Hunter and still knew next to nothing about it. There was no way I could judge a formation at a glance.
I could at least sense the qi flowing through it.
*Looks like it’s drawing in qi from the natural world to block the magical power... The principle is similar to a magic circle.*

Compared with modern magic circles, though, the formations I’d seen and heard about in Murim were much more limited in variety and power. Murim’s emphasis on martial arts themselves probably had a lot to do with that.
*They did this faster and better than I expected.*
The natural qi flowing through the formation was enough to block the magical power leaking from the Gate completely. For now, it was the best solution we had.
After looking it over carefully, I turned to Zhuge Feng.
“How long will the Demon-Sealing Formation last?”
“Do you think the Yangtze will ever run dry?”
“Ah.”
“It will keep drawing in the qi around it and continue operating. Assuming my theory is correct.”
“And if it isn’t?”
“My theory? You might as well call Zhuge Wuhou a halfwit.”
Clang!
“You bastard, Zhuge Feng!”
“Great-Uncle, no! Put your sword down!”
“Someone shut the Family Head’s mouth!”
The atmosphere had suddenly turned murderous.
Before blood could be spilled among the relatives, I hurried to speak to Zhuge Feng, who was using a grappling technique against the family members rushing him.
“Can you keep installing these?”
“Huh?”
“What?”
“What do you mean?”
For the benefit of the Zhuge Clan members who had stopped in their tracks, I said it again, slowly and clearly.
“Keep installing them. Dozens of times. Hundreds, if necessary.”
The air around us instantly turned cold.
Zhuge Feng, who had been held by the collar by an old man, straightened his clothes. When he looked at me again, his eyes were steady and his voice had gone quiet.
“Now I’m curious what the Divine Dragon has in mind.”
I clicked my tongue bitterly.
“It’s obvious, isn’t it? You already know, Sir Zhuge.”
“I do. If it happened once, it could happen ten times. A hundred.”
“Then we’re thinking the same thing.”
“I wasn’t as certain as you. I was only considering every possibility.”
Something unreadable flashed in Zhuge Feng’s eyes.
“Why are you so certain that things like this will continue happening? What grounds do you have for speaking with such confidence?”
Plenty. I just couldn’t tell him.
The Zhuge Clan might have celebrated when Zhuge Feng was born, but when I was born, all of humanity celebrated. The Demon King Asmodeus had fallen, and the long Great Cataclysm had ended.
There was no explaining the difference.
An entire lifetime—my lifetime—had passed since then. Yet Gates still existed in the modern world, and new ones kept appearing.
Once a dam starts to crack, no matter how sturdy it is, there’s no telling how far the damage will spread.
That was Murim now.
*I can’t exactly tell them all of this.*
In the end, there was only one answer I could give.
“I saw it and felt it in the memories the Water God Dragon passed on to me. Dark Heaven intended this from the start. They planned it and carried it out. And they’ll keep doing it.”
“You’re a better liar than I expected.”
“You’re more suspicious than I expected.”
“I can’t believe you. No—that’s not quite true. I don’t want to.”
“Zhuge Wuhou must have felt the same way. And yet he still served that stupid emperor until the very end. Even if it fucking sucks, you have to accept it.”
“Even if it fucking sucks, you have to accept it...”
Zhuge Feng gave a short laugh and turned to Jin Wikyung.
“What do you think, Lesser Family Head?”
“I agree with my younger brother,” Jin Wikyung said calmly.
“I do wonder what the others will think.”
“Then why don’t we ask them?”
“What does that mean...?”
Zhuge Feng studied Jin Wikyung. Then he murmured, “Henan.”
“Yes.”
Jin Wikyung looked into the distance.
“The New Murim Alliance.”
